The tool is read there and moved into the combine’s coordinates by the occurrences’ placements at the combine’s point of the timeline, so the combine follows when either occurrence moves. A body is a tool once per occurrence: two occurrences of one component (two screws of one part) are two tools, each cutting (joining, intersecting) where it is and each following its own occurrence; the occurrences not listed do nothing. The same body in the same occurrence twice is refused (body F2.b0 in O1 is listed more than once). A consumed tool (without keep_tools) leaves its own component, once however many occurrences it was a tool in. The target stays a body of the combine’s component: a cut changes that component’s definition, so every occurrence of it shows the cut.

A plain id is a body of the combine’s own component, or, as files of earlier versions and imports write it, a body of another component whose link tool_links holds (saved and read as it was written):

{"type": "combine", "target": "F7.b0", "tools": ["F2.b0"], "operation": "cut",
 "keep_tools": true, "tool_links": {"F2.b0": {"source": "O1", "target": "O2"}}}

A tool_links entry for a body that is not a plain-id tool is refused (linked but not a tool); a tool of another component without an occurrence or a link fails the combine (body F2.b0 (from Extrude1) belongs to A; …). Paste New, moves into components and occurrences moved into others carry both forms’ links. Tests: core/model-tests/links/src/link_tests.rs (a_combine_cuts_with_a_body_in_two_occurrences_each_where_it_is, a_combine_joins_a_body_in_two_occurrences, a_combine_of_an_earlier_version_with_tool_links_loads_and_recomputes_as_before, paste_new_keeps_a_combines_tools_in_occurrences).

move, align, scale 

{"type": "move", "bodies": ["F2.b0"], "copy": false,
 "transform": {"type": "translate_xyz", "x": 10, "y": 5, "z": 0}}

transform: {"type": "free", "matrix": [[r00, r01, r02, tx], [r10, …], [r20, …]]} (a rotation and a translation), translate_xyz (x, y, z), translate_along (axis, distance), rotate (axis, angle, right-handed), point_to_point (from, to), point_to_position (point, x, y, z). A moved body keeps its id and face names; with copy the moved copies are new bodies <move>.b<j> with faces <move>:inst1(<face>) (a copy that does not move is a copy and paste). A rotation and a translation (a move or an align) place the body as a location on its own shape (mitcad#838, Kernel::move_shape): its faces keep their geometry and the display meshes they have, so the view meshes nothing again; the body before the move is not changed. A mirror or a scale makes a transformed copy.

A point or an axis may be geometry of another component, picked where an occurrence shows it (mitcad#699): from_occurrence, to_occurrence, point_occurrence or axis_occurrence beside the reference is that occurrence’s absolute path from the root ("O1/O4"; "" the root), as pattern_at_points gives its points’ occurrences. move, move_occurrence and move_face take them alike:

{"type": "move_occurrence", "occurrences": ["O2"],
 "transform": {"type": "point_to_point",
   "from": {"body": "F2.b0", "vertex": "V{…}"}, "from_occurrence": "O2",
   "to": {"body": "F2.b0", "vertex": "V{…}"}, "to_occurrence": "O1"}}

The reference is resolved in the component the path ends in (a vertex of its body, a sketch point or construction point of it), placed where the occurrence puts it at the feature’s point of the timeline, and taken into the coordinates of the feature’s component (its first occurrence). So two copies of one component are told apart, and the move follows when either occurrence moves later. A point on an occurrence the feature itself moves is where it was before this motion. Sketches and construction geometry must be in the component the path ends in (Sketch1 is in B, not in Root); a path that leads nowhere fails the feature. Without an occurrence a reference is in the feature’s component’s coordinates, as in earlier versions (and a body of another component fails the feature: body F2.b0 (from Extrude1) belongs to Part; …); definitions are written back without the fields they did not have. Moving an occurrence a path runs through to another parent is refused. Tests: core/model-tests/assembly/src/component_tests.rs (a_move_of_an_occurrence_takes_points_where_their_occurrences_place_them, a_move_of_an_occurrence_tells_the_copies_of_a_component_apart, a_move_takes_a_sketch_point_of_another_component_by_its_occurrence, a_move_without_occurrences_takes_its_points_in_its_component_as_before).

{"type": "align", "bodies": ["F2.b0"],
 "from": {"type": "plane", "plane": {"body": "F2.b0", "face": "F2:start(…)"}},
 "to": {"type": "plane", "plane": "xy"}, "flip": false, "angle": 0}

from and to are {"type": "point", "point": …}, {"type": "axis", "axis": …} or {"type": "plane", "plane": …}: a point goes onto a point, line or plane; an axis onto an axis (direction and line; circle centres meet); a plane onto a plane with the normals opposite (faces against each other) and origins together (a face’s middle). flip turns the moved geometry over; angle turns about the target axis or normal.

{"type": "scale", "bodies": ["F2.b0"], "point": "origin",
 "scale": {"type": "uniform", "factor": 2}}

scale: {"type": "uniform", "factor"} or {"type": "non_uniform", "x", "y", "z"} along the model axes; factors greater than zero. A non-uniform scale turns faces into B-splines (names stay).

box, cylinder, cone, sphere, torus 

{"type": "box", "plane": "xy", "corner": [0, 0],
 "length": 30, "width": 20, "height": 10, "symmetric": false, "operation": "new_body", "participants": []}
{"type": "cylinder", "plane": …, "center": [u, v], "diameter": 20, "height": 30, "symmetric": false, "operation": …}
{"type": "cone", "plane": …, "center": [u, v], "radius": 10, "top_radius": 4, "height": 30, "symmetric": false, "operation": …}
{"type": "sphere", "plane": …, "center": [u, v], "diameter": 30, "operation": …}
{"type": "torus", "plane": …, "center": [u, v], "diameter": 40, "section_diameter": 10,
 "position": "on_center" | "inside" | "outside", "operation": …}

Placed on the plane at plane coordinates (the frame a sketch on the plane has), height or axis along the plane’s normal (negative height: against it). Each coordinate of corner and center is a number or, like the sizes, a value (mitcad#689): an expression or a parameter, such as "corner": ["-L/2", "-W/2"], which becomes a dimension of the feature (slots corner.x, corner.y, center.x, center.y) and moves the primitive when the parameters it uses change. A plain number stays a number, without a parameter, as documents and imports have always written it, so stored documents load unchanged; the feature query gives a value’s parameter name. operation and participants as for extrude. Faces: <feature>:bottom, top, side0..side3 for a box (side0 at the corner’s y, side1 at x + length, counter-clockwise) and side0 for curved faces.

Cone (mitcad#2239): a cone or a frustum, placed as a cylinder (plane and center, or at). radius is the base’s, on the plane; top_radius the radius at the height, left out or 0 for a full cone ending in an apex. A negative height goes against the plane’s normal with the base still on the plane (the cone turned over, not moved); symmetric puts the base half the height below the plane (above it for a negative height). Its faces keep their names when the values change, so a fillet on the base edge E{<feature>:bottom|<feature>:side0} follows a new radius: bottom the base disc (none when radius is 0), top the top disc (a frustum only) and side0 the conical face. Refused in words: a negative radius, both radii 0, a zero height, and equal radii (that is a cylinder, use Cylinder); a parameter changed into one of them fails the feature with the same words. The kernel builds it with Kernel::primitive (PrimitiveShape::Cone; OCCT’s BRepPrimAPI_MakeCone; test_primitives_name_their_faces of the geometry suite, geometry/tests/test_transform.cpp). Tests: core.model.features-solid (cone_tests) and core.model (features::primitive), both with the mock kernel, cli.primitive_cone (OCCT: the volumes pi r^2 h / 3 and pi h (R^2 + R r + r^2) / 3, a fillet on the base edge through a radius change, a cone cut from a box), the .solidcraft import’s format-50-cone test design and the UI test primitive-cone.

bounding_solid 

{"type": "bounding_solid", "bodies": ["F2.b0", "F4.b0"], "margin": 5}
{"type": "bounding_solid", "margin": 0}

A new body (BoundingSolid<n>, mitcad#460): the box around the bodies, grown by margin on every side (a negative margin shrinks it; one that leaves no box fails the feature). bodies empty or left out: every body of the feature’s component at its point of the timeline (an earlier bounding solid too). The box is aligned with the component’s axes and holds the bodies’ exact geometry (Kernel::bounding_box, the tight box of their faces, not of a display mesh); it is built with the box primitive (Kernel::primitive), so its faces are named as a box’s: <feature>:bottom at the lowest z, top at the highest, side0 at the lowest y, side1 at the highest x, side2 at the highest y and side3 at the lowest x. The bodies are only read: the box is built again from them on every recompute and follows their edits and the margin’s. A body is listed once and must be of the feature’s component; no bodies at all fails the feature. Patterns and mirrors cannot repeat it as a feature (it has no tool); its body is patterned, mirrored or moved like any other.

Tests: core.model (features::bounding_solid, mock kernel), cli.bounding_solid (OCCT) and the .solidcraft import’s bounding-solid test design.

construction_plane, construction_axis, construction_point 

{"type": "construction_plane", "definition": {"type": "offset", "plane": "xy", "distance": 10}}

Named Plane1, Axis1, Point1; they make no bodies. Their result is a datum, which follows parameter edits and is cached like a body.

A construction plane may take the faces, edges and vertices its definition names from bodies of other components (mitcad#196): "links": {"F2.b0": {"source": "O1", "target": ""}} (an OccurrenceLink per body, as an extrusion’s object_links, Geometry of other components) reads the body in its component and moves it into the plane’s coordinates by the occurrences' placements at the plane’s point of the timeline, so that a midplane between faces of two components lies where the design places them and follows when they move. Without a link another component’s body is out of reach and the plane fails.

Construction axes and points take the same links (mitcad#1029): an axis through an edge of another component, a point at its vertex, an axis or point on its face are read in that component and moved into the axis’s or point’s coordinates by the placements, so that they lie where the design shows the geometry and follow when its occurrence moves. The application’s Construct commands send a link for each face, edge or vertex picked in an occurrence of another component than the one the datum is made in (the active one, or an edited datum’s own), with target the occurrence the view shows that component at, so the other component does not have to be activated.

A construction plane, axis or point of another component is made in that component’s coordinates, so without a link a construction feature that names one in its definition ("plane": "F5") is refused, as any feature using another component’s sketch or construction geometry (F6: “Plane1 is in Motor; a feature of Frame cannot use it”). "datum_links": {"F5": {"source": "O1", "target": "O2"}} (an OccurrenceLink per datum feature, mitcad#1035) lets it through and moves the datum into the plane’s, axis’s or point’s coordinates by the placements, as links moves a body, so that an offset plane from another component’s plane or an axis through its axis lies where the design shows it and follows when its occurrence moves. A link whose source occurrence shows another component than the datum’s is refused (“Plane1 is in Motor, not in Frame, where the link O2 leads”; at recompute, after later edits, the feature fails). The application’s Construct commands send a link for each construction datum of another component than the one the new datum is made in. The links follow reparenting, copies and moves as links do and count as references for the design policy.

A sketch of another component named in the definition (a sketch line, point or path, {"sketch": "F3", "curve": "c1"}) is likewise made in its own component’s coordinates and refused without a link (F6). datum_links takes a link keyed by the sketch too ("datum_links": {"F3": {"source": "O1", "target": "O2"}}, mitcad#1039): it lets the sketch through, and the sketch’s frame is moved by the placements, its curves and points with it, so an axis along another component’s sketch line, a point at its sketch point or a plane along its sketch curve lies where the design shows that sketch. A link whose source shows another component than the sketch’s is refused as for a datum. The Construct commands send a link for each sketch of another component.

An edge is a line where it runs straight, whatever curve the kernel stores it as (mitcad#1537): a B-spline or Bezier edge whose poles lie within 1e-6 mm of the segment between its ends is a line to line, line1, line2 and edge (the kernel’s edge_geometry), as a planar spline face is a plane to plane. The straight edges and planar walls of a sheet body with a bend (a Fold, a Convert to Sheet Metal with bends) are such splines, so datums on them work as on a solid’s and follow the sheet when it changes (tools/cli/tests/sheet_datums.json: each datum on a converted plate, a converted channel and a folded sheet, within 1e-6 mm, after the plate’s length and the fold’s angle change too).

Every reference that takes a plane reads a flat face alike, whatever surface the kernel stores (mitcad#1554): a face within 1e-6 mm of a plane is that plane (its normal out of the material) as Mirror’s plane, a construction feature’s plane, a sketch plane (with the face’s edges as the sketch’s references), Split Body’s and Split Face’s tool (extended along its plane), Draft’s fixed plane, Align’s plane, an extrusion’s start or to_object face, a hole’s end face and the faces whose middle Kernel::face_plane gives (holes and joints on a face) (face_geometry, and detail::reference_plane in geometry/src/face_select.cpp). A face that is not flat (a bend’s surfaces, the side of a bend whose boundary is not square to the bend line) stays refused: face … is not planar (bspline). tools/cli/tests/sheet_face_planes.json mirrors a block about the flat faces of a converted plate, a converted channel and a folded sheet (its B-spline walls among them), splits, aligns, sketches and extrudes on a wall, and checks that the images follow the sheets when the channel’s height and the fold’s angle change, within 1e-6 mm.

A face is round where it is round, whatever surface the kernel stores it as (mitcad#1855): a face whose stored surface (an extrusion of a circle, a revolution, a B-spline or Bezier surface) lies within 1e-6 mm of a cylinder, cone, sphere or torus all over the face is that one to every reference that reads a face’s surface through Kernel::face_geometry (Axis Through Cylinder/Cone/Torus’ face, a point’s center on a sphere or torus, joint and mount frames, section picks, helix and coordinate system references) and to Kernel::face_cylinder (Bearing, thread fits, hole callouts); an edge within 1e-6 mm of a circle is that circle to Kernel::edge_geometry (a point’s center, joint frames on a circular edge). The walls of holes in a sheet body with a bend are such B-spline cylinders and their rims B-spline circles once a sheet feature (a Hole, a Flange) has rebuilt the body, also where the hole was cut by Sketch + Extrude Cut. The recognition is OCCT’s (GeomConvert_SurfToAnaSurf, GeomConvert_CurveToAnaCurve), checked again over the face or edge (geometry::analytic_surface and geometry::is_circular in geometry/src/datum.cpp). The faces and edges queries read such items the same way since mitcad#1863 (Faces and edges with geometry); Kernel::face_geometries and Kernel::edge_geometries, which the imports and sheet features read large bodies with in one pass, still give them their stored type. tools/cli/tests/round_faces_recognised.json takes the walls of a cut and a Hole in a plate and in a sheet’s flange as axes, the flange wall’s rim as a centre point, and a cut wall in each as a Cylindrical joint’s origin.

Fractions and lengths beyond a path’s ends continue straight along the end tangent. A plane’s frame (x_axis, y_axis) is what a sketch on it uses: offsets and angles move the reference frame; other planes take the model X axis projected onto them (Y when X is along the normal). Inputs that do not fit (parallel lines, collinear points, lines that pass each other) fail the feature with a message. The preview of a construction feature adds its datum.

base 

{"type": "base", "source": "bracket.step",
 "bodies": [{"name": "Bracket", "color": [0.8, 0.8, 0.8],
             "brep": {"format": "occt", "compression": "zlib", "size": 6146, "data": "eJy1V..."}},
            {"name": "Scan", "mesh": true, "brep": {…}}],
 "operation": "new_body", "participants": []}

Bodies without history: imported files, the bodies of .f3d files and the .f3d importer’s fallback (features/base.rs). Normally created with import_file or the shape API, not written by hand.

  • bodies: B-rep data (OCCT’s binary format, zlib-compressed, base64; compression may be "none") with an optional name and color (sRGB, 0..1); mesh marks a mesh body (triangles only, from STL or OBJ). In a project the data is a reference into the project’s store (sha256 instead of data, see Design files). A linked design’s body records the material and appearance (ids in this design) its source design gives it (Materials of inserted components); they do not change the body.
  • operation: new_body (default; body i is <feature>.b<i>, named after its name, made unique with (2), …), or join, cut, intersect with participants (all bodies when empty), with the same results as an extrusion’s. Mesh bodies can only be new bodies; placed by a moved or turned occurrence they are measured and reported where the design shows them, like other bodies.
  • replaces: ["F2.b0", …] (new bodies only): body i takes the id and display name of the i-th listed body, so later features that use that body continue on the new one; listed bodies beyond the new ones are removed. The importers’ fallbacks use it.
  • Faces are <feature>:import(<j>), j counting the faces of all bodies in order (body 0’s first) in the kernel’s face order, so the names stay as long as the data does. Edges and vertices follow: E{F4:import(0)|F4:import(3)}.
  • cage (optional, per body): the control cage an imported Form body was made from, kept as data (Control cages of imported Form bodies).

Component features 

{"type": "component_from_bodies", "bodies": ["F2.b0"]}
{"type": "move_occurrence", "occurrences": ["O2"],
 "transform": {"type": "translate_xyz", "x": 0, "y": 0, "z": 30}}
{"type": "capture_position", "positions": [{"occurrence": "O2",
 "transform": [[1, 0, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0, -50], [0, 0, 1, 0]]}]}

move_occurrence takes the motions of move (rigid ones only) and is named Move<n> like moves of bodies; its points and axes may be on other components with the occurrence they were picked in (from_occurrence …, move, align, scale, mitcad#699), a point on a moved occurrence where it was before the move; capture_position is Position<n>. See Components and occurrences.

Mesh bodies in surface operations

A mesh body (triangles without surfaces: STL and OBJ files, the face sets of IFC files and the meshes of other imported models; kind mesh in the bodies query) has no surfaces for the operations that intersect, offset or round faces (mitcad#399; OCCT’s boolean read a face’s null surface and crashed on Windows, mitcad#392). The features refuse one before the geometry kernel gets it (features/surface_bodies.rs), with an error naming the body: body F5.b0 (from Base1) is a mesh body (triangles without surfaces), which Combine cannot use; it works on solid and surface bodies.

  • Refused where a feature names it: combine’s target and tools; the participants of extrude, revolve, sweep, loft, pipe, coil, helix, rib, web, hole, emboss (its face’s body too), base and the patterns’ features; an extent up to its face or the body; the body of fillet, chamfer, the face features (shell, draft, offset_face, delete_face, replace_face, split_face), split_body and thread; a face of it as a hole’s face, a loft section, a sweep’s guide surface, a draft’s fixed plane, a replace target or a splitting tool; a pattern of its faces; and a mirror or pattern of bodies with combine.
  • Left out where an operation takes all bodies (Join, Cut or Intersect without participants, a cut’s cut_scope targets, Extrude’s automatic operation): mesh bodies are not cut or joined, the others are.
  • Taken as they are: moves, copies, patterns and mirrors of bodies without combine, scales, remove_body, components, appearances, measurements, physical properties, interference (which skips them), Section Analysis (which cuts their triangles, mitcad#392) and export.

The geometry facade refuses faces without surfaces too (detail::require_surfaces: booleans, unions, fillets, chamfers, face operations, splits, removed material and joins of near copies, for every other caller such as the importers): join: a mesh body (faces without surfaces) cannot be used; the operation works on solid and surface bodies. A tool’s contacts take a mesh body as apart, a mesh face’s face_geometry is mesh (not planar), and a sketch’s section of a mesh face is an error (mesh_section cuts a mesh body into sketches instead: Mesh tools for reverse engineering).

Body ids of a split’s pieces

A feature that leaves a body in several pieces (a Cut or Intersect of extrude, revolve and the other profile features, of box and the other primitives and of the copies of patterns and mirrors; a combine cut; split_body; a cut’s cut_scope) gives the body’s id to one piece and new ids of the feature (F4.b0, F4.b1, …) to the others. The first time, the pieces come in geometric order (along a planar splitting tool’s normal for split_body) and the first keeps the body. The feature then remembers each piece’s volume and centre of mass, and later evaluations give the ids by matching the new pieces with the remembered ones (mitcad#408, core/model/src/features/pieces.rs), so an upstream edit that changes the order or the number of the pieces does not hand a later feature’s body (a remove_body’s, a fillet’s, a combine’s) to another piece:

  • A piece matches a remembered one when its volume is within a factor of two of it and its centre moved less than a quarter of the size of the pieces (the diagonal of their bounding box). The closest pairs are taken first (volume change and shift, each 1 at the limit, added); ties go to the remembered piece listed first, then to the piece first in geometric order.
  • The body that was split keeps its id for the piece that matches it. Without one it takes the piece left that comes closest to it, and every later feature that names the body warns (timeline status warning): body F2.b0 is now another piece of what Extrude2 split it into (volume 40000 → 8000 mm³, centre moved 0 mm). The warning lasts while that result stands (until the split is evaluated again). When every piece matches another remembered piece, the body is gone.
  • A remembered piece that no piece matches is no longer made: its id goes to no other piece, and new pieces get new ids. remove_body passes such a body by with a warning (body F4.b1 is a piece Extrude2 no longer makes (its pieces changed): nothing to remove); any other feature that names it fails with the same words. A piece like it that comes back gets the id again.
  • A body left whole that never was in pieces is not remembered: when a later edit splits it, its pieces come in geometric order as the first time. Pieces the geometry kernel cannot measure (no volume) also come in geometric order.

What a feature remembers is saved with it in the design file, so a design opens with the ids it was saved with:

{"uid": "F4", "name": "Extrude2", "type": "extrude", …,
 "split_pieces": [{"body": "F2.b0", "size": 70.71,
   "pieces": [{"body": "F2.b0", "volume": 40000, "centre": [25, 20, 10]},
              {"body": "F4.b0", "volume": 20, "centre": [54.5, 0.5, 10], "gone": true}]}]}

body is the body split (pass numbers the splits of one body when the feature splits it more than once, as a pattern’s copies do), size the diagonal of the pieces’ bounding box (mm), each piece’s volume (mm³) and centre (mm, in its component’s coordinates), and gone for a piece the last evaluation did not make. A file without split_pieces (saved before mitcad#408) opens in geometric order and takes it on its first recompute. The document takes what each evaluation remembers without an undo step; it is an input of the feature’s evaluation like a parameter, and a result fits both what it was evaluated with and what it leaves, so the recompute cache and the result store reuse results as before. Sheet-metal cuts (sheet_cut) keep the geometric order. Tests: core.model (piece_ids_tests.rs, features::pieces).

A remove_body of every piece below a volume ({"smaller_than": …}) is not offered: a definition’s values are lengths, angles or unitless numbers, and a size filter over a component’s bodies would take small bodies that are no fragments as well; with the ids kept, the named pieces stay right.

The extended tool of a split or trim (mitcad#712)

A preview of split_body, split_face or trim_surface with extend (the default) and a plane or face tool shows the tool as the feature extends it: the preview reports "tool": true and preview_tool_shape() returns it (with tool_instances), so that a display can show where the cut runs. It is the faces the operation itself cuts with (a plane as a face across the box, a face grown along its surface: the same construction, Kernel::extended_tool, the OCCT kernel’s geometry::extended_tool), clipped to the box of the bodies split (of every body of a split_body together) grown on every side by 5 % of its diagonal, at least 1 mm. A split_body with further tools (more_tools) shows every plane or face tool, in one compound. Without extend, with a body or sketch curves as the tool, or where the kernel cannot make it (a tool that does not reach the box), there is none; the split itself is not affected.

Only a preview makes it (Evaluate::preview_tool, for the feature Cache::preview names while Document::preview_state computes): it is made again for every preview of the feature, also when the split’s result comes from the cache, and is kept in the preview’s result (Recomputed::preview_tool), never in the feature’s output, the cache or the result store. Recomputes, commits (which reuse the preview’s result) and imports do not make it. Tests: core.model (f2_tests.rs, surface_modelling_tests.rs), geometry (test_split.cpp).

Commands

command takes one command object ({"cmd": "<name>", …}) or an array of them. An array runs in order, each command its own undo step, and stops at the first failure (commands[2]: …); the result is the array of results.

Every result has "recomputed": the number of features the command evaluated (results from the cache, including a preview’s, are not counted), and "error": the first failed feature ("Fillet1: …") or null. A command that took results from the result store has "restored", their number. A failed feature does not reject the command: it is skipped, and the timeline query shows its error. When any feature fails, the result also has "failed_features": each one and whether this command added or edited it (Failed features in command results).

A command that brings a warning to a feature that was there before it says so in its result (mitcad#1729): "warnings" lists each warning such a feature has now and did not have before the command, as "<feature's name>: <warning>" in timeline order, the text the feature query gives (with the names, for agents), and "warning_messages" says the same in plain words. So set_parameter, suppress_feature, set_marker, undo and the others tell, for example, that a driven dimension split an extruded profile and the extrude kept its region as the pieces ("Extrude1: region r{…} found as r{…} + r{…} after a change in Sketch1"), without a look at the timeline; a warning that stays as it was is not repeated, and one that goes brings nothing. In add_feature and edit_feature they come after the feature’s own warnings (which are without its name; no "warning_messages" there); in a sketch command after its own, in both lists. A feature the command added is left out (add_feature gives its own, an import reports its items). A command whose "warnings" say something else (an export’s, a count) keeps them as they are. In every case each is also a warning among the result’s "notices", with the feature’s uid as its target and its places. Tests: core.model.sketch-refs (profile_selection_tests.rs), cli.mcp (mcp-test.py, with "timeline": "none").

Timeline and parameters

CommandFieldsResult
add_featuredef, name (optional), component (optional: a component’s uid or name; the active component when left out), after or index (optional: where in the timeline, see Adding a feature in the middle of the timeline); fit_faces and shared (a thread, at the marker: its faces fitted to it in the same undo step, Fitting the face to the thread)uid, name, parameters (created); with fit_faces fitted and fit_left; for a new-component operation placed beside a component that takes no components placed_in, instead_of, placement_warning (Design policy)
edit_featureuid, def (same type)parameters (created); user_parameters and notes when a value that uses its slot’s own parameter kept that parameter as a user parameter (Values, mitcad#1536); when the edit makes a new component placed beside a component that takes no components placed_in, instead_of, placement_warning (Design policy)
delete_featureuid, dependents (default false)deleted: uids in timeline order; notices for the cut-scope exclusions it dropped (Assembly scope for Extrude Cut). What a joint that goes as a dependent placed stays where it is (mitcad#1820)

reorder_featureuid, index (new timeline index)

rename_bodyuid (body), name
set_markerposition: the number of features before the marker; temporary (default false)

set_parametername, and any of: value (number in mm or rad, written in the parameter’s unit, or an expression) or expression, unit, comment, favorite, min, max, step, strict (Parameter limits), group (a user parameter’s; "" takes it out of its group, Parameter groups)changed: parameters whose values changed, the text parameters whose texts changed among them, whether value or expression was given
rename_parametername, new_name
remove_parameter_namename: a dimension’s or a feature’s parameter (or a driven dimension’s reference)name: its automatic name now (the next free d<n>), rewritten: the parameters whose expressions were rewritten (Values, mitcad#1577)
delete_parametername (only when no feature and no other parameter uses it)
add_parameter_groupgroup: a path nested with / (Cabinet/Doors); the parent groups it lacks are made too (Parameter groups)group: its path
rename_parameter_groupgroup, new_group (the whole new path)group: the new path
delete_parameter_groupgroup: its parameters move to its parent group, its subgroups up a levelmoved: the parameters that were in it
set_parameter_groupnames (user parameters), group ("": out of their groups)group
set_unitslength: the document’s length unit (mm, cm, m, in, ft, …)changed
group_featuresfeatures (uids of a run of features next to each other in the timeline, in any order, none in a group yet), name (default the next free Group<n>)name
ungroupnamethe features stay
rename_groupname, new_name
recomputeall (default false): every feature evaluated again from the start, without cached or stored results (Recompute All)notices: one information for each drawing of a design file written before mitcad#1293 whose views were pinned to the bodies shown (Drawings in the design), when there are any; with all, changed
sketch.*see Sketch commands
  • New features go in at the timeline marker, which moves after them (with after or index, at that place before the marker).
  • add_parameter and set_parameter reject commands containing both value and expression. set_parameter also accepts only unit, comment, favorite or group; a unit-only edit keeps the existing expression.
  • Parameters copied from another document retain that document’s default units for implicit units inside expressions. The parameters query and saved parameter record expose them as expression_units (length, angle). Editing the expression or applying a configuration keeps these defaults; the parameter’s own unit still takes precedence for its dimensions. Changing the destination document’s units does not reinterpret these copied expressions. Their parameter references remain editable.
  • delete_feature refuses while other features refer to the feature (Extrude1 is used by Fillet1; …); with "dependents": true they go too (the dependents query lists them). A cut whose cut_scope only excludes the feature’s component or body does not refer to it (mitcad#1236): the delete goes ahead, the cut stays, and an exclusion of a body the feature made is dropped with an info notice. A joint that goes as a dependent (one on a face, an edge, a frame or a joint origin of what goes) leaves what it placed where it is (mitcad#1820), as build_remove and delete_occurrence do (mitcad#1811): its sides keep their pose, a move of them on the timeline taken into account (Document::held_placements); only the joints to what goes are removed, and undo brings back the features, the joints and the occurrences’ own placements. A free part of a flexible occurrence such a joint placed stays as that occurrence’s own placement of it (mitcad#2017, Flexible subassemblies). A joint deleted by itself (its own uid) still lets what it placed go back where it was placed.
  • reorder_feature refuses a position where a feature would come before something it refers to (the can_reorder query asks first).
  • Features after the marker are rolled back (not evaluated); suppressed features are skipped.
  • set_marker with "temporary": true evaluates a command editor’s rollback without adding an undo step, dropping redo or changing the revision. The editor must restore the original marker with the same flag before committing an edit or saving. Cancellation leaves the marker, history, revision and displayed results unchanged. Ordinary marker moves keep their existing undo behavior.
  • After a command, new bodies get display names (Body1, Body2, … the next free number), which are saved.
  • A timeline group stays a run: deleted features leave it, a feature added or moved between its members joins it, a member moved away leaves it (the only member takes the group along), an empty group goes. Saved as "groups": [{"name", "features"}]; a favourite parameter as "favorite": true.

Recompute All (mitcad#1982)

{"cmd": "recompute", "all": true} evaluates every feature again from the start of the timeline, with none of the results the memory cache or the result store holds (Document::try_recompute_all); its result’s recomputed counts every feature it evaluated. The results of the run become the cache; a cancelled run leaves the document, its results and its cache as they were. What the run measures anew (a driven dimension’s value, a Flex item’s nodes) is one undo step, Recompute All, when it differs from the state, and changed is true; otherwise there is no step and changed is false. A failed feature is reported as in every command (error, error_notice, failed_features). The application’s Manage › Design › Recompute All runs it. Test: core.model.api (recompute_all_tests.rs).

Feature names are not unique (mitcad#1107)

Features may share a name: a sketch and the extrude made from it can both be named Holder (add_feature, sketch.create and rename_feature take a name in use; an empty name is refused). Default names (Extrude3) still skip the names in use. The model’s own references, the timeline and the application go by uid; other names stay unique as before (bodies, components, parameters, annotations, drawings).

A field that takes a feature by uid or name (a script’s feature and sketch expectations, export_sketch’s sketch, the joint of drive_joint (also previewed), add_motion_link, add_motion_study, edit_motion_study, set_study_key and remove_study_key, the profiles query’s sketch) reads it so:

  • the uid of an existing feature is that feature;
  • a name one feature has is that feature (a field of one kind then says when it is not of that kind: Holder is not a joint);
  • a name several features have is refused with their uids and kinds, Holder names several features: F1 (sketch), F2 (extrude); give the uid, unless the field takes only one kind and exactly one of them is of that kind: a sketch field and one sketch named Holder find that sketch.

An import that names a feature after the item of the file keeps that name, also one another feature has (before, it took the default name). A design file saves and opens features of one name; only a version 1 file, whose features refer to each other by name, still needs each name once.

Undo, revisions and the saved state

CommandFieldsResult
undo, redolabel of the step, or null
begin_commandtoken: an opaque string identifying a checkpoint of the current definition, revision, saved state and both history stacks
restore_commandtokenrestores that checkpoint after its scene recomputes successfully; keeps the token for retries
discard_commandtokenreleases the checkpoint without changing the current definition or history
merge_undodepth: the undo depth before the action, labelmerges the undo steps after depth into one step named label (clears redo), and the sketch work steps they recorded into one per sketch (The work steps of a sketch); undo_depth. Refuses a depth past the last step
mark_savedrevision; the definition state is the design file’s (saved or opened). No undo step, nothing recomputed
  • Undo and redo restore the whole definition (parameters, timeline, marker, body names). Cached results make them fast.
  • An asynchronous frontend begins one command checkpoint before temporary marker moves or applied sketch previews. Cancel restores and then discards it; accept discards it. Restore recovers the exact preexisting redo stack, even when a command completed before cancellation reached the worker. A failed or cancelled restore changes nothing and retains the token for retry. Only one checkpoint may be active per document; stale tokens are rejected. Tokens and newly allocated revision numbers are never reused. Checkpoints are session state, absent from saved designs; finish the command before marking a saved file or replacing the document.
  • One user action is often several commands (a rectangle snapped to the origin is sketch.add_point, sketch.rectangle and a coincident constraint; a drag a sketch.drag per mouse move). The caller reads undo_depth (document query) before the action, runs its commands and merges them, or undoes back to that depth to take the action back.
  • Every accepted command gives the state a new revision, also one that recomputes nothing (a rename, a named view); a rejected command, a command that changes nothing, a recompute and a preview keep it. Undo and redo take back the revision of the state they restore, so undoing to the saved state is unmodified again; merge_undo keeps the current revision. A new command after undo gets a new revision even when it makes the same definition. update_links gives a new revision when it takes new bodies (no undo step).
  • A new document is not modified. A design file read (Document::from_json, the bridge’s load_document) is modified until mark_saved, since it need not be the file it will be saved to (an imported design, recovered work). Saving (to_json) does not mark it saved by itself.
  • Document::to_json_with_marker(marker) (bridge to_json_with_marker) writes the design file with another marker without changing the document (autosave while an edit has rolled the timeline back).

Visibility and display

CommandFieldsResult
set_feature_visibleuid (a sketch or a construction plane, axis or point), visibleundo step Show Sketch1 / Hide Plane1 unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed
set_body_visibleuid, visible, or expression (a condition; Bindings)
set_body_materialuid, material (a built-in id below or one of the design’s materials, or null: its component’s default, steel when none is set), appearance (replace: the material’s appearance becomes the body’s; keep: the body keeps its own; left out: replace unless the body’s appearance was set by hand, see Materials), or expression (a text naming the material; Bindings)undo step Set Material of Body1 (material and appearance together); nothing recomputed
set_body_appearanceuid, appearance (an id of the library or the document, see Appearances, or null for the default look), or expression (a text naming the appearance; Bindings)
set_origin_visiblevisible, opening (default false: an undo step; true: as a new design opens, mitcad#1683, with no undo step and no new revision, so the document stays as modified as it was; the application shows the origin of every new design it opens so)the root’s Origin folder shown; undo step Show Origin / Hide Origin unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed
set_isolationitems: {"body": "F3.b0", "occurrence": "O1"} (a body, in the occurrence that places it, none for the root’s) or {"occurrence": "O1/O4"} (an occurrence by its path); none: unisolateundo step Isolate 2 item(s) / Unisolate; an occurrence that is not there is refused
  • Body commands are undo steps (Hide Body1, Show Body1, Set Material of Body1, …) unless nothing changes; the body must exist at the marker. The bodies query and the design file list "visible": false, "material" and "appearance" when set, and "appearance_set_by_hand": true for an appearance that is not its material’s. Built-in materials: steel (7.85 g/cm³, the default), stainless_steel, cast_iron, aluminum, copper, brass, titanium, abs, pla, nylon, polycarbonate, glass, water, resin_standard (core/model-base/src/analysis.rs, core/model/src/material.rs), and the woods and panels wood_pine, wood_oak, wood_birch, plywood_birch, mdf_raw (mitcad#1706, their values from the bundled dataset); a design’s own materials and components' default materials are in Materials.
  • Sketches and construction features: by default a sketch is hidden while a feature uses it (a profile, curves or points; suppressed features and those after the marker count too) and shown while none does; construction geometry is shown. A sketch or a 3D sketch that projects or intersects another sketch’s curves or points (sketch.project, also with section, and a 3D sketch’s linked projections) does not use that sketch: the source stays shown while more of its curves are picked (mitcad#2045). A light bulb set with set_feature_visible wins; it is kept and saved with the feature ("visible": true or false) only where it differs from the default, so showing a hidden sketch that no feature uses forgets it.
  • The command that gives a sketch its first consumer or takes its last one away forgets the sketch’s light bulb in its own undo step: the new extrusion’s sketch hides, and shows again when that extrusion is deleted, even if it was hidden by hand meanwhile. A second consumer keeps a light bulb set by hand. Deleting a feature forgets its visibility; paste_new and copied designs start with the defaults. Code: document/browser.rs.
  • The display state (Origin folder, isolation) is per user: the design file keeps it as "display": {"origin": true, "isolated": [...]} (left out when nothing is set), and a project keeps it outside the design file (Design files). Isolation lists only the items there at the marker; none left isolates nothing.
  • Occurrences have set_occurrence_visible (Components and occurrences).

Transparent bodies and occurrences (mitcad#1093)

CommandFieldsResult
set_body_transparentuid, transparentundo step Make Body1 Transparent / Make Body1 Opaque unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed; the body must exist at the marker
set_occurrence_transparentoccurrence (uid, name or path, as for set_occurrence_visible), transparentundo step Make Bracket:1 Transparent / Make Bracket:1 Opaque unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed
  • Transparency is kept like visibility: per body (in every occurrence that places it) and per occurrence, in the definition state, so it is saved with the design and undo restores it. It is independent of the light bulb: a hidden transparent body or occurrence is transparent again when it is shown. It changes no appearance or material.
  • An occurrence’s transparency applies to its contents, the bodies of its component and of the occurrences inside it.
  • The bodies query lists "transparent": true for a body set so, the components query’s occurrences "transparent": true for an occurrence set so, and the instances query "transparent": true for a placed body that is transparent itself or lies in a transparent occurrence (left out otherwise). The design file keeps "transparent": true on the body and on the occurrence (left out when false). A copy of an occurrence (Paste) starts opaque, as it starts shown; Paste New copies the transparency of the occurrences inside it. The design comparison lists a change as transparent or opaque.
  • The application draws a transparent body as a faint shaded surface with its edges in its own appearance’s colour, and a click goes through it to what lies behind (app/COMMANDS.md, “Transparent bodies and components”).

Display size of construction planes and axes (mitcad#1748)

CommandFieldsResult
set_datum_display_sizeuid (a construction plane or axis), size (mm, greater than 0 and at most 1 000 000; null or left out: drawn fitted to what it is made from, or at the default size)undo step Resize Plane1 / Resize Axis1 unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed

  • How large the application draws a construction plane (its square’s side) or axis (its line’s length): its resize handles in the 3D view send this command (app/COMMANDS.md, “Origin planes and the size of construction geometry”). Display only: the datum’s plane or line, what sketches and features use, does not change. Other features, construction points among them, are refused (Point1 has no display size: …).

  • The datums and datum queries list "display_size" for a datum that has one (left out otherwise); the design file keeps it on the feature ("display_size": 40, left out when not set), a design comparison lists it as a display_size change. Deleting the feature forgets it; a file with a size on another feature reads without it, a size that is not a positive number is refused. Code: document/browser.rs. Tests: core/model-tests/api/src/datum_display_size_tests.rs.

  • Where it is drawn (mitcad#1827, GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#321): without a display_size a construction plane or axis is drawn at the size and shape of what it is made from, worked out with the feature (features/construction/drawn.rs), so it follows the model. The datums and datum queries (and a construction feature’s preview, under datum) give it as drawn:

    FieldMeaning
    sourcefitted (what it is made from), display_size (its resize handles’ size) or default (nothing to measure)
    recta plane’s: center, x_axis, y_axis (unit, in the plane), width, height (mm, the margin included)
    segment, lengthan axis’s: start, end (along its direction), and the distance between them
    sizewith display_size and default: the square’s side or the line’s length
    • A plane made on or from a face (offset, offset_through_point, angle, tangent, tangent_at_point, midplane): a rectangle over the faces’ outlines seen along its normal (Kernel::face_boundary, else Kernel::face_outline), along their longest straight edge, else along the plane’s x_axis; made from another construction plane, over that plane’s extent (without its margin).
    • A plane through edges or points (and one on a face without an outline, and perpendicular_at_point, edge-on to its face): a square over where it cuts the boxes of the bodies its references are on, else over the referenced geometry.
    • An axis: along its edge’s, faces’, planes’ or points’ extent, else where it passes through their bodies’ boxes.
    • The margin all round: 5 % of the larger side, at least 3 mm. Nothing to measure (a fixed or flange_wall plane, an offset of an origin plane, a fixed axis): default, 100 mm about the datum’s origin.
    • A display_size draws a square of that side (a line of that length) about the middle of the fitted extent (about the origin without one); null brings the fitted extent back. Origin datums, points, joint origins and coordinate systems have no drawn.
    • Tests: core/model-tests/api/src/datum_drawn_extent_tests.rs (a plane off a face and one off that plane, an axis along an edge, the default, a display size over it, the file, an edit followed), the unit tests in features/construction/drawn.rs; app.ui-*construction-size.

Acknowledged warnings (mitcad#1935)

CommandFieldsResult
acknowledge_warningsuids (features that built with warnings), acknowledged (default true; false shows them again)undo step Acknowledge Fillet1 / Acknowledge 3 Warnings (Unacknowledge … when shown again) unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed
  • A feature’s warning the user has seen (GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#380): the design keeps the warning’s text as it was acknowledged (its warnings joined with ; ). While the feature builds with that very text, the timeline query gives it "acknowledged": true (left out otherwise); its status, level and notices stay those of a warning, so agents still read it. The application does not paint it yellow nor count it in the warnings badge (app/COMMANDS.md, “Acknowledged warnings”).
  • It lapses by itself: when the feature fails, or builds with another warning text or none, it is no longer acknowledged, and the edit that recomputed forgets it in its own undo step, so the same warning coming back later shows again. Suppressed and rolled back features keep theirs.
  • Refused: a feature that failed (Fillet1 failed: an error cannot be acknowledged), one without a warning (Fillet1 has no warning to acknowledge), an unknown uid. One already acknowledged, or shown again without an acknowledgement, is left as it is.
  • The design file keeps it on the feature ("acknowledged_warning": "<text>", left out when none); deleting the feature forgets it. Code: document/acknowledged_warnings.rs. Tests: core/model-tests/api/src/acknowledged_warnings_tests.rs.

Named views

CommandFieldsResult
add_named_viewname (the next free NamedView<n> when left out), eye, target (points, mm), up, perspective (default false), height (mm of the model the view shows at the target), replace (default false: a name in use is refused)name; undo step Add Named View Detail (Change Named View Detail when replaced) unless nothing changes
rename_named_viewname, new_name
delete_named_viewname

Named views change no geometry and recompute nothing; they are saved in the design file ("views", left out when there are none). The view named Home is the document’s home view.

Analyses

Section analyses (mitcad#41), print analyses (mitcad#620) and draft analyses (mitcad#2166) kept in the document (core/model/src/document/analyses.rs): the browser’s Analysis folder.

CommandFieldsResult
add_analysisdef, name (the next free Section<n>, Print<n> for a print analysis or Draft<n> for a draft analysis, when left out)name; undo step Add Section1. It is shown and the others are hidden
edit_analysisname, def, visible (optional: true shows it and hides the others, false hides it; as it was when left out)undo step Edit Section1 unless nothing changes
set_analysis_visiblename, visibleundo step Show Section1 / Hide Section1 unless nothing changes; showing hides the others
rename_analysisname, new_nameundo step Rename Section1
delete_analysisnameundo step Delete Section1

A def is {"type": "section", "plane": <plane reference>, "offset": mm, "flip": bool} (offset default 0, flip default false): the bodies cut at plane moved by offset along its normal, the side the normal points to cut away; flip reverses the normal. The plane is a plane reference (origin plane, construction plane, planar face, fixed plane); add_analysis and edit_analysis refuse one that is no plane at the marker, and other fields than these.

An optional occurrence is the selected plane’s UID path from the design root, for example "O1/O3" (empty for the root). Component-owned faces and construction planes are transformed through that path into design coordinates before applying the offset. Flip reverses only the normal, after offsetting, and leaves the physical plane in place. Without a path, older analyses infer a component’s unique placement; repeated components require an explicit path. A path that does not own the referenced face or datum is refused. Fixed planes and origin planes without a path remain in design coordinates.

{"query":"section_plane","plane":<reference>,"occurrence":"O1/O3", "offset":-5,"flip":false} resolves the same definition without adding an analysis. It returns design-space origin, normal, and the resolved occurrence; the optional fields have the same defaults as an analysis.

A section can be turned by an angle about an axis (mitcad#823): angle (radians, default 0, not written when 0), axis (a line reference: a straight edge, a sketch line, a construction axis or an origin axis) and axis_occurrence (the axis’ UID path from the design root, as occurrence is the plane’s; inferred and checked the same way). The picked plane is first turned rigidly by angle about the axis, right-handed about the axis’ direction, in design coordinates after both occurrence paths; then it is moved by offset along the turned normal; flip then reverses only the normal. An axis with angle 0 leaves the plane as it is. add_analysis and edit_analysis refuse a non-zero angle without an axis, and an axis along the plane’s normal; an analysis whose axis cannot be found at the marker gets the analyses query’s error and cuts nothing, as a plane that cannot be found. The section_plane query takes the same three fields and then also returns axis ({"origin", "direction"} in design coordinates) and the resolved axis_occurrence. Analyses without an angle are written as before; a MitCad older than mitcad#823 refuses a design with these fields. Drawing section views cut by a Section Analysis follow its angle.

The analyses query lists them in the order added: name, type, visible, the def’s fields, and section: {origin, normal} (the plane in design coordinates at the marker, offset and flip applied; the origin is the plane’s origin, see References to geometry), or error when the plane cannot be found there (a face of a body that is gone or rolled back). A face reference follows the model by its topological name, as features’ do.

A def of "type": "print" is a print analysis: its bodies, bed face and settings, and in the analyses query down (the print direction at the marker) or error (a body or the bed face is gone).

A def of "type": "draft" is a draft analysis (mitcad#2166, default names Draft1, Draft2, …): its bodies, pull direction, flip and angle, and in the analyses query pull_direction (the unit pull at the marker) or error (a body or the pull reference is gone).

  • At most one analysis is shown at a time: one section cuts the bodies. Showing one hides the others, also in a file read with several shown (the first shown stays).
  • Analyses change no geometry and recompute nothing. They are saved in the design file ("analyses": [{"name", "visible" (only when false), "type", "plane", "occurrence" (when supplied), "offset", "flip"}], left out when there are none; files without it have none), and the comparison of versions lists them by name.

A section through a pick (mitcad#1769)

plane also takes one face or edge that places a plane, stored as the reference (with its occurrence) so that the section follows the model:

  • a cylindrical face (also a conical or toroidal one: a hole, a boss, a countersink, a fillet): the plane contains the face’s axis;
  • a circular edge or arc: the plane contains the circle’s axis (through its center, along its normal);
  • a straight edge: the plane passes through the edge’s midpoint, normal to the edge (its normal runs from the edge’s start to its end).

For the first two the axis points along its largest component (as an axis reference) and the plane’s turn about it starts at the first of the origin planes XY, XZ and YZ (of the reference’s component) whose normal is at least 45 degrees from the axis: that normal, made square to the axis, is the plane’s. For an axis along a model axis this is the first origin plane that contains it (XZ for a hole along Z, XY for one along X or Y); it never depends on the view. angle then turns the plane about that axis without an axis field (an axis, when given, is used instead); offset and flip work as for any plane. A straight edge’s plane needs an axis for an angle, as a plane does. The section_plane query returns the picked axis as axis (without axis_occurrence), so that a panel can draw the Angle’s ring about it. A face that is neither planar nor round about an axis, or an edge that is neither straight nor circular, is refused; an analysis whose face or edge is gone at the marker gets the analyses query’s error, as a plane that cannot be found. A MitCad older than mitcad#1769 reads such an analysis but cannot find its plane, and refuses a design with one turned without an axis.

Appearances

How bodies look (mitcad#46, core/model-base/src/appearance.rs, core/model/src/document/appearances.rs): a physically based parameter set, a subset of OpenPBR’s and the Principled BSDF’s. MitCad’s library is built in and read-only; a document keeps appearances of its own, saved in the design file. A body names its appearance by id (set_body_appearance), and single faces can have their own (Appearances of faces, mitcad#53).

ParameterRangeDefault
base_colorsRGB [r, g, b], 0–1[0.8, 0.8, 0.8]a dielectric’s diffuse colour, a metal’s reflection, the tint of transmitted light
metalness0–101 for metals
roughness0–10.50 a mirror finish
specular0–11the weight of a dielectric’s specular reflection
transmission0–10light going through (glass, clear plastic)
ior1–51.5index of refraction
coat, coat_roughness0–10, 0.03a clear coat over the base (lacquer, car paint)
emission, emission_color0–1000, sRGB0, [1, 1, 1]emitted light: 1 is the colour’s own radiance
opacity0–11a cut-out (glass transmits instead)
texture{"path", "size": [w, h] mm (default 100 x 100), "rotation" rad, "projection": "box" (default), "planar", "uv" or "grain", "data", "normal", "roughness", "metalness", "occlusion", "source"}nonean image for the base colour (PNG or JPEG), with the other maps of its set and where it came from (Texture map sets), projected in the body’s coordinates: planar along Z, box from the axis each point of the surface faces most; one repeat of the image is size, turned by rotation about the projection’s axis. uv (mitcad#1862) lays it by the body’s own texture coordinates (a mesh body imported with them, as a glTF file’s), once over 0 to 1 of each, without size and rotation; a body without them is projected as by box. Versions before it refuse uv. grain (mitcad#2186) lays it along each face’s grain: each face from a plane of its own, the image’s width along the face’s longest side (Built-in wood and panel textures); versions before it refuse grain. path is relative to the design file’s folder or absolute; data (base64 of the image file, at most 32 MB) embeds the image in the design file (Textures). The rendered view draws it with all its maps, the shaded view its base colour image (mitcad#2186; by uv the base colour)
classmetal, plastic (General Plastic), fdm_plastic, resin, othernone: otherwhat it is a look of (mitcad#1102): a material’s Add… and the Appearance tool offer the appearances of the material’s class first. Set by the user (null or other takes it away), or on a filament’s colour (fdm_plastic: a material’s own colour, a printer profile’s or a 3MF import’s filament); the library’s come from their ids and are never written
CommandFieldsResult
create_appearanceid (letters, digits, _, -; the next free custom<n> when left out), name (Appearance<n> when left out), based_on (a library or document appearance whose parameters it starts from; the defaults above without it), any parametersid; undo step Create Appearance Red
edit_appearanceid, name and any parameters ("texture": null removes the texture)undo step Edit Appearance Red unless nothing changes; the library’s are refused (copy one with based_on)
delete_appearanceidbodies: those that used it, which get the default look, and faces ({"body", "face"}) that used it, which get their body’s, in the same undo step Delete Appearance Red
  • Ids are unique among the library’s and the document’s appearances, and names too; parameters out of range and unknown fields are refused.
  • The appearances query lists the library’s appearances in the application’s order, then the document’s: id, name, the parameters, library (true for the built-in ones), display_color (sRGB: the colour of the shaded view and exports; the base colour), class (its own, a library appearance’s by its id, else other; mitcad#1102), bodies (the uids of bodies that use it, also those not at the marker) and faces ({"body", "face"} of faces that use it).
  • Library: steel_satin, aluminum_anodized, brass_polished, copper, cast_iron, paint_red, paint_blue, paint_green, paint_yellow, paint_black, paint_white, plastic_black, plastic_orange, rubber, glass, wood_oak (their colours as before mitcad#46), chrome, gold_polished, steel_polished, plastic_red, plastic_white, plastic_blue, plastic_clear, glass_clear, glass_frosted, wood_walnut, wood_maple, emissive_white, resin_grey, resin_white, resin_clear (mitcad#1102), and the basic colours of generic filaments (mitcad#1133, named Filament - <Colour>, the look of a printed thermoplastic: dielectric, roughness 0.55, specular 0.5, no coat): filament_white, filament_black, filament_grey, filament_silver, filament_red, filament_orange, filament_yellow, filament_green, filament_blue, filament_light_blue, filament_purple, filament_pink, filament_brown, filament_beige (natural) and filament_translucent (natural, transmission 0.7); their ids are stable; and the looks of the material dataset’s woods and panels (mitcad#1552; with built-in texture sets since mitcad#2186, Built-in wood and panel textures: dielectric, specular 0.5, no coat): wood_birch, wood_cedar, wood_cherry, wood_douglas_fir, wood_eucalyptus, wood_pine, wood_teak, panel_chipboard (Chipboard), panel_mdf (MDF), panel_osb (OSB), plywood_birch, plywood_eucalyptus, plywood_pine, plywood_spruce; their ids are stable too. Their classes (mitcad#1102): the steels, aluminum_anodized, brass_polished, copper, cast_iron, chrome and gold_polished metal; the plastic_* ones plastic (General Plastic); the filament_* ones fdm_plastic (FDM Plastic); the resin_* ones resin; the wood_*, plywood_* and panel_* ones wood (mitcad#1552, wood_oak, wood_walnut and wood_maple too, other before); the paints, rubber, the glasses and emissive_white other. An appearance of the design or a library without a class is other, as are those of the .f3d, .FCStd and .ipt imports.
  • A body without an appearance, or with an id in neither list (an imported one), has the default look. A material carries an appearance (mitcad#640): setting a body’s material sets the body’s appearance to the material’s, unless the body’s appearance was set by hand (one that is not its current material’s) or set_body_material says keep; see Materials.
  • The commands change no geometry and recompute nothing. The design file keeps the document’s appearances as "appearances": [{"id", "name", parameters...}] (left out when there are none; parameters left out of a file are the defaults; files without it have none), and the comparison of versions lists them by id.
  • A library id taken since (mitcad#1133): a design file whose own appearance has another library id is refused (no design can save one), but one with an id the library took only later (one of the filament_* colours, or of the woods’ and panels’ looks of mitcad#1552) opens; that appearance keeps its values under a free id, the first of <id>_2, <id>_3, … (and a free name, <name> (2), when the library’s has its name), and every reference follows: the bodies’ and faces’ appearances, the materials’ default and list, the components’ appearances and the bindings’ quoted texts ('filament_red'). The document’s load warnings say so once per appearance (appearance filament_red of this design is now filament_red_2: …); a parameter’s text that spells the old id names the library’s from then on.
  • A component’s unknown appearance (mitcad#1150): a component’s appearance in component_materials that neither the design nor the library has is dropped when the file opens, with a load warning (component_materials[0]: there is no appearance …; the component shows its material's); the component keeps its material.
  • Older versions (before mitcad#1102) open a design or a library file unless it holds an appearance with a class (an unknown field, as embedded images); one is written only when set.

Appearances of faces

Faces of a body can have appearances of their own, which override the body’s (mitcad#53, core/model/src/document/bodies.rs): a label area, a painted face, a rubber pad.

CommandFieldsResult
set_face_appearanceuid (body), faces (topological names of faces of the body at the marker, F2:side(c1[c4,c2])), appearance (an id, or null: the faces show the body’s again), or expression (Bindings)undo step Set Appearance of Face of Body1 / Set Appearance of 2 Faces of Body1 / Clear Appearance of Face of Body1 unless nothing changes; faces that are not there and names that are no face names are refused
clear_face_appearancesuidundo step Clear Face Appearances of Body1 unless the body has none
  • A face appearance names its face as assigned (the canonical text of the name) and follows it as features’ face references do: a later feature that changes the face keeps the name, all pieces of a split face (#k) keep it. When a change renames the face (a sketch edit after which a side face’s segment ends on another curve: F2:side(c1[c4,c2]) becomes F2:side(c1[c4,c5])), the name finds the face of the same feature and role whose key has the most curves in common with it (for a side face: the same curve), as a profile’s region key does; the name kept is still the one assigned. A face that is gone finds nothing and its appearance is kept for when it comes back (undo).
  • The bodies query lists them per body as face_appearances: [{"face" (as assigned), "appearance", "faces" (a name of each face it finds at the marker; empty when the face is gone)}], left out when there are none.
  • They recompute nothing. The design file keeps them with the body’s other attributes: "face_appearances": {"F2:side(c1[c4,c2])": "paint_red"} (left out when there are none; files without them have none); copied designs rename the feature ids in the names. The comparison of versions lists them with the body.

Textures

An appearance’s texture is an image file or an image embedded in the design file (mitcad#53).

  • "data" in a create_appearance or edit_appearance texture embeds the image: base64 of a PNG or JPEG file (checked by its first bytes; at most 32 MB). path then names the file it came from. The appearances query lists an embedded texture with "embedded": true and "image_sha256" (the digest of the image file) instead of its data; that form sent back keeps the embedded image ("embedded": true without data keeps the image the appearance has, or that of based_on for a new one; refused when there is none), so the application changes a texture’s size or rotation without sending the image again. A texture without data and embedded reads its file again.
  • The appearance_image query (id) gives an embedded image: data (base64), format (png, jpeg) and sha256.
  • The design file keeps the image in the texture’s data; the comparison of versions shows sha256 <digest> for it. A file with shared images or embedded maps keeps each image once instead (Texture map sets).

Texture map sets

A texture can be a full set of physically based maps (mitcad#313, core/model-base/src/appearance.rs), so that a design looks the same on another computer without the image files: besides the base colour image (the texture’s own path and data), each of

MapImage
normala tangent-space normal map, OpenGL convention (green up)
roughnessroughness, grey 0 (mirror) to 1
metalnessmetalness, grey 0 (dielectric) to 1 (metal)
occlusionambient occlusion, grey 0 (occluded) to 1

is an optional object of the texture, {"path", "data"}, a PNG or JPEG file as the base colour’s: path relative to the design file’s folder or absolute, data (base64, at most 32 MB per image, each map one image) embeds it. The maps share the base colour’s size, rotation and projection; a set needs its base colour image. A map left out of an edit_appearance texture is removed (the texture is replaced as a whole). A grey map (roughness, metalness, occlusion) may take its values from one colour channel of its image, "channel": "red", "green" or "blue" (mitcad#1862), where an image packs several maps, as a glTF file’s image of roughness (green) and metalness (blue), whose occlusion is red; without it the image’s grey value counts. Versions before it refuse channel. The roughness and metalness maps may scale their values by a "factor" from 0 to 1 (mitcad#1874: glTF’s roughnessFactor and metallicFactor, which multiply its image’s channels); without it the map’s values count as they are. Another map with a factor, or a factor outside 0 to 1, is refused (texture: normal: only the roughness and metalness maps take a factor, texture: roughness: the factor must be from 0 to 1, got 1.5). Versions before it refuse factor.

{"cmd": "create_appearance", "name": "Oak veneer", "texture": {
  "path": "oak_diff_2k.jpg", "data": "/9j/4AAQ…", "size": [300, 300],
  "normal": {"path": "oak_nor_gl_2k.png", "data": "iVBORw0K…"},
  "roughness": {"path": "oak_rough_2k.png", "data": "iVBORw0K…"},
  "source": {"id": "polyhaven", "asset": "oak_veneer_01", "resolution": "2k",
             "license": "CC0-1.0", "url": "https://polyhaven.com/a/oak_veneer_01"}}}
  • Embedding: the application embeds the images of a set it takes from a texture source; a map given by path alone stays a file of the user’s, read when the view renders.
  • Source: source records where the set came from: id (the texture source: polyhaven, folder, …; letters, digits, _, -), asset (the asset’s id in it), and optionally resolution (2k), license (an SPDX identifier, CC0-1.0) and url (the asset’s web page, http or https). The model keeps and lists it; it never fetches anything.
  • Listing: the appearances query lists each embedded map image as the base colour’s, {"path", "embedded": true, "image_sha256"}, and source as given. That form sent back keeps the images. "embedded": true with image_sha256 keeps the image of that digest the design embeds, also another appearance’s (so a set is reused without sending its images again; refused when the design has none of that digest); without image_sha256 it keeps the image of the same map of the texture it replaces (or of based_on).
  • appearance_image takes map (base_color, the default, or a map above) and gives that image.
  • One copy per image: an image the design embeds already (the same SHA-256) is shared, not copied: in memory, in the states undo keeps, and in the design file. The file keeps a texture’s embedded image in its data as before while no map image is embedded and no image is embedded twice; otherwise every embedded image is kept once in the top-level "images": [{"sha256", "data"}] (in the order of first use) and the textures and maps refer to it by "image": "<sha256>". Opening checks each image (PNG or JPEG, at most 32 MB, its digest, listed once) and refuses a reference to an image that is not there. Files without images and maps open as before, and a design with one embedded texture is written as before. Older versions of MitCad do not open a file with images or maps (an unknown field).
  • The comparison of versions shows each map’s image as sha256 <digest>.

Built-in wood and panel textures

The library’s woods and panels (mitcad#2186: wood_birch, wood_cedar, wood_cherry, wood_douglas_fir, wood_eucalyptus, wood_pine, wood_teak, panel_chipboard, panel_mdf, panel_osb, plywood_birch, plywood_eucalyptus, plywood_pine, plywood_spruce) each have a texture set: a base colour, a normal and a roughness map, 1024 × 1024 JPEG images shipped with MitCad (core/model-base/src/appearance/wood_textures.rs; the images in core/model-base/textures, MitCad’s own, made by tools/wood-textures/generate.sh, MIT licence, listed in core/model-base/textures/README.md).

  • Shipped once, read at run time (mitcad#2218): the images are files in the installation, not data inside the programs, so the application and mitcad-cli share one copy: bin/textures on Windows (beside the programs), usr/share/mitcad/textures in the AppImage, Contents/Resources/textures in the macOS bundle. The model reads them when it first builds the library, from the first of these folders beside the running program that has them, else from the source tree’s core/model-base/textures (a build tree’s programs and the tests). Without the files the looks have no texture and show their colours.

  • Listed as embedded images: the appearances query lists each image as "embedded": true with its image_sha256, as a design’s embedded ones, path <id>-color.jpg, <id>-normal.jpg, <id>-roughness.jpg, and source {"id": "mitcad", "asset": "<id>", "resolution": "1k", "license": "MIT"}; appearance_image gives the bytes. The query lists no image data for any appearance (the images are megabytes, and the application asks often).

  • Real-world size, along the grain: projection grain, one repeat size 800 × 800 mm for the woods, 1000 × 1000 mm for the plywoods' faces, 400 mm for chipboard and 600 mm for MDF and OSB. The images' grain runs along their width; grain lays the width along each face’s longest side, so a panel’s grain follows its length on its faces and long edges, whatever way the body lies; a short end takes its own longest side. The rule (appearance::grain_axes): u and v are the directions of the largest and the middle second moment of the face’s area (exact per triangle, so the mesh does not change them), u’s largest component positive, v turned so that u × v points out of the face; a face about as wide as long (the middle moment more than 0.9 of the largest) takes the longest of X, Y and Z seen in its plane (X first); a point p is at (p · u, p · v) mm, then turned by rotation and divided by size as in the other projections. The application follows the same rule (app/render/GrainProjection.hpp); the USDZ export too.

  • The colour stays: the appearances keep their ids, names, colours and parameters; each base colour image’s mean in linear light is the appearance’s colour, which stays the shaded view’s colour without a texture, the colour of exports and drawings, and display_color.

  • Designs do not change: a library appearance is never saved, so a design that uses one of these ids shows the textures when it opens, its file unchanged; a design’s own appearance (a copy made before) keeps what it has. A copy made now (create_appearance with based_on) takes the set and embeds its three images in the design file, once each.

Render settings

How the rendered view (docs/rendering.md) lights and shows the design (mitcad#47, core/model-base/src/render_settings.rs), kept per document so a design keeps its look. Sections of fields with defaults: the four below and output, the final render’s (Render output, mitcad#48); later sections are added the same way, and files without a section have its defaults. The user’s lights are a list beside them (Render lights, mitcad#54).

FieldValuesDefault

environment.strength0–1001a factor on all of the environment’s light
environment.rotationrad, within two turns0turns the studio’s lights or the image about Z (counter-clockwise from above)
environment.sun_elevation0–pi/2 radpi/4outdoor: the sun’s height above the horizon
environment.sun_azimuthrad, within two turns5/4 pioutdoor: where the sun is, counter-clockwise from X seen from above (5/4 pi: front left)

background.colorsRGB [r, g, b], 0–1[1, 1, 1]

ground.reflectionsboolfalsethe ground is glossy and catches the bodies’ reflections too (with shadows)

reset_render_settingschanged; the defaults, undo step Reset Render Settings unless they are already
  • Values out of range, unknown fields and sections are refused with the section’s name (ground: unknown field `depth` ); nothing changes then.
  • The commands change no geometry and recompute nothing.
  • The render_settings query gives every section with every field (image and height only when set), and lights.
  • The design file keeps them as "render": {"environment": {...}, "background": {...}, "ground": {...}, "film": {...}} when they are not the defaults (fields left out of a file are the defaults); the comparison of versions lists each changed field as a document change (render.environment.preset studio -> outdoor).

Render lights

Lights of the user’s own (mitcad#54), besides the environment’s: the render settings’ lights, a list in the render_settings query ([] without any), saved with the other sections (files without it have no lights) and changed by commands of their own. Lengths in mm, angles in radians, Z up. Every light keeps every field; those of other kinds are ignored.

  • The comparison of versions lists a light added or removed (render.lights.light1 (none) -> Light1 (area)) and its changed fields (render.lights.light1.power 40 -> 60).

Render output

The final render to an image file (mitcad#48; File > Render Image and mitcad-cli render, docs/rendering.md “Final render”): the render settings’ fifth section, output, with the same rules as the others (set_render_settings with "output": {...}, null for a field’s default; saved when not the defaults, so files of mitcad#47 open with them; compared field by field, render.output.format png -> exr).

The cameras of the Render workspace’s Frame stage (mitcad#2013, core/model-base/src/render_settings.rs): each shot a named camera that an image is rendered through, as a named view keeps one. The render settings’ shots, a list in the render_settings query ([] without any), changed by commands of their own. Lengths in mm, Z up.
