  • A constraint implied only in part is kept. sketch.add_constraint (and sketch.add_dimension, sketch.set_driven, sketch.set_active and the holds of Move/Copy) refuse what the others imply in full: it raises the solve’s redundant count and takes no degree of freedom away (SketchEdit::require_needed with edit::Freedom; “the new constraint would over-constrain the sketch: it takes no freedom away, the others already fix all it constrains (a dimension can be added as driven)”). A constraint that contradicts the others is refused by what blocks it ("… can’t hold with the new constraint", Conflicting constraints). One that raises the count but takes at least one degree of freedom away is added: the centre of an arc tangent to two parallel offset lines slides along the corner’s bisector (its radius is free); a coincident of the centre with the corner is two equations of which one (the centre on the bisector) follows from the tangents, and it fixes the radius. Before, it was refused as if the others fixed all it constrains. Where removing older geometric constraints brings the count back, they still go in its favour first (A constraint that replaces one it makes redundant); else its redundant part is listed in redundant like any other, and undo, the constraint list and the sketch’s status show it as any constraint.
  • A constraint redundant only in part is information (mitcad#1992, GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#420). The solver reports the newest constraint of a dependent set as redundant, also when only some of its equations follow from the others: a Symmetry of a construction arc’s ends about the y axis, the arc’s centre on the origin, is two equations (the ends' middle on the axis, the ends level), and with the ends equally far from the centre one follows from the other, while the Symmetry still takes a degree of freedom away. The sketch query tries each of the sketch’s own redundant constraints and dimensions (at most eight; none of an offset or a pattern) without it, from the solved positions (SketchDef::freedom_taken): one whose leaving out raises the degrees of freedom stays in redundant, is listed in partly_redundant ({"k9": 1}: the degrees of freedom it takes away; only when there is one), is no warning, and is information about it in notices (its target the constraint’s id): “the Symmetry between two points about an axis partly repeats the others; it still removes one degree of freedom” (several: “… removes 2 degrees of freedom”; conflict::partly). One the others imply in full takes nothing away and stays a warning (“Redundant: … follows from …”). Tests: core/model-tests/sketch/src/sketch_partly_redundant_1992_tests.rs and, with MITCAD_MITCAD_REPORTED, the reporter’s design in core/model-tests/files/src/sketch_partly_redundant_reported_1992_tests.rs.
  • Redundant constraints in words. The sketch’s own redundant constraints and dimensions (of no offset or pattern), when there are at most three and no fixed entity among them, are each a warning that says what it follows from: “Redundant: the Coincident between a point and a projected point follows from the Tangent between a line and an arc and the projected geometry” (conflict::follows), with the entities it names; more are counted as before (“Redundant: 4 constraints follow from the others”).
  • Singular points (mitcad_solver’s analysis::regular_nearby): without the tangents, each arc’s radius is free (3 degrees of freedom), but where an arc touches the line it ends on (its circle meets the line in a double point) the linearized equations lose rank: the arc’s ends seemed free to slide along the lines (6 degrees of freedom), the lines' distances followed from the rest, and a drag got nowhere. Where a part of the sketch has consistent dependent equations and free unknowns, the analysis moves every unknown by up to 1e-3 of the sketch size (the same pseudo-random amounts every time), solves again from there, and takes the rank found there (with a stricter tolerance) where it is higher: a rank only drops at special points of the solution set. A drag that gets nowhere from such a point is taken again from a point beside it, and kept when it gets nearer (solve::nudge). The sketch then has 3 degrees of freedom, nothing redundant, and dragging an arc changes its radius. Where the lines are an offset’s results (the reporter’s), each solve started them at the offset of their sources’ ends (mitcad#641), which put a dragged arc back to the distance; an end of a result line that a curve the offset did not make goes through now starts where it is along the line (offset::seed), so the drag stays.
  • A line distance between lines that are not parallel: line_distance holds (and measures) the distance of the middle of the second line from the first, which is the lines’ distance only where they are parallel. The solved sketch lists such dimensions in not_parallel (the sketch query, and an edit’s status, only when there is one; the ends of the second line lie at distances from the first that differ by more than 1e-5 mm), and warns “a distance between lines that are not parallel: it holds the middle of one line, not the lines’ distance (the Dimension tool gives an angle for such lines)” (several: “2 distances between lines that are not parallel: …”), a warning of the sketch’s evaluation and a notice of the query, whose warning_entities are their lines. The application draws them as in conflict. The equation of line_distance stays as it is.
  • Arcs keep their side. A change of driving values (a dimension, a parameter, a configuration’s value) is solved in steps (the solver’s continuation); a step after which an arc lies on the other side of its chord (the sine of its sweep changed sign, each clearly away from a half circle) is taken again in halves, up to 8 times (System::arc_sides). Linked projections that moved are solved in steps the same way (project::solve_followed, up to 6 halvings), and one solve after which an arc changed its side is taken again in 4 steps. A fillet’s arc keeps its sweep and its side when its dimensions are scaled by 1.5 and back.
  • Corners: Round (sketch.offset and sketch.edit_offset with "corners": "round", the record’s round): at each corner where two curves of the chain meet at an angle, two lines, a line and an arc, or two arcs (mitcad#1786), and the chain turns away from the offset (it turns left there for an offset to its right, a positive distance; the ends of the two results lie apart by more than 1e-7 of the chain’s size, as a derived offset’s outer corners are judged), the two results no longer meet; an arc about the source’s corner point (its centre is that point, so it follows the source) joins their ends, counter-clockwise, and is listed in the record’s corners ({"join": 0, "arc": "c12"}, join the result before it). Its radius is the distance: a line’s result lies at the distance from the corner, an arc’s result ends at the distance from it along the arc’s radius, so that the corner arc touches both. It has no dimension: the solve holds it tangent to both results at their ends (offset::tangent_corners, the offset’s own, not stored), and leaves out the own dimension of the curve after each arc (offset::independent: the arc places it, its radius that of the curve before it): a line’s distance, an arc’s helper length. So the outline is fully defined by the offset and its arcs follow a new distance. Of an outline whose every result is so placed (a closed chain rounded at every corner, or rounded and tangent all round), the first result keeps its own dimension, and the loop of tangencies that closes on it is the offset’s own, not listed in redundant (Extra::restating). The offsets of a line and an arc, or of two arcs, need not cross at an outer corner: with Round they are not sought there, and what vanishes at the distance is found with the outer corners round, as for a derived offset (exact_vanishing’s sharp). Corners the chain turns toward the offset at (inner corners) stay trimmed, and tangent joins stay one shared point. A changed corners makes the offset again (SketchEdit::set_offset_corners), the user’s constraints on its curves kept. Freed from its source, a corner arc gets a centre of its own and its tangencies become tangent constraints, as an offset’s tangent corners do.
  • Tests: core/model-tests/sketch/src/sketch_rounded_offset_1774_tests.rs (the triangle with partly implied coincidences, the singular arcs, the line distance turned, a fillet scaled, the Round offset, and the reporter’s design under MITCAD_MITCAD_REPORTED/github-324 when it is there), the solver’s analysis.rs and solve.rs tests, and for corners at arcs (mitcad#1786) a line and an arc closed at two corners outward, a line and an arc meeting at a tangent join, two arcs at an angle, and inward (trimmed) in the same file.

Conflicting constraints

A sketch whose constraints and dimensions contradict each other does not solve, and its message says what cannot hold in the words the user sees, never by ids (mitcad#1566, sketch/conflict.rs): a constraint by its type and the entities it is on (“the Equal between two lines”, “the Horizontal on a line”), a dimension by its value (“the 2.00 mm distance”, “the 45.00° angle”), the first three named and the rest counted (“and 4 more”); fixed entities are summarised as “projected geometry” (or “fixed geometry” when none is projected), never listed.

  • A sketch that does not solve (its error, the timeline’s): every constraint and dimension of the conflict, “conflicting constraints: the Equal between two lines, the 2.00 mm distance and 3 more can’t all hold with projected geometry”. The ids are the sketch query’s conflicts.
  • A sketch.* edit refused for a conflict names what blocks the change: “the Equal between two lines can’t hold with the fillet”. Of the constraints and dimensions of the conflict, those the user had (not fixed geometry, not what the command adds itself, such as a fillet’s tangents and radius, not a dimension whose value it changes or what it activates), each is left out in turn; those whose leaving out lets the sketch solve with the least movement of the points that were there are named (up to 24 are tried; more, or none found, and all of them are named). The change is named by the command: the fillet, the chamfer, the trim, the new constraint, the new dimension, the new value, the activated constraints, … With no constraint of the user’s in the conflict: “the new dimension can’t hold with fixed geometry”.
  • The refusal’s last line lists the named ones’ ids, for agents, the log and the application: [conflicts: k5], [conflicts: none] (conflict::split takes it off). The application shows the message without it and paints those constraints and dimensions, and the curves and points they are on, in the view while the message shows.

An upright sketch frame

sketch.create with "upright": true (and no frame; mitcad#692) gives the new sketch the own frame (frame) that shows the design upright when the sketch opens: the application looks along the frame’s normal with the sketch’s y axis up, so the frame decides what is up on the screen. Create Sketch in the application asks for it; scripts and other callers get the plane’s frame unless they ask.

  • y, the screen’s up: the design’s +Z projected onto the plane, when the plane’s normal is not along Z (the XZ and YZ planes, vertical and slanted faces); the design’s +Y when it is (the XY plane, top and bottom faces).
  • The normal stays the plane’s, the side the sketch is drawn on, so the sketch is not mirrored; x = y × normal. The screen’s horizontal stays the sketch’s x, so Horizontal and Vertical constraints, the grid and the dimensions stay horizontal and vertical on the screen.
  • The XZ origin plane has no outside, and its own normal (+Y) would show it from the view cube’s BACK with the design’s +X to the left. A new upright sketch on it is seen from FRONT instead (mitcad#1060): its normal is -Y, and x = y × normal is +X, still not mirrored. An extrude of such a sketch takes -Y (towards the front) as its positive direction; a sketch on XZ without upright (the plane’s own frame) and every XZ sketch made before keep +Y. XY (normal +Z, seen from TOP) and YZ (normal +X, seen from RIGHT) need no turn; a face is always seen from outside it.
  • Results: XY keeps its frame (x = +X, y = +Y). XZ gets x = +X, y = +Z, normal -Y (the plane’s own frame has y = -Z, normal +Y; before mitcad#1060 the upright frame was x = -X, y = +Z, normal +Y). YZ gets x = +Y, y = +Z (the plane’s own x = -Z). A face facing ±X or ±Y gets y = +Z whichever way it faces; a top face y = +Y, x = +X, a bottom face y = +Y, x = -X.
  • The design’s axes are taken where the sketch is shown: in the coordinates of its component through the occurrence context or occurrence names (else the component’s first occurrence).
  • The frame is stored only when it differs from the plane’s: a sketch on XY or a top face has none. The sketch keeps it as any own frame, also when its plane moves later; existing and imported sketches keep theirs (an XZ sketch with the earlier upright frame, x = -X, opens from BACK as before, and its extrudes keep their direction). The command stays one undo step (Add Sketch2). sketch.redefine_plane with upright gives a sketch moved to a new plane the same frame, XZ’s seen from FRONT too.

Projected outlines and their offsets

An edge projected again, or a face projected after one of its edges, used to add a second curve on the edge with points of its own, so the outline was no chain for sketch.offset (mitcad#741). Now:

  • sketch.project joins the new entities to the projected geometry already in the sketch (sketch/project.rs, join_existing): a curve the same as one there is not added again (the result’s warnings name it), and ends and loose points where an end or a loose point is are that point. A linked projection joins only the entities of linked projections of the same body and link, an unlinked one only projected entities in no projection, so a static curve never ends on a point that follows a source. Points of arcs are never shared between linked projections (a line takes either place when two sources part, an arc would no longer fit its centre); an arc the same as one there is left out only when no other new curve ends on it. A join that would make three non-construction curves end at one point is not made: a face projected beside one it shares an edge with keeps its own line on that edge, so that each outline stays a chain (Chain Selection stops where three curves meet). A projection that adds nothing gets no record. Within one projection, ends closer than half of 1e-7 of its size share a point (a model’s edges meet within its tolerance), as following allows.
  • sketch.offset counts curves that are the same (within 1e-7 of the sketch’s size, a line or a spline either way round) once: of such a pair, picked or not, it takes the one that shares its ends with more of the other listed curves, the listed one when that is as good, and warnings says so (“c3 lies on c9 (the same curve twice): c9 is offset”). Curves that are no chain are refused with the reason: where they branch, or the curve that does not join and how far its nearest end is from theirs (two ends within 0.01 mm that are two points: a Coincident constraint joins them). An open chain whose free end lies within 0.01 mm of another curve’s end on a point of its own (of the same construction kind) warns. The exact offset’s refusal at a corner names the two curves.
  • A sweep’s or a pipe’s sketch path (path.rs) takes a curve the same as an earlier one once, chained or listed.
  • Chain Selection in the application (Offset) starts from the curve a picked one lies on when the picked one joins nothing and that one does.

Projecting a curved face

sketch.project of a face gives the face as it is seen along the sketch’s normal, its outline (mitcad#1265; Kernel::face_outline, geometry/src/face_outline.cpp), not only its boundary edges: a cylinder seen from the side was its two circles (seen edge on) and its seam, so one long side of the rectangle was missing and the seam could lie inside it.

  • The curves are the face’s boundary edges as before, without a seam edge that is not on the outline (a seam is where the surface’s parameters close, no edge to see), and the face’s silhouettes: the curves along which its normal is at right angles to the sketch’s normal, clipped to the face. A seam on the outline comes once (a silhouette along an edge is that edge), and so does a seam seen end on: not at all (no point).
  • A cylinder or a cone (its axis parallel to the plane or slanted) has the generator lines where it turns away from the view, worked out exactly and clipped to the face’s boundary: a whole one two, a part of one as many as its angle holds (0, 1 or 2; one on a straight side of the face is that side); a face cut slanted gets each line up to the cut. A cylinder’s side face on a plane parallel to its axis is the rectangle, a tube’s inner face too, a cone’s the trapezoid. Seen along its axis (or from inside a cone’s angle) a face has no silhouettes: its circles only.
  • Other curved faces (spheres, tori, surfaces of revolution, B-spline faces) have the outline curves of the geometry kernel’s hidden line removal of the face alone, visible and hidden ones; a plane has none. The curves are projected as edges are (lines, conics, B-splines).
  • A linked projection of a face records "outline": true and follows the outline: its silhouettes are worked out again at every evaluation with its boundary edges, so the rectangle follows a change of the cylinder’s radius or place. A projection without it (files of earlier versions, imports, a kernel without outlines) follows the face’s boundary edges as before, its seam line included, with no warning. Edges, vertices and section curves ("section": true) are unchanged.

Insert Point on a spline

sketch.insert_spline_point (mitcad#836, sketch/spline_points.rs): sketch, curve (a spline or a fitted_spline), at [x, y] (a place on or near the curve). One undo step, Insert Spline Point in <sketch>; result made: the new point.

  • Fitted spline: a new fit point where the curve is nearest to at, listed between its two neighbours in the curve’s order (in a closed spline after the last point when the place is on the stretch back to the first). The curve still passes through every fit point; between the new point’s neighbours it may change shape a little, as the cubic now interpolates one more point. Refused on an existing fit point.
  • Spline by control points: a knot inserted once at the parameter nearest to at (Boehm’s algorithm; rational splines too): one more control point and the same curve, exactly, at every parameter. The knots (and weights) are written out in full. The control points next to the new one move to keep the shape (degree - 1 of them, fewer where the knot is there already); they keep their ids. Refused at the ends of the curve (a closed spline: where it closes), where the knot is there degree times already (the curve passes through a control point there), and when a point that would move is listed twice in control.
  • Closed splines work alike: a closed fitted spline, and a spline by control points whose ends are one point (or whose knots are unclamped).
  • Every existing point keeps its id, its constraints and its dimensions; a constraint on a control point that moved may then pull the curve when the sketch solves. Refused for a projected curve and for a curve a derived offset computes, as Trim is.

Dragging a selection

sketch.drag with entities (points and curves, mitcad#837) and by [dx, dy] drags them together, as sketch mode does when the press is on one of several selected curves or points:

{"cmd": "sketch.drag", "sketch": "F1", "entities": ["c1", "c4", "p3"], "by": [5, 3]}
  • Every point of the entities (a curve’s ends, centre and control points) is pulled by the offset from where it is now, as far as the constraints allow; a point that several of them share, such as a selected end of a selected curve, is pulled once. All of it is one solve, as a single drag’s, and one undo step Drag in Sketch1.
  • Constraints and dimensions hold: those among the entities keep the set rigid, fixed geometry holds and geometry constrained to something outside the set pulls back as the solver decides, and geometry outside the set follows its constraints and shared points.
  • A derived offset’s curve or point pulls its source chain, as in a single drag.
  • entities takes by only, and not together with entity; an empty list is refused.

Rotating sketch geometry

sketch.move turns its entities with rotate and moves them Point to Point with from and to (mitcad#1563, GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#212):

{"cmd": "sketch.move", "sketch": "F1", "entities": ["c1", "c2", "c3", "c4"], "from": "p5", "to": "p10"}
{"cmd": "sketch.move", "sketch": "F1", "entities": ["c1"], "rotate": {"angle": 1.5707963267948966}}

(angle is a number in radians.)

  • Point to Point moves by to − from, each an existing point ("p5") or a position ([x, y]), both read before the move: a point of the moved entities is where it was. It takes neither by nor rotate.
  • Without center, the turn is about the entities’ middle: the center of the box round their points, a circle’s whole round included.
  • A move drags the points to their turned places as far as the constraints allow. The constraints and dimensions that hold the moved geometry to the sketch’s axes, those whose points all move, turn with it, since kept as they were they would pull it back: a horizontal line turned by 90 degrees collapsed to a point, and a rectangle with it (the selection disappeared).
    • By a quarter or three quarters of a turn, a horizontal becomes vertical and the other way round (also horizontal_points, vertical_points, an equal spacing’s horizontal and vertical modes, and a horizontal_distance or vertical_distance); a half turn keeps them. A signed distance whose sign the turn would change measures from its other point instead (its a and b swap).
    • By any other angle the horizontal and vertical lines are held to the first of them instead, parallel to it where they ran the same way and perpendicular where they did not; a horizontal or vertical distance between two points level or plumb becomes their distance; the other directional constraints and dimensions are deactivated (turned off the sketch's axes by a rotation). The result’s notes say which.
  • A copy (copy) leaves out the directional constraints of turned copies, as before.

Holding moved geometry where it was dropped

sketch.move takes hold (mitcad#1645, GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#245): constraints, as sketch.add_constraint takes them, that hold the moved geometry where the user dropped it on a point or a curve (the application’s Move/Copy: its Target Point, its handle). They are added after the move, in its undo step:

{"cmd": "sketch.move", "sketch": "F1", "entities": ["c4"], "from": "p3", "to": "p7", "copy": true,
 "hold": [{"type": "coincident", "point": "p3", "entity": "p7"}]}
  • With copy, a moved entity a hold names stands for its copy: above, the copy’s centre is held on p7, the original stays free.
  • Two curve ends held together stay two points (unlike sketch.add_constraint, which makes them one, “Points that become one”), so the copy’s made ids stay what they are.
  • A hold the sketch refuses (it conflicts with the others, or they imply it) is left out and the sketch is as it was without it; the move is kept, and the result’s warnings say so (not held where it was dropped: …, the constraint for agents in the detail).
  • Code: SketchEdit::hold_moved (core/sketch/src/modify.rs). Tests: core/model-tests/sketch/src/sketch_move_hold_1645_tests.rs.

Moving and copying texts

sketch.move takes texts (mitcad#1911, GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#369): the sketch’s texts (QR codes too) moved or copied with the entities, by any of its moves (by, from and to, rotate); either list may be empty, not both:

{"cmd": "sketch.move", "sketch": "F1", "texts": ["t3"], "by": [10, 0]}
{"cmd": "sketch.move", "sketch": "F1", "entities": ["c1"], "texts": ["t3"], "rotate": {"angle": 1.5707963267948966}, "copy": true}
  • A text without a frame or a path moves its anchor (at) where the move takes it; a rotation also turns its angle (kept in (-π, π]).
  • A text in a frame follows its frame’s rectangle: its corner points, the fourth corner where a line from the x corner and one from the y corner meet, and the lines between those corners move with the entities (a rotation turns their horizontal and vertical constraints, as in Rotating sketch geometry); the text’s at and angle become its frame’s corner and direction.
  • A text on a path follows its curve and is refused, a text on a path follows its curve: move the curve instead (the text and the curve for agents in the detail): move the curve.
  • Without center, rotate turns about the middle of the entities, the frames’ rectangles and the anchors of the other texts.
  • With copy, each text is copied (a text in a frame with a copy of its rectangle), and the copy follows the text parameter the text follows where that is a parameter or an expression of parameters; made lists the copied entities and then the copied texts (t<n>).
  • Code: core/sketch/src/text_move.rs. Tests: core/model-tests/sketch/src/sketch_move_text_1911_tests.rs.

Scaling a sketch

sketch.scale (mitcad#860, sketch/scale.rs): sketch, factor (a number greater than zero), center (a point id or [x, y] of numbers: a scale is made once, and a coordinate written as an expression is refused in words, mitcad#1912; the sketch origin when left out). It scales the whole sketch about center, one undo step Scale <sketch>:

{"cmd": "sketch.scale", "sketch": "F1", "factor": 2.5}
  • Every point of the sketch’s own geometry moves away from or towards center by the factor; circles’ radii and ellipses’ minor radii, the texts’ places, heights and line spacings (a QR code’s module size) and the places of the dimensions’ values scale with it. The sketch’s origin point and axes stay where they are.
  • The values of its driving length dimensions (every kind but angle), of its offsets’ distances and of its rectangular patterns’ spacings are multiplied by the factor, so that the sketch keeps its shape and its constraints. Angles stay.
  • Refused for a sketch with projected, intersected or linked geometry (it follows its source), and when one of those length values is another parameter or an expression of one (change that instead).

Scaling a selection (Sketch Scale, mitcad#2109). entities (points, curves and texts of the sketch: p3, c4, t5) scales only them, with the points their curves use, about center; dimensions says what their driving lengths do: scale (default) or keep; copy (default false) scales their copies instead and leaves them where they are. The application’s Sketch Scale sends it; one undo step Scale <sketch>:

{"cmd": "sketch.scale", "sketch": "F1", "entities": ["c3", "c4", "t5"], "factor": 1.5, "center": "p2"}
{"cmd": "sketch.scale", "sketch": "F1", "entities": ["c3"], "factor": 2, "center": [10, 0], "dimensions": "keep", "copy": true}
  • The points move by the factor about center; the selected circles' radii and ellipses’ minor radii, the selected texts’ heights and line spacings scale. A text in a frame takes its frame’s rectangle with it; a text on a path is refused unless its curve is selected too. The sketch’s origin point and axes in the selection stay where they are.
  • Inside the selection (every curve and point a constraint or a dimension refers to scaled): the constraints are kept. With scale, the values of the driving length dimensions (every kind but angle), of the offsets’ distances and of the rectangular patterns’ spacings among them are multiplied by the factor; one that is a parameter or an expression is refused in words (“a dimension of the selection takes its value from a parameter”), its id on the refusal’s [conflicts: …] line so that the application paints it. With keep, they keep their values and the scaled geometry is solved with them, pulled toward where the scale put it while the geometry its ties to the rest refer to is held where it is; refused in words when they can’t hold, or when they fix every size of the selection (a rectangle with its width and height kept), their ids on the [conflicts: …] line.
  • Ties to the rest (a constraint or a dimension between scaled and other geometry, or on a curve with a scaled point): kept when it still holds after the scale (a coincident at center, a parallel), removed otherwise; the result’s notes count them (“Constraints that tied the scaled geometry to the rest were removed: 1”) and removed lists them. Nothing outside the selection moves.
  • An offset or a pattern the selection takes only in part is refused in words, its id on the [conflicts: …] line (what is left out would no longer follow it); a circular pattern’s center counts as taken when it is center. Projected, intersected or linked geometry in the selection is refused (it follows its source); outside it, it does not block the scale.
  • copy: the copies are scaled, with the constraints among them (no dimensions, as Move/Copy’s Create Copy); made lists the copies of entities in their order, then of the texts.
  • Without entities but with keep or copy, the selection is every point, curve and text of the sketch’s own.
  • Code: core/sketch/src/scale.rs. Tests: core/model-tests/sketch/src/sketch_scale_selection_2109_tests.rs.

The first dimension scales the sketch. sketch.add_dimension with "scale_sketch": true (default false; the application sends it while the preference Scale the sketch to its first dimension is on, its default) applies the first-dimension rule to a driving dimension: when the sketch was drawn out of proportion, its geometry is first scaled uniformly about the sketch origin by the dimension’s value over what it measures now, as sketch.scale does, so that the dimension holds; then the dimension is added as usual. Both are one undo step, Add Dimension to <sketch>.

  • Only a length, distance, radius or diameter (every kind but angle), and only when the sketch has no other dimension, offset or rectangular pattern, no projected, intersected or linked geometry, and no fixed entity other than its origin point and axes (sketch.axis). Otherwise, and for a driven dimension, nothing is scaled, as without the flag.
  • The constraints are kept; text heights scale too. The dimension’s text place, given on the sketch as drawn, scales with it.
  • Result: as other edits, and scaled (the factor) when the sketch was scaled. A value equal to what the geometry measures scales nothing; so a drawing tool’s typed value, which draws its shape at that size, scales the sketch only where the shape was drawn at another size.

Sketches on cylindrical and conical faces

A sketch can lie on the side of a cylinder or a cone instead of a plane (mitcad#1768; code: core/model-base/src/developed.rs, the map; core/model/src/features/developed.rs, its evaluation and features; Kernel::wrapped_curves). It is a normal 2D sketch for the solver, its tools, constraints and dimensions; its coordinates are the face’s developed coordinates:

  • A cylinder: x is the length around the face at its radius (the arc length), y the distance along its axis. A line along y is a line along the face, a line along x a circle (an arc) around it, a slanted line a helix; lengths and angles on the face are the sketch’s.
  • A cone: its development, the cone unrolled flat about its apex (lengths and angles on the face are the sketch’s): y runs along the generator under the sketch’s origin, the apex lies on the sketch’s y axis, a line through the apex is a generator and an arc about it a circle around the cone.

plane in sketch.create (and sketch.redefine_plane) takes {"face": "F2:side(c1)", "body": "F2.b0", "developed": {"angle": 0.5}} (body optional, angle radians, default 0) for a cylindrical or conical face of the bodies before the sketch:

  • Where the sketch lies is found again from the face at every evaluation, so it follows the face’s radius, length, place and angle as a sketch on a planar face follows its face. The sketch’s y axis runs along the face’s axis, counted towards the design’s +Z (else +Y, else +X, as Emboss’s Along Axis counts); its origin is at the face’s low end along that direction (a cone’s at its other end when the low end is the apex), at angle about the axis from the reference direction across it (the design’s X axis across the axis, else its Y axis), turned right-handed about the sketch’s y axis. Its x axis runs to the right as the face is seen from outside the material (from the axis for a bore’s wall), so a text reads the right way on the face.
  • upright is ignored (the sketch is upright on the face); a frame, a placement (offset, x, y, angle, flip) and a plane of another component (occurrence) are refused. A face that is neither cylindrical nor conical fails the sketch, its place the face.
  • The sketch query has surface (null on a plane): kind (cylinder, cone), axis (origin, direction: a cylinder’s at the sketch’s y = 0 and along its y axis, a cone’s at its apex where its radius grows), radius (a cone’s at the sketch’s origin), half_angle and apex (a cone), internal (the material outside: a bore’s wall) and frame, the carrier plane: the sketch’s frame (the query’s frame too) is a plane parallel to the axis through the sketch’s origin, the face’s outward normal its normal; a sketch point is wrapped from it onto the face as Emboss wraps a sketch (the emboss section). The profiles query’s regions and the sketch’s own geometry are in these flat coordinates.
  • Projections (sketch.project, linked or not) of edges and faces are their developments in the sketch: each point of the curve goes to the sketch point of the face’s point nearest to it (the angle followed along the curve). A circle around a cylinder’s axis, a helix on it and a line along it are lines; other curves are B-splines through their points (within 1e-7 of the radius); a point a point.

sketch_surface query ({"query": "sketch_surface", "sketch": "F3", …}): a sketch’s points on its face and back, for the view and the pointer. A sketch on a plane answers the same way on its plane (kind plane).

FieldMeaning
pointssketch points [[u, v], …]: answered points, each {"at": [x, y, z], "normal": […]} (the face’s outward normal there)
rays[{"origin": […], "direction": […]}, …]: answered rays, each {"hit": true, "point": [u, v], "at": […], "normal": […], "distance": d} for the nearest place ahead where the ray meets the (unbounded) cylinder or cone (a cone’s other nappe left out), else {"hit": false}: the pointer’s place in the sketch
nearmodel points [[x, y, z], …]: answered near, each the sketch point of the face’s point nearest to it, null on the axis: snaps to body vertices and edges
arounda sketch point [u, v] (default the origin): rays and model points are taken on the turn of the face nearest to it, so that a pointer going on past the far side keeps going on in the sketch
curvestrue: answered curves, each of the sketch’s curves {"id": "c3", "polyline": [[x, y, z], …], "length": L} on the face (pieces at most segment mm, default 0.5) with its length on the face; only (["c3", …]) limits them

Always answered: surface (as in the sketch query; on a plane {"kind": "plane", "frame": …}).

Features of the sketch:

  • Extrude raises a developed sketch’s profiles out of the material by its distance along the face’s normals, or sinks them into it with flip or a negative distance, as Emboss wraps them (Kernel::wrapped_emboss; faces named as an emboss’s: side(<segment>), start(<region>) on the face, end(<region>)): a distance extent without a taper, from the face, with its operation (join, cut, new_body, …). Join and Cut work on their bodies as a planar sketch’s do (mitcad#1908): participants (the bodies of its own component; all of them when empty), and a Cut’s cut_scope (the targets it cuts, in other components too, Assembly scope for Extrude Cut) when it has one; a Join’s or a New Body’s dormant cut_scope does nothing. Thin walls (an extrusion of a sketch on a curved face has no thin walls), wrap, direction, another start and a taper are refused, each in its own words.
  • Emboss without a face raises or sinks them on the sketch’s face (depth, mode, taper_angle, and along_axis, around_angle, rotation_angle moving them on the face, as on a wrap); a face, projection or direction of its own is refused.
  • Split Face with the sketch’s curves ("tool": {"sketch": "F3", "curves": ["c5"]}; every curve but construction curves when the list is empty) splits the face along them: each curve is laid onto the face and ruled a little along its normals both ways (Kernel::wrapped_curves, a surface body of bands <feature>:band(<curve>)), which cuts the face. A line once around a cylinder is a closed ring; open curves must cross the face. A direction is refused. A closed region across the face’s seam (where its surface closes) is one face (mitcad#1853): the split’s pieces on either side of the seam are joined again (geometry::split_faces, for every tool), unless a cut runs along the seam.
  • Paths (Sweep, Pipe, a sweep’s guide rail, Helix, …) and curves of the sketch taken into other sketches (sketch.project of a sketch’s curve or point) are the curves on the face: lines along a cylinder’s axis or a cone’s generator, circles and arcs around the axis, helices, and B-splines through the points of other curves (within 1e-7 of the radius).
  • Other features that take a sketch’s profiles (Revolve, Sweep’s profile, Loft, Patch, Hole, …) and those that grow from its curves in their plane (ribs, webs, thin walls, surface extrusions) refuse a developed sketch: its profiles and curves lie in no plane.

Components and occurrences

The design is a root component (C0, named Root until renamed); other components (C1, …) are placed in it, or in each other, by occurrences (O1, …, named <component>:<n>, e.g. Plate:2). Code: core/model/src/assembly.rs, commands in document/components.rs. Examples: tools/cli/tests/f6_*.json.

  • One timeline. Every feature belongs to a component: the active one when it is added (or component of add_feature). A feature works on the bodies of its own component, in that component’s coordinates: a body of another component fails the feature (body F3.b0 (from Extrude2) belongs to Component1; …), and a sketch or construction geometry of another component is refused when the feature is added. Sketch planes and projections, and a combine’s tools, may name another component’s geometry with where it was picked (Geometry of other components).
  • Shared definitions. A component’s bodies are built once, in its own coordinates; every occurrence shows them placed by its transform, and a component placed in another is placed again with every occurrence of that one. The bodies query lists the definitions, the instances query the bodies as placed in the design. For display, draw each instance’s body_shape moved by its transform.
  • New components. create_component makes an empty one placed in the active component. The operation new_component of extrude, revolve, the primitives and base features, and combine’s new_component, make a component placed in the feature’s component (identity; beside it when its design policy takes no components, Design policy), named Component<n>, holding the bodies the feature creates (a combine: its target); editing the operation away removes it (refused while something was added to it), and deleting the feature deletes it unless something else is in it. components_from_bodies adds, per body, a component_from_bodies feature in the body’s component: the body moves into a new component named after it, where it is, keeping its id and name; later features on it belong to that component. The features that made a body can move into a component with it instead (Moving features into components).
  • Placements. An occurrence’s transform is rigid (rows of a rotation and a translation, [[r00, r01, r02, tx], …], in its parent’s coordinates). Timeline features place occurrences of their own component: move_occurrence moves them, capture_position puts them at captured placements. set_occurrence_transform sets an occurrence’s own placement while no feature before the marker places it, or with "capture": true adds a capture_position feature. A grounded occurrence does not move: the command is refused and a feature that would move it fails (Plate:2 is grounded), except a move_occurrence that lists it itself (mitcad#1196: the app’s Move/Copy of a grounded BUILD part): it moves there and stays grounded at the new place, fixed for the joints after it. The occurrences jointed to it before the move stay where those joints put them, as with any move_occurrence; a grounded member a rigid group would take along still fails the move.
  • Copies. copy_occurrence places the same component again (one definition). paste_new makes a new component, a copy of the definition with its history: its features (new ids and default names; references among them follow), their own parameters (copied with their expressions; other parameters are shared), the components placed in it and, for a component a new-component operation made, that feature. A component made from bodies, or linked, is copied as its bodies (a base feature), retaining body material, visibility and appearance assignments; face overrides follow the snapshot’s new face names. Both go into the active component, which must not be in the copied one.
  • External components. insert_component places another design file in the active component: linked (default) as a read-only component whose bodies are a base feature holding the file’s visible bodies as that design places them (its link: path, a digest of the text and the feature), or with "link": false as a copy of the file’s design with its history (its root becomes the new component; its user parameters come along, renamed name_1 when the name is taken). A whole design that has components keeps them, with its joints and grounding, read only (A whole design linked with its components). Linked components cannot be activated or edited. update_links (with the design file’s directory as base for relative paths) reads the linked files again and takes the bodies of those that changed; a missing file keeps the saved bodies. Callers run it when they open a design (no undo step; what changed is a load warning). Only files in the design’s project are followed (mitcad#929; for a design in no project, its folder and the folders in it): a link whose path is absolute outside it, or whose .. leads out of it, is not read at all, and its component keeps the saved bodies with the message “: the file is outside the project, so the link is not followed and it keeps the bodies saved with the project; to follow it, move the file into the project, or make the folder that holds both a project (File › Project › New Project…), then Update Link” (mitcad#1719: in words, no path). Without base no link is followed ("…: the design is not saved yet, so the link is not followed…"). So that links stay followed, insert_component records a file in the project by its path relative to base (../parts/plate.mitcad, with /), whatever form path had; a file outside the project keeps path as given, and its link is not followed when the design opens again, unless copy_into_project copies it in first (Linked designs from outside the project). Linked or a copy, the inserted bodies are made of the materials their source design gives them and show its appearances, and a linked one follows a change of them when it is read again (Materials of inserted components).
  • Deleting. delete_occurrence deletes an occurrence; the last one of a component deletes the component with its features, the feature that made it and what depends on them, and the components only it contained (a component made from bodies gives them back to its parent). A cut that excludes the occurrence stays: its exclusion is dropped, with an info notice in the result (mitcad#1236, Assembly scope for Extrude Cut).

componentsactive; components (the root first): uid, name, created_by, link (path), library (a library part’s record, or null), features, bodies, occurrences (count), policy (Design policy); occurrences: the tree from the root, each uid, name, path, component, transform (rows, in the parent, at the marker), world (4x4 into the design; inside a flexible occurrence where it is for that one), grounded, visible, children; a flexible occurrence also flexible and joint_values (Flexible subassemblies)
instancesproperties, hidden (default false)the bodies as placed: path (occurrence uids), occurrence (path name, empty for the root’s), component, component_name, body, name, visible, transform (4x4); with properties the placed body’s volume, area, center, bbox
  • An occurrence is given by its uid (O3), its name (Plate:2) or its path from the root (Arm:1/Pin:2 or O1/O4: the last one).
  • A transform is 3 or 4 rows of 4 numbers (a 4x4 matrix ends with [0, 0, 0, 1]), or {"translation": [x, y, z], "rotation": {"axis": [x, y, z], "angle": a}} (both optional; the rotation about the origin comes first).
  • Each command is an undo step (New Component Plate, Ground Plate:1, Hide Plate:1, Paste Plate:2, Paste New Plate (1), Insert part.mitcad, …); hiding, renaming and activating recompute nothing.
  • Renaming a component renames its body (mitcad#291): a component (not the root) with exactly one body at the marker whose name is still a default one (the generated Body<n>) gives the body its new name too, in the same undo step, unless another body already has that name. A body the user named is never renamed; once renamed with its component the body’s name is no longer a default one, so later renames leave it. The reply’s renamed_body names it (null when no body was renamed), so the application refreshes the browser and the timeline without asking again.
  • The text report (mitcad-cli info) lists the components and the placed bodies.
  • Design file (version 2 and later), when there are components: root_component (the root’s name when renamed), components (uid, name, created_by, link), occurrences (uid, component, parent, number, transform rows unless the identity, grounded, "visible": false), active_component, and a feature’s component when it is not the root. Files without them load with every feature in the root component.

Saving a component as a design

Save Component as Design (mitcad#1057, document/save_component.rs) writes a component as a design file of its own: the component’s definition becomes the new design’s root. Insert Component’s unlinked insert does the same the other way round, and the same copy does the work (copy.rs), so the new design holds the component’s features and timeline (before the timeline marker; the features keep their names), its sketches and construction geometry, the design’s parameters its expressions use (as the new design’s own, with the tables they look values up in), the components placed in it with their occurrences, placements and joints, its materials, appearances, property sets, drawings and design policy, in the design’s units. Linked components and library components inside it stay linked: a link’s path is recorded from the new file’s folder.

CommandFieldsResult
save_component_as_designcomponent (uid or name), path (the design file to write), replace (default false), base (the folder of this design’s file, for link paths; the folder it was read from or saved to when left out)component, path (absolute), references (below), replaced, link (the path this design records for the new file, with replace; else null)
QueryFieldsResult
save_component_as_designcomponentcomponent, name, references, blocked (why it cannot be saved, or null)
  • Refused for the root (it is the design: Save As), a linked component (… is linked from part.mitcad, a design of its own already) and a library component. The query answers with blocked instead of an error, for the application’s dialog.
  • References outside it. What the component’s features (and those of the components inside it) refer to outside it cannot be carried. Each reference is frozen at its current geometry in the new design, the way a broken link keeps what it last had; this design does not change:
    • a sketch on another component’s face or plane lies on that plane, fixed: the XY plane with the sketch’s frame (frame) where the plane is now;
    • a projection of another component’s geometry keeps its curves where their sources are now, unlinked, as fixed references (as Clean Up Stale Projections unlinks one);
    • a construction plane, axis or point on other components’ geometry (links, datum_links) becomes a fixed one where it is now;
    • bodies of other components a feature reads (a combine’s tools, an extrusion’s or revolution’s objects, a sweep’s path and guide surfaces, a split’s tools, a derive’s bodies, a pulley’s, gear’s or bearing’s shaft) become hidden copies of those bodies as they are before the feature, in a base feature of the feature’s component just before it; the feature reads the copies, and the references to their faces, edges and vertices (in it and in the features after it) name the copies’ faces (<base>:import(<k>)). A later feature that reads the same body as it was (the same link, the same feature’s result) reads the same copy (mitcad#1150); one that reads it after another component’s feature changed it gets a copy of its own. A body transfer from outside becomes such a base feature of the bodies it moved in, shown, and the transfer goes;
    • the bodies a feature of another component made in it (a new-component operation, Create Components from Bodies) become a base feature of the component before its first feature, as they are after that feature, and its features’ references to their faces follow;
    • a move’s points and axes (from_occurrence, to_occurrence, point_occurrence, axis_occurrence; Move, Move of occurrences, Move Face) and a point pattern’s target and anchor points (occurrence) picked on another component (mitcad#1069) become fixed points and axes in the feature’s component’s coordinates, without an occurrence: where the feature last found them (the points and axis its motion was worked out from, the pattern’s anchor moved by each element’s translation), or, for a move along an axis and a feature without a result, where the geometry and its occurrence are at the timeline marker. One that cannot be found at all stays as it is and is listed as left out (the feature then fails in the new design, as it does in this one);
    • an assembly cut’s targets in other components (cut_scope) are left out;
    • joints, rigid groups, motion links and assembly constraints of other components that join an occurrence inside it stay in this design and are listed as left out.
  • references, in timeline order: feature and feature_name (the feature that refers; for made bodies and joints the one outside), kind (sketch_plane, projection, construction, body, made_bodies, cut_target, joint, point, axis), target (where it points: an occurrence path’s name such as Plate:1, or the component a feature outside is in), frozen (false: left out) and message, one line for the user (Sketch2: its projection of Plate:1, frozen at its current geometry; Move3: its point on Plate:1, frozen at its current geometry).
  • A joint, bound length or pattern of the component’s own that names an occurrence outside it cannot be frozen: the command is refused, naming them (Box cannot be saved as a design: Joint3 refers to Plate:1; edit them to refer to geometry inside it first).
  • The file is a single-file design (version 2), written whole or not at all. Without replace nothing in this design changes and there is no undo step.
  • Replace with a link (replace): after the file is written, the component in this design becomes a linked component of it (as insert_component links one), in one undo step (Replace Box with a Link to Box.mitcad): its features and the components only it holds go, with the occurrences placed in it; a base feature where its first feature was holds the bodies it shows (the visible bodies of it and of the components inside it, where its first occurrence places them, in its coordinates, keeping their materials and appearances); the feature of another component that made it goes (a new-component operation) or takes its bodies out of the design (remove_body, for Create Components from Bodies), and so does a body transfer’s source. Its occurrences, their placements, grounding and visibility stay. What refers to its bodies from outside (joints and their origins, links of other components’ sketches and features, the picks of annotations, mitcad#1150; print plate items of its bodies, comment targets and the drawings’ recorded view bodies and picks, mitcad#1318) follows: body ids become the base feature’s, face, edge and vertex names its faces’, and an occurrence path through it ends at its occurrence. The body link maps of features outside it (object_links, body_links, tool_links, a derive’s and a construction feature’s links) are re-keyed to the base feature’s bodies where their link is seen in it, and their links' source and target through it end at its occurrence too (mitcad#1144). Refused while a feature of it is after the timeline marker, for a component a combine made, for one without bodies to show, while a component inside it is placed in it more than once (Box cannot be replaced by a link while Pin is placed in it more than once: the references to its body name no placement, so they could not follow the right base body), and while a construction plane, axis or point outside it is on its sketches or construction geometry or those of the components in it (datum_links seen in it: Box cannot be replaced by a link while Plane4 is on Plane2 in it: …), since a linked component keeps none; nothing is written then. The links of linked components inside it are read from base as well (mitcad#1150: a design never saved has no folder of its own). The link’s path is relative to base when the file is in the design’s project (or, for a design in no project, in its folder), so that it is followed when the design opens (Components and occurrences).
  • Tests: core/model-tests/assembly/src/save_component_tests.rs, core/model/src/document/save_component.rs (the renames).

Joints

Joints connect occurrences and say how they may move against each other (mitcad#55). They are timeline features of the component they are added in (the active one, or component), recomputed in order like move_occurrence and capture_position, and edited, suppressed, reordered and deleted like other features (edit_feature takes the def the feature query gives). Code: core/model/src/joints.rs (kinds, frames, what recompute does), features/joint.rs (definitions), document/joints.rs and api/joints.rs, the joint solver core/solver/src/rigid.rs (README); tests joint_tests.rs, joint_solver_tests.rs, core/solver/tests/rigid.rs, tools/cli/tests/joints.json.

Joints are stored, checked, reported and solved (below), the application’s ASSEMBLE group adds, edits, drives, drags and animates them (app/COMMANDS.md, “Joints”), and the .f3d import brings the file’s joints in as these features (.f3d import with the timeline, From the dump IR).

Kinds and frames

A joint joins origin a to origin b. Each origin resolves to a frame (an origin and x, y, z axes) on geometry of an occurrence’s component, moved into the joint’s component by the occurrences’ placements. The joint holds when

frame_a = frame_b · motion(values) · Rz(angle) · Tz(offset) · flip

motion is the kind’s free motions at some values, along and about frame b’s axes, composed in the order listed; flip turns frame a over (half a turn about its x axis). Without flip the two z axes point the same way: to put a face on a face (both outward normals), flip.

KindFree motionsValues
rigidnone
revoluteturns about zrz
sliderslides along slide_axis (x, y or z, default z)tx, ty or tz
cylindricalslides along z, turns about ittz, rz
pin_slotslides along x, turns about ztx, rz
planarslides along x and y, turns about ztx, ty, rz
ballturns about z, y and xrz, ry, rx

Slides are millimetres, turns radians (right-handed).

Origins. {"occurrence": "O1/O4", "geometry": <reference>, "frame_override": {...}}. occurrence is a path of occurrences from the joint’s component (uids in definitions; add_joint also takes names, Arm:1/Pin:2), empty or left out for the component’s own geometry (which never moves). geometry is a reference to geometry of the component the path ends in, resolved there:

GeometryOriginz axis
planar faceits middle (Kernel::face_plane)the outward normal
cylindrical or conical facethe axis point nearest to the face’s middlethe axis (along its largest component)
toroidal facethe centrethe axis
spherical facethe centrethe component’s z
circular edgethe centrethe axis (along its largest component)
straight edgethe middlealong the edge
vertex, sketch point, construction point, the origin, a fixed pointthe pointthe component’s z
sketch circle or arcthe centrethe sketch’s normal
sketch line, construction or origin axis, fixed axisthe start or the axis’s originalong it
origin plane, construction plane, joint origin, fixed planeits originits normal (its x axis kept)

Other x axes are the model X projected across z (Y when z is along X). frame_override replaces parts of the frame, in the component’s coordinates: origin [x, y, z], z_axis, x_axis (projected across z); shift [x, y, z] then moves the origin along the frame’s own axes as they are after the override, so that it follows geometry that moves (BUILD’s corners on a profile’s end, mitcad#417). A body is no origin. A sketch or construction geometry of another component than the path’s is refused when the joint is added (a: Sketch1 is in Plate, not in Pin); a body of another component fails the joint at recompute (body F2.b0 is not in Pin at this point of the timeline).

Feature definitions 

{"type": "joint", "kind": "revolute",
 "a": {"occurrence": "O2", "geometry": {"body": "F4.b0", "face": "F4:start(r{…})"}},
 "b": {"occurrence": "O1", "geometry": {"body": "F2.b0", "face": "F2:end(r{…})"}},
 "offset": 0, "angle": 0, "flip": true,
 "limits": {"rz": {"min": "-90 deg", "max": "90 deg", "rest": "30 deg"}},
 "position": {"rz": "45 deg"}}
{"type": "joint", "kind": "cylindrical", "a": {…}, "b": {…}, "offset": 300,
 "start": {"tz": 0, "rz": 0}}
{"type": "as_built_joint", "kind": "revolute", "a": "O2", "b": "O1",
 "origin": {"occurrence": "O2", "geometry": "F9"},
 "relative": [[1, 0, 0, 100], [0, 1, 0, 0], [0, 0, 1, 0]], "limits": {}}
{"type": "joint_origin", "geometry": {"body": "F2.b0", "face": "F2:end(r{…})"},
 "frame_override": {"origin": [5, 5, 10]}, "offset": 0, "angle": 0, "flip": false}
{"type": "rigid_group", "occurrences": ["O2", "O3"]}
  • joint (named Joint<n>): kind, slide_axis (sliders only), a, b, offset (along z, a length), angle (about z), flip, limits, position, start; offset, angle and flip default to 0 and false. The two origins must be on different occurrences, and at most one may be the component’s own geometry.
  • limits: per free motion of the kind, {"min", "max", "rest"}, each optional and a value (parameters and expressions: a turn’s slots are angles, limits.rz.min_angle, a slide’s lengths, limits.tz.min). min ≤ rest ≤ max is checked when the joint is added or edited, and a parameter change that breaks it fails the joint.
  • position: per free motion of the kind, the value it is driven to (a value: position.rz.position_angle, position.tz.position), within its limits (checked like rest). drive_joint and drag_occurrence set it.
  • A free motion is driven (held at a value) by its position, else by its rest value; without either it is free: it moves as the joints need, stays within its limits, and otherwise stays where it is. Driven values say where a motion is, not whether it can move: degrees of freedom leave them out.
  • start (mitcad#1745): per free motion of the kind, a number (mm, radians): where the motion is when the joint places its moving side, instead of the value nearest to where that side is. The application’s Joint command writes 0 for every free motion of a new joint, so that the moving side goes where its origin meets the other at the offset and angle (a cylindrical joint’s offset then moves it), and drag_occurrence writes the values a drag leaves its free motions at. Unused for a driven motion (its position or rest), for a joint that closes a loop (the solver iterates those from where the occurrences are) and when a later joint’s solve places the joint again where it holds (it starts at the values it is at there, mitcad#2199); kept within the motion’s limits. A joint without it (older designs, imports, add_joint without it) keeps its free motions nearest to where the moving side is, so that its offset along a free slide only shifts the slide’s value.
  • as_built_joint (AsBuiltJoint<n>): two occurrence paths a and b joined where they are: relative is a’s placement in b’s coordinates when it was made (rows of a rotation and a translation; add_as_built_joint records it; without it the joint takes the placements as they are at its point of the timeline). origin (optional, an origin as above) is the frame of the free motions, b’s coordinates without it; an origin on a’s side is taken where the recorded relation puts it. The joint holds when a’s displacement from where the recorded relation puts it is the kind’s motions in that frame (values 0 at the recorded relation). Same kinds, limits and position.
  • joint_origin (JointOrigin<n>): construction geometry of its component, a frame on geometry (as an origin’s) with frame_override, then moved by angle about and offset along its z axis and turned over by flip. Its datum is a plane with that frame (the datums query; a sketch can be placed on it); joints use it as "F9". It has a light bulb like construction geometry. With mount it is a mount frame of the part (mitcad#525, Mount frames).
  • rigid_group (RigidGroup<n>): two or more occurrences placed in the feature’s component that move as one from its point of the timeline: the joints after it move them together, and a move_occurrence of one member moves the others by the same motion (capture_position sets each occurrence it lists). A group with a grounded member stays where it is: a move of another member fails (Base:1 is grounded).
  • Joint features recompute nothing of the bodies and are never written to the result store.

What recompute does

A unit is a top-level occurrence of the joint’s component (the one its path starts with) with those its rigid groups join to it; it moves as one rigid body. A unit is fixed when a member is grounded; the component’s own geometry (an empty path) is fixed too.

At its point of the timeline, a joint resolves its frames (in the components its paths end in, with that point’s bodies, sketches and construction geometry) and the joint solver solves it together with the joints in effect before it in the same component that share moving units with it, directly or through each other, from where the occurrences are at that point:

  • What needs no iteration is placed first, in timeline order: a joint between a side that is fixed (or joined to something fixed by the joints before it) and one that is not moves the free side, with every unit joined to it so far, so that the joint holds at its driven values and, for free motions, at its start values, else at the values nearest to where it is; between two free sides side a moves onto side b. An open chain needs nothing else.
  • Joints that close a loop are iterated: the units move as little as possible (turns weighed by the size of the joints’ layout) until every joint holds, driven motions at their values and free motions within their limits.
  • A joint moves only what it needs to hold (mitcad#2199). The joints before it that hold where the occurrences are (driven motions at their values, free ones within their limits) are placed again at the values they are at, not at their start values. Units that hang on the rest only by such joints (one joint cuts them off from everything fixed, from the joint’s own sides and from joints that motion links couple) are left out of the solve and move as the unit they hang on moves: a component an earlier joint holds on a body keeps its place on that body, also when a loop the new joint closes turns the body. Only top-level units that are not flexible occurrences hang so. Driven values still apply: an earlier joint whose driven motion is not at its value is solved as before.
  • The units that moved get placement changes of the joint feature (each occurrence’s placement set), applied as move_occurrence’s are; the occurrences’ own placements stay the starting ones (state placed, moved; satisfied when nothing had to move). Placements set by joints are not cached: grounding, ungrounding and moving an occurrence recompute them.
  • Joints whose sides cannot move only hold or fail, saying in words, with the components’ names, what holds each side (mitcad#1745): neither side can move (Pin:1 is grounded, and Plate:1 is in a rigid group with Base:1, which is grounded) and the joint does not hold, both sides move as one (a rigid group joins Pin:1 and Pin:2) and the joint does not hold, or … is not at its position. A side cannot move when it is the component’s own geometry (an origin on Box's own geometry does not move), when its unit has a grounded member (Pin:1 is grounded, … is in a rigid group with Base:1, which is grounded), or when joints before it that let nothing move (rigid ones, or those whose motions are all driven and in no motion link) join it to such a unit (Plate:1 is joined rigidly to Base:1, which cannot move). The error’s places are the occurrences that hold them ({"kind": "occurrence", "path": "O1/O4"}, the path of uids from the root; the application paints every body the occurrence places).
  • A joint whose moving occurrence a move_occurrence or capture_position later in the timeline places again warns, the occurrence its place: Pin:1 is placed again by a move later in the timeline, so it does not stay where this joint puts it (… by a captured position …; the detail names the feature).
  • Joints that contradict each other fail the joint feature, which moves nothing. The message says in words which joints work against each other, by the names the timeline shows, and what to do (mitcad#1753): Joint1, Joint2 and Joint3 work against each other and cannot all hold: free a motion of one of them, or remove one of them; with driven positions among them Joint1 and Joint4 cannot all hold at their positions: free a motion of one of them, remove one of them, or drive only one of them. A loop that cannot close from where the occurrences are (lengths or limits keep it apart): Joint1, Joint2, Joint3 and Joint4 cannot all hold from where the occurrences are, as limits or sizes keep them apart: change a limit or a size, …. The error’s places are the joints ({"kind": "joint", "feature": "F7"}), painted as the pointer over a joint’s Browser row draws it. The detail (the queries' error) keeps the solver’s analysis: over-constrained: Joint1 (at its rz position), Joint2 and Joint4 cannot all hold (the rank analysis of the joints’ equations, newest last; at its … position names driven values in the contradiction), or the joints cannot all hold (Joint1, Joint2, Joint3 and Joint4) from where the occurrences are: …. The joints after it are solved without it.
  • A path below a top-level occurrence only locates geometry: the joint moves the top-level occurrence (the whole sub-assembly), never an occurrence inside it; joints inside a sub-assembly are the sub-component’s own features, solved in its coordinates. A flexible occurrence is the exception (Flexible subassemblies): a path through it to an occurrence its component’s joints move, or to a free part of it (mitcad#2016), moves that occurrence, for the flexible occurrence alone.
  • At the marker each joint reports its frames and values where the occurrences are; a later feature that moved a side (a move_occurrence) leaves values null and solved false.

A joint whose origins cannot be resolved (an occurrence that is gone, a face that is no longer there, a body of another component) fails like any feature and moves nothing.

drag_occurrenceoccurrence (uid, name or path; a path through a flexible occurrence drags in its parent, Flexible subassemblies), point (in the parent component’s coordinates, moving with the occurrence; its origin when left out), targetas joint_drag; one undo step Drag Pin:1
{"cmd": "drive_joint", "joint": "Joint1", "values": {"rz": "crank_angle", "tz": null}}
{"cmd": "drag_occurrence", "occurrence": "Rocker:1", "point": [130, 0, 0], "target": [140, -10, 0]}
  • drive_joint edits the joint’s position: a parameter (crank_angle) makes the mechanism follow the parameter. With contact sets, drive_joint, drag_occurrence and joint_drag stop where bodies of a set touch (Motion studies and contact sets).
  • drag_occurrence keeps where joint_drag puts the occurrences: their own placements become the dragged ones, every driven motion that moved is driven to its new value (its position becomes the number), and a joint whose free motions moved keeps their new values as its start (mitcad#1745). The joints before the marker then reproduce the dragged placements. An occurrence a move_occurrence or capture_position before the marker places keeps its own placement: the drag is kept when the joints, with their start values, put it where the drag left it, else refused (capture the position instead). A drag after which a joint, as-built joint, rigid group, constraint set or motion link that held would fail, recomputed in timeline order, moves nothing (mitcad#1666): Arm:1 was not moved: where the drag would leave it, AsBuiltJoint1 would no longer hold (AsBuiltJoint1: over-constrained: …). (An as-built joint whose motion origin is on another occurrence is one such: the drag cannot know that its axis moves with that occurrence.)
QueryFieldsResult
jointsjoints: every joint and as-built joint in timeline order: uid, name, type, kind, slide_axis (sliders), component, a and b {occurrence (path name), path (uids)}, motions, limits (per motion min, max, rest as values), position (per driven motion its value), status and error (the feature’s), state (placed, satisfied, or the status: failed, suppressed, rolled_back), solved (it holds at the marker), message (why not), moved (occurrences placed), values (per free motion, at the marker; null when the joint does not hold there), within_limits, beyond_limits, frames {a, b: origin, x_axis, y_axis, z_axis in the joint’s component, at the marker; an as-built joint’s motion frame as each side carries it}; rigid_groups: uid, name, component, occurrences, names, active, status, error; dof: per component with joint features, component, total, overconstrained, redundant and conflicting (joint uids), units (occurrences moving as one, names, grounded, dof, mobile, joints, under inside a flexible occurrence); flexible (Flexible subassemblies)
joint_dofoccurrence (uid, name or path)in its parent component: occurrence, name, component, grounded, group (the occurrences moving with it), dof, mobile, motions (none when grounded, all six without joints, its joint’s with one, null with more), joints (uid, name, kind, other, motions)
joint_dragoccurrence, point, target (as drag_occurrence)placements (the occurrences that would move: occurrence, name, transform rows in the parent component), values (per joint uid of the parent component, its motions’ values), design (each moved path from the root and its 4 x 4 transform in the design), inside a flexible occurrence also flexed and flexible_values; changes nothing
joint_frameoccurrence (a path from component, uids or names; empty: its own geometry), geometry, frame_override, component (the root when left out)the frame the origin gives at the marker, placed by the path into component’s coordinates: origin, x_axis, y_axis, z_axis; component (the one the path ends in) and local (the frame in its coordinates); refused for geometry of another component than the path’s
  • Degrees of freedom are exact: the rank of the joints’ equations where the occurrences are (the joint solver’s analysis; driven values left out). total is what all units can do together (6 per unit that is not grounded less the rank); a unit’s dof is what it can do with the other units held where they are, 0 when grounded. A four-bar linkage has total 1 while each link alone has 0. A unit is mobile when it moves in some motion of all units together (the others free too): each link of the four-bar linkage is; a unit rigidly joined to the component’s own geometry or to a grounded one is not (nor is a grounded one), and a drag of it moves nothing. redundant lists joints whose equations repeat earlier ones (they hold: two hinges on one axis, the closing joint of a planar loop), conflicting those that contradict earlier ones where the occurrences are; overconstrained when either is not empty. Only joints that recomputed count.
  • joint_drag pulls point toward target while every joint in effect at the marker in the occurrence’s parent component holds (driven motions follow like free ones, limits hold), moving the other units as little as possible: as near as the joints let it. A grounded occurrence does not drag (Crank:1 is grounded). The joints BUILD placed its parts with keep their driven values, and a part BUILD placed does not drag (Arm:1 stays where it was placed: move it with Placement), but a carriage on its rail (BUILD: drags and travel limits, mitcad#2088). For a UI’s drag preview: call it per pointer position, then drag_occurrence on release.
  • delete_occurrence deletes the joints, as-built joints and rigid groups that name an occurrence that is gone, with what depends on them; they are in its deleted. Copies of components (paste_new, an inserted copy) take their joints along, naming the copies’ occurrences.
  • Joint features are saved as features (design file round trip); files without them have none.

joint_posesjoint (uid or name), motion (one of its free motions), values (numbers: mm for a slide, radians for a turn), occurrence (optional: a flexible occurrence the joint moves inside, Flexible subassemblies)frames, one per value: placements (the occurrences placed elsewhere in the design than the document places them: path of uids from the root, transform 4 x 4 in the design, as a preview’s placements), values (per joint uid of the joint’s component, its motions’ values; with occurrence, the occurrence’s joints’ values there); changes nothing
