  • Each frame is the joint solver’s alone, as joint_drag solves a drag: the joints in effect at the marker in the joint’s component, with motion driven to the value (held within its limits) and the motions that motion links couple to it following (their own positions let go, as drive_joint lets them go), solved from the frame before (the first from the placements at the marker). Nothing is recomputed: the shapes, and the joints of other components, stay as they are, so a frame costs a solve, not a recompute and new meshes. Animate Joint asks for all its frames at once and moves the bodies it shows.
  • Refused where only a recompute shows the motion, and the application then previews each frame (drive_joint with from, Motion studies and contact sets): while a contact set applies (contact sets apply: only a recompute checks where the bodies touch), and when a joint of another component holds an occurrence inside one that moves. Also refused: a joint that is not in effect at the marker, a motion it does not have, values that are not finite, and values at which the joints do not hold (the joints do not hold with rz at 95.000 deg).

Flexible subassemblies (mitcad#1793)

An occurrence of a component with components in it or joints of its own (joints, as-built joints, constraint sets) can be made flexible: its component’s joints then move in its parent too, for this occurrence alone, and the parts those joints do not place are free in the parent (mitcad#2016, below). Other occurrences of the component stay rigid unless they are flexible as well, and the component’s design does not change. A linked design kept with its components can be flexible too (A whole design linked with its components); an occurrence inside a linked design is flexible only as that design has it. Code: joints.rs (flex_into_parents, flex_unit, kept_flexed, Flexed, Unit), document/flexible.rs; tests core/model-tests/joints/src/flexible_tests.rs, (mitcad#1805) flexible_nested_tests.rs and (mitcad#2016) flexible_free_parts_tests.rs, the UI tests tools/ui-flexible-subassembly-test.sh and tools/ui-flexible-free-parts-test.sh.

CommandFieldsResult
set_occurrence_flexibleoccurrence (uid, name or path), flexible (default true)flexible; one undo step Make Hinge:1 Flexible (… Rigid), none when nothing changes
drive_jointalso occurrence: a flexible occurrence of the joint’s component, or one the joint moves inside through flexible occurrences nested in it (mitcad#1805)the joint driven for that occurrence alone: uid, occurrence, values (its values there); with contact sets, contact and warnings where it stopped (mitcad#1805); one undo step Drive Joint1 in Hinge:1
QueryFieldsResult
joint_posesalso occurrence (mitcad#1805): a flexible occurrence the joint moves insideAnimate Joint’s frames of the joint inside that occurrence, for it alone (Animate Joint’s frames)
{"cmd": "set_occurrence_flexible", "occurrence": "Hinge:1"}
{"cmd": "drive_joint", "joint": "Joint1", "occurrence": "Hinge:1", "values": {"rz": "90 deg"}}
{"cmd": "drag_occurrence", "occurrence": "Hinge:1/Arm:1", "point": [50, 0, 0], "target": [0, 50, 0]}
  • Its own values. A flexible occurrence keeps its own values of its component’s joints (the design file’s occurrence flexible: position and start, per joint uid and motion, mm and radians): a motion driven for it (drive_joint with occurrence, held within the motion’s limits) and where its free motions start (kept by a drag). Without them a joint’s motion is as the component has it (its position, rest value or start). Made rigid again, the occurrence drops them. Refused for an occurrence whose component has neither components in it nor joints of its own (Plain:1 cannot be flexible: Plain has no components in it to move), and drive_joint with an occurrence that is not flexible (Hinge:1 is not flexible: make it Flexible to drive Joint1 in it alone) or a joint of another component (one that does not move inside it).
  • Copies keep them (mitcad#1805). A copy and paste of a flexible occurrence (copy_occurrence) is flexible with the same values. A copy of its component with new feature uids (Paste New, an unlinked insert, Save Component as Design) keeps the flexible occurrences placed in it and the one pasted flexible, their values renamed to the copied joints; the values of joints the copy leaves out (after the timeline marker) are left out.
  • Contact sets stop it (mitcad#1805). With contact sets, drive_joint with occurrence moves the joint from where it is for the occurrence toward the values and stops where bodies of a set touch, as the joint’s own drive and a drag do: the occurrence’s own positions are then where it stopped, and the answer has contact and warnings.
  • In the parent’s solve. When a joint, as-built joint or constraint set of the component recomputes, it is also brought into the solve of each flexible occurrence’s parent: its paths from the parent through the occurrence, the occurrence’s own values in place of the component’s, solved with the flexible occurrence held where it is, so that what is inside it moves. One that does not hold there warns on the joint feature (In Hinge:1, which is flexible, this does not hold: …, the occurrence its place) and stays out of that solve. The component’s motion links come along the same way.
  • Nested flexible occurrences (mitcad#1805). The joints, constraint sets and motion links a flexible occurrence brings into its parent’s solve are brought on in the same way into the parent of each flexible occurrence of that parent, through the chain of flexible occurrences (Frame:1/Hinge:1/Arm:1 moves the Arm inside Hinge:1 inside Frame:1 for Frame:1 alone, when both are flexible), held where they are. A flexible occurrence keeps its own values of these nested joints as of its component’s, by joint uid (drive_joint with it, a drag), so two flexible placements of one component inside it share them. A rigid occurrence on the way ends the chain: what is inside it is where its component places it.
  • Units inside it. In the parent’s solve, an occurrence placed in a flexible occurrence’s component (with those the component’s rigid groups join to it) is a unit of its own when a joint of the component in effect has a side on it, and it is not grounded there; the rest stays with the flexible occurrence. So a joint of the parent whose path goes through the flexible occurrence to such an occurrence (Hinge:1/Arm:1) moves that occurrence inside it, not the whole subassembly, while the component’s joints hold; parent joints, constraint sets and motion links reach into it alike. The parent’s degrees of freedom (joints query, dof) list these units with under, the flexible occurrence (nested, also within: the chain of uids, outermost first); the flexible occurrence’s own unit does not count its component’s joints as its own.
  • Free parts (mitcad#2016). In a flexible occurrence, an occurrence placed in its component that the component’s joints, rigid groups and grounding do not place is free in the parent: a unit of its own there too (with what a rigid group of the component ties to it), which the parent’s joints place alone. So a Gantry with a Carriage and two joiners and no joints of its own, made flexible, takes one rigid joint of the parent from each joiner to a rail carriage: each joiner moves onto its rail carriage, the Carriage stays where the Gantry places it, and a rigid group of the Carriage and a joiner moves the two together. With no joint of the parent on it, a free part stays where the component places it (or where a drag left it). Through the model API (drag_occurrence, joint_drag) such a part drags freely, for the flexible occurrence alone, as an occurrence with no joints in its parent component does (mitcad#2017); the application refuses both drags with a status message, as components move only through joints there (mitcad#150). The parent’s dof lists the free parts (names, under, six motions each while nothing holds them), so loose parts show and can be tied by a rigid group or joints. A joint of the parent that works against an inner rigid group fails naming the group among the joints (… and RigidGroup1 work against each other and cannot all hold), the group’s parts its places; one against an inner joint names both joints. The design file keeps it as the occurrence’s flexible free_parts (true). A flexible occurrence saved before (0.63.0 and earlier) has none: a joint of the parent on a part its component’s joints do not place moves the whole occurrence there, as it did, so such designs open with the same positions; made rigid and flexible again it has free parts. A drag (drag_occurrence) keeps where it leaves a free part as the flexible occurrence’s own placements (path of uids from it through nested flexible occurrences to the part, and its transform in the component it is placed in, linear rows and translation), from which the joints solve as from an occurrence’s own placement; the component’s design and its other occurrences do not change. They follow the parts by uid (a part added, a component renamed, a linked design read again); one whose part is gone is left out without an error, and the design file no longer has it. A move_occurrence of the component that moves a free part moves it from there too, for the flexible occurrence as for the component’s own placement of it (mitcad#2025): a kept placement is where the part is before those Moves, so the part follows a Move as it is edited and goes back to its kept placement when the Move is suppressed or deleted. When the joints of the parent that place a free part go with what they are joined to (delete_occurrence, delete_feature with dependents, build_remove), the part stays where they left it, kept the same way (mitcad#2017, Document::held_free_parts), as an occurrence of the parent keeps its pose then (mitcad#1811, mitcad#1820); undo brings the joints back and drops it. A joint deleted by itself lets the part go back, as it does for an occurrence of the parent: where a drag left it, else where its component places it.
  • Where the occurrences inside it are. Each placement inside a flexible occurrence is kept for that occurrence alone, in its component’s coordinates; the occurrence’s own placement (what the other occurrences show) stays. The instances (instances query, display, exports), path placements (joint_frame, joint origins, contact sets' bodies) and the components query’s transform and world use them; its tree entry of a flexible occurrence has flexible and joint_values (per joint uid, the motions’ values for it).
  • Dragging inside it. joint_drag and drag_occurrence with a path from the root whose last occurrence is inside a flexible occurrence and moved by its component’s joints (Hinge:1/Arm:1) drag in the flexible occurrence’s parent, the points still in the dragged occurrence’s parent’s coordinates; inside nested ones, in the outermost one’s parent. The answer has besides placements flexed (flexible, occurrence, name, transform rows in the flexible occurrence’s component; nested, also within, the chain of flexible occurrences, outermost first) and flexible_values (per flexible occurrence, per joint uid, the values). Every drag answers design too: the occurrences the drag shows elsewhere, each path of uids from the root with its transform (4 x 4 in the design), as a preview’s placements. drag_occurrence keeps a flexible occurrence’s moved values as its own: a driven motion’s as its position, a free one’s as where it starts.
  • The joints query also has flexible: per flexible occurrence its occurrence, name, component, parent and values (per joint uid of its component, at the marker), and dof lists the parents of flexible occurrences.
  • Motion links reach into it. A link side’s occurrence ({"joint": "Joint1", "motion": "rz", "occurrence": "Hinge:1"}; the definition stores the uid) names a flexible occurrence placed in the link’s component and a joint of that occurrence’s component: the link couples that joint as the occurrence moves it (its values for that occurrence), so a crank of the parent can turn an arm inside one Hinge alone. The occurrence must be flexible (Joint1 moves in Hinge:1 only when Hinge:1 is flexible fails the link otherwise). Driving the other side lets go of the occurrence’s own position of the linked motion. A link of the component itself comes into each flexible occurrence’s parent with its joints; one whose side names a flexible occurrence of the component comes along too (mitcad#1805), that side’s joint through both (Frame:1 then Hinge:1), so a crank of the Frame turns the arm in Frame:1’s Hinge for Frame:1 alone. Contact sets reach into it as their occurrence paths do: a body inside a flexible occurrence is checked where it is for that occurrence.
  • Animate Joint inside it (mitcad#1805). joint_poses with occurrence animates a joint of the occurrence’s component (or one moving inside it through nested flexible occurrences) as the occurrence moves it: the joint solver’s frames in the occurrence’s parent, the occurrence held, its own values the start; each frame’s values are the occurrence’s joints’. Refused for an occurrence that is not flexible (Frame:2 is not flexible: make it Flexible to animate Joint1 in it alone) and a joint that does not move inside it, and like the joint’s own frames while contact sets apply.
  • Linked geometry sees it (mitcad#1805). Features that read geometry of other components through a path (a sketch’s plane and projections, a construction plane, axis or point on a face, the bodies a combine, extrusion or split reads) see an occurrence inside flexible ones where they have it at the feature’s point of the timeline, as the design shows it, like any placement there; the evaluation records those placements as read (Read::Flexed), so a change of them recomputes the feature. Only the part of the link’s paths after the part both share counts: a feature of a component inside a flexible occurrence sees that component’s own placements, since its result is the component’s design, which the component’s other occurrences share. The geometry an open sketch offers to pick and project, and Save Component as Design’s frozen references, agree.

Placements kept rigid

(mitcad#1664.) An occurrence’s own placement is always a rotation and a translation, also after many drags:

  • The joint solver’s placements (at each recompute, joint_drag) and the placements drag_occurrence keeps are made rotations and translations first: one whose orthonormality products (Mᵀ·M against the identity) are off by more than rounding (1e-15) is replaced by its nearest rotation (the orthogonal factor of its polar decomposition), the translation kept. (mitcad#1666: each solve that places an occurrence from a frame a little off doubles how far off the result is, so placements kept anywhere up to 1e-9 off crept there drag after drag; a product of two such, as a body is seen from another occurrence, then failed the geometry’s rigid test, and its circular edges became B-splines that joints could not use.) drag_occurrence answers with the placements it kept. A placement with no rotation near it (off by more than 1e-3, a mirror, a scale, not finite) moves nothing: the joints would place Arm:1 by a transform that is not a rotation and a translation; nothing was moved.
  • Every other command that stores occurrence placements does the same for the placements it changes, keeping one off by at most 1e-9 as it is (Arm:1 would be placed by a transform that is not a rotation and a translation refuses it). Commands that take a transform (set_occurrence_transform and the rest) still refuse one that is not a rotation and a translation within 1e-6.
  • Opening a design straightens an occurrence placement that drifted off a rotation (more than 1e-6) to its nearest rotation, the translation kept, with a warning, the placement of Arm:1 was distorted and has been straightened to a rotation and a translation. Drifted means a positive determinant and every singular value (the stretch along each principal axis) between 0.5 and 1.5: older builds compounded the drift over many drags, up to 0.147 off a rotation (determinant 0.853, mitcad#1666). A deliberate scale (2), a mirror, a degenerate transform or a number that is not finite still refuses the file. Saving writes the straightened placement, and never one that opening would refuse.

What each side is on

The joints query says what each side of a joint is built on (mitcad#523), so that the application can highlight it (app/COMMANDS.md, “Joints”, Joint highlight) without reading the definitions:

  • A joint’s a and b, and each constraint row’s a, b (and a2, b2 when given), have besides occurrence and path: geometry, the reference as the definition stores it ({"body", "face"}, "F9", "xy", {"point": [x, y, z]}, {"mount": "F7:mount(end_a)"}, …); on, what it is: face, edge, vertex, body, sketch_curve, sketch_point, origin (an origin plane, axis or the origin), construction (a construction plane, axis or point), joint_origin, fixed (a fixed plane, axis or point: in no geometry) or mount (a derived part’s mount frame, BUILD); frame_override when the side has one, as the definition has it; and component, the component the path ends in (the feature’s own for an empty path; left out when the path leads nowhere).
  • An as_built_joint’s a and b have on occurrence and their component; its motion origin, when it has one, is origin, a side as above.
{"name": "Joint1", "kind": "revolute", "component": "C0",
 "a": {"occurrence": "Pin:1", "path": ["O2"], "component": "C2", "on": "face",
       "geometry": {"body": "F4.b0", "face": "F4:start(r{…})"}},
 "b": {"occurrence": "Plate:1", "path": ["O1"], "component": "C1", "on": "face",
       "geometry": {"body": "F2.b0", "face": "F2:end(r{…})"},
       "frame_override": {"origin": [5, 5, 10]}},
 "frames": {"a": {"origin": [20, 20, 10], …}, "b": {…}}}

Model test: joint_tests.rs, the_joints_query_says_what_each_side_is_on.

The component that holds the picks (mitcad#1856)

A joint, an as-built joint, a rigid group or a constraint set moves, joins or holds only the units of its own component. Made in a sub-assembly, it cannot place that sub-assembly in its parent; made in the parent (add_feature’s or add_joint’s component), the same joint moves the sub-assembly’s occurrence whole, its own joints and rigid groups kept. The joint_holder query finds the lowest component that holds every pick, so that the application can offer it (app/COMMANDS.md, “The component that holds the picks”):

QueryFieldsResult
joint_holderoccurrences (two or more: each pick’s occurrence path from the root, uids or names; "" for the root’s own geometry), component (the one compared with it; the active one when left out)component (the holder’s uid) and name, path (the occurrence path from the root that places it, uids; "" for the root), active and active_name (the component compared), relation, picks (per pick, in order: path from the holder, top the holder’s top-level occurrence it lies in, null for the holder’s own geometry, occurrence its name, name its component’s name, the holder’s for its own geometry), with inside also whole (a component name) and whole_occurrence; error when no joint joins the picks even there
  • relation: same (the compared component is the holder), inside (it is placed under the pick of whole_occurrence: a joint made in it moves only its own parts, one made in the holder moves whole as a whole), above (it holds the holder: every pick lies in one of its top-level occurrences, which a joint made in it moves only whole) or apart.
  • error, in words: every pick on one occurrence (both picks are on Pin:1: a joint joins two different components). A rigid group that joins both sides in the holder is not found here: the joint’s recompute says so (both sides move as one (a rigid group joins …)).
  • Refused: fewer than two picks, a path that does not lead from the root (no occurrence Frame:1/X).

Assembly constraints

Assembly constraints (mitcad#148) hold geometry of one occurrence against geometry of another, each taking away only some motions, and are solved together with the joints. A constraint_set feature holds rows, each one constraint; one row is a constraint, several are solved together. Code: core/model/src/constraints.rs (what each type holds, references), features/constraint_set.rs (the definition), recompute in joints.rs (apply, solve_new), the solver’s partial equations core/solver/src/rigid.rs (README); tests constraint_tests.rs, core/solver/tests/rigid_constraints.rs, tools/cli/tests/constraints.json, tools/ui-constraint-test.sh.

{"type": "constraint_set", "rows": [
  {"type": "insert", "offset": -10,
   "a": {"occurrence": "O2", "geometry": {"body": "F4.b0", "edge": "E{F4:bottom|F4:side0}"}},
   "b": {"occurrence": "O1", "geometry": {"body": "F2.b0", "edge": "E{F2:end(r{…})|F3:side0}"}}},
  {"type": "align", "limits": {"min": 0, "max": "10 mm", "rest": 2},
   "a": {"occurrence": "O3", "geometry": {"body": "F6.b0", "face": "F6:start(r{…})"}},
   "b": {"occurrence": "O1", "geometry": {"body": "F2.b0", "face": "F2:end(r{…})"}}}]}
  • constraint_set (named Constraint<n>): rows, one or more. A row has type, a and b (references as joint origins: an occurrence path from the feature’s component and geometry of the component it ends in, a frame_override allowed), and per type offset (a length), angle, flip, limits (min, max, rest), lock_rotation, and for a center a2 and b2 (on a’s and b’s occurrence). a and b must be on different occurrences, at most one the component’s own geometry. Fields a type does not take are refused (row 1 (align): lock_rotation is for insert rows).
  • References. Each resolves to a frame as a joint origin does, and a kind: a point (a vertex, sketch or construction point, a sphere’s centre for an align), a plane (a planar face, a plane; z its outward normal), an axis (a straight edge, an axis, a cone or torus), a circle (a circular edge, a sketch circle or arc; z the outward normal of a planar face the edge bounds, else the axis), a cylinder (its axis and radius) or a sphere (centre and radius).
TypeReferencesHolds
alignplane (or circle) and planea’s plane offset above b’s along b’s normal, normals facing; flip: the same way
aligntwo pointscoincident; at a distance with an offset
aligntwo axes, cylinders or circlesconcentric (axes along each other, either way); offset apart
aligna point and a plane, a point and an axis, an axis and a planethe point on the plane or the axis (offset off it), the axis in the plane (offset above it)
angleplanes or axesthe angle between the normals or axes, 0 to 180°; 0 and 180° are parallel; flip measures from a’s reversed normal
centera (and a2); b, or b and b2a’s point (the middle of a’s and a2’s) on the plane midway between b and b2 (parallel planar faces); with b alone on b’s normal through its middle (a cylinder: on its axis)
tangentplanes, cylinders, spherestouching from outside: a plane on a plane facing, a cylinder lying on a plane, cylinders side by side (axes the sum of the radii apart), spheres; flip: inside (the other side of the plane, the difference of the radii)
insertcircle, circlethe centres together, a’s plane offset along b’s normal, the planes facing (a pin’s bottom rim into a hole’s top rim); flip: the same way
insert_axiscircle, a cylinder (a hole) or circlea’s centre on b’s axis, the axes along each other, the depth free
  • Values. An align’s offset and an angle’s angle are values (parameters and expressions; rows.0.offset, rows.0.angle). With limits (min or max given; an angle row’s are angles, rows.0.limits.min_angle) the value is free between them, held at rest when given, instead of fixed (offset and angle are then refused). Angles are between 0 and 180°; min ≤ rest ≤ max.
  • Lock rotation. An insert (either) with lock_rotation also holds the turn about the axis: a’s x axis at angle about b’s z axis from b’s x axis. The application records the turn where the picks are (the constraint_row query’s twist); without angle it is 0.
  • Recompute. At its point of the timeline the rows are solved with the joints and constraints in effect before it in the same component that share moving units with them, exactly as a joint is (What recompute does): constraints place their free side first by the smallest motion that makes each row hold, join nothing, and leave the rest to the iteration; a row whose sides cannot move only holds or fails (row 1 (align): neither side can move (Pin:1 is grounded, and Plate:1 is grounded) and the constraint does not hold, with the occurrences’ places). Contradictions name rows: over-constrained: Joint1 and Constraint2 row 1 (align) cannot all hold, a value at its rest (at its offset). Constraint rows count in the degrees of freedom, redundant and conflicting (by the set’s uid; an align of faces with an axis insert repeats the axes’ direction: redundant, it holds) and hold while dragging (joint_drag, drag_occurrence: a value between limits moves with the drag and goes back to its rest value at the next recompute).
  • Like joints, sets are never written to the result store, are deleted with an occurrence they name (delete_occurrence), follow copies of components and are saved as features.
