Part Box, Cylinder, Sphere, Torus, Cone, Prism, Wedge, Ellipsoidthe primitives as above, new bodies
Part Extrusion of a sketchextrude new body: LengthFwd (else, when LengthRev is zero too, the direction’s length), LengthRev → two_sides (alone: one side against the direction), Symmetric, Reversed, TaperAngle(Rev); along the normal or a custom direction along it; a custom direction or an edge’s (DirMode Custom, Edge: Dir) off the normal → extrude with that direction (mitcad#541: the lengths along it, the tapers too); into faces (Solid off, mitcad#539) → a surface extrude (surface, curves: the sketch’s curves that are not construction), off the normal along the direction, tapered a surface extrude of the regionsthe direction, the taper’s sign
Part Extrusion of another object’s faces (mitcad#539, mitcad#541)per face of the base’s bodies (all of them; where another object uses the base too, the copy of its first body and its others) an extrude new body with profile_face, the lengths and TaperAngle(Rev) as above, along the face’s normal, or off it along Dir with direction (a curved face only so, untapered; Solid on or off: a solid, as FreeCAD makes it), then a base feature without bodies that removes the faces’ bodiesthe direction, the taper’s sign
Part Extrusion of an object’s edges (mitcad#541)an object without faces that only Part extrusions use (a Part Circle, RegularPolygon, Polygon or Line, a Draft wire; any type the import has no translation of) is included; each extrusion makes a construction_plane (fixed: the object’s placement where its edges lie in it, else the plane through its straight edge and Dir) and a sketch of the edges as fixed geometry on it, extruded as a sketch is (Solid on: its material regions, any number of loops, mitcad#547; off: a surface extrusion of its curves); edges in no one plane (Solid off, mitcad#547) → per plane they lie in a fixed plane, a sketch and a surface extrude of its curves along Dir (direction); a helix (a Part Helix from its Pitch, Height, Radius, LocalCoord, or one helix edge; Solid off, mitcad#547) → a fixed plane, a sketch of a line from the helix’s start along Dir and a surface sweep of it along a fixed helix path, parallel; a conical Part Helix, a helix among other edges, a spline in no plane (Solid off, mitcad#548) → the walls of the planar edges as above and per curve in no plane such a sweep along its own fixed helix or fixed_curves path (the stored curve; a conical Part Helix its stored curves); partial (the object’s own sizes are not carried over); what FreeCAD fails itself (a curved face, a helix or non-planar edges along the base’s normal, tapered, or with Solid on) falls back with that reasonas for a sketch
Part Face of sketches (mitcad#539)patch of each sketch’s regions inside an even number of wires (FaceMakerClass Bullseye, Cheese, Extrusion; Simple, mitcad#547, where no wire lies in another; of nested wires, mitcad#548, a face filling each wire: a region without holes patched, one with holes patched, its outer opening patched (boundary) and the region’s patch removed)
Part Revolution of a sketchrevolve new body about a fixed axis (Base, Axis); 360° → full, Symmetricthe angle’s sign
Part Sweep of sketches along a sketch (mitcad#543)new body: one section → sweep along the spine’s edges, several → loft with the spine as its centerline; Frenet → frame frenet; Solid off → surfaceFrenet also at right angles to the spine
Part Sweep along or of other objects (mitcad#547)a cylindrical Part Helix spine → a fixed helix path (Pitch, Height, Radius, LocalCoord, the placement); edges of an object with a body → the body’s edges; edges of an object without one → one straight edge a fixed line, else a construction_plane (fixed) and a sketch of the edges as fixed geometry, the path its curves; a section of an object’s closed planar edges → such a sketch’s region, of one vertex → a fixed point section; the objects of edges or a vertex only Part extrusions and sweeps use are included; partialas for sketches
Part Sweep, the remaining inputs (mitcad#548)a conical Part Helix spine (Angle) → its stored curves as a fixed_curves path; edges in no plane of an object without a body → a fixed_curves path; one section of an open planar wire → a surface sweep of its fixed sketch’s curves, of a wire in no plane → a surface sweep of fixed_curves (FreeCAD makes no caps of either); spines and sections of PartDesign features’ results → their Body’s body’s edges and faces (the Body replayed for them); the spine and sections make no copy of a body and use none up; several sections of open wires or wires in no plane, and a section of several wires, fall back with that reasonas for sketches
Pad, Pocket, Revolution, Groove of several faces (AllowMultiFace, mitcad#543)one extrude or revolve per face (profile_face), the first with the feature’s operation, the others joined to it (named " (face 2)", …), as many as there are (mitcad#547)as for one face
Part Cut, Fuse, MultiFuse, Common, MultiCommoncombine (the first operand the target)
Part Fillet, Chamferfillet / chamfer of the edge list: a fillet’s edges of one radius a constant set, each edge of two radii a variable set of its own from the first radius at the vertex where FreeCAD’s edge starts (start_vertex) to the second (mitcad#539); unequal chamfer sizes two_distancesflip both ways; a fillet edge without a start vertex here (closed) its radii either way
Part Mirroringmirror of the source’s body (plane Base, Normal or 1.0’s MirrorPlane), then a base feature without bodies that removes the source’s body
others (binders, Draft objects, plain shapes, …)a base feature of the stored shape (scripted objects and plain shapes: fallback_group no_counterpart)
  • Profiles of Pad, Pocket, Revolution and Groove that are not a whole sketch (mitcad#539): a planar face of a body (Profile = (object, Face<n>); FreeCAD takes the first element unless AllowMultiFace) → the extrude or revolve of that face (profile_face), along its outward normal with the extents of a sketch’s (mitcad#2033: Length, TwoLengths, Midplane, ThroughAll, UpToFirst, UpToLast, UpToFace, UpToShape and their Offset; TaperAngle(2) → taper, mitcad#541; a custom direction off the normal, mitcad#547, → the face’s extrude with that direction, the lengths along it as for a sketch’s) or by angles; chosen edges of a sketch (Profile = (sketch, Edge<n>, …) with 1.0’s AllowMultiFace) → the sketch’s regions inside the areas those edges bound (both readings as for a whole sketch); without AllowMultiFace FreeCAD takes the whole sketch whatever edges the link names, and so does the import. Several faces, and faces of lofts and pipes, fall back.
  • An operand of the Part workbench that a later object uses too is copied (move with copy) for each earlier use.
  • The features of one FreeCAD object are named after its label, those that help the main one with a suffix (hidden when they are construction planes or sketches): <label> (plane) and <label> (section) of a cone, a prism or a part of a turn, <label> (bottom plane), (bottom), (top plane), (top) of a wedge, <label> (sphere), (scale), (placement) of an ellipsoid (a part of one also (plane) and (section)), <label> (mirror 1), (mirror 2), (axis) of a MultiTransform’s mirrors, <label> (transformation 1), (transformation 2), … of its chain of patterns and mirrors, <label> (thread) of a hole, <label> (source removed) of a mirroring, <label> plane of a sketch on an offset or turned construction plane.

Parameters and expressions (freecad/params.rs), before the timeline:

  • User parameters: spreadsheet cells with an alias (named after it), cells an expression names by address (<sheet>_B3), VarSets’ numeric properties (1.0), the history’s feature properties that expressions refer to (<label>_<property>: Pad_Length), and sketches’ named constraints. A name MitCad cannot take, or one several share, gets its owner’s label in front. Each has FreeCAD’s expression translated, else FreeCAD’s value (a cell without a value that does not translate is skipped).
  • Bound expressions become the expressions of the values the import carries over (pads’ and pockets’ lengths, offsets and tapers, revolutions’ angles, fillets’, chamfers’ and holes’ sizes, patterns' distances, angles and counts, draft angles, thicknesses, primitives' sizes, Part extrusions’ lengths and tapers, sketches’ dimensions), using the parameter made of the property where there is one (the feature, or the sketch for a named constraint, adopts it). Attachment offsets of sketches and datum planes: bound along the normal → a construction plane offset from the support; a bound turn about the support’s x or y axis → an angle construction plane; turned a quarter (by a value) so that a bound side offset moves it along its normal → the parallel origin plane offset by that expression. A cone’s and a partial cylinder’s radii and height are length dimensions of their section sketches. Side offsets that only move a sketch or plane within itself, and turns about other axes or with shifts, keep FreeCAD’s values.
  • Translation: references (Spreadsheet.Width, <<Sheet>>.B3, .Constraints.width, Sketch.Constraints.width, VarSet.Depth, Pad.Length, .Height.Value as a plain number), units (° as deg, gon as grad, thou as mil, " and ' as in and ft, dm, nm, ′, ″ by their factors), pi, e as PI, E, c ? a : b as if(c; a; b), log, log10 as ln, log, mod(a; b) as a % b, hypot, cath, cbrt, trunc, sum and average (over ranges too) written out, min and max of several; FreeCAD’s signs bind tighter than ^ and its ^ is left-associative (-2^2 = (-2)^2). A unitless result where FreeCAD has a length or an angle gets FreeCAD’s unit (B3 * 1 mm).
  • Every translated expression is compared with FreeCAD’s stored value (1e-9 relative; an integer property’s expression is rounded as FreeCAD rounds it, round(Count / 2), when that gives FreeCAD’s value); one that differs (mismatched) or does not translate keeps FreeCAD’s value, with the reason in the report.

The result: file, design (the document’s label), items (objects), bodies, counts (objects per outcome: body, component, occurrence, parametric, partial, fallback, included, skipped) and report:

  • program_version, schema_version, units, objects_by_type;
  • items: per object index, name, label, type, outcome, note, bodies, component, stale when its stored shape may be out of date;
  • bodies: each with its object, file when from another document, uid, name, component, kind, volume, area, center in its component, color, visible;
  • placed: where each body, part, link and array element of the document shows its geometry: path, bodies, world volume, area and center;
  • components, occurrences, files and missing_files (linked documents), stale, warnings;
  • sketches: per sketch object, label, outcome, feature, component, plane, FreeCAD’s geometry and constraints counts, MitCad’s entities, mitcad_constraints, dimensions, error of the solved points, dropped, notes, dimension_sources, expressions, shape against the stored shape, and the profile curves’ edges, length and world center;
  • features: the history in timeline order, per object object, label, type, body (its PartDesign Body), outcome, features (the MitCad features made), mitcad (their type), check against the stored shape (volume, area, center, solids and FreeCAD’s, distance, pass), notes (which reading was kept, or why it fell back) and a fallback’s fallback_group (mitcad#539): missing (a translation MitCad does not have yet: the reason says “not translated”), no_counterpart (a scripted object, a plain shape, or one FreeCAD failed itself), other (translated, but it did not build or give FreeCAD’s shape); the readable report counts them (fallbacks by group: …);
  • parameters: per parameter name, source, object and its cell, property or constraint, describe, FreeCAD’s expression freecad, MitCad’s expression, value, freecad_value, outcome (parameter, value, mismatched, skipped) and note;
  • expressions: every expression FreeCAD binds to a property: object, path, expression, mitcad, outcome (parameter, expression, value, mismatched, unused) and note;
  • with reference, reference: checked, differences, pass (volumes of solids and areas within 1e-9 relative, world centres of mass within 1e-6 mm, places with bodies of the history (placed[].replayed) within the replay’s 1e-6; sketches’ edge counts, lengths and centres within 1e-6 relative; parameters’ values against FreeCAD’s values of the cells, properties and constraints within 1e-9 relative). A place of stored shapes also has placed[].fixed: their volume, area and center with the kernel’s plain fixed-point integration, as FreeCAD measures; where FreeCAD’s measures are those, a difference is listed as not compared (MitCad integrates faces bounded by B-splines of many spans more exactly, mitcad#139).

Tests: core/freecad/tests/parse.rs, core/freecad/tests/sketch_corpus.rs, core/import-fcstd/src/tests.rs (mock kernel), cli.import_fcstd (tools/cli/fcstd-test.cmake), freecad.corpus (MITCAD_FCSTD_CORPUS; core/import-fcstd/docs/freecad.md) and tools/ui-import-test.sh.

.ipt import

{"cmd": "import_ipt", "path": "part.ipt", …} (C++ Document::command, or Document::import_ipt(path, json) for the report alone) imports an .ipt part file (mitcad#60; core/ffi/src/ipt_import.rs, the reader is core/ipt):

  • With its history (the default when the file’s definitions segment has features or parameters; stages 2 and 3): the part’s parameters with their expressions, its sketches, work planes and features, decoded into the import’s dump IR (mitcad_ipt::design) and replayed by the same importer as the .f3d import (.f3d import with the timeline): each feature is checked against the state of the ASM history stored in the B-rep record that its operation made, and comes in as the bodies of that state where it cannot be replayed (fallback); the final bodies are compared with the stored ones. The report adds history (true), parameters (the definitions segment’s parameter records: records, model, user, outside (not the part’s: annotations, reference dimensions, features' own tables), internal (RDxVar<n>), unread), expressions (translated, agree: evaluated to the stored value, differ, not_translated, computed (parameters whose value the model computes, not their expression: the stored value comes in), each name: why), features (items with a history state), features_with_states (of them, those whose state the history has), counts (items per outcome), design (the importer’s report: items, parameters, history, bodies, warnings, as for import_f3d), design_text (its text), replayed (false when the hang watchdog gave up on the replay outside its items, so that the stored bodies came in without the timeline; mitcad#507) and seconds {read, import}; imported lists the document’s bodies after the replay (feature is the feature that made the body, feature_name its name for a person, mitcad#1741). Sheet-metal faces, flanges on one edge and cuts through the sheet replay as sheet_rules (named Sheet rules <style>, before the first face), sheet_face, sheet_flange and sheet_cut (mitcad#211; the .f3d import’s base and edge flanges likewise, its open and flat hems as sheet_flanges of 180 degrees, mitcad#1364, its rolled hems as flanges past 180 degrees with no wall and its teardrop, rope and double hems as flanges with that hem form, mitcad#1378; core/import/docs/f3d-sheet-metal.md, Sheet metal).
  • Bodies only (bodies_only, and files without definitions; stage 1): one base feature per body (solids and sheet bodies), built from the file’s B-rep record with OCCT.

Either way the triangles of the part’s mesh features come in as mesh bodies (source PmGraphicsSegment#<record>, mesh true, closed, triangles; after the replay with the history), and a part without bodies and meshes opens empty with a warning that says why: its file holds none, or its result lists bodies that neither its B-rep records nor its mesh features hold (mitcad#1913; bodies that cannot be built are still an error).

Either way the document’s length unit becomes the part’s when the document has no features yet (else a warning says so), and the bodies get the part’s material when MitCad’s library has one of that name or id (case does not matter). One undo step (Import part.ipt). A job does not cancel it.

FieldMeaning
textimport_ipt returns a readable report
report_pathalso write the JSON report to this file
referencea STEP file of the same part: each of its solids is matched with the imported solid of the closest volume and their volumes and areas compared
max_relativethe largest relative difference of a volume or area that passes (default 1e-6)
deviationwith reference, also the sampled surface deviation (as compare_step)
bodies_onlythe bodies only, as base features (stage 1)
no_verify, no_fallback, no_compareas for import_f3d: do not check the replay against the history; leave out features that cannot be replayed; compare the final bodies by volume only
time_limitseconds after which the remaining features take the file’s bodies
hang_limitseconds without progress after which a geometry kernel call counts as hung (an empty document only): as for import_f3d, the replay runs again on its own thread with the item it hung on taking the file’s bodies, a warning saying so
dump_pathalso write the decoded design (the dump IR, core/import/SCHEMA.md) to this file
design_pathreplay this dump (as dump_path writes it) instead of the decoded design

The command’s result: file, design (the part number), bodies (the number imported) and report: format (ipt), part_number, material, mitcad_material (the material set, or null), release (the release that saved the file, as it says), units (the document’s new length unit, or null) and unit_code; records (each B-rep record: source, asm_version, bodies, history_states (the states of the ASM history the record carries), truncated); imported (each body: source <segment>#<record>/<body>, solid, valid (OCCT’s checker), volume, raw_volume (before the solids were oriented), area, faces, issues, messages (the builder’s, with what the checker finds wrong), feature (its uid), feature_name (its name, the one the import report dialog shows, mitcad#1741), bodies with uid, name, kind); skipped (bodies not built: source, error); geometry (the import of the stored bodies only: bodies, or why there are none: none in the file, or listed bodies not found, mitcad#1913); warnings; seconds {read, build}; and with reference, reference: file, step_solids, solids (pairs: step_body, step_volume, step_area, body, name, volume, area, volume_difference, area_difference), unmatched_step, unmatched_bodies, max_difference, max_relative, valid, with deviation max_deviation, and pass (every STEP solid and every imported solid matched, all within max_relative, every imported solid valid).

Tests: core/ipt (core.ipt, no OCCT), the design replayed on the mock kernel (core.model.imports, core/model-tests/imports/src/ipt_design_tests.rs), core.exchange (core/tests/test_exchange.cpp), cli.import_ipt*, cli.ipt_design_file, ipt.corpus (MITCAD_IPT_CORPUS, core/import/docs/ipt.md) and tools/ui-import-test.sh.

.iam import

{"cmd": "import_iam", "path": "assembly.iam", …} (also import_ipt with an .iam file; C++ Document::command, or Document::import_iam(path, json) for the report alone) imports an .iam assembly (mitcad#60, stage 4; core/ffi/src/iam_import.rs, the reader is core/ipt):

  • Every distinct part file is imported once with the .ipt import, in a document of its own: its stored bodies, which become one base feature of a component of this document (the shapes shared, not copied), or with history its parameters and features replayed, that design copied into a component (Document::add_component_copy); each of its occurrences is an occurrence of that component, named after the file and the instance number (part:2) or the label the file stores.

  • A sub-assembly is a component whose occurrences are placed in it the same way; each sub-assembly file comes in once, however often it is placed.

  • Placements are the file’s (cm become mm); hidden occurrences are hidden, grounded ones grounded, suppressed ones left out (counted).

  • A placement that mirrors or scales (mitcad#1903) comes in as a copy, as other imports copy the blocks they insert so: a component of its own at its parent’s origin holds the part’s bodies mapped by the placement, where the file has them, with the warning <occurrence>: the placement mirrors or scales it; a copy is placed where the file has it; a sub-assembly placed so is a component whose occurrences are copied the same way. Copies are counted (copied) among the placed occurrences; their checks compare the file’s own placement.

  • Referenced files are found as saved, else relative to the assembly as it was when saved (the saved paths of both), else by the saved path’s tail under the assembly’s folder and the folders above it, else by name in the assembly’s folder tree and search folders. A part found there is checked to be the referenced document: its own file list names the version id the occurrence stores (identity). A file not found is an empty component with the occurrences placed, and the report names it.

  • Checks against the file: each occurrence’s placement in the document against the transform the file displays it with (where the file keeps one), and each placed part’s bodies (their bounding box in the component) against the range box the file stores for the document: they must lie within it, to 1 % of its diagonal (at least 0.05 mm); the stored box is not tight (curved faces make it larger), so how much larger it is (box_slack) is information only. The stored centre of the placed range box is compared too, for information only: the file does not always keep it up to date.

  • With history (mitcad#507): a part whose replay fails (the .ipt import’s error, also a replay the hang watchdog gave up on in every try) comes in as its stored bodies instead, as without history (not with no_fallback, where it fails); a part without a design history (no features or parameters) and one whose replay came in without its timeline (replayed false) come in as their stored bodies too. An item the watchdog gave up on takes the file’s bodies within the part’s replay, as in the .ipt import (hangs). Each part’s outcome is in its file’s part.

  • Progress: every referenced file is resolved before the first part is imported, so that the parts are counted. With MITCAD_IMPORT_TRACE set each part file is traced on standard error, import: [<s>] part <n> of <m>: <file> when its import starts and import: [<s>] part <n> of <m>: <file>: replayed in <s> s (or bodies) when it is done; <m> counts the part files found. A part’s replay traces its items as the .ipt import does, between those lines.

The document’s length unit becomes the assembly’s when the document has no features yet. One undo step (Import assembly.iam); a job does not cancel it.

FieldMeaning
textimport_iam returns a readable report
report_pathalso write the JSON report to this file
searchmore folders searched for referenced files by name (with their subfolders)
historyeach part with its design replayed (as import_ipt without bodies_only), not only its stored bodies: much longer and much more memory
no_verify, no_fallback, no_compare, time_limit, hang_limitwith history, each part’s import, as for import_ipt

The command’s result: file, occurrences (placed) and report: format (iam), release, units, unit_code; occurrences (counts: placed, suppressed, hidden, of_missing_files, not_placed, without_file, without_placement, copied, not_rigid: a placement that is not finite or flattens space, placed at the origin); parts (part files: files, imported, missing, failed, identity_confirmed, identity_differs, replayed, as_bodies; without_geometry: parts whose files hold no bodies, without_geometry_reported: of them those an assembly’s translation report says something of, bodies_not_found: parts whose result lists bodies not found, mitcad#1913); history (the option); assemblies (sub-assembly files); resolution (files per way they were found); files (each: saved, path, found, kind, status, identity, occurrences, component, translation (what the translation report of an assembly converted from another format says of a part without geometry, mitcad#1913), and for parts part: the part import’s bodies, solids, valid, not_built, history (the part’s design was read), outcome (replayed: its design replayed and copied into the component; bodies: its stored bodies), reason (why bodies: the stored bodies chosen without history, the part has no design history, the replay failed: <error>, the replay hung: <notes>; null when replayed), items (the replay’s timeline items), verified (of them, those checked against the part’s history), parameters (made), counts (items per outcome), features, hangs (the watchdog’s notes), warnings (how many), units, material, geometry (as import_ipt’s), seconds); display, boxes, centers (each compared, agree, worst in mm, failures); pass (every display and range box check agrees); occurrence_list (each placed or suppressed occurrence with its path name, file index, occurrence uid, grounded, hidden, copied, checks); warnings; seconds.

Tests: core/ipt (core.ipt: the reader on assemblies made by mitcad_ipt::testassembly), core.model (add_component_copy), cli.iam_files, cli.import_iam, cli.info_iam, cli.import_ipt_iam (a test project of those assemblies: a sub-assembly, parts found relative to the assembly and by name, a missing one; hidden, grounded and suppressed occurrences), cli.import_iam_history_parts and cli.import_iam_history_fallback (with history: the parts’ outcomes and progress lines; MITCAD_TEST_IAM_REPLAY_FAIL=<file name> makes that part’s replay fail, for tests), cli.import_iam_mirrored and cli.info_iam_mirrored (placements that mirror or scale a part and a sub-assembly, copied where the file has them), cli.import_iam_converted and cli.import_ipt_listed (an assembly converted from a building model: parts without geometry, one its translation report says so of, and a part whose result lists a body its B-rep record lacks, mitcad#1913), and iam.corpus (tools/cli/iam-corpus.cmake, every .iam under MITCAD_IPT_CORPUS).

IFC import

{"cmd": "import_ifc", "path": "building.ifc", …} (C++ Document::command, or Document::import_ifc(path, json) for the report alone) imports an IFC building model (mitcad#273): IFC2X3, IFC4 or IFC4X3, .ifc text or an .ifczip archive. The reader is core/ifc; the import core/import-ifc/ (generic over the kernel, tested on the mock kernel) and core/ffi/src/ifc_import.rs.

  • Structure. Each site, building, storey and facility (IFC4X3’s bridges, roads, railways and their parts) is a component in its parent’s, named after it and placed where the file places it; a storey’s elevation is a fixed construction plane in its component (<storey> level), each grid axis a fixed construction axis in its grid’s component (<grid> <tag>). Spaces, annotations, ports, the structural analysis model and virtual elements are not imported.
  • Elements. Each element’s Body representation (else Facetation, else another 3D one, else Box) comes into the component of the spatial element it is in (its container, its assembly’s, its opening’s element’s), in one command of its own (Document::add_features_with):
    • swept solids and CSG as features: a sketch of the profile (in a frame of its own; parameterised profiles with their fillet radii as arcs) and an extrusion, a sweep along a fixed line for a slanted one (orientation: parallel), a revolve, ruled lofts for a tapered extrusion, a sketch of the directrix and a sweep for a profile swept along a planar curve, a pipe for a swept disk along a planar curve; blocks and cylinders are extruded rectangles and circles, cones and spheres revolutions;
    • booleans: the second operand cuts, joins or intersects the first’s bodies as its feature’s operation, or is built on its own and combined (combine); a half space is a rectangle on its plane extruded through all on the material’s side (cut), a polygonally bounded one its polygon extruded from the plane on;
    • breps (faceted breps and surface models, advanced breps with their B-spline and elementary surfaces) as base features of the bodies the kernel builds from their faces (Kernel::boundary_body), solids where the shells close; face sets (triangulated and polygonal) as mesh bodies (Kernel::triangle_body); swept disks along a curve that is not planar as the kernel’s pipe, a base feature;
    • its openings (IfcRelVoidsElement) are cut from its solid bodies with their own shapes (as tools of the same kinds); mesh bodies are not cut.
  • Types. A representation map that an element uses with a rigid transform, when the element has no openings, is one component (named after its type), built once; each such use is an occurrence of it. Other uses copy the map’s items into the element, moved by the transform: a scale or a mirror is applied to the items themselves (a profile’s curves under a non-uniform scale become ellipses or rational B-splines; revolutions and curved faces of breps take uniform ones only).
  • Names and appearances. An element’s bodies are named <name> <GlobalId> (then (2), …); a surface style’s colour (the item’s, else the element’s material’s) is a document appearance, made once per colour and transparency.
  • Units. Lengths become millimetres and angles radians; an empty document takes the file’s length unit (mm, cm, m, ft, in).
  • The report has a line for every product of the file: parametric (every item as features), stored (breps), mesh, mixed, occurrence, partial (some items did not build), component, axes, cut (an opening), not_imported (with why) or failed. Each element’s bodies’ volume (closed meshes’ measured from their triangles) is compared with the file’s element quantities (NetVolume where openings were cut, else GrossVolume; within 1e-3 relative they agree). What did not build stays on the timeline as an import note on the element’s first feature, or a suppressed placeholder when nothing of it was built (The import’s outcomes on the timeline).
  • Memory. The import process’s memory guard (mitcad#80) stops the import before the next element when the process is low on memory; the remaining elements are reported as not imported (low_memory).

One undo step (Import building.ifc); a job does not cancel it.

FieldMeaning
textimport_ifc returns a readable report
report_pathalso write the JSON report to this file
openingscut the elements’ openings (default true)
occurrencesrigid uses of a type’s shape as occurrences of one component (default true; false copies the items into each element)
memory_limitthe most memory (MiB) the import may use before it stops; the process’s limits otherwise

The command’s result: file, products, bodies and report: format (ifc), file, schema (IFC2X3, IFC4, IFC4X3), schema_name, view_definition, originating_system, project, length_unit, angle_unit, units (the document’s units when set), products (each: id, global_id, kind, class, name, outcome, component, bodies, occurrences, features, parametric and stored (item kinds), volume, quantity, quantity_difference, notes), outcomes (products per outcome), maps (each: map, name, component, occurrences, bodies, volume, notes), components, storey_planes, grid_axes, appearances, features, bodies, quantities (compared, agree, worst, differ), total_volume (mm³, each map’s bodies counted once per occurrence), warnings, low_memory, seconds, read_seconds, instances, left_out_instances, text_report.

Tests: core.ifc (the reader), core.import (ifc::: the test building on the mock kernel, every product’s outcome), core.model (add_features_with), cli.ifc_file, cli.import_ifc, cli.info_ifc (the test building with OCCT: volumes, the opening cut, the window type’s occurrences), and ifc.corpus (tools/cli/ifc-corpus.cmake, every .ifc of MITCAD_IFC_CORPUS; faceted twins compared by volume).

.rvt import

{"cmd": "import_rvt", "path": "project.rvt", …} (C++ Document::command, or Document::import_rvt(path, json) for the report alone) imports an .rvt project’s building elements (mitcad#274, mitcad#275, mitcad#333; core/ffi/src/rvt_import.rs and mitcad_import_rvt, the reader is core/rvt). .rte templates likewise; an .rfa family (or .rft template) opens with its metadata and report only (its forms are a later ticket).

  • One component per level (named as the level, lowest first; a component Elements for elements of a file without levels), each with a construction plane <level> level at the level’s elevation. The grids are construction axes of the root component (Grid <name>); an arc grid is a sketch of its arc.

  • Walls, floors (and pads), roofs, columns, beams and monolithic stair runs are rebuilt from their parameters as features of their level’s component, one command per element (mitcad_import_rvt::plan): a sketch and an extrusion (a wall’s footprint with its ends where its joins put them; a floor’s boundary loops down from its top; a roof’s footprint or extrusion profile under its slopes’ planes; a column’s or beam’s section, rectangular, round, I, L, U or hollow, along its axis; a run’s steps down to its support), with the cuts of the inserts it hosts (doors and windows: their type’s cut loops) and of the elements whose geometry cuts it. Their bodies are named Family:Type:Id and take the appearance of their material (a layered type’s exterior layer’s, a family type’s first).

  • Attached walls (mitcad#348): a wall whose top (or base) is attached to a roof, floor, ceiling or reference plane follows that element’s lower (or upper) surface, below or above its own top (or base): its prism runs from its base to above the surface, and the half spaces above the surface’s planes are cut away (a roof’s slopes: above each slope’s lower plane; a base below its one plane), its line noting its top follows roof 44's lower surface (2 slopes). The cut is fixed: the features do not follow the roof when it is changed later. An attachment the import cannot apply (a face roof’s surface, several elements of different heights, a sloped roof whose footprint does not cover the wall, a base on several slopes) leaves the wall at its own height and its line names it (its top's attachment to … is not applied: …). An attached wall checked against its stored box is checked both ways there in height (its top must reach the box’s, not only lie within it).

  • Openings (mitcad#345): every insert that opens a wall (the inserts whose cut the wall takes, the doors and windows it hosts, the other elements it hosts whose types have cut loops or void geometry) cuts it by its type’s cut loops, else by its type’s void geometry (its family’s void forms as faceted bodies at the instance’s transform), else by the IFC export’s opening its GlobalId fills when the export is the reference (reference_ifc, or found next to the project; mitcad_import_rvt::reference_openings); a rectangular wall opening cuts its rectangle through the wall. An opening without a tool is named on the wall’s line (insert 47 is not cut: …); a wall that comes in as the geometry the file keeps or the reference’s body holds its openings, as a saved mesh or a box it does not. The report counts them (and its text summary: walls' openings: N cut, M missing (…)): openings_cut, openings_missing (by reason) and openings_missing_lines (insert 47 in wall 31: …), and the insert’s own line says it (its opening in wall 31 is not cut: …). Elements a wall hosts that cut nothing (trims) are counted on its line.

  • Each element built is checked: against the IFC export given as reference_ifc, or found next to the project as <name>.ifc (unless no_reference_ifc), by its GlobalId (which the import derives from the element’s creation episode): its volume within 1 % and its box within 5 mm of the export’s solid; else against its stored box (its body within 5 mm of it). An element whose features fail or disagree is undone and comes in as below, the reason on its report line.

  • Every other element (family instances: doors, windows, furniture, curtain panels and mullions, …; curtain walls, railings, stairs of parts, wall sweeps, slab edges, sections of no known kind, …) is a body of its level’s base feature <level> elements, from the first of these that gives one (mitcad#333):

    1. a mesh of the geometry the file keeps of it (the B-reps of its partition’s geometry chain: its own bodies and the types it places at their transforms, core/rvt), when it agrees with the reference’s solid of its GlobalId (its box within 5 mm, a closed mesh’s volume within 1 %) or else lies within its stored box (but for a tenth of the box’s largest extent);
    2. the reference’s bodies of its GlobalId (the IFC export’s);
    3. the triangle mesh its record saves;
    4. its box: a family type’s box at the instance’s transform (when it agrees with the element’s own box within 0.01 ft), else the element’s box in model coordinates. A box is hidden (its body’s visibility off; showing it shows it) unless the element is structural: of a kind built as features but curtain panels and mullions (walls, floors, roofs, ceilings, stair runs, landings, columns, beams, sweeps, slab edges, rails; by class or category).

    Its report line says which, and a box’s line why the others gave nothing. Lengths in feet become millimetres.

  • Groups: the members of a placed group (ElementGroup) that it places where they are come in as any element; members of a group’s definition placed nowhere stay out, and a member placed elsewhere comes in there too, as the mesh of its geometry moved by the group’s transform (group_copies), on the group’s level.

  • Built as features too (mitcad#333; core/rvt): ceilings like floors (their boundary loops between their two horizontal reference faces, else down by their type’s width); curtain panels (a system panel’s cell extruded by its thickness) and mullions (a rectangular, corner or custom profile along the mullion’s path; a trimmed mullion’s ends cut along its symbol’s stored end faces, mitcad#385); stair runs of treads and risers (spiral ones about their centre, mitcad#385) and landings; wall sweeps, slab edges, fascias, gutters and rails (their profile family’s profile along their path, a body per line; a spiral rail along a fixed helix; a wall sweep’s ends mitred where its returns turn and where it meets another sweep, and cut by the sweeps joined to cut it, mitcad#385). A curtain wall and a railing whose geometry is their parts’ have no body of their own (outcome parts; curtain_walls, railings); the balusters and posts come in as family instances. The batch of elements built in one command is 64 elements; one whose features fail or disagree is left out of it and comes in as below.

  • An element’s level is the one its records name (its associated level, a level field, a level its records hold, a level parameter, its host’s); one that names none goes on the highest level at or below its box (counted as by_elevation).

  • Links: each linked model (an RvtLinkInstance) is a component of the root, <file> : <instance>, placed by the instance’s transform; the linked file (found by its name in link_files, else next to the project, at the relative path the project stores, or in link_folder) comes in there the same way (its own links are not followed). The name and path come from the project, so only a bare file name is looked for and a stored path only below the project’s folder (no root, drive or ..; mitcad#924). A link not found leaves its component empty, the report naming it. A linked IFC model (a link whose file is an .ifc) comes in from its cached model (<name>.ifc.RVT) when found, else from the IFC file by the IFC import into its component. The application asks for the missing files (list_links); the command line never does.

  • Left out, counted by reason (left_out): types, view-specific elements (annotations), members of groups’ definitions that no placed group places where they are, placed groups themselves, elements without a box or mesh, elements of categories that are no building elements (levels, grids, rooms, lines, views, materials, …), elements without records.

  • The memory guard (mitcad#80) watches the reading and the building: when the process runs low on memory the remaining elements are left out (memory_low) and a warning says so.

  • Each base feature gets an import note (the timeline’s yellow badge, The import’s outcomes on the timeline): how many meshes and boxes (and how many boxes hidden), and that the report says why each one is not built.

One undo step (Import project.rvt). A job does not cancel it.

FieldMeaning
textimport_rvt returns a readable report
report_pathalso write the JSON report to this file
report_onlyread and report; import no elements
reference_ifcthe IFC export of the same project to check the features (and meshes) against, whose bodies stand in for elements without geometry, and whose openings cut the inserts without a cut tool of their own
no_reference_ifcdo not take an IFC export next to the project as the reference
link_fileslinked models’ files by the links’ file names ({"linked.rvt": "C:/…/linked.rvt"}; the application’s file dialogs)
link_foldera folder to look for linked models in, besides the project’s
list_linksonly list the links and where their files are: {"links": [{"id", "file", "stored_path", "found"}]} (the project’s elements are read without the geometry the file keeps; the application lists them once, mitcad#413)
mesh_onlyevery element as its mesh or box, no features
elementsonly these elements (ids; mitcad#385: checking a few elements of a large project), the others left out

The command’s result: file, design (the family’s name, else the file’s), bodies and report: format (rvt or rfa), kind (project, family), release and build (from BasicFileInfo), family and family_categories (a family’s PartAtom), external_files (linked models and other files by name: name, kind, element), preview (bytes, size), schema (classes, id_width, unknown_encodings), elements (declared, with_records, walked, read_in_part, not_read), levels (id, name, elevation mm), materials (count), import (projects: levels with id, name, elevation, component, feature, link, features, bodies, meshes, boxes; features and built (elements built as features, by kind), fallbacks (elements of those kinds that came in as meshes or boxes), reference, reference_agree (the reference’s solids agreed with, by IFC class) and reference_unmatched (its walls, slabs, roofs, columns, beams and members no feature agrees with, and why), bodies, meshes, oriented_boxes, boxes, level_planes, grid_axes, grid_arcs, appearances, links (id, file, found, component, elements, note), categories, left_out, by_elevation, not_built, memory_low, warnings, and geometry_meshes and geometry_triangles (meshes of the geometry the file keeps), reference_bodies, hidden_boxes, curtain_walls, railings, group_copies, openings_cut, openings_missing, openings_missing_lines, and elements: a line per element (id, link, global_id, kind, category, name, level, outcome (features, mesh, reference body, box, parts, not built), features, bodies, volume, checked_against, reference_volume, volume_difference, box_difference, hidden, notes)), warnings and seconds.

Tests: core/rvt (core.rvt, no OCCT; its corpus test reads MITCAD_RVT_CORPUS), core/import-rvt/src (mock kernel: the reader’s building test project’s walls, floor, grid, link and its chair’s hidden box; the mesh of a placed type’s B-rep; the house variant of the project with a gable roof over a wall attached to it, its top under both slopes, a door’s opening and a window type that cannot cut, counted in the report), core.exchange (core/tests/test_exchange.cpp), cli.import_rvt, cli.import_rfa, cli.import_rvt_building, rvt.corpus (MITCAD_RVT_CORPUS, with MITCAD_IFC_CORPUS the IFC export of the MIT-licensed project: every wall, slab and column agreed with; and a link) and tools/ui-rvt-import-test.sh.

.solidcraft import

{"cmd": "import_solidcraft", "path": "design.solidcraft"} (a document command of the bridge, like import_fcstd; mitcad-cli import-solidcraft, File › Open and Import, the headless MCP server’s document_open) brings a SolidCraft design in with its history (mitcad#450; core/solidcraft reads it, mitcad_import::solidcraft maps it, core/ffi/src/solidcraft_import.rs). Options:

OptionMeaning
textthe report as text (the bridge’s import_solidcraft)
report_pathalso write the JSON report there
expecteda JSON file of values to check against: body_count, total.volume_mm3, bbox, bodies[] (by name: volume_mm3, area_mm2 (a surface body’s, mitcad#455), bbox), timeline[].name, params[].name, sketches[] (curves, constraints, dimensions), parametric (at least so many), links (the motion links that came in, exactly), valid (true: every body valid by the geometry kernel’s checker, measured only then, mitcad#2175); SolidCraft’s own solidcraft-cli eval output is such a file. Volumes within volume_tolerance (relative, 1e-3), boxes within bbox_tolerance (0.01 mm); every placed body counts unless "scope": "root"
set_parameters{"name": "expression"}: parameters (the design’s names) changed after the import, before the report measures the bodies

The result has file, design, format (solidcraft), items, bodies, counts (features parametric, partial, unmapped, failed, skipped) and report: per feature its id, name, kind, outcome, the MitCad features it became and notes; the parameters (the design’s expression and MitCad’s, a renamed one’s MitCad name); the sketches with their points, curves and constraint and dimension counts (the file’s and those that came in) and what was left out; the joints; the motion links (links: per link its number, name, coupling, outcome, feature and notes); the bodies measured (volume, area, world box per placed body; valid when expected asks for it); the kinds without a MitCad counterpart with their counts; notes; and check with expected.

  • Files: .sc, as SolidCraft saves designs now (mitcad#1622), .solidcraft and the legacy .solvecraft, in any case. Other programs use .sc too, so a .sc file is read only when its JSON’s top-level format (within its first 64 KiB) starts with solidcraft/ (or the legacy solvecraft/), or when it is a design container; any other is refused with “Not a SolidCraft design: …” and the reason (not a JSON object, no format key, another format, a SolidCraft drawing, a zip that is no design container), before anything is imported. File › Open, Import, drag and drop and the system’s open refuse it so before the import starts (the bridge’s solidcraft_file_check).
  • Formats: any solidcraft/N (or the legacy solvecraft/N) up to 63, SolidCraft 0.45.0’s (mitcad#1331, mitcad#1994, mitcad#2153), and a design saved while changes were pending (format_pending); upgraded first by SolidCraft’s own steps (third_party/solidcraft/format.rs). A design a newer SolidCraft saved (a format past 63, or changes this import does not know) opens with a warning that names its format and says features may build differently (the first warning of notices, and the report’s newer: format, reads_up_to, unknown_changes, left_out, warning): what the import reads comes in, features it cannot read are placeholders with the reason, and sections and parameters it cannot read are left out and named. A SolidCraft drawing (solidcraft-drawing/N) is refused with a message saying so. The container (solidcraft-container/1: a zip of container.json, document.json and blobs/) is read with its STEP and mesh blobs.
  • Parameters: user parameters, the model parameters of sketch dimensions and each feature input’s parameter keep their names (a name MitCad reserves gets _ appended) and their expressions in MitCad’s language (mitcad_solidcraft::expr: SolidCraft’s juxtaposed products, units as values, mixed numbers and decimal commas, pi, log10, hypot, mod, trunc and its signum sign translated). A dimension’s or input’s parameter is its slot’s (d3 = height), owned by the MitCad feature; where MitCad’s slot is a function of the file’s value (a cylinder’s diameter of its radius, a symmetric revolve’s half angle) the file’s parameter is a user parameter and the slot that function of it. Slots the file does not name get names of the import’s own (d<n> past the file’s), so that MitCad’s names never collide with the file’s.
  • References: a face or edge is found by SolidCraft’s persistent name where the import translates it (extrusion caps by their height over the sketch, sides by their sketch curve, box and cylinder faces, roundings and bevels, shell insides, pattern copies, a removed face’s rim), the pick choosing among the faces the name means; else at the pick point (within 0.05 mm). Bodies by the file’s names: a feature’s new bodies are named as SolidCraft names them, the pieces a cut or split leaves <name> (k), ordered so that the picks later features make on them by name lie on them.
  • 3D curves and frame members (mitcad#2157): a sketch’s 3D curves are a spatial_sketch on the component’s XY plane (the sketch itself when it has nothing else, else <name> 3D after it), ends that meet one point, format 58’s 3D relations and dimensions its sketch3d relations and dimensions, a design before them fixed where the file has it; a frame member is one pipe per line (a round bar or tube along its centre, the diameter and wall the file’s inputs) or per line a construction plane along_path at the line’s start, the section sketched on it in the member’s frame and a sweep along the line, its body named as the file names it (details).
  • What maps to what: core/import-solidcraft/docs/solidcraft.md. Unmapped kinds and failed features become suppressed placeholder features with the reason as their import note (The import’s outcomes on the timeline).

Tests: core.solidcraft (the reader, formats and upgrades, the container; tests/sc_extension.rs: every test design copied to .sc reads as its original, other programs’ .sc files refused), core.import-solidcraft (tests/sc_extension.rs: a .sc copy imports as its original, mock kernel; src/frames_tests.rs, mitcad#2157: 3D curves, 3D relations and a parameter, linked pieces, pipes and sweeps of frame members on the mock kernel), core.import (solidcraft::tests, mock kernel), cli.import_solidcraft (tools/cli/solidcraft-test.cmake: the hand-written test designs of core/solidcraft/tests/designs against their worked-out values, a parameter change (also the rail of frame-members moved by its 3D line’s length), the container, the MCP open), solidcraft.corpus (MITCAD_SOLIDCRAFT_CORPUS), cli.solidcraft_pipe_network_reported (tools/cli/solidcraft-pipe-network-reported-test.cmake, mitcad#2175: GitHub #526’s reduced pipe network under MITCAD_MITCAD_REPORTED, its 3D sketches, one pipe per line of the file’s diameters and walls, every feature parametric and every body valid; skipped without the file) and tools/ui-import-test.sh.

.dwg import

{"cmd": "import_dwg", "path": "drawing.dwg", …} (C++ Document::command, or Document::import_dwg(path, json) for the report alone) imports a .dwg drawing’s 3D content (mitcad#453; core/ffi/src/dwg_import.rs, the reader is core/dwg), R13 to R2018. Bodies only: a drawing keeps no history.

  • Bodies: 3D solids, bodies, regions and surfaces with B-rep data, each converted by the .f3d reader’s ASM code and built by the B-rep builder of the imports (one body per body of the record); 3D faces as one mesh body per block, layer and colour; polyface, polygon and subdivision meshes (the control mesh) as a mesh body each. Coordinates are drawing units scaled to millimetres ($INSUNITS; none: millimetres assumed, with a warning).
  • Components: each named block with 3D content (in itself or its inserts) is a component named as the block, placed by an occurrence per insert (MINSERT: per cell), nested blocks in their blocks. Anonymous blocks, and inserts whose transform is not rigid (a scale or a mirror), are copied into the inserting component, the bodies moved by the transform (Kernel::transform_shape). A block that inserts itself is left out there with a warning.
  • Features: the bodies of a component on one layer are one base feature named Layer <name> (in a component <component> layer <name>, so that each has a name of its own), source <file>, layer <name>; bodies are named Solid n, Mesh n (the block’s name when a component has one body) and coloured by the entity, its layer or the inserting entity (BYBLOCK; a block placed more than once takes its first insert’s). The drawing’s units become the document’s when it was empty. One undo step.
  • Options: text (the report as text), report_path, expect (data sheet values checked: length_mm the side of the bodies’ box nearest to it, chord_distance_mm with tube_diameter_mm the nearest of the other sides, tube_diameter_mm and tube_wall_mm cylindrical faces of the outer and inner diameter, mass_kg the solids’ volume times density_kg_m3 (2700), volume_mm3 the solids’ volume, solids, components). Besides these, the checks are that every body built and is valid, every 3D entity was taken, a drawing with 3D entities gave bodies, and the bodies lie within the drawing’s extents (when it has them: extents never computed are stored empty).
  • Report (report): version, units, drawing_units, unit_mm, units_assumed, extents ($EXTMIN/$EXTMAX, mm), bounds (every placed body’s box), entities and taken (by type), left_out (type, count, why: 2D entities, wires, entities without B-rep data, …), paper_space, objects, objects_failed, components (name, bodies, occurrences, placed in all), copied_inserts, bodies, solids, meshes, valid, solid_volume (mm³, every placement), cylinder_diameters, not_built, records (each B-rep record’s form: text, binary or binary from the data storage, and ASM version), checks (every body built and valid, the bounds within the extents, the expect values) and pass, warnings. The command’s result: file, bodies, components, report.

Tests: core.dwg (the reader on drawings its tests write in every version: header variables, classes, objects, data storage, both forms of the B-rep record, the plan of components), cli.import_dwg_<version> (the test drawing through OCCT) and dwg.corpus (MITCAD_DWG_CORPUS).

.3dm import

{"cmd": "import_3dm", "path": "model.3dm", …} (C++ Document::command, or Document::import_3dm(path, json) for the report alone) imports a .3dm model (mitcad#1715; core/ffi/src/import_3dm.rs, the reader is core/3dm), files of format versions 5 to 8. Bodies only: a .3dm model keeps no feature history; a SubD object becomes an editable Form feature (below).

  • Bodies: B-reps (polysurfaces and surfaces, which the format saves as B-reps of one face), extrusions (each segment of a profile a side face, the caps where the extrusion has them) and untrimmed NURBS and plane surfaces, converted to the neutral B-rep model of the imports and built by its B-rep builder; meshes as mesh bodies. A B-rep that cannot be built comes in as the render mesh saved with it where it has one, with a warning (render_mesh_fallbacks). Coordinates are the model’s units scaled to millimetres (no unit: millimetres assumed).
  • Components: each block is a component named as the block, placed by an occurrence per instance; nested blocks in their blocks. An instance whose transform is not rigid (a scale or a mirror) is copied into the component that holds it, the bodies moved by the transform (Kernel::transform_shape). Block definitions are read from files of format version 6 and later; in older files their instances are left out with a warning. An instance of a block inside that block (directly or through other blocks) is left out (a block placed inside itself), and copies stop at 10,000 instances and 100,000 bodies.
  • Features: the bodies of a component on one layer are one base feature named Layer <path> (Parent::Child; in a component <component> layer <path>), source <file>, layer <path>; a body is named after its object, else Solid n, Surface n or Mesh n, and coloured by its object’s display colour (its own, its layer’s, or for a block’s geometry the instance’s); black, the format’s default, leaves the body MitCad’s colour. The model’s unit becomes the document’s when it was empty and MitCad has it (mm, cm, m, in, ft). One undo step.
  • SubD objects (mitcad#1757): each becomes a Form feature in the component that holds it, named after the object (Form1 … where it has no name or the name is taken), its body named so too. Its cage is the SubD’s control net (level 0) in mm: the vertices and faces with the file’s own ids (1, 2, … where they are not all usable), each face turned to run counter-clockwise seen from outside (a closed net’s faces out of it), the creased edges creases sharp for good, a smooth edge with a sharpness (format version 8) a crease of that sharpness (the mean of its ends’ where it changes along the edge, with a warning), the corner vertices corners. Vertices on no face are left out with a warning. A net that makes no cage (an edge of three faces, a one-sided surface, a face that does not go round its edges in order) is in not_built with why. Not carried: the file’s symmetry (the cage holds both halves, without a symmetry plane), the subdivided levels, texture, material and colour per face, and the format’s own sector rules at creases and corners (the Form’s surface is MitCad’s Catmull-Clark limit surface of the cage). An instance that scales or mirrors a block moves a copy of the cage with it. The Form is edited with the form.* commands like any other.
  • Left out: hidden objects and objects on hidden layers, curves, points, annotations and other classes that are not solids, surfaces or meshes (left out by design: design true, no notice) and objects that could not be read (a warning each kind). A file the reader refuses (not a .3dm file, a version before 2) is an error; a damaged object is left out as not read, the rest of the file imported.
  • Options: text (the report as text), report_path.
  • Report (report): format (3dm), version (the archive’s: 50, 60, 70, 80), application, units (the document’s, when set), file_units, unit_mm, units_assumed, tolerance (the model’s absolute tolerance, its units), layers, objects and taken (by kind), left_out (type, count, why, design), components (name, bodies, occurrences, placed, component), copied_instances, bodies, solids, meshes, valid, solid_volume (mm³, each body once), render_mesh_fallbacks, not_built (source, error, and for agents object: the object’s index in the file; a SubD whose net makes no cage, or whose Form fails, is one), forms (each SubD’s Form: name, uid, source, object, component, the cage’s vertices, faces, creases, corners, closed, built), checks (every body built and valid, every solid, surface and mesh taken) and pass, warnings, warning_details, notices. The command’s result: file, bodies, components, notices, report.
  • Words, not places (docs/ui-conventions.md, “What a message says”): warnings, not_built’s source and error and the error of a file that cannot be read say what is wrong in words and name an object by its kind, name, block and layer (“the B-rep "Bracket" in the block Bolt on the layer Parts cannot be read: the data ends early”), never by its index in the file, a byte offset, a typecode or a class id. Those are for agents: warning_details gives each warning with its detail (“object 17: the data ends early (8 bytes needed at offset 4096, 2 left)”), not_built its object, and the log (the import process’s standard error, import: .3dm: …) the same.

Tests: core.3dm (the reader and the conversion on its test models, cut short and damaged; the models of MITCAD_3DM_CORPUS read and converted), cli.import_3dm (the sample model through OCCT), cli.import_3dm_block_in_itself and 3dm.corpus (the models an index.tsv under MITCAD_3DM_CORPUS lists, through OCCT; its SubD model written by the format’s own application imports as an editable Form with the file’s cage, mitcad#1810), cli.render_3dm_plane_surfaces (plane surfaces drawn facing up in each of the file’s forms come in facing up and render lit from above, mitcad#1738), cli.import_3dm_subd and cli.import_3dm_subd_edit (a SubD cube of the test writer as an editable Form, mitcad#1757).

glTF import

{"cmd": "import_file", "path": "robot.glb"} imports a glTF 2.0 file (mitcad#1826): the binary form (.glb) or the JSON form (.gltf), its buffers and images embedded (data URIs, the binary chunk) or in files beside it. The model reads it itself (core/gltf, core/model/src/exchange/gltf_import.rs) and makes mesh bodies with the kernel’s triangle_body (textured_triangle_body for a mesh with texture coordinates, mitcad#1862); no history.

  • Components: a node with children is a component named after the node (else its mesh’s name, else Node <n>), placed by an occurrence with the node’s placement; its mesh and its children go into it. Nodes whose subtrees are the same (names, meshes and placements) are one component with an occurrence each, as MitCad’s export writes a component placed twice. A node whose placement scales, shears or mirrors is no component: its meshes and its children’s come in moved into place in the component that holds it (a warning says so). A scene of one root node with children and no mesh is the design itself: its children come in straight into the component imported into, its placement moved into theirs (a writer’s turn of the axes, MitCad’s own root).
  • Bodies: a node with a mesh is a mesh body named after the node in the component that holds it, its placement moved into the triangles; a mesh of several materials is a body per material (<node> (<material>)). Corners at the same point are one vertex (writers split them where texture coordinates or normals differ); a mirrored placement turns the triangles so that they face out. A body whose material has a base colour image keeps the file’s texture coordinates of that image (mitcad#1862: the set its texCoord names, TEXCOORD_0 by default, moved by its KHR_texture_transform, v turned to run up the image), one per vertex, so its corners at the same point stay apart where their coordinates differ (a seam of the image); a mesh body keeps them as its triangulation’s UV nodes, which the design file’s B-rep data and the result store carry, and which a Move, a Scale (also a non-uniform one), a Mirror and the patterns keep on the copies (mitcad#1874). Each component’s bodies are one base feature (source the file name), and the bodies outside components one more in the component imported into (named by name).
  • Units and axes: metres become millimetres (unit_mm is not read) and glTF’s Y up becomes Z up ((x, y, z) to (x, -z, y)): each root node’s placement is turned.
  • Appearances: each material a body uses becomes one document appearance named after it (made unique; glTF material <n> without a name): the base colour (glTF’s linear colour as sRGB), metalness, roughness, the opacity of a blended one (alphaMode BLEND: its alpha), emission (its strongest component as the strength, the colour scaled to it), transmission and the index of refraction (their extensions); its base colour image (PNG or JPEG) embedded as the texture, with its normal image, its occlusion image (channel red) and its image of metalness and roughness (one embedded image as the roughness map, channel green, and the metalness map, channel blue; mitcad#1862) as maps (Texture map sets); the projection uv where its bodies kept their texture coordinates, else box. The factors stay the appearance’s values, used where there is no map; where the image of metalness and roughness is a map, the factor that is not 1 goes with it too (factor, mitcad#1874), as glTF multiplies the channels by them. A material with other images but no base colour image has no texture (a warning says so). The bodies also keep the base colour as their colour.
  • Wrap: into a design with content, the file comes in inside a new component named after the file by default, as STEP (Imports into a component of their own); file_structure answers wrap true for it.
  • Result: as a STEP assembly’s (structure components, components, occurrences; the bodies outside components first in bodies), or one base feature’s when the file has no node with children. warnings say in words what is not taken: animations, skins, morph targets, points and lines, compressed meshes, sparse accessors, images other than PNG and JPEG, images of a material without a base colour image, extensions the reader does not read (the file's extension KHR_lights_punctual is not read), scenes other than the default one, a textured mesh without texture coordinates or with ones that cannot be read (a textured mesh has no texture coordinates: its texture is projected as MitCad projects textures), nodes that scale or mirror. One undo step (Import robot.glb); nothing stays of a failed import. A file without triangles is refused (robot.glb has no triangles to import: points and lines are left out: MitCad imports triangles); a damaged one with words (robot.glb: the glTF binary file is damaged), its detail (offsets, indexes) in the log (import: glTF: …).
  • Untrusted files: every index, count, offset and stride is checked before use; files beside the file are read only from its folder or below (not an absolute path, a parent folder or a URL); more than 50 million triangles are refused; the node tree is walked once per node, at most 64 deep.

The query {"query": "gltf_file", "path": "robot.glb"} answers the file as the import reads it, without changing anything: generator, nodes (each node the scene places, in the order of a walk from the roots: name, path (names joined by /), mesh, children (count), triangles, texture_coordinates (its mesh has some for its image, mitcad#1862) and uv_bounds (their box as MitCad keeps them, [[u, v] low, [u, v] high], else null), materials (per primitive: name, base_color sRGB, alpha, metallic, roughness, texture, metallic_roughness_texture), transform (rows of 4 in the parent, millimetres, a root’s turned to Z up) and world (in the design)), meshes, triangles, materials, images (read), notes (the words) and note_details (each note with its detail for agents).

Tests: core.gltf (the reader on its test writer’s files in every form, cut short and damaged, and the public-domain sample), the model’s gltf_tests (core/model-tests/files: components, occurrences, appearances, texture coordinates and packed maps, one undo step, wrapping, refusals, the sample) and the plan’s unit tests (gltf_import.rs: the triangles in millimetres with Z up, mirrored nodes, seams of texture coordinates), cli.import_gltf (the sample through OCCT: volumes, placements, appearances; tools/cli/tests/gltf_sample.json), tools/ui-gltf-test.sh (MitCad’s export read back), gltf.corpus (openly licensed sample files under MITCAD_GLTF_CORPUS, each checked by its script of facts read from the file; development.md).

.serp import

{"cmd": "import_file", "path": "vase.serp"} imports a .serp file (mitcad#1870), the native file of an open-source NURBS modeller built on OCCT, format versions 1 (a bare JSON scene) to 9 (a zip of the scene, its metadata, a thumbnail and binary members). The model reads it itself (core/serp, core/model/src/exchange/serp_import.rs); the shapes are bodies without history.

  • Bodies: an object whose shape is a B-rep (OCCT’s binary format, as the file keeps it) is a body read by the kernel’s import_brep, a solid or a surface; an object’s mesh is a mesh body (triangle_body). A body is named after its object and coloured by the object’s colour, else its layer’s. The design’s bodies are one base feature (source the file name, named by name) in the component imported into.
  • Layers: when the bodies lie on more than one layer, each body goes into a folder of the Bodies folder named after its layer’s path (Parts::Bolts; Folders of the Bodies folder). A hidden object, or one on a hidden layer (or below one), comes in hidden.
  • Blocks: a block is a component named after it holding the block’s shapes as bodies (named after the block, <block> <n> for several; the colour of its first placement), placed by an occurrence per placed block. The file keeps no placements, only each placed block’s shapes where it is: the kernel finds the rigid motion from the block’s shapes onto them (Kernel::rigid_copies, within 0.01 mm). A placed block that is not such a copy (scaled, mirrored, or changed after it was placed), and a hidden one, comes in as a body of the design where the file has it (a warning counts them). A block placed nowhere is left out (a warning names it).
  • Units: the file’s unit (mm, cm, m, in, ft) scales the shapes to millimetres (unit_mm is not read) and becomes the design’s unit when the design has no features yet; a file without a unit, or with one MitCad does not know, is read in millimetres (a warning says so for an unknown one).
  • Left out: curves and points (B-reps without faces), texts, hatches, dimensions, pictures, point clouds, scan paths, layouts and history records: one warning counts them by kind (not imported: 2 curves and points, 1 point cloud, 1 text, 1 layout, 3 history records). An object whose data cannot be read is left out with a warning in words (the object "Bracket" on the layer Parts cannot be read: left out); its index and why go to the log (import: .serp: …). A body the kernel’s check finds not valid comes in as the file has it, with a warning.
  • Refused: a file of a newer format version than the reader knows (vase.serp: the file was made by a newer version of its program (format version 10; MitCad reads versions 1 to 9)), never read half; a file that is not a .serp file or whose container is damaged, in words; a file without solids, surfaces or meshes (vase.serp has no solids, surfaces or meshes to import: …).
  • Wrap: into a design with content, the file comes in inside a new component named after the file by default, as STEP (Imports into a component of their own); file_structure answers wrap true for it.
  • Result: as a STEP assembly’s (structure components, components, occurrences; the design’s bodies first in bodies) when the file has a placed block, else one base feature’s; warnings as above. One undo step (Import vase.serp); nothing stays of a failed import.

Tests: core.serp (the reader on its test writer’s files: both forms, every version, a newer one, meshes, layers, colours, blocks, damaged and cut-short files), the model’s serp_tests (core/model-tests/files, the mock kernel: names, colours, folders, hidden bodies, units, blocks as components, the summary of what is left out, refusals, wrapping, one undo step), cli.import_serp (the test file of mitcad-cli serp-test-file through OCCT: B-reps OCCT wrote, a B-spline surface, a mesh, a block placed twice; tools/cli/tests/serp_sample.json), cli.import_serp_newer (a newer version refused in words), tools/ui-serp-test.sh (File › Open and File › Import), serp.corpus (real files under MITCAD_SERP_CORPUS, each checked by its script; development.md).

3MF import

{"cmd": "import_file", "path": "plate.3mf"} imports a 3MF file (mitcad#2156): a model of the core specification, and a slicer’s project whose meshes are in other model parts of the package (the Production extension: a component or build item of the root model whose p:path names 3D/Objects/object_1.model). The model reads it itself (mitcad_3mf::read_for_import, core/model/src/exchange/threemf_import.rs) and makes mesh bodies with the kernel’s triangle_body; no history. The print settings in the package are left alone (Import from Slicer reads them, Print profiles).

  • Bodies: each part of the file (a mesh object, followed through the build’s items and the components) is a mesh body named after the part: its name, else the name the package’s settings file gives its object (Metadata/model_settings.config: the name metadata of the part with the mesh object’s id in the object of the root model that places it, else the object’s; Metadata/Slic3r_PE_model.config: the object’s), else Object <id>. A part placed once comes in moved into place in the component imported into, all such parts one base feature (source the file name, named by name).
  • Components: a part placed more than once (by several build items or components) is a component named after the part, holding its mesh once in the part’s own coordinates (a base feature of its own), with an occurrence per placement. A placement that scales, shears or mirrors can be no occurrence: that copy comes in as a body moved into place (a warning says so).
  • Units: the file’s unit (micron, millimeter, centimeter, inch, foot, meter), read in millimetres; unit_mm is not read.
  • Appearances: each base material colour (basematerials) becomes one document appearance named after the material (made unique; 3MF color #RRGGBB without a name) with the colour as its base colour, set on the bodies; the bodies also keep the colour as their colour.
  • Open meshes: a mesh of an object of type model that is not closed, or faces inwards, comes in as a mesh body with a warning (Shell: its mesh is not closed (…): it came in as a mesh body, which Convert Mesh cannot make a solid), as an STL file’s; Convert Mesh refuses it later. Triangles that use a vertex twice are left out (a warning says how many).
  • Refusals: a file that cannot be read is refused in words, nothing changed: not a zip archive (plate.3mf cannot be imported as a 3MF file: not a zip package, as a 3MF file is: …), no model part, a model part that is not a 3MF core <model>, an extension it requires other than the Production extension (the file requires the 3MF Slice extension, which MitCad does not read; Materials and Properties, Beam Lattice, Secure Content, … by name), a reference to an object that is not there, a vertex index out of range, or a build without items.
  • Wrap: not by default: a 3MF file goes into the active component as STL and OBJ do; wrap true puts it in a new component named after the file.
  • Result: as a STEP assembly’s (structure components, components, occurrences; the bodies outside components first in bodies) when a part is placed more than once, else one base feature’s; warnings as above. One undo step (Import plate.3mf); nothing stays of a failed import.

Tests: core.3mf (the reader: a package whose root model places objects of 3D/Objects/object_1.model through p:path, its names from the settings file, the colour of the other part’s base material; other required extensions, missing parts and objects, a p:path outside the root model refused; an open mesh kept by read_for_import with its warning), the model’s threemf_import_2156_tests (core/model-tests/files, the mock kernel: a file of mitcad_3mf::write with two coloured parts and a repeated placement as mesh bodies, appearances and a component of two occurrences at their positions, one undo step; an open mesh with its warning; refusals), 3mf.corpus (each slicer project under MITCAD_3MF_CORPUS imports its meshes, named as its settings file names them), tools/ui-3mf-import-test.sh and app.ui-windows-3mf-import (MitCad’s 3MF export opened and imported with File › Import).

The import’s outcomes on the timeline

The importers that replay a history (the .f3d and .ipt imports, FreeCAD documents) leave on the features they make what their report says of them (mitcad#170): an import note, in the definition state and the design file (a feature’s import_note), so that a saved import shows it when it is opened again.

  • A fallback’s base feature (base with replaces; one per component that changed) says which items it stands in for, each with the report’s note as the reason: Stands in for Extrude5 (its result is not in the file's history); items in a row with the same reason share it (Stands in for Fillet2, Fillet3 (the import was stopped)), and after eight the rest are counted (and 37 more items (see the import report)). A base feature the import added for another reason (the bodies brought to a history state exactly, the stored bodies at the end) has the report’s warning about it.
  • An item that came in partly (partial) has Partly imported: and the report’s note (left out: 3 constraints ...).
  • An item skipped because it was suppressed or failed in the file (the .f3d import’s suppressed in the file, the file keeps no result for it ..., failed in the file: ...; FreeCAD’s suppressed in FreeCAD) becomes a placeholder at its place: {"type": "placeholder", "item_type": "ExtrudeFeature"}, suppressed, named after the item (when the name is free, else Placeholder<n>), its note the report’s note. It builds nothing; unsuppressed, it warns that it builds nothing. Items skipped for having no geometry (occurrences, groups, relationships the import does not translate) get none.
  • An .f3d item suppressed in the file whose definition translates (mitcad#180) comes in as that feature, suppressed, with the note suppressed in the file; not checked against the file's history; unsuppressed, it builds (status warning with the note until it is edited). Only where its definition does not come in is it a placeholder (suppressed in the file; its definition did not come in: ...). Suppressed sketches come in suppressed, their note ending suppressed in the file. A placeholder of an item the file suppressed only through an item it depends on ends (suppressed through an item it depends on).
  • An .f3d modelling item after the file’s timeline marker (rolled back in the file) whose definition translates comes in as that feature after the marker (status rolled_back), with the note rolled back in the file (after its timeline marker); not checked against the file's history; the timeline marker is before the first such item. Where its definition does not come in it is a placeholder (rolled back in the file (after its timeline marker); its definition did not come in: ...).

A feature with a note has the status warning while it builds (the note first in error, before its evaluation’s warnings); a placeholder stays suppressed with the note as its error; a failed feature shows its error. The timeline and feature queries give the note as import. A command that changes the feature’s definition or one of its dimensions (the parameters it owns) clears the note when the feature then does not fail; renaming, suppressing and moving it do not, and undo brings the note back. The report’s texts are the source: the timeline’s notes are made from the report at the end of the import.

Command (Rust, Document)FieldsResult
set_import_notes[(uid, note)] (an empty note removes it)one undo step Import notes, no recompute
add_import_placeholdername, item_type, note, componentthe placeholder, suppressed with the note (Add <name>)
import_note, import_notesuidthe note of a feature; every feature’s

Tests: core.model (document::import_notes: status, message, save and reopen, an edit clearing the note), core.import (timeline_note_tests: fallbacks, partial sketches and placeholders of an .f3d design; a_suppressed_feature_becomes_a_placeholder and the fallback’s note of a FreeCAD Body), and tools/ui-import-status-test.sh.

Mesh refinement

export’s refinement (STL, OBJ, 3MF, USDZ) is a preset or the tolerances themselves (mitcad#398):

PresetSurface deviationAngle between facet normalsTriangles a face at most (about)
low0.1 mm30°5 000
medium (default)0.03 mm15°20 000
high0.01 mm8°50 000
  • A doubly curved face (a sphere’s, a torus’s, most freeform faces) that would get more triangles at the deviation meshes with a larger deviation instead, which grows with the face’s size: about 0.8 × ∫√|K| dA / triangles (K the Gaussian curvature; 1.1 mm for a sphere face of 4.5 m radius at medium).
