A corner may take a whole adjacent boundary, to its far vertex (mitcad#242); a longer one is refused, unless the contour continues on an arc beyond it: then a round takes that side whole and is tangent to the arc (mitcad#280). All corners of one feature are found on its input sheet. Convex corners remove material; concave hole corners add the bounded wedge and reduce the void. Oversized, degenerate or ambiguous corners fail. Saved corner_slots retain removed selections as tombstones, so reordering or readding a corner does not change its provenance.

sheet_state keeps its reference-frame panels projection and additionally reports authoritative charts, bends, joins, opened and curve lineage. Charts have a tagged panel/bend domain ID, exact bounded material curves and a plane or cylinder embedding. Plane front_to_back_sign is positive or negative; this is independent of chart winding and remains explicit when a bend is opened by the geometry primitives. A failed or disconnected folded result publishes no partial pieces and blocks only the intended input sheets.

Walls of one sheet that meet (mitcad#1409)

A flange (or another folded feature) whose walls meet walls of the same sheet that no bend joins them to is built only where they touch along a line or at a point: a full open corner, the closing wall’s end on the corner line of the other wall at the exact inside dimension, is accepted as it is, neither fused nor its faces merged. Walls that touch over a face (a half open corner) are refused, sheet walls SheetFlange1 and SheetFlange3 touch over a face, which a sheet body cannot hold: leave a seam gap between them; walls that pass into each other (more than 1e-6 mm deep) are refused, sheet walls SheetFlange1 and SheetFlange3 pass through each other. A wall is named by its feature, a further wall of it SheetFlange3 (wall 2), a bend SheetFlange1 (bend). No clearance is added. See the sheet-metal contract.

Corner joints of a closing flange (mitcad#1410)

A sheet_flange whose wall closes against another wall of the same sheet (the last side of a box section) takes corner, the joint the two walls make: "open" or "half_open" (left out: the wall’s end is free; the list is open for further joints). With a corner the flange’s length is the inside dimension of the closed section, measured by "mode": "inner" (other modes, and a hem with it, are refused), and the joint sets the wall’s end from the sheet’s thickness t:

  • open: the wall ends on the other wall’s inner surface, the two walls meeting only along the corner line (a full open corner, whose outer V is welded); the body holds them as they are (mitcad#1409).
  • half_open: the wall reaches t / 2 further, over half of the other wall’s end. Walls that touch over a face do not make one sound body, so the other wall is cut back by a seam of 0.00001 mm (10 nm) where the wall lies over it (its new end the flange’s generated curves 60 to 63); that seam is the only clearance. It is the smallest seam that is a gap at all, ten times the 1e-6 mm modelling tolerance: the check of mitcad#1409 accepts walls 0.0000005 mm apart and refuses them at 0.0000001 mm, and gaps from 0.000001 mm to 0.01 mm all gave a valid body, a cut through the corner and a hole. The other wall is the flat wall normal to the flange’s wall whose material lies under the wall’s last t / 2 and whose end lies on its surface; none, or more than one, refuses the flange.
{"type":"sheet_flange","body":"F3.b0",
 "boundary":{"panel":{"feature":"F5","slot":0},"curve":{"type":"generated","feature":"F5","slot":51}},
 "angle":1.5707963267948966,"length":{"mode":"inner","value":10},"position":"outside",
 "corner":"half_open"}

On a 1 mm sheet with Outside flanges of Inner Length 10 on both long edges of a 10 mm wide base, this third flange closes the 10 x 10 section: its wall reaches 0.5 mm over the first wall’s end, and the first wall ends 0.00001 mm under it; the inside stays 10 x 10. The Flat Pattern keeps the two walls at the strip’s two ends.

A flange’s profile sketch (mitcad#1648)

A sheet_flange may take profile, a sketch before it whose closed region on the bend line is the wall’s outline instead of the rectangle of length, offsets and width (GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#237). The sketch is read in the wall’s own sketch frame: its origin on the wall’s root line (the bend’s moving tangent line) at the middle of the selected boundary, x along that line (against the boundary’s canonical axial direction e) and y along the wall away from the bend, on the wall’s front surface. Its x axis is the bend line:

  • the wall is the one region of the sketch with a straight side on the bend line and its material above it (holes in it stay holes; regions away from the line are not used). That side, drawn by one line or by several in a row, is the bend’s span: it lies within the boundary (from -L/2 to L/2 for a boundary L long), and the flange’s offsets are where it leaves the boundary free, with the reliefs a flange with offsets gets;
  • the rest of the outline may slant, taper, curve (lines, arcs, circles, ellipses and splines) or pass the boundary’s ends beside the bend (an overhang, as a width from the middle makes one; it starts at the bend’s moving tangent line);
  • the outline’s curves name the wall’s edges ({"type":"sketch", "sketch":"F5","segment":…}), its side on the bend line is the flange’s generated curve 53, as the rectangular wall’s root.

The flange keeps one bend: a profile takes no offsets, width, hem or corner (refused in words), and its length is not used. A region across the bend line, none or more than one with a side on it, a side on the line in more than one place, or one past the boundary’s ends is refused in words without ids, as The flange's profile crosses the bend line; the wall's outline must stay on the wall's side of it. Editing the sketch updates the flange, Unfold and the Flat Pattern; the profile’s 2D outline is used wherever the sketch lies.

The profile sketch’s plane follows the wall (mitcad#1776, GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#310): sheet_flange_profile puts it on a construction plane of the type flange_wall, which is the wall’s sketch frame above, worked out again at every recompute from the sheet before the plane and the boundary, angle, radius and position of the flange whose profile is a sketch on it (the first such flange in the timeline). After the sheet’s edge moves (a base sketch’s dimension changed) or the flange’s angle, radius or position changes, the sketch lies on the wall when it is opened and shown; its curves stay where they are in the wall’s frame. Until a flange names the sketch (while a new flange’s profile is drawn) the plane is the frame stored with it. A design from an earlier version whose profile sketch lies on a fixed construction plane of its own (one no other feature refers to) gets the flange_wall plane when it is opened, with the same frame, so nothing moves in the wall’s frame. A flange whose sketch the user put on another plane, and that no longer lies on its wall, warns The flange's profile sketch no longer lies on its wall; Edit Profile in the Flange panel puts it back there.

{"cmd":"sheet_flange_profile",
 "def":{"type":"sheet_flange","body":"F3.b0",
        "boundary":{"panel":{"feature":"F3","slot":0},
                    "curve":{"type":"sketch","sketch":"F2","segment":"c2[c1,c3]"}},
        "angle":1.5707963267948966,"length":{"mode":"tangent","value":15},
        "position":"inside"}}

sheet_flange_profile makes a flange’s profile sketch from its definition def (as add_feature takes it; its values may be expressions), read against the sheet at the timeline marker (while a Flange is edited the marker stands just before it): a hidden flange_wall construction plane on the wall and a sketch on it (Plane1, Sketch2), both at the marker, before the flange, in one undo step Add Sketch2 as a flange's profile. The sketch holds the wall the flange’s length and width give now: a rectangle over the part of the boundary the bend covers (an overhang past the boundary’s ends is left to the sketch), its two corners on the bend line fixed there, its sides vertical, its far side horizontal and its length along the wall a dimension (a flange without a wall starts with 10 mm). For a def that has a profile already, the command makes that profile’s plane a flange_wall plane (a fixed plane of an earlier design) with its stored frame where the definition’s angle, radius and position put the wall (Move Plane1 onto the flange's wall; nothing when it is such a plane there already; a sketch that is not on a fixed or flange_wall plane of its own is refused). Once the flange is in the timeline, the plane follows the flange as it is there. It answers {"sketch":"F5","plane":"F4","added":2} (added: the features it put before the flange, 0 when it moved the plane). The flange then names the sketch: "profile":"F5".

A flange along a straight run (mitcad#2117)

"run": true on a sheet_flange of one edge makes its edge the straight run of its boundary: the boundary and the boundaries before and after it in its loop that continue it in a line and are joined to no other domain (a face over collinear sketch lines has a wall per line). The flange is then one bend and one wall along the whole run, its offsets and width measured along the run (a width from the run’s middle), the face cut back along all of it, as on a body whose edge there is one (the .f3d import’s flange on such an edge). A run that is the boundary alone is the plain flange. It is refused with boundaries, a corner gap or miters, a profile, and at position edge (the bend needs a setback line to cut back to). Left out it is false and not written.

"relieve_ends": true (mitcad#2117) gives a flange over its whole boundary (no offsets, width or profile) the bend relief at each end where the panel goes on along the bend line (the outline turns away from the material there, a concave corner, or goes on straight past the end): that end is an offset end of the relief’s width, the relief cut there as at any offset end, so the bend never meets unbent material. Ends at convex corners stay whole. The .f3d import sets it on its edge flanges (their bend relief). Left out it is false and not written.

A flange on several edges (mitcad#1872)

A sheet_flange may take boundaries, further straight boundaries after boundary (GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#337): one wall on each edge, all with the flange’s angle, length, position, radius and relief. Edge k (0 is boundary) has the flange’s bend slot k and wall panel slot k, its curves numbered from 100 k as a single flange’s (the bend’s strip 40 to 43, the wall’s sides 50, 52, far end 51, root on the bend 53). The edges are connected at their ends, at a common corner of a face or across the side of a bend between two faces (one end on each of its tangent lines, at the same place along it), also on faces turned differently, or across a corner gap the sheet records (mitcad#2098, GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#480); they make one chain or a closed loop. Edges that meet none of the others, more than two at one corner, or edges that leave a corner the same way are refused in words.

Corner gaps. The sheet’s state records each corner gap (gaps in the sheet_state query: the two panels, panels; the corner’s line, line; the gap, width): Convert to Sheet Metal one at each rip (the rip’s edge), a flange on several edges one at each corner between its walls (the line in the corner’s bisecting plane along the walls from where their roots meet). Two edge ends on the two panels of a recorded gap face each other across it when both lie at the same place along its line, neither further from it than the gap and twice the thickness: they are one corner, its point (for a refusal’s places and the sheet_flange_corners query) where the two edges’ lines come closest. So the rim edges of a converted tray, or of a tray whose walls are a flange on several edges, take one flange whose walls meet mitred at the corners. A gap is never guessed from the ends’ distance: ends of panels with no recorded gap between them meet only as above. A state without gaps (from before them) reads as one with none; a design saved before them records them when it is recomputed, its geometry unchanged.

Where two edges meet, their walls are mitred. Sheet walls are cut normal to their surfaces, as a laser cuts them, so a miter is a straight cut of each wall where a plane meets the surface of it that reaches further:

  • "miter": "bisect" (the default): the plane bisecting the corner, the one through the walls’ root lines (where the two lines in the middle of the walls’ thickness come closest) normal to the difference of the two edges’ directions away from the corner. Each flange stays on its side, corner_gap / 2 off it: its wall is cut there, and its bend ends square where all its material clears the plane. Two walls at an angle then meet at most along a line with a gap of 0 (an open corner); two walls in one plane (flanges on the sides of two faces that a bend joins, both turned to the inside of that bend) meet exactly on the bisecting line and need a gap above 0.
  • "earlier_runs_past" / "later_runs_past": the wall of the edge earlier (later) in the list runs on to the other wall’s outer surface and the other wall ends corner_gap short of the passing wall’s inner surface; both bends end at the bisecting plane as above. Not for walls in one plane, and the gap must be above 0 (walls that touch over a face make no sound body, mitcad#1409).
  • corner_miters, [{"edges": [0, 1], "miter": "later_runs_past"}], sets one corner’s miter in place of miter.

corner_gap (a length, expression allowed) is the gap at the corners; left out it is the sheet’s thickness. Where a corner shortens a bend, the face beside it is cut back to the bend’s tangent line up to the edge’s end (generated curves 70 to 73 at the edge’s start and 80 to 83 at its end, plus 100 k), across a bend there as a flange’s trim goes on through it (mitcad#211); the wall runs on past its bend’s end (its root there free: curves 55 before, 56 after the bend) to the miter, also beyond the edge’s end where the corner lets it (a hopper’s walls leaning outward), the miter’s edge the curve 58 at the edge’s start and 59 at its end. A free end of the flange that meets an existing flange of the sheet across a bend ends corner_gap short of that flange’s wall, which is never cut (mitcad#1877); a single-edge flange with corner_gap does the same. The end lies at an end of a bend’s tangent line (on either side of the bend), and across the bend lies either a wall of another flange (the end lies where that flange’s bend starts, or on the far side of a bend from a flange’s wall): that wall runs past, and this flange’s wall and bend keep corner_gap short of its surface; or a panel with another flange on the edge that meets this end across the bend (its bend ends across from the end, at most that flange’s setback away, where its trim cut the bend across back): this flange keeps corner_gap short of that flange’s wall, and where the two walls lie in one plane (or touch face to face) short of the plane square to that flange’s edge through the farthest its wall and bend reach towards this end; walls in one plane need a gap above 0, else the flange is refused in words. A flange on several edges, or with a corner_gap, covers each edge whole with a plain wall: profile, hem, corner, offsets and width are refused, as are Position edge and a length that leaves no wall. Every edit of the edges, the faces they lie on, the length, angle, radius or position recomputes the miters; Unfold and the Flat Pattern develop the walls with their gaps. At a corner across a recorded gap the walls are mitred exactly as at a touching corner: Miter, corner_miters, corner_gap, a negative angle (Flip) and every Position work unchanged, and each new wall and bend stays on its side of the corner’s bisecting plane, clear of the gap’s other panel. Walls that still meet are refused naming the flanges (sheet walls SheetFlange3 and SheetFlange3 (wall 2) pass through each other. Make the Corner Gap larger, or change the flange's angle, length or position so that its walls clear each other at the corners.).

The refusals at a corner (mitcad#1877: walls that still meet, a gap that leaves no room for a wall or a bend, a miter the corner cannot take, a corner’s miter on edges that do not meet) say what is wrong in words; their places (docs/ui-conventions.md, “What a message says”) are where it is, in the flange’s body as it was before the flange: the side faces its edges were picked by (F3:sheet_side0(F2:sheet_curve(c1[c4,c2]))), the front face of an existing flange’s wall or bend it meets (F5:sheet_front(0)), and the corner’s point. The application paints them while the pointer is over the message.

The query sheet_flange_corners gives the corners a flange on several edges would have, for the Flange panel’s per-corner Miter: {"query": "sheet_flange_corners", "body": "F3.b0", "edges": [boundary, …]} (the boundaries as the definition gives them, on the sheet at the timeline marker) answers {"body": …, "corners": [{"edges": [0, 1], "at": [x, y, z]}, …]}: each pair of the edges that meet, by their indices, and the corner’s point (the middle of the two ends on the front surface). Edges that are not one chain are refused in words. The panel takes a picked corner (an edge or a vertex) as the corner nearest the pick.

{"type":"sheet_flange","body":"F3.b0",
 "boundary":{"panel":{"feature":"F3","slot":0},"curve":{"type":"sketch","sketch":"F2","segment":"c1[c4,c2]"}},
 "boundaries":[{"panel":{"feature":"F3","slot":0},"curve":{"type":"sketch","sketch":"F2","segment":"c2[c1,c3]"}},
               {"panel":{"feature":"F3","slot":0},"curve":{"type":"sketch","sketch":"F2","segment":"c3[c2,c4]"}}],
 "angle":1.5707963267948966,"length":{"mode":"tangent","value":10},"position":"inside",
 "corner_gap":1}

On a 1 mm sheet (inside radius 1, K 0.44) of 40 x 30, these Inside flanges of 10 mm on three edges meet at two corners: each wall ends on the 45-degree line through the corner, its inner corner 1/sqrt(2) mm short of it, and each bend ends where its tangent line on the face meets that line, shifted the same. Tests: CLI cli.sheet_flange_edges (the box Inside and Outside at gaps 0 and 1, turned up and down, the earlier edge running past, Flat Pattern areas, refusals) and cli.sheet_flange_edges_bend (flanges on the sides of a face and of an inclined wall that a bend joins: walls in one plane mitred on the bend’s bisecting line; gap 0 refused), cli.sheet_flange_edges_existing (mitcad#1877: a flange on the inclined wall’s side meeting a plain flange on the face’s side across the bend, 1 mm short of it with the volume and the measured gap, the existing wall uncut, gap 0 refused; the sheet_flange_corners query), the model’s sheet_edges_tests.rs (the places of a corner refusal, the corners found).

Sheet Unfold, Refold and Flat Pattern

sheet_unfold and sheet_refold are timeline features of a valid native sheet (mitcad#208). They change the actual evaluated body between folded and developed configurations and keep every panel, bend and curve identity, so later features, cuts and a Refold work on the same named material.

{"type":"sheet_unfold","body":"F3.b0","stationary":{"feature":"F3","slot":0},
 "bends":[{"feature":"F4","slot":0}]}

stationary is a planar panel that stays fixed; bends is an explicit nonempty set of distinct bends. Unselected bends keep their folded shape and move rigidly with their panels. The labelled panel/bend graph is traversed from the fixed panel across the registered tangent ports; coplanar panels whose boundaries meet along a curve (a disc of a Face filling a round hole of another of its regions, which no straight port pairs, mitcad#1942) are one material and move together. A developed bend becomes the neutral strip [0, BA] x axial in the tangent plane of the side it is reached from: the front surface continues the neighbouring front surface, developed lengths are neutral-surface lengths |angle| * (r + K*t), and the panel beyond follows it rigidly. A bend already open, a missing or stale bend record (its allowance no longer matches the current rules), a stationary domain that is not a planar panel, material not connected to the fixed panel through registered seams, or a second graph path whose placement does not close (a non-developable cycle) fail explicitly. Coplanar developed material of distinct panels and strips must not overlap (shared seams are not overlaps); a self-overlap names both domains. Folded configurations are checked for collisions by the constructed solid.

{"type":"sheet_refold","body":"F3.b0","unfold":"F5",
 "bends":[{"feature":"F4","slot":0}]}

unfold is an earlier sheet_unfold of the same body. bends is the subset to close and defaults to every bend still open by that Unfold. A bend opened by another Unfold, or one already folded, is refused. Refold holds the panel that the Unfold held, so it restores the folded placement exactly. It rebuilds the cylinder from the bend’s own radius, angle, K and material-side parity at the current material; it never restores an old shape, so material edited while the bend was open is folded with it. sheet_state.opened lists each open bend with the Unfold that opened it (by) and its fixed panel (stationary). Nested and partial Unfold/Refold operations are ordinary timeline features: suppression, rollback, Undo and reopening give the configuration of the features before the marker.

Cut across bends 

{"type":"sheet_cut","body":"F3.b0","stationary":{"feature":"F3","slot":0},
 "open_bends":[{"feature":"F4","slot":0}],
 "profiles":[{"sketch":"F8","region":"r{c1[c4,c2],c2[c1,c3],c3[c2,c4],c4[c3,c1]}"}]}

sheet_cut removes material through the thickness inside closed regions (mitcad#208, production form mitcad#209). profiles may come from several sketches; each sketch must lie on the front or back surface of the developed stationary panel, and a region whose key no longer exists after a sketch edit resolves as for extrusions, all pieces of a region the edit split, with a warning (Profile references after a sketch change). Regions may have holes, and several contours may overlap. The listed open_bends are developed while stationary stays fixed (bends already open stay open). Every chart developed into that plane is trimmed in one operation whose seams are the registered ports, so a contour crossing a tangent line splits both sides of the seam at the same axial position, and a strip can keep several material pieces under one bend identity. A contour ending exactly on a tangent line removes material on one side only: that interval stops being a seam and becomes a free edge of the other side, also at the seam of a bend that is not developed, when the panel’s boundary keeps one stretch of it (mitcad#280). The input configuration is then restored: charts keep their coordinates, so the cut is folded with the material and survives a later Unfold/Refold, rule edits and sketch edits that change which seams it crosses. Fragments of one boundary curve get distinct piece numbers ordered by their midpoints.

A domain the profiles cover completely is removed with its ports; a removed bend also loses its record and its open state, so a later Unfold or Refold of it fails (“not a bend of this sheet”). When the cut disconnects the material, every connected piece becomes a body with its own sheet state (its charts, ports, bends, open bends and lineage): the first piece in geometric order (centre of mass, then the lower corner of the bounding box) keeps the body’s id, the others become the Cut’s bodies F<cut>.b0, F<cut>.b1, … in the same component. A Flat Pattern item stays with the original body id. A cut that reaches a seam to material that is not developed (“open that bend for it”), a sketch off the fixed panel’s surfaces, or profiles removing all material fail; profiles that touch no material give a warning.

With "mode": "straight" (mitcad#242) the cut is an extrusion’s: the profiles of one sketch, anywhere, swept along the sketch’s normal ("flip": true against it) from the sketch’s plane as far as "extent" ({"type": "distance", "distance": d} or {"type": "through_all"}), are cut from the folded sheet; it has no stationary or open_bends. Where the result is still the sheet’s material changed through its thickness, the domains are re-derived from it as for an ordinary feature (below). Where the cut crosses a bend or an inclined panel its walls follow the sweep, which the domains cannot hold: the cut is kept in sheet_state.overlays (its profiles, frame, direction, extent and the volume it removed) and is cut again from the solid every later sheet feature rebuilds. A rebuild in which it would remove more material than it did (material added later in its way) is refused, and so are Unfold, Refold, Fold, Bend and the Flat Pattern of a sheet with overlays (its developed form does not exist).

{"type":"sheet_cut","body":"F3.b0","mode":"straight","extent":{"type":"through_all"},
 "flip":true,"profiles":[{"sketch":"F7","region":"r{c1[c4,c2],c2[c1,c3],c3[c2,c4],c4[c3,c1]}"}]}

The developed chart of an opened bend keeps its chart coordinates: u along the neutral strip from its stationary-side tangent line (u = 0) to the moving side (u = BA), v along the axis. A bend’s folded_embedding in sheet_state is its cylinder while folded, and the cylinder refolding would build while holding its u = 0 side while it is open.

Corner relief 

{"type":"sheet_corner_relief","body":"F3.b0",
 "bends":[{"feature":"F4","slot":0},{"feature":"F5","slot":0}],
 "relief":{"type":"round","width":6,"depth":2}}

sheet_corner_relief (mitcad#209) relieves the junction of two bends. The junction is found with a panel held and the bends developed into its plane: the panel both bends leave (panel selects it when they share several). Bends that leave no common panel (mitcad#125: their panels meet through planar seams, other panels or bends) are developed together with every bend on the seam path between them, holding the panel next to the first bend on the shortest such path, or panel, which must then join one of the two bends (“joins neither” otherwise). s measures distance from the tangent line through which the development reaches a bend (the one on the common panel) into its strip; the s = 0 lines meet at the junction J0 and the centrelines (s = BA/2) at C, which does not depend on that choice. The relief is cut from all material in the panel’s developed plane exactly as sheet_cut does, then the input configuration returns. relief overrides the rules’ corner_relief:

typeRemoved region
rounddisc of diameter width centred at C
rectangularthe crossing of two bands of width width centred on the two centrelines: for perpendicular bends the square of side width centred at C with sides along both bends’ developed directions, otherwise the parallelogram with sides parallel to both bend lines and width across each strip (area width^2 / sin(angle); mitcad#125)
tearexactly the crossing zone 0 <= s1 <= BA1, 0 <= s2 <= BA2, the minimum separation of the two bend zones; no size

depth is used by bend reliefs only. Relief curves are generated curves of the feature (F<relief>/g<k>) and keep that provenance through later cuts, Unfold and Refold. Parallel bends (no junction), bends not connected through registered seams, a relief that removes a whole panel or strip (the flange is too short for it) or disconnects the sheet, and one reaching a seam of a third, folded bend fail. A relief that removes nothing gives a warning.

Flat Pattern

A Flat Pattern is a derived document item, one per sheet-metal body, saved in the design file (flat_patterns). It is not a timeline feature and never a body: body lists, occurrences and physical properties do not see it, and all occurrences of a component share it. It is evaluated on demand at the timeline marker from the body’s current sheet state, so edits made after it was set are included.

{"cmd":"set_flat_pattern","body":"F3.b0","stationary":{"feature":"F3","slot":0},
 "x_axis":{"type":"panel_x"},"reference_side":"front"}
{"cmd":"remove_flat_pattern","body":"F3.b0"}

set_flat_pattern creates or changes the item; omitted fields keep their previous values, and a new item fixes the body’s first panel, the panel’s own x axis and the front side. It fails for a body that has no sheet state at the marker or a panel the sheet does not have. Setting the same values again is no undo step; each change and remove_flat_pattern is one undo step that recomputes nothing.

Paste New and inserting a copy of a design (mitcad#125) copy the items of the copied bodies, split pieces F<cut>.b<k> included, with their settings and the fixed panel’s feature mapped to its copy; each copy has its own item. A component copied as bodies (made from bodies, or linked) has no sheet state and no item.

{"query":"flat_pattern","body":"F3.b0"}

Every bend is developed while the fixed panel stays where it is. The drawing is in the fixed panel’s material coordinates (its chart), so it does not move with the body and does not depend on which bends the timeline has opened. reference_side: "back" views the back surface: the drawing is mirrored (x -> -x). A valid answer has status: "valid", the source sheet_version, stationary, x_axis, reference_side, thickness, the 3D frame of the drawing on the viewed surface in the body’s coordinates (origin, x_axis, y_axis, normal), regions (the union of all developed charts: one closed material region, exterior loop first, then holes, as exact bounded curves), the developed area, the developed solid’s volume, 2D bounds, domains (domain and to_flat, each chart’s isometry into the drawing) and bends. Each bend has bend, signed angle, radius, k_factor, allowance, direction (up when its inside is on the viewed side, otherwise down), centerlines at u = BA/2 and tangents at u = 0 and u = BA, each line clipped to the bend’s remaining material. A sheet without a body or sheet state at the marker gives status: "unavailable"; an invalid sheet, a stale or inconsistent development, a self-overlap or a developed solid that does not build gives invalid; a later failure that blocks the sheet gives blocked. They return diagnostics and no regions, so nothing can be exported from them. For an invalid or blocked sheet the one diagnostic says why in words, as a sheet feature on that sheet does (mitcad#1636): the feature that took the sheet meaning away by its name, its reason and a pointer to Sheet Cut (this body is no longer sheet metal: Extrude3 changed it in a way its sheet metal cannot hold (it adds material where it crosses a bend); to cut across bends, use Sheet Cut instead), or the feature that failed on a blocked sheet (this body's sheet metal is blocked: Move1 failed on it), without internal ids; the browser’s Flat Pattern row shows it. The sheet’s stored diagnostics with the features’ ids are its causes (feature, message), for agents. Every other diagnostic is in words too (mitcad#1639): the body is “this body”, the walls a failed development names are named by their features as the timeline names them (SheetFlange3, SheetFlange3 (wall 2), SheetFlange1 (bend)), the feature of an overlay by its name; the same diagnostics with the ids (body F3.b0 has no Flat Pattern, panel F6 slot 0 does not develop flat: …) are its details, given only where they differ. Omitting body lists every item. Repeated queries reuse the evaluation while the sheet state, rules, settings and algorithm are unchanged.

{"query":"flat_point","body":"F3.b0","flat":[2.8,10]}
{"query":"flat_point","body":"F3.b0","model":[3.5,10,-0.5]}

flat_point maps a drawing position to the body (model, on the front surface), or a point of the body (inside its material) to the drawing (flat), both with the domain, its chart coordinates and the material depth from the front surface. A point outside the material fails. Both queries are available through MCP’s read-only query interface. The DXF export and what the command UI asks follow (mitcad#210).

Sheet-metal command UI and Flat Pattern DXF

What the Sheet Metal commands, the browser and the export use (mitcad#210; the application’s side in app/COMMANDS.md).

A Face with rules of its own 

{"cmd":"add_feature","def":{"type":"sheet_face",
 "profiles":[{"sketch":"F1","region":"r{c1[c4,c2],c2[c1,c3],c3[c2,c4],c4[c3,c1]}"}],
 "rules":{"thickness":"2 mm","bend_radius":"1 mm","allowance":{"type":"k_factor","k":0.44},
          "reference_side":"front","bend_relief":{"type":"round","width":1,"depth":2},
          "corner_relief":{"type":"round","width":1,"depth":2}}}}

In add_feature and its preview, a sheet_face whose rules is a rules definition (type sheet_rules may be left out) adds a sheet_rules feature just before the Face and the Face using it: one undo step named after the Face (Add SheetFace1), one recompute, the Face’s uid and name and the new rules uid in the answer. The preview evaluates both on a copy and reports the Face. A saved Face always refers to its rules by uid; edit_feature takes no inline rules (editing the rules is editing their feature, which every Face using them follows).

Picks as semantic references 

{"query":"sheet_reference","body":"F3.b0","face":"F3:sheet_side0(F2:sheet_curve(c2[c1,c3]))"}
{"query":"sheet_reference","body":"F3.b0","edge":"E{F3:sheet_front(0)|F3:sheet_side0(F2:sheet_curve(c2[c1,c3]))}","at":[5,10,0]}
{"query":"sheet_seam","body":"F3.b0","stationary":{"feature":"F3","slot":0},"moving":{"feature":"F3","slot":1}}

sheet_reference names what a face or edge of a sheet body picked in the view stands for. Sheet faces are named by their domains: sheet_front(<slot>) and sheet_back for a panel, sheet_bend_front/sheet_bend_back for a bend, and sheet_side<slot>(<curve>) (sheet_bend_side on a bend) for the wall along a boundary curve, whose key is <S>:sheet_curve(<segment>) for a sketch curve or <G>:sheet_curve(<slot>) for a generated one. The answer has body and domain ({kind, id}); a wall, or the edge between a wall and its own panel’s surface, adds boundary (the Flange/Bend form {panel, curve, piece?}), pieces (how many pieces of the curve the panel has) and straight; the edge between two walls of one panel adds corner (the Corner Round/Chamfer form, incoming and outgoing in the contour’s direction, with pieces when the curves have several) and straight. When a curve has several pieces, at (a point of the pick in the body’s coordinates) chooses the nearest; without it piece is left out and the feature reports the ambiguity. The kernel joins the coplanar caps of panels that meet at a seam into one face named after one of them: on a panel’s surface, an at outside the named panel’s material that lies on another panel’s surface picks that panel. A face of another kind, a domain the sheet does not have or a body that is no sheet at the marker fail. sheet_seam gives the two boundaries of the registered seam two panels share (a coplanar seam a Bend can fold), stationary first; none or several fail.

The edges of stored corners (mitcad#1766) 

{"query":"sheet_corner_edges","body":"F3.b0","corners":[{"panel":{"feature":"F6","slot":0},
 "incoming":{"type":"generated","feature":"F6","slot":53},
 "outgoing":{"type":"sketch","sketch":"F5","segment":"c2[c1,c3]"}}]}

sheet_corner_edges gives the thickness edge each corner of a sheet_corner_round or sheet_corner_chamfer (the form sheet_reference answers, pieces included) lies on in the body at the marker, in the corners’ order: {"body": "F3.b0", "edges": ["E{F6:sheet_bend_side0(F6:sheet_curve(40))|F6:sheet_side0(F5:sheet_curve(c2[c1,c3]))}"]}. It is the body’s edge between a wall along one of the corner’s curves and another wall, of the same panel for a corner between two walls or the side of a bend for a corner beside a bend (mitcad#1765, whose tangent line to the bend has no wall), that sheet_reference names as that corner (the edge’s middle choosing among pieces). A corner the body has no edge for is null: one the feature’s own round or bevel took away (asked after it), or curves that no longer meet. Where the kernel lists no edge between two walls of the body, a corner between two walls is the edge named after the walls of its curves. A body that is no sheet at the marker fails, as for sheet_reference. The command UI asks it when it edits a Corner Round or Corner Chamfer, once the timeline is rolled back to the feature, so the view highlights the corners where the feature finds them (app/COMMANDS.md). It is an MCP read-only query.

Sheet bodies for the browser

{"query":"sheet_bodies"} lists every sheet-metal body at the marker: body, name, status, rules and rules_name, the resolved thickness, bend_radius and k_factor, the numbers of panels, bends and open bends, and flat_pattern: null without an item, else its status (with area and bends when valid, diagnostics otherwise: the reason in words, as flat_pattern gives it), shown, stationary and reference_side.

Showing the Flat Pattern

set_flat_pattern takes shown (default: as before, false for a new item): the application then shows the developed solid in place of the folded body. It is a display choice saved with the item (flat_patterns[].shown): an undo step labelled Show Flat Pattern or Show Folded Body that evaluates nothing again (it is not part of the evaluation’s fingerprint). The solid comes from analysis_shape {"shape":"flat_pattern","body":"F3.b0"}, in the body’s coordinates (the fixed panel where it is folded); null for a pattern that is not valid.

DXF export 

{"cmd":"export_flat_pattern_dxf","body":"F3.b0","path":"flat.dxf",
 "units":"mm","version":"r2000","tangents":false,"reference_side":"front"}

Writes the body’s (uid or name) Flat Pattern to a .dxf file: the item’s settings, or those a new item would get when the body has none (its lowest panel, the panel’s x axis, the front); reference_side views the other side for this file only. Only a valid pattern is written; an invalid, blocked or unavailable one fails with its reasons and writes nothing. The refusal a person reads names the body as the browser does, or says “this body” or “this sheet” when it has no name at the marker, never by its uid (mitcad#1639, the rule of mitcad#1327): the Flat Pattern of Bracket is invalid: this body is no longer sheet metal: Scale1 changed it …; its detail for agents (the text after the error’s [placed: …] line) has the body’s uid, the reasons with their ids and each cause as [F5: …]. The Flat Pattern’s own refusals (set_flat_pattern, remove_flat_pattern) do the same (Bracket has no Flat Pattern, the chosen fixed panel is not a panel of Bracket). The drawing is made from the evaluated outline and bend lines, never from the solid: each cut contour once (no front/back duplicates), with consecutive pieces of one line or circle that chart seams split joined again (a straight edge across a bend is one LINE, a hole one CIRCLE); exact arcs, ellipses and splines are kept.

LayerEntitiesColour
CUT_OUTERthe exterior contour7
CUT_INNERholes and other inner contours6
BEND_UPcentre lines (u = BA/2) of bends whose inside is on the viewed side3
BEND_DOWNcentre lines of the other bends1
BEND_TANGENTwith tangents: lines at u = 0 and u = BA8

All four (five) layers are declared even when empty. Coordinates are the pattern’s frame (the fixed panel’s material axes on the viewed side; back mirrors x), so the drawing stays put when the body is edited, and are written in units (the design’s length unit when left out, mitcad#1408; mm, cm, m, in, ft and the other units set_units reads; unit is its older name) with $INSUNITS and $MEASUREMENT set (DXF units). version is r2000 (default) or r12. The answer has path, body, unit and units (both the unit written), stationary, reference_side, entities, layers (name, entities), bends (up, down) and bounds (in the unit). mitcad-cli export-flat runs it; MCP’s model_export takes format: "dxf" with flat_pattern (the body) instead of sketch. The sheet_reference, sheet_seam and sheet_bodies queries are MCP read-only queries, and the sheet feature types and set_flat_pattern/remove_flat_pattern are MCP model commands.

Bend table export 

{"cmd":"export_bend_table","body":"F3.b0","path":"bends.csv",
 "format":"csv","reference_side":"front"}

Writes a UTF-8 CSV or JSON file from the same evaluated Flat Pattern as the DXF export, including its fixed panel and viewed side. An explicit reference_side applies only to this export. The command accepts a body uid or name. Without format, a .json path selects JSON and other paths select CSV. An invalid or blocked sheet gives the Flat Pattern’s refusal.

Each centre-line piece is a row. A cut-out that splits a bend gives multiple rows with the same bend id. The columns carry the body and rule names, thickness, K-factor, bend id, signed rotation from flat, direction from the viewed side, inside radius, allowance, line length, start and end coordinates, and the included angle between the two sides. Lengths are in millimetres and angles in degrees, as the names thickness_mm and angle_deg indicate. The JSON file has the number of written bends and a rows array whose bend preserves the Flat Pattern’s {feature, slot} id. CSV uses feature:slot for that id. Its text fields are quoted and a leading apostrophe protects names that a spreadsheet could read as formulas. The result gives path, body, format, reference_side, bends (the number of distinct written bends) and rows (the number of line pieces). This is a file IO command.

Design policy

Every owner, the root and each component, has a policy of nine settings of its own (mitcad#220, core/model/src/policy.rs, core/model/src/document/policy.rs); nothing is inherited through the hierarchy. A policy governs new actions only: changing it never deletes, moves, detaches or recomputes anything, and what breaks it is reported as a violation.

The general defaults allow everything (mitcad#421): every setting is true, so a design is a hybrid of parts and assemblies, and the part and assembly presets are the stricter choices.

SettingAllowsGeneral default
sketchescreating or moving sketches directly into the ownertrue
featurescreating or moving modelling features directly into ittrue
componentscreating, inserting, pasting or moving components directly under ittrue
attach_to_othersits sketches on another owner’s face or planetrue
attachments_from_othersother owners’ sketches on its faces and planestrue
first_sketch_attachesits first sketch on another owner’s face or plane, also when attach_to_others is false (mitcad#293)true
first_sketch_attachments_from_othersother owners’ first sketches on its faces and planes, also when attachments_from_others is false (mitcad#293)true
reference_othersits sketches and features referencing other owners’ geometrytrue
references_from_othersother owners referencing its geometrytrue
  • Containment. A sketch counts under sketches only; a child occurrence (also one a feature makes: Component from Bodies, a new component operation, a pattern of occurrences) under components. Assembly features that arrange occurrences (joints, as-built joints, joint origins, rigid groups, assembly constraints, occurrence moves, captured positions, patterns at points) are not modelling features.
  • Sketch attachment is a sketch’s plane_link to another owner: both the sketch’s owner’s attach_to_others and the other owner’s attachments_from_others must allow it. It is not also checked by the reference settings. An owner’s first sketch (a sketch of the owner that no other sketch or modelling feature of the same owner precedes in the timeline) may also attach when the sketch’s owner has first_sketch_attaches and the other owner first_sketch_attachments_from_others (mitcad#293): on each side either of its two settings allows it. So under the part preset a new component can start with a sketch on another component’s face. Later sketches follow the first pair only. When both settings of a side are off for a first sketch, the violation and the refusal name the first-sketch setting (… does not allow its first sketch to attach to other components, … does not allow first sketches of other components to attach to it). Reordering or deleting follows the usual rules: a sketch that stops being the first, and so breaks the policy, is a violation (refused by a command, listed and counted, never detached).
  • References are every other link to another owner’s geometry: linked projections, an extrusion’s or revolution’s object_links, a combine’s tools in occurrences, a combine’s or split’s tool_links, a sweep’s body_links and a construction plane’s, axis’s or point’s links and datum_links. The consumer’s reference_others and the source’s references_from_others must allow them. An unlinked projection ("linked": false) keeps no link and is never refused. Joints and assembly constraints are not governed by the reference settings.
  • Same-owner attachments and references are never governed.

Presets. hybrid (Hybrid in the application): the general defaults, everything allowed; defaults, its name before mitcad#421, is accepted as an alias. part: sketches and features, no components; assembly: no sketches or features, components allowed. part and assembly refuse sketch attachment in both directions, except first sketches (part: both first-sketch settings on; assembly: first_sketch_attaches off, as it has no sketches, and first_sketch_attachments_from_others on), and allow references in both directions. A preset is only a set of values; a policy without sketches is recognised as assembly whatever its first_sketch_attaches.

New designs (Document::new_design, the bridge’s new_design_document, File > New, MCP’s document_create and the live document_new, a project’s new_design) start with the root and an empty component Component1, active, both with the general defaults (mitcad#421): the first sketch or feature goes into Component1, Component1 takes components, and a component’s sketches may lie on Component1’s faces. Component1 is named as any new component is (Component1, Component2, …; mitcad#711): designs made before keep their Part1, as the name is stored in the file. Neither policy is stored, as they are the defaults. They are in millimetres unless made in another unit (Document::new_design_in, New designs in other units). Document::new (and so the importers and mitcad-cli) has the general defaults everywhere. Components get the general defaults when made (create_component takes policy, a preset name or settings; the application’s New Component, the command and the browser’s, gives none); copies (Paste New, Make Unique, an unlinked insert) keep their source’s policy and an inserted design brings its root’s; a new component that Move Features into a Component makes keeps the link settings of the owner the features came from, with containment allowed.

Existing designs (mitcad#421). The file format did not change. A stored policy (root_policy, a component’s policy: written whenever it differed from the general defaults of its time, so every part and assembly and every changed setting) keeps its values. An owner without a stored policy reads the general defaults of now, everything allowed: the root and Part1 of a design made before mitcad#421 kept the presets they were saved with, and an attachment that broke the old defaults (attach_to_others and attachments_from_others false) is no longer a violation. Nothing is recomputed, moved or detached when a design is opened; the policy governs new actions only.

Enforcement. Every JSON command and preview (Document::command, run_script, preview, the bridge’s add_base_feature) is checked: the change is computed on a copy of the definition and refused, with the reason, when it adds a violation, before anything is evaluated or committed. Violations are counted per owner, setting, object and owner on the other side, so editing an existing sketch or feature that breaks a setting is allowed, a new link of it that breaks one is not, and removing violations always is. Moves (move_to_component, also into an existing component), pastes, inserts and new components are covered by the same check: a move that would put a sketch where sketches are refused, or change which owner an existing link reaches into one that refuses it, is refused atomically. Importers that call the model directly replay a file as it is and are not checked (Document::without_policy_checks around commands they run). Activating an owner is always allowed; nothing is redirected into another component, except a new component (below).

A new component beside a part (mitcad#292). A new component that would go under an owner whose policy has components false, from create_component (New Component, also the browser’s on a part) or from a feature’s new-component operation (add_feature, and edit_feature when the edit makes the component), is placed instead in the nearest owner above it that takes components: along the owner’s first occurrence path from the root, its parent, then that one’s parent, up to the root. The new occurrence’s transform composes the owner’s placement in that owner (at the marker) with the one asked for, so nothing moves; a feature itself stays in its own component, with the same geometry, and only its component’s parent changes. The reply names where it went: placed_in (that owner), instead_of (the refusing owner) and placement_warning, the text the application shows as a hint (Bracket does not take components (its policy): New Component made in Assembly instead, or …: Extrude3's new component made in …). It is one undo step, and the active component follows the usual rule (the new component when create_component activates it). When no owner above takes components, the command is refused as before, with that reason. Commands run without policy checks (importers) place it where asked. Under the general defaults every owner takes components, so this happens only below an owner set to part or with components turned off (mitcad#421).

CommandFieldsResult
set_policycomponent (uid or name; the active one when left out), preset (optional, applied first), policy (optional: settings to change, the others stay)component, policy

set_policy is one undo step named Policy of <name> that recomputes nothing.

QueryFieldsResult
policycomponent (default: the active one), preset and policy (optional: report as if set)component, name, active, policy (the nine settings and preset: hybrid, part, assembly or null), settings: per setting in the order above setting, allowed, count, items (each type: sketch, feature or occurrence, uid, name, component, component_name, others: uid, name of the owners on the other side); refusals: for each blocked containment setting the reason a new object is refused
policiesevery owner: component, name, policy, violations (count)
sketch_supportscomponent (default: the active one)component; denied: owners whose faces and planes its next sketch (made at the marker; while the component has no sketch or modelling feature before the marker, its first, and the first-sketch settings apply) cannot be attached to, component, name, reason; denied_paths: the occurrence paths (O1/O4, "" for the root) that show them, with the reason; sketches: the reason the component refuses sketches, or null

Violations list each object once per setting: for containment the objects directly in the owner (not the whole subtree), for attachments and references the consumer sketch or feature (not each projected edge), with the owners on the other side. The components query includes each component’s policy, and the design file stores root_policy and a component’s policy when they are not the general defaults (missing settings are their general default, true; a stored policy has every setting except, when stored before mitcad#293, the two first-sketch settings, which then read as on). The application leaves denied geometry out of sketch-plane picking and its hover highlight (app/COMMANDS.md, “Design policy”). set_policy is an MCP model command and the three queries are MCP read-only queries. Tests: core/model-tests/assembly/src/policy_tests.rs.

Equal spacing in sketches

An equal spacing (mitcad#221) keeps the successive intervals between independent sketch objects equal: one constraint, without copies, construction lines or chains of dimensions, and without binding the objects’ sizes or shapes. Code in core/sketch/src/spacing.rs; the solver’s EqualSpacing and Spacing equations (core/solver/README.md).

{"id": "k4", "type": "equal_spacing", "anchors": ["p1", "c2", "c5", "c9"],
 "mode": "along", "direction": "c12"}
{"id": "k5", "type": "spacing", "constraint": "k4", "value": "d3"}

  • anchors (at least three, in order): a point p<n>, a circle or an arc c<n> (its centre), a line c<n> (its midpoint). Nothing else is an anchor (no centres of ellipses, splines or boxes); two anchors for the same point (a circle and its centre) are refused. As with any constraint on an arc’s centre, a moved centre leaves the arc’s ends where the solve can keep them: a radius dimension keeps its size.

  • mode: what equal intervals mean between A-B, B-C, C-D (successive anchors only, never every pair):

    ModeEqual quantity
    horizontalsuccessive x offsets
    verticalsuccessive y offsets
    alongsuccessive offsets projected on the direction of the line direction (kept as a reference, so the spacing follows the line when it turns)
    point_to_pointthe distances between successive anchors (a chain; it may bend)

    The directional modes compare signed offsets, so the stored order holds; nothing across their direction is constrained, and a point-to-point chain is not made straight. Alignment is a separate constraint.

  • The common spacing is free unless one spacing dimension (dimensions[k5].spacing, positive, a value or an expression like any dimension) drives it: every interval is that value; no interval is a master and no other interval has a dimension. A driven spacing dimension measures it. At most one per constraint; removing it leaves the intervals equal with a free size; removing the constraint removes it too.

  • Order: stored, and never sorted again by later geometry edits (a drag stretches the row as it is). A new or edited horizontal, vertical or along spacing is sorted along its direction unless keep_order; two anchors at the same place along it (within a millionth of the row) are refused, naming them, so the caller gives their order. A point_to_point chain takes the order given.

  • Deleting an anchor’s entity takes it out of the chain (the others keep their order and its neighbours become successive); a chain left with fewer than three anchors, or without its direction line, is removed with its dimension. No anchor reference is left dangling.

  • Refused, with nothing changed: anchors that are all instances (originals or copies) of one sketch pattern (its spacing governs them: sketch.edit_pattern), and, like other constraints and driving dimensions, a spacing the other constraints already imply (redundant) or contradict (conflicting).

  • A copy (sketch.move with copy) of all the anchors copies the constraint among the copies (a turned copy drops a horizontal or vertical one).

CommandFieldsNotes
sketch.add_equal_spacinganchors, mode, direction (a line, for along), keep_order (default false), dimension (default false), spacing (a value), driven (default false), text [x, y]the constraint and, with dimension, spacing or driven, its common spacing dimension (driving with spacing, else with the mean of the current intervals; driven with driven), in one undo step Equal Spacing in Sketch1; result as other edits, made [the constraint’s id]
sketch.edit_equal_spacingconstraint (k4), and any of anchors, mode, direction, keep_orderthe members, their order, the mode or the direction; what is not given stays, a directional spacing is sorted again unless keep_order; its dimension stays and keeps driving; undo step Edit Equal Spacing in Sketch1

sketch.add_dimension with {"type": "spacing", "constraint": "k4"} adds the common spacing to an existing equal spacing (measured: its first interval), sketch.set_dimension changes it and sketch.remove removes it, as for any dimension.

Classes of commands and queries

Every command, query and feature type of this API has a class (mitcad#265, classes.rs): what it works on besides the document’s data. External clients allow and refuse by the class, not by lists of names of their own: the MCP server (docs/mcp.md, headless and live) runs the model class and refuses the others.

ClassWhatCommands and queries
modelthe document’s own dataevery feature type (add_feature, edit_feature), the sketch commands but sketch.import_dxf, parameters, bodies’ attributes, components, joints, configurations, views, analyses, groups, policy, undo, redo, merge_undo, recompute; every query but those below
file IOreads or writes filesimport_file, export, export_sketch, export_flat_pattern_dxf, export_bend_table, export_drawing, sketch.import_dxf, insert_component, update_links, mark_saved (the design file’s saved state); the queries dxf_info and compare_step
remotethe library resolver’s repositoriesupdate_library_parts
internalthe application’s own workflowsbegin_command, restore_command, discard_command (a command panel’s checkpoints), clear_cache

Three commands are classified per call (classes::command_class_with, mitcad#383): create_appearance, edit_appearance and set_render_settings are file IO by name, because a texture or an environment image may be read from its path, but a call that names no file is the model’s own and MCP runs it. A texture reads a file when its base colour image or one of its maps has neither data nor "embedded": true; a texture that is null or left out reads none; set_render_settings reads a file when environment.image is a path (null clears it). classes::file_path_read(request) gives the path, which the MCP server names in its refusal.

api::classes::command_class(name), query_class(name) and feature_class(type) give the class (none for a name the API lacks); external_command_allowed and external_query_allowed are the model class. A cache query with disk also reads the result store’s files: the MCP server refuses that form. The module’s tests read the command and query names from the API’s own enums and fail for one without a class, and for a classified name the API no longer has.

Body geometry in a sketch’s plane

{"query": "plane_geometry", "sketch": "F3"} (mitcad#256, document/plane_geometry.rs) lists the edges and vertices of the visible bodies before the sketch that lie in its plane, in sketch coordinates: what the sketch Dimension tool picks and the drawing tools snap to (mitcad#258, mitcad#1967), each projected (sketch.project, linked) only when a dimension or a point is made from it. The answer is an array:

[{"source": "E{F2:end(r{…})|F2:side(c1[c4,c2])}", "body": "F2.b0", "kind": "line",
  "geometry": {"start": [-30, -20], "end": [30, -20]}},
 {"source": "V{F2:end(r{…})|F2:side(c1[c4,c2])|F2:side(c2[c1,c3])}", "body": "F2.b0",
  "kind": "vertex", "geometry": {"at": [30, -20]}}]
  • source, body and occurrence are what sketch.project takes to project the item; occurrence (the occurrence path from the root, as in Geometry of other components) only for a body of another component, which counts at each occurrence that shows it, moved into the sketch’s coordinates, and only when the design policy lets the sketch reference that component’s geometry. The sketch’s own component’s bodies come once, without occurrence.
  • kind: vertex (geometry.at), or the sketch entity type the edge projects to, line, circle, arc, ellipse, elliptical_arc or spline, with geometry as the sketch query gives a curve’s (a circle’s or an arc’s center is where a centre pick lies).
  • An edge counts when every point of it is in the plane within the model’s linear tolerance (1e-6 times the body’s size, at least 1e-6 mm): a line’s ends, a conic as a whole (an arc of a circle that leaves the plane meets it in two points only), a B-spline’s poles. Edges the kernel names none for are left out. A vertex counts when its point is in the plane.
  • The kernel lists a body’s named edges with their curves at once, by index (Kernel::named_edge_curves, mitcad#1656: what Kernel::curves_of gives for each edge’s name, without resolving the names back; a kernel without it lists Kernel::edges and asks Kernel::curves_of each name), and its vertices with their names and points (Kernel::indexed_element); the coplanarity test is the model’s. A body whose bounding box does not reach the plane is skipped. Its enclosing box (Kernel::enclosing_box, cheap and kept by the shape) is tested first: one that stays off the plane by its own tolerance needs no tight box, which the kernel works out at a cost on first use (seconds for an assembly of hundreds of bodies); the answer is the same, since the tight box lies inside it (cli.plane_geometry_bodies compares both forms with the answers before mitcad#1656).
  • Visibility is the model’s (the body and every occurrence on its path shown, as the instances query’s visible); Hide Above Sketch only cuts what the view draws, so the edges in the plane stay in the answer.

Out of the plane

With "out_of_plane": true (mitcad#866, the sketch Dimension tool) the answer also lists every other named edge and vertex of the same bodies, after the items in the plane (which come first, as without it). Each is what sketch.project makes of it: projected onto the plane along its normal, kind and geometry as above (a line as its line, a circle in a parallel plane as its circle, a tilted one as an ellipse or a line, a vertex as its point), and an edge along the normal (seen end on: a line whose projection has no length) as kind point with geometry.at. Each also has:

{"source": "E{…}", "body": "F2.b0", "kind": "line",
 "geometry": {"start": [30, -20], "end": [30, 20]},
 "in_plane": false, "height": -10,
 "path": [[30, -20, -10], [30, 20, -10]]}
  • in_plane: false (the items in the plane have no such field);
  • path: where it is, for a client that picks it where the view shows it: its points in sketch coordinates with their height above the plane along its normal (negative below), from its start to its end: a line’s two ends, 25 points of a conic, a helix or a B-spline (its poles when its knots do not fit), a vertex’s one point;
  • height: a vertex’s height, a conic’s centre’s, else that of the middle of path (where a client shows a circle’s centre).

The bounding box test that skips a body is not made in this form; the enclosing box still saves a tight box for a body that stays off the plane. A job the query runs in stops between bodies when it is cancelled (the application reads this form off the UI thread, mitcad#1656).

The visible bodies are those the view shows: a body hidden by its light bulb or by one of an occurrence above it is left out, and so is one that Isolate (set_isolation) leaves out of the view (mitcad#1702, GitHub #254: the Dimension tool hovered and picked edges of components Isolate hid), the sketch’s own component’s included when the isolation leaves it out. Isolate and Unisolate change the bodies looked at, so the key too.

Tests: core/model-tests/analysis/src/plane_geometry_tests.rs, cli.isolated_sketch_geometry_reported (the reported design under MITCAD_MITCAD_REPORTED).

Angle dimensions

An angle dimension between the lines a and b (mitcad#296) measures one of the four sectors the two lines’ extensions make where they meet, from 0 to 180 degrees. reverse_a and reverse_b say which: the sector between the rays a.end - a.start and b.end - b.start, each reversed where its field is true. The sector’s angle is what the dimension measures and the solver holds: a new value keeps the side, also one closer to the other angle. Reversing both rays gives the opposite sector (the same angle); reversing one, a neighbouring sector (the supplement).

  • Sketch Dimension sends both fields, from the sector the value is placed in: cursor - corner = s (a.end - a.start) + t (b.end - b.start), reverse_a = s < 0, reverse_b = t < 0.
  • Without either field (sketches stored before, sketch.chamfer’s angle, commands that give neither), the dimension measures the angle between the directions when driven, and a driving one the angle between the directions or its supplement, whichever is closer to its value where the lines are when the sketch is solved, as before. One field alone counts as the other false. The sketch query and saved files give the fields only when the dimension has them.
  • Clean Up Projections keeps the side when a line is replaced by one running the other way (the replaced line’s field is flipped).
  • The .f3d and .ipt imports set both from the file: the sector its value is shown in (textPosition) when that sector’s angle is the file’s value (within 0.001 rad), else the neighbouring sector nearer to the text when the supplement is (without a text position, the sector between the directions or a neighbour of it); without a value, or with neither angle being it, none (as before).

Tests: core/model-tests/sketch/src/sketch_tests.rs (an_angle_dimension_*), core/sketch/src/tests.rs, core/model-tests/sketch-refs/src/projection_tests.rs, core/import/src/tests/constraint_tests.rs, tools/ui-sketch-angle-test.sh.

Tangent chains

{"query": "tangent_chains", "body": "F2.b0"} (mitcad#290) gives the tangent chains of a body at the timeline marker: what a pick takes with Tangent Chain on, so that the application’s hover can show it before the click (Kernel::tangent_chains, geometry/include/mitcad/geometry/tangent_chain.hpp).

FieldsResult
bodykind edges, chains: the groups of two or more edges (names) that a fillet or chamfer with a tangent chain rounds together when one of them is selected
body, faces: truekind faces, chains: the groups of two or more faces (each by its first name) that a shell, draft or replace face with a tangent chain takes together
body, edge (or face)chain: the chain that holds the edge (face), or the edge (face) alone; count: its length. An edge or face the body lacks is an error; a missing edge’s error lists existing edges that share a face with it (Suggestions for an edge that is not found)
  • Every edge and face is in at most one chain; one in none stands alone.
  • An edge chain is the dressups’ own (fillet, chamfer): an edge continues into every edge that meets it end to end in the same direction (within 0.01 rad) and lies between faces at an angle, and on from those, until the chain closes or stops. It stops where the edges turn, as the fillet’s contour does (mitcad#241), and where a concave edge meets a convex one (mitcad#439). A rounding with a variable radius, an asymmetric one or one of curvature continuous (G2) cross-sections follows the geometry kernel’s own chain instead, which can be shorter (it also stops at a vertex where a third sharp edge meets). An edge between tangent faces (no dressup rounds it) is in no chain.
  • A face chain is the faces connected through smooth edges (the faces meet at less than 0.001 rad along the whole edge), as the face tools grow their selections.
  • The chains are worked out for the whole body at once, so a client asks once per body and looks each hovered item up; the application does so per command run (app/COMMANDS.md, withHoverChain).

Join tolerance of imported designs

A design the .f3d import made (import_f3d) has a join tolerance: the import’s geometric tolerance (geometric_tolerance, default 0.01 mm, mitcad#224, mitcad#298). The bodies it keeps match the file’s within that tolerance (mitcad#285), so a tool the file joins to a body can miss the replay’s body by a few micrometres, touch it only along an edge, or meet it on a face so nearly coincident that the exact join’s result is invalid. With a join tolerance, the joins of the features that apply a tool (extrusions, revolutions, sweeps, lofts, base features, primitives and patterns; Kernel::join_within) are widened only where the exact join fails:

  • a tool that touches no target joins the targets within the tolerance;
  • a tool solid the exact join leaves on its own beside a target within the tolerance is merged with it;
  • a join whose result is invalid is tried again;
  • a join that builds no solid of the targets, or leaves faces unused or loose beside its solids (OCCT cannot orient them: a tool against a stored body’s rounded wall, mitcad#235), is tried again, and a fuzzy value is taken only where it builds solids of the targets with every face;
  • a join that leaves more edges shorter than 1e-5 mm than its operands had (two vertices a micrometre apart kept apart, as where a sketch’s tangent point is found a micrometre along a wall, mitcad#326) is tried again until it leaves no more.

Each takes the smallest fuzzy value that works (1e-5 mm, then 3 and 10 times each power of ten up to the tolerance). A join that works exactly is the exact one, and tools farther away stay apart. The design file keeps it as "join_tolerance" (mm; left out without one), so a saved import recomputes the same; a design made in MitCad has none and its joins are exact. Rust: Document::join_tolerance, Document::set_join_tolerance (one undo step, part of the import’s own). Tests: core.model (document::import_notes), core/import (tests.rs), geometry (test_boolean.cpp).

Cuts within the join tolerance of imported designs

The cuts of the features that apply a tool in an imported design with a join tolerance (above) are widened alike where the exact cut fails (Kernel::cut_within, mitcad#235): a cut of a body that gives an error, an invalid result, a result whose solids could not be built with all their faces, or one with pieces of the tool left inside it (where the section edges of neighbouring faces of a body kept within the tolerance end micrometres apart and the tool lies on a face of the body, OCCT’s boolean leaves faces out or puts the tool’s pieces inside) is tried again with the smallest fuzzy value, as above, that gives a valid result of all its faces. A cut that works exactly is the exact one. Tests: core/import (tests.rs), and the named parts of mitcad#235.

Joins that lose volume (mitcad#964)

A union never holds less than the bodies it joins, so a join of a feature’s tool whose result holds less volume than a target it merged (by more than a millionth of the target’s box, measured on the faces the two do not share) is wrong, with or without a join tolerance: it is tried again with the smallest fuzzy value from 1e-5 mm (up to the join tolerance where the design has one) whose result merges every target and loses none. Where none does, the exact result stands. Found on a reported FreeCAD model: OCCT’s exact join of a pad flush with two tangent walls of the body (its faces merged by the earlier joins and cuts) took the pad’s overlap with the body away; a fuzzy value of 1e-5 mm gives the union. A join that holds its targets is the exact one. Test: geometry (test_boolean.cpp, test_join_that_loses_volume_is_retried, on that model’s two bodies from MITCAD_GEOMETRY_CASES; no synthetic layout reproduced OCCT’s failure).

Combine’s joins within the join tolerance; the .rvt import’s tolerance

A design the .rvt import made (import_rvt, mitcad#397) has a join tolerance too, the default geometric tolerance (0.01 mm): its rebuilt elements meet in the faces the file keeps of them, which can lie on each other only within a micrometre (a rail’s sloped elliptical piece and the level arc after it, their joint faces 1.2 µm apart). In a design with a join tolerance a Combine’s join (Kernel::unite_within) is widened alike: a union whose result is invalid is tried again with the smallest fuzzy value, as above, that gives a valid one; a union that works exactly is the exact one. Tests: core.model (document::import_notes), core/import-rvt (tests/corpus/rvt_rails.rs).

Two more repairs of the geometry kernel’s results apply to every design (mitcad#235):

  • A cut that removes nothing from a body with a cylindrical or conical face whose seam steps (a face merged from two whose seams lay apart, joined along an arc of the circle between them) is tried again on the body with that face rebuilt with one straight seam, the boundary edge the seam crosses split in the neighbouring face too; the faces keep their names. OCCT’s cut of a thread’s helix removed nothing from such a bore. Test: geometry (test_boolean.cpp).
  • A rounding’s or chamfer’s result whose vertex tolerances OCCT inflated far beyond what the vertices’ edges need (above 1 mm and ten times it) has them cut down to that; where the result is not valid without them (a corner left open behind a tolerance of hundreds of millimetres) the rounding fails instead of handing the later booleans a body they build nothing from. Test: geometry (test_fillet_results.cpp).

Extrude’s automatic operation

Extrude previews can suggest an operation from where the tool lies (mitcad#289, mitcad#575; the app: app/COMMANDS.md, Extrude). The preview of an add_feature or edit_feature asks for it with "auto_operation": true (optional, false by default). The application asks it only for a new extrusion: while it follows the suggestion, and, after the user chose the operation, with the preview of a direction flip, whose failure then tries the suggested operation (mitcad#2216). An edited one keeps its stored operation (mitcad#868), so it sends no auto_operation with an edit_feature; the model still answers one that does. A failed preview of def (a Join or Cut that reaches no body) still carries the suggestion:

{"cmd": "add_feature", "auto_operation": true,
 "def": {"type": "extrude", "profiles": [...], "extent": {"type": "distance", "distance": -5},
         "operation": "new_body"}}

An edit uses the same response field:

{"cmd": "edit_feature", "uid": "F4", "auto_operation": true,
 "def": {"type": "extrude", "profiles": [...], "extent": {"type": "distance", "distance": -5},
         "operation": "join"}}

The model evaluates the extrusion as a new body first (its tool does not depend on the operation, and a Cut that reaches nothing makes none), tries the tool against the visible bodies of the feature’s owning component, and then evaluates def as it is; the report is def’s, with

"auto_operation": {"operation": "cut", "objects": ["F2.b0"]}
  • cut with the bodies the tool goes into: the inside of a solid of the tool is inside the body (a profile on a body’s face extruded into it);
  • else join with the bodies it touches or overlaps (extruded away from the face); a tool that touches a body only along an edge or at a point is suggested join too, and that join then makes the tool a body of its own and warns (extrude, mitcad#2127);
  • else new_body with no objects (nothing near, an empty design, hidden bodies, other components’ bodies).

An addition considers bodies at the current marker. An edit considers the bodies strictly before the edited feature’s timeline position, regardless of the current marker: its own result and later features’ geometry and bodies never count. Visibility is the document’s current body visibility; the active component does not change the edited feature’s ownership. The returned geometry and retained preview are the ordinary def preview, including its stored participants or assembly Cut scope, even when the suggestion differs. Computing that suggestion changes no stored definition, marker, body result, revision or undo/redo step. A cancelled computation clears the preview and leaves the document unchanged.

The test is cheap enough to follow a dragged distance: bodies whose bounding boxes the tool’s does not reach are apart without more (Kernel::enclosing_box); the others get Kernel::tool_contacts, the contact test Join uses (geometry/include/mitcad/geometry/contact.hpp) and a point inside each solid of the tool classified against the body. Only extrusion previews answer it; other feature types return their normal preview without auto_operation. The suggestion is optional report data: the application decides whether to follow it, and the stored definition is always the one explicitly committed.

BUILD: profile assemblies

The BUILD tab (mitcad#375; the app: app/COMMANDS.md, BUILD) places library parts with a build block (docs/libraries.md): slot profiles, connectors and their nuts and screws, panels and linear parts. Everything it makes is ordinary design content: components, occurrences, features, joints and parameters on the one timeline, editable with every other command. What is new is a part’s source, kept once in the design; the derived part a placed part’s body is made from; the bound length; and the commands and queries below. Code: core/model-build/src/ (placement rules, junctions, cut list), core/model/src/build/ (what the design file keeps), features/derived_part.rs, features/bound_length.rs, api/build.rs; tests core/model-tests/build-frames/, core/model-tests/build-timber/, tools/cli/tests/build_*.json, tools/ui-build-test.sh, and on the generated parts library the ctest build.profiles (tools/cli/build-profiles-test.cmake, with MITCAD_PROFILES_LIBRARY).

Sources 

"library_sources": [
  {"id": "S1",
   "library": {"library": "mitcad-parts", "url": "...", "rev": "<commit>", "label": "v1.0.0",
               "component": "p30x30-b8", "path": "profiles/p30x30-b8.mitcad",
               "license": "MIT", "authors": ["Mitcad contributors"]},
   "design": {"sha256": "..."},
   "build": {"role": "profile"},
   "supplier": "Motedis", "part_number": "P30_N8_B", "supplier_url": "https://..."}]

A design’s top-level library_sources (left out when empty) holds each library part that BUILD placed, once, whatever its configuration row or length. Each source has:

  • its id (S1);
  • the library record (as a component’s library, Library parts); its designation is the library’s pattern ({L} and the source’s other parameters in braces are replaced by each part’s values in mm), its config is left out (each derived part has its own row);
  • name and standard, the component’s in the library;
  • the part’s design text (in a project, a reference into the project’s store, like a base feature’s B-rep, {"sha256"}; inline {"sha256", "text"} in a single-file design). A hand-written file may give the design itself as an object in text and leave out sha256; a design whose B-rep data was in the library’s store is written as a single file with its data inside;
  • the manifest’s build, supplier, part_number and supplier_url as they were at that version.

A part without build can be a source too: the nuts, screws and clamps a connector or a panel brings are derived parts of their own sources.

A source is read from the library when it is first used (class remote, as insert_component with library). After that the design needs no library to open or recompute. A source that no derived part uses any more is removed with the last one, in the same edit; a source no derived part has used yet (one a file brings along) stays until one uses it and that one goes.

update_library_parts takes {"source": "S1", "rev": "..."} in its changes. The source takes the other version’s design and build, and every derived part made from it recomputes, in one undo step (Update Profile 30x30 B8 to v1.1.0). A change names a source or a component, not both; one command changes sources or components, not both; a source’s rows are its parts’ own (build_edit’s config). The library_parts query lists each source as an entry of parts with source, component (null), name, library (the record: library, url, rev, component, label, …), url, rev, label, designation (the pattern), build, supplier, part_number, supplier_url, config (null), version and uses (the derived parts).
