The design file keeps the design’s materials as "materials": [{"id", "name", "density", "appearance", "appearances", "filament", "slicer", "variants", "based_on", "class", "version", "origin"}] (fields left out when not set) and the components’ defaults as "component_materials": [{"component", "material"}], both left out when there are none (files without them have none); a body’s "material" may name either. Copies of components into another design bring the materials their bodies and components name (a different one of the same id gets another id, <id>_1) and the components’ defaults; a BUILD part brings a material of its library design. The comparison of versions lists the design’s materials by id and a component’s default material with the component.

Tests: material_tests (built-in ids and their looks, replace and keep, the design’s materials made, edited, deleted and taking a built-in’s place, components’ defaults up the occurrence path, the design file and the comparison), material::tests, tools/ui-material-test.sh (Material… in the context menus).

Print settings key map

MitCad’s keys of print settings, in three sets (mitcad#640; core/print-keys/src/): Print Printer (only what MitCad uses: bed_shape, bed_exclude_area, max_print_height, nozzle_diameter, filament_slots, printer_model, printer_settings_id), Print Process and Print Filament. A key is PrusaSlicer’s where PrusaSlicer has the setting, else Bambu Studio’s (else OrcaSlicer’s); one that would carry a vendor’s name gets a neutral one. Each has a type, a unit, choices, a plain name for the interface and, per slicer dialect (bambu_studio, orcaslicer, qidi_studio, prusaslicer, cura), the slicer’s key and how a value converts (percentages, ratios written as percentages, choices by meaning, percentages of another value resolved through their basis, yes/no, settings split over two keys, Cura’s bed by its sizes). The module documentation names the slicers’ sources it was built from and what the Bambu family’s loader needs to take a 3MF’s settings.

Categories (mitcad#655). Every key has one place in the settings form, the same in the material editor, the profile editor and Property Sets: a category of its set (a tab) and a group in it (a headed section), and is advanced or common. Advanced keys show only with Advanced on, or when an item sets them. The order of the categories, of the groups and of the keys in a group is the display order; the keys come in that order (by set, category and group, common keys first in each group), so that the application keeps no table of its own.

  • Printer: basic_information (groups printable_space, printer_presets), extruder (nozzle).
  • Process: quality (layer_height, line_width, seam, precision, ironing, wall_generator, order_and_flow, bridges_and_overhangs, travel), strength (walls, top_and_bottom_shells, sparse_infill, infill_details), speed (first_layer, other_layers, overhangs, slow_down_by_height, travel_speed, acceleration, jerk, smoothing), support (support, raft, contact_and_interface, support_body, tree_supports, support_filament, support_ironing), others (bed_adhesion, prime_tower, filaments, interlocking, special_modes, fuzzy_skin, gcode_output, process_presets).
  • Filament: filament (filament_basics, flow, nozzle_temperature, bed_temperature, chamber, volumetric_speed, scarf_seam, purge (Purge volumes), filament_presets), cooling (part_cooling_fan, slow_down_for_cooling, overhangs_and_bridges, auxiliary_fan, exhaust_fan), setting_overrides (retraction, toolchange_retraction, override_speed), advanced (filament_change, filament_prime_tower, loading_and_ramming, circle_compensation).

Group ids are unique over the sets; their titles are not (travel and travel_speed are both “Travel”). A choice’s values are MitCad’s (in commands, files and properties), each with a plain name for the interface (inner_outer, “Inner, then outer”).

QueryFieldsResult
print_keysset (printer, process or filament; all when left out)keys in display order: key, set, name, kind (boolean, integer, number, percent, number_or_percent, text, color, choice, points), unit, category, group (ids), advanced, of (a percentage’s basis), choices ({value, name}), per_dialect (the value names a slicer’s own preset: one per slicer), for a number (integer, number, percent, number_or_percent) min and max (mitcad#746: the widest range the key’s slicers take, in its unit, a number_or_percent key’s for its numbers; each left out where there is no bound: an angle of a direction or a compensation has neither, a length only min 0), dialects: {dialect, key, list} (list: one value per filament or extruder), with that dialect’s own min and max where it takes less (Bambu Studio’s -1 for “automatic” is out of OrcaSlicer’s range of Tree support walls, min 0 and max 2), for a number_or_percent key also percent (mitcad#655: whether that dialect takes a percentage, a form of its own or the same as MitCad’s; Bambu Studio’s line widths do not); layout: per set asked for, {set, categories}, each category {id, title, groups} and each group {id, title}, in display order

Tests: print_keys::tests (the table’s consistency and conversions in both directions between the dialects; every key in a group of its set’s category, no group empty, the rows in display order, every choice named, the layout as the enums), material_tests (print_keys_are_listed_for_the_interface).

Print profiles

Printer and process profiles, the print settings of components, occurrences and bodies, the libraries of materials and profiles, and slicers’ files (mitcad#640; core/model/src/print_profile.rs, document/print_settings.rs, print_library.rs, document/print_library.rs, print_files/, document/print_import.rs, api/print_profiles.rs).

Profiles. The design keeps printer and process profiles: id, name, kind (printer or process), values (keys of the Print Printer or Print Process set of the key map in their JSON form: numbers in the key’s unit, a percentage as its number, a number or a percentage of another value as 0.45 or "110%", choices by name, an outline as [[x, y], ...]; a key that names a slicer’s own preset, printer_settings_id, print_settings_id, printer_model, as {"<slicer id>": "<name>", ...}), slicer (a slicer’s settings the map does not have, by slicer id: its keys as text, written back only to that slicer), raw (a printer’s whole block from a Bambu-family project, by slicer id: not shown, not edited, written back to that slicer only; the queries list only raw_slicers), based_on, version and origin (as a material’s). A printer carries only what MitCad uses: the bed (bed_shape, bed_exclude_area), the printable height, the nozzle, the filament slots, the printer model and the slicers’ preset names; a profile is complete in the design. Values given as text are read in the key’s form ("15%" is 15).

CommandFieldsResult
create_print_profilekind, id (the name’s when left out, bench-printer; else printer1, process1, …), name (Printer 1, Process 1, then Printer 2, … when left out: one pattern for every kind, mitcad#655, never New …, mitcad#828; a copy <its source's name> (copy), (copy 2), …; free among the design’s and the libraries’ names), values, slicer, based_on (a design profile whose fields it starts from, by id, or a library’s item {library, id}: Duplicate), version, origin, project, choose (true: the design, the root, chooses it in the same undo step, mitcad#655); with library see Items where they live (Print profiles)id; undo step Create Profile Bench printer. Refused: keys of another set, values not of their key, a name another profile of the kind has
edit_print_profileid, and what changes: name, values (a key’s null removes it), slicer (a key’s null removes it), version, origin; with library see Items where they live (Print profiles)undo step Edit Printer Bench printer (Edit Process ...) unless nothing changes; the kind and id cannot change
delete_print_profileid; with library (and kind when the library has a printer and a process of the id) see Items where they live (Print profiles)owners: the components, occurrences and bodies that chose it, which no longer do; undo step Delete Profile Bench printer

The Print property sets. On a component (C0 the root: the design’s), an occurrence or a body (Properties):

  • Print Printer and Print Process hold the profile chosen there (profile, of the own type Print printer profile or Print process profile, whose values are the design’s profiles of the kind) and values set there under MitCad’s keys, typed by the key: yes/no, integers, lengths in mm (length, shown in the design’s units), areas and volumes, other numbers with their unit as a label (°C, mm/s, percentages %), a number or a percentage, text, colours and outlines as text, choices as an own type Print <key> with the choices as its values. set_property takes the key and a value of it (its type and unit are the key’s); a key of another set, a value not of the key, a profile the design has not and a key kept per slicer are refused. The queries give each such property its plain name too. The profile choice is the undo step Use Printer Bench printer (Use Process ...); with library (base, user, project) and project the profile value is that library’s item, copied in first (or the design’s copy of it reused) in the same undo step (mitcad#655).
  • Print Slicer (<slicer>) (Print Slicer (PrusaSlicer), or by the slicer’s id) holds a slicer’s own keys as text, written only to it.
  • Print Filament is the material’s (edit_material): set_property refuses it.
  • An imported value has the source 3mf (Properties: edited and source_value as for the other imports).

Inheritance. A body prints with the values of the root, then of the components down the occurrence path that places it (each occurrence after its component), then its own: the nearest wins. On a level a value set there comes before the values of the profile chosen there, so that a component that chooses a profile prints with that profile whatever the root set, unless it sets a value itself. The filament is the body’s material’s (Materials): its filament values, its density as filament_density and, when it sets no colour, its appearance’s colour as filament_colour; its own slicer keys follow those of the levels and profiles. Without a path a body inherits from its own component and the root. property_sets is unchanged: an occurrence shows only its component’s values as inherited.

QueryFieldsResult
print_profilesthe design’s profiles: their fields (without raw), raw_slicers, chosen_by (the owners that chose each)
print_settingsbody (uid or name) with occurrence (the path that places it), or occurrence (a path), or component; the root’s when none is givenlevels (owner, level, name: nearest first), printer and process: profile (id, name, owner, level, owner_name: the nearest chosen) and values, filament: material (id, name) and values; each value key, name, value, text, unit, from (property: owner, level, owner_name; profile: profile, profile_name, owner, level, owner_name; material: material, material_name); slicer: each slicer key’s slicer, key, value and where it comes from
build_volumethe root’s printer: printer (id, name) or null, bed (its outline moved so that its middle is on the origin; null without one), excluded, height, shift (what the bed was moved by), outside: the shown bodies whose box is beyond the bed’s outline or height, below the bed or over an excluded area: body, occurrence (uids O1/O4), name, path_name, min, max, reasons

Libraries. Materials and profiles come from three libraries, one JSON item file each (docs/libraries.md, “Materials and print profiles”): the base library (MitCad’s parts library mitcad-parts, its newest version fetched on this computer, through the library resolver), the user’s (print-library in MitCad’s data folder beside libraries, MITCAD_PRINT_LIBRARY_DIR) and the project’s (print-library in the project’s folder, given as project). The same kind and id in several: the nearest wins (project, user, base); the others are listed as shadowed. The design keeps complete copies of the items it uses, with their origin ({"library", "id", "version"}, and declined: a library version the design kept its own values over; an import’s 3mf and the file’s name), so that a library change never changes the design by itself; a material’s appearances (its default and the others of its list, mitcad#1067, A filament’s colour is its appearance) come with it as design appearances.

CommandFieldsResult
copy_from_print_librarylibrary (base, user, project; the nearest when left out), kind (material, printer, process), id, projectid in the design, library, version; a copy of the same item is replaced (an update), another of the same id keeps its id and the copy gets <id>_1; undo step Copy Acme PETG from Library
update_from_print_librarykind, id (the design’s copy), projectversion taken: the copy’s fields become the library item’s of its origin, its id stays; undo step Update Draft from Library
decline_print_library_updatekind, id (the design’s copy), projectversion declined (mitcad#655, “Keep these”): the copy keeps its fields and its origin remembers the library’s version as declined, so the change is not offered again until the library changes again; undo step Keep Draft
save_to_print_librarylibrary (user or project), kind, id (also a built-in material), projectpath, version: the next version of the item the copy was saved as before, else a new item (version 1) under the design’s id, a free one (bench-2) when the library has another item of that id; a name another item of the library has gets a counter (Bench 2), which the design’s copy takes too; the design’s copy then names it as its origin. The file and the copy are one undo step (Save Bench to Library): undo takes the file back. The base library is not written
QueryFieldsResult
print_libraryprojectitems: library, kind, id, name, version, path, shadowed, in_design (the design’s copies of it), item (its fields; a material’s display_color); updates: the design’s copies whose library item was changed elsewhere (see changed below: kind, id, name, library, library_id, version, newer); folders; problems (files that could not be read)

Items where they live (mitcad#655; document/library_items.rs). The user never handles a copy: choosing an item copies it in, and an item is edited where it lives. An item has a place: mitcad (the built-in materials and the base library; read-only), user, project, or design (the design’s own, in no library: made in the design, imported, or its library item deleted). The app shows only two states: built-in (read-only) or the user’s own, saved in a library or not yet.

  • One list. library_items gives one row per item of a kind the user can choose: the built-in materials the design does not replace (in their order, first), the nearest of each library item (shadowed ones are left out) and the design’s items that are in no library (a copy of a library item that is shadowed now keeps that item’s row), sorted by name. An item and the design’s copy of it are one row, showing the copy’s fields (what the design uses).
  • Made in a library. create_material and create_print_profile with library (user or project) write a new item file (version 1) and change nothing in the design: from based_on (an item of the design, a built-in material, or a library’s item {library, id}: Duplicate) or empty (a material of 1 g/cm³; a profile needs its kind). The name is <name> (copy) (then (copy 2), …, mitcad#828) after the item it is based on, else Material 1, Printer 1, Process 1 (then … 2), free among the libraries’ and the design’s names; the id is the name’s (acme-petg-copy) when not given, free among the libraries’ items. A material’s appearance that is not one of MitCad’s goes with it into the file. The file is an undo step of its own (Create Material Material 1): undo removes it. The print managers (mitcad#704, mitcad#1135, app/COMMANDS.md) make them in the library the user chooses with these commands, on the open design’s model or, with no design open, on an empty design of their own, so that the empty window does not change.
  • Edited in its library. edit_material and edit_print_profile with library read that library’s item, apply the change key by key on top of its newest version (so an older copy never overwrites newer keys) and write it as the next version. The design’s copies of it take the same change; a copy that had the library’s version is then at the new one, an older copy stays older. The file and the copies are one undo step (Edit Material Acme PETG, Edit Process Draft): undo and redo write the file back too, unless another design saved it since (then it stays as it is). An edit to the values the library’s newest version has already (another design made them, this one kept its own) writes no file and keeps the version; the design’s copies that differ still take it, as an undo step of its own (mitcad#758). version and origin are the library’s own and refused.
  • Changed elsewhere. A row’s changed is true when the library has a newer version than the design’s copy (another design or a hand changed the item), the design did not decline that version, and its fields differ from the copy’s. The app asks once: the changes are taken with update_from_print_library, the design’s values kept with decline_print_library_update (asked again only when the library changes again). An edit made here keeps a declined change declined.
  • Deleted from its library. delete_material and delete_print_profile with library remove the item’s file. A design copy that bodies or components use (a material) or an owner chose (a profile) stays as the design’s own unsaved item (its origin goes); an unused copy goes. The file and the design are one undo step: undo brings the file back.
  • Chosen in one step. set_body_material, set_component_material and set_property (the profile of Print Printer or Print Process) take library (base, user, project) beside the id, and project: the design’s copy of that item is used, else the item is copied in, in the same undo step as the choice (named as the choice).
  • The base library (mitcad) is read-only: a write there is refused. These commands and library_items read or write folders (class file IO).
CommandFieldsResult
create_material, create_print_profile with librarylibrary (user or project), project, based_on (an id, or {library, id}), id, name, the item’s fields (a profile’s kind when not based on one); not version, originid, library, version (1), path; the file’s undo step
edit_material, edit_print_profile with librarylibrary, project, id (the library’s), the fields that change (a profile’s kind when the library has a printer and a process of the id)version (the library’s new one; the old one when nothing changed), path; one undo step for the file and the design’s copies
delete_material, delete_print_profile with librarylibrary, project, id, kind (a profile’s, when needed)path (removed), kept (the design’s copies that stay, its own unsaved items now), removed (unused copies taken out); one undo step with the file
QueryFieldsResult
library_itemskind (material, printer or process), project, by_place (mitcad#1135: see By place below)items, each row: kind, id (where it lives: the library’s id, else the design’s), name, place (mitcad, user, project, design), library (base, user, project; null for a built-in material and the design’s own: give its id alone), read_only (the mitcad place), in_design (the design’s copy’s id, null when it has none; a built-in material’s own id), changed (the library item was changed elsewhere: see above), chosen (a profile the design, the root, chose), item (its fields: the design copy’s when it has one, else the library’s; a profile’s without raw); a material also class (metal, plastic, fdm_plastic, resin, other, mitcad#1102: fdm_plastic for a material with print settings, filament values, slicer keys or variants, whatever it stores; else the material’s own; without one, in a design or library file from before classes, a built-in metal or resin or a material based on one is metal or resin, one based on a built-in plastic plastic, else other), class_fixed (true when print settings make it an FDM plastic: the Class cannot change) and group, its class’s (metals, plastics (General Plastic), fdm_plastics with the filaments, resins, wood, mitcad#1552, other), display_color, bodies and components (that use the design’s copy); a profile also chosen_by (the owners that chose the design’s copy), the design’s chosen one overrides (mitcad#655: the owners below the root that set values of its set, {owner, name, keys, values}); for printer and process also print_overrides, the same owners whatever the design chose (mitcad#747: also with Slicer default, when no row is chosen; the export writes their values all the same); problems (library files that could not be read)

The parts of a profile’s name (mitcad#1108: the 3D Print panel’s Printer and Process picker). A printer row of library_items also gives bare_name, its name without the nozzle it ends with (Acme X1 0.4 nozzle and Acme X1 (0.4 nozzle) are Acme X1), and name_nozzle, the diameter that nozzle says (null without one; nozzle stays the profile’s nozzle_diameter); a process row bare_name, its name before its @ (0.20mm Standard @Acme X1C is 0.20mm Standard), and for_printer, what follows the @ (null without one). Names without those parts give themselves as bare_name.

The printers of a process (mitcad#1216: the Processes manager’s groups by printer and the process pickers’ order, app/COMMANDS.md). A process row of library_items also gives printers ([{"printer", "nozzle"}], empty: any printer), by the rule of the filament presets (A filament’s variants per printer and nozzle, Import): the printers of the process’s compatible_printers (any slicer’s kept text, a JSON list or "a";"b"), else the printer its name’s @ part names (“0.20mm Standard @Bench X 0.6 nozzle” is Bench X with a 0.6 mm nozzle), else none; each printer named without its nozzle. A printer row also gives printer_names, the names it goes by (its printer model, its name and its slicers’ preset names, each also without the nozzle), which a process’s printers are matched against in any case and spacing. The import of an installed slicer’s presets (import_slicer_presets) keeps a process’s or filament’s compatible_printers as the slicer has it, and an empty list of a preset’s own does not hide the list of the preset it inherits from. Tests: process_printers_tests (core/model-tests/print) and print_profile::tests.

By place (mitcad#1135: the Materials, Printers and Processes managers, app/COMMANDS.md). library_items with by_place: true lists each item where it lives and nowhere else, the managers’ one list model:

  • first every item of the kind the design has (place design, library null), a copy of a library item too: its source names that item (library, place, id, name) while the library has it, and its changed says that the library item was changed elsewhere; chosen, chosen_by, bodies and components are the design’s as above;
  • then each library item with its own fields, never its copy’s: the project’s (with project), the user’s, then MitCad’s (the built-in materials the design does not replace, in their order, then the base library’s), each place by name. A shadowed item is listed too, with shadowed: true. A library row has no in_design and is never chosen; copy is the design’s copy of it (null without one) and copy_used whether the design uses that copy.

The answer’s places lists the places in that order: design, project (only with a project), user and mitcad. Commands name a row as any other: a library row by library and id, a design row by its id alone, so that an edit of the design’s copy leaves its library item as it is, and an edit of the library item reaches the design’s copies as described above.

Headless MCP import. model_command permits import_print_profile and import_slicer_presets into the design only (into omitted or design). project paths and library targets are refused. Source paths, including folder, selected presets and every inherited preset, must stay inside the configured workspace; relative paths start there. The live connection continues to refuse these file commands. MCP reads neither installed slicer folders nor print libraries. For inherited JSON use import_slicer_presets with a copied data folder containing user/<account>/ and/or system/; import_print_profile can infer this folder when its preset lies in the same layout. A standalone inherited JSON file or a missing base is refused. All array sources are checked before any entry runs, under the command memory guard. A whole call shares a limit of 4,096 file reads, 4,096 directory entries and 64 MiB of input bytes plus expanded preset snapshots, including repeated sources in an array. The existing package reader also bounds unpacked entries and reads archives in memory without extracting files.

Import. import_print_profile reads a slicer’s settings, never its geometry:

  • a 3MF project: the Bambu Studio family’s Metadata/project_settings.config (the member by the model’s Application: BambuStudio-, OrcaSlicer-, QIDIStudio-; dialect when the file does not say), PrusaSlicer’s Metadata/Slic3r_PE.config, or Cura’s stacks under Cura/ (the global and extruder stacks’ instance containers the file carries, the nearest first, and the materials’ own files for the type, maker, colour and density; values Cura works out by formulas are left out);
  • a Bambu-family preset (.json) or exported bundle (a zip of presets), a PrusaSlicer configuration (.ini) or config bundle (its print, filament and printer sections, inherits within the bundle; the presets only others inherit from are left out).

Each gives a printer and a process profile (named after the presets) and a material per filament: named after its preset, its density the filament’s (else the built-in of its type’s), a plastic appearance in the filament’s colour, based_on the built-in of its type, the rest its filament values. Every filament gets an appearance (mitcad#1053): its filament_colour, else the Bambu family’s default_filament_colour (a preset of that family keeps no filament_colour: the slicer takes it from the project), else, when no colour is found anywhere, a neutral light grey plastic (#BFBFBF) named for the material (<name> color). The material’s colour is its appearance’s from then on: the material keeps no filament_colour of its own, and the export writes the appearance’s colour. A Bambu-family preset file that inherits from another is read with every value of the chain filled in, as an installed slicer’s presets are (below): from the slicer data folder the file lies in, else from the installed slicers’ system presets (those of the dialect first); when none has its base, the values it inherits are reported as left out. The report’s log has a line per filament, Slicer import: <preset> inherits <chain>, colour <#RRGGBB|none> (the chain the nearest first, A > B, a base not found as C (missing), nothing when it inherits nothing); the application writes them to its log. Keys the map has become MitCad’s values; other keys are kept per slicer as text in the layer their name tells; a Bambu-family project’s printer block is also kept whole (raw) with the preset it inherits from and the project’s filament presets in its order, and so is a Bambu-family printer preset’s (mitcad#2008: its lists per extruder and per nozzle variant keep their shape). A preset’s bookkeeping is neither read nor kept (see A preset’s metadata in a project below). Per-object settings, plates and height ranges do not target MitCad’s bodies: the report counts them as left out.

CommandFieldsResult
import_print_profilepath, dialect, into (design the default, user, project), project, choose (into the design: the root chooses the printer and process read; true by default)into the design (one undo step Import Print Settings plate.3mf): printers, processes (id, name), materials (id, name: a name the design already holds is numbered, PLA (2), PLA (3), …; colour: its appearance’s #RRGGBB; source: the file it came from, mitcad#1728), chosen; into a library: items (kind, id, name, version, path); both dialect and report: mapped, mapped_keys, kept, kept_keys, left_out, problems, log

An installed slicer’s presets (mitcad#830, print_files/installed.rs, document/slicer_presets.rs). The user presets of the Bambu-family slicers installed (Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer, QIDI Studio), read straight from their data folders, never changed: %APPDATA%\<key> on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/<key> on macOS, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/<key> (else ~/.config/<key>) on Linux and a Flatpak’s ~/.var/app/<id>/config/<key>, <key> BambuStudio, OrcaSlicer or QIDIStudio; a slicer is installed when its folder has user/, or system/ and an app config (below) whose models enables a printer (mitcad#871). Its presets are user/<account>/{machine,process,filament}/*.json (default without an account). After them come the slicer’s own presets the user enabled there (mitcad#871, system), read from system/<vendor>/{machine,process,filament}/ as the slicer’s app config <key>.conf says: the printers whose model and nozzle are in its models ({vendor, model, nozzle_diameter}), the processes for one of them (compatible_printers), and the filaments named in its filaments (with a printer model’s default_materials when none listed suits one of its printers) that suit one of them, each kind by name in any case; only presets meant to be chosen (instantiation not false), never the bases, and none without an app config. A preset’s inherits is filled in from the user’s own presets of its account and the slicer’s system/ presets (those of its vendor folder first), up the chain, the nearer value winning; a base that is missing stays named and the report says so (as for a preset file). The templates a preset includes (include, mitcad#2008: a two-extruder printer’s machine G-code, a filament’s values per nozzle variant) are filled in too, found by name as the bases are, each preset of the chain with its templates under its own values and over its base’s, a later template’s over an earlier one’s, a template’s own templates and base under its values; templates not found are reported as left out (“the values … takes from its templates …”), never as a complete import, and templates that include each other in a loop or nest deeper than 8 are the import’s error. Every key comes through the chain, the filament’s colour and temperatures as much as the rest (mitcad#1053). A ticked preset whose kind and name the target has (same) either overrides that item (same_name: override: into a library its next version, as edit_print_profile / edit_material with library; into the design the design’s item of that name; a filament’s appearance with it) or comes in as a copy under the next free name (copy, the default: Fine 2, Fine 3, …); two of one name in one import make the second a copy. New items get ids no library has for their kind, version 1. Into the design the whole import is one undo step Import Presets of Bambu Studio, the overrides with it; it chooses nothing.

CommandFieldsResult
import_slicer_presetsdialect (bambu_studio, orcaslicer, qidi_studio), folder (the slicer’s data folder, slicer_presets’ folder), presets ([{path, same_name}], same_name copy or override), into (design the default, user, project), projectas import_print_profile’s (into the design printers, processes, materials, each id and name; into a library items), the overridden items among them, with overridden (kind, id, name; in a library version, path), copied (kind, name, from: the preset’s name), dialect, into, report

A preset’s metadata in a project (mitcad#2008, print_files/source.rs, print_files/bambu.rs). A Bambu-family preset’s bookkeeping (name, version, from, type, instantiation, setting_id, base_id, user_id, updated_time, is_custom_defined, url, description, renamed_from, inherits, include) is one text of the preset’s own to the family’s loader, which stops reading a project at an array there: the import neither reads nor keeps it, and the export writes none of it (a design imported before that keeps some: left out, with a warning, which for include adds that the printer’s template values may be its base’s until it is imported again). A filament preset’s filament_id is kept and written in the project’s form, filament_ids (an entry per filament slot). The printers and processes a filament preset is for (compatible_printers, compatible_prints and their conditions) are not a slot’s setting and are not written per slot. Every value of project_settings.config is a text or a list of texts (numbers and yes/no as their text); a value of another type is left out with a warning.

The printer’s extruders, its nozzle variants and the filaments’ slots stay distinct lists: lists per extruder (nozzle_diameter, extruder_type, extruder_printable_area, extruder_printable_height, default_nozzle_volume_type, nozzle_volume_type, physical_extruder_map, extruder_variant_list) and per nozzle variant (printer_extruder_id, printer_extruder_variant, nozzle_volume, nozzle_flush_dataset) keep the length the printer’s block gives; a key the map keeps as one value (the nozzle diameter) keeps the block’s entries while that value is unchanged, and one changed in MitCad is written for every entry with a warning when the entries differed. A printer that keeps one nozzle diameter beside lists of more extruders (a design imported before) gets the diameter for each, with a warning; a printer without nozzle_volume_type gets its default_nozzle_volume_type. Lists per extruder or per variant of different lengths, a variant of an extruder the printer does not have and a filament mapped to one (filament_map) are warnings, not fixed. A material’s kept key is written as an entry per slot: a key only some slots’ materials keep is left to the slicer for every slot, and a slot’s list of several values (a filament preset’s values per nozzle variant, filament_extruder_variant) gives the entry of the printer’s variant (its first extruder’s type and nozzle volume type, Direct Drive Standard), else the first; both are warnings. These are checks of the file: whether the slicer slices it is a check in the slicer itself. Tests: slicer_project_form_tests (core/model-tests/print) and the installed.rs unit tests.

QueryFieldsResult
slicer_presetsinto (design the default, user, project), project, folders ([{dialect, path}]: data folders to read instead of the installed slicers’, for tests)slicers: dialect, name (Bambu Studio), folder, flatpak, presets (the user’s, then the enabled system ones): kind (printer, process, material for a filament), name, path, account (null for a system preset), inherits, system, vendor (a system preset’s vendor folder, else null), same (the target’s item of its kind and name: id, name, place design, user or project; null when it has none)

Export. export of a 3MF with dialect (bambu_studio, orcaslicer, qidi_studio, prusaslicer, cura; 3MF) writes each body’s effective settings (print_settings of its placements written, a part per group that prints alike: below): the printer and process values every part shares as the project’s, the others per part, a filament slot per distinct material in the order of first use (more materials than the printer’s filament slots is a warning). The result adds dialect, filaments (each part’s slot from 1) and warnings (values a slicer does not take). A value out of the range a dialect takes (Bambu Studio’s -1 for “automatic” in raft_first_layer_expansion, tree_support_wall_count, which OrcaSlicer refuses; the key map’s range of the dialect key) is left out of that dialect’s file, and the slicer keeps its default, with a warning.

No material, no printer (mitcad#1727). A body without a material of its own or of a component up its path prints as the print default, the built-in pla (PLA Plastic, the material print analysis assumes), in its own appearance where it has one, else PLA’s: not as the design’s default steel, which only stands for its density. body_material of such a body (source default) gives that print default as print_material (id, name). With nothing chosen at all (no material, printer, process or value) the export is geometry only and writes no project settings (Print jobs: geometry only or a print project, mitcad#2008). A print project without a printer (no profile chosen and no slicer’s preset name kept) names a stand-in printer, Mitcad printer, which the slicer does not know and slices nothing with until a real printer is chosen there; the Bambu family’s and PrusaSlicer’s exports then warn no printer profile was imported: …; import the printer's profile first (import_print_profile, or the Printer row of Send to Slicer). That warning is the agents’ text; the result then also has warning_messages, every warning as the application shows it, this one in plain words without the command (docs/ui-conventions.md, “What a message says”).

Filament values some materials set (mitcad#1052). A slicer reads every filament’s value of a key from one list, an entry per filament: a key no material of the written slots sets stays the slicer’s, but one that some set is written for every slot, so that each value reaches its own filament (a PETG HF part’s nozzle temperature beside a part of the default material). A slot whose material does not set it takes the value of MitCad’s generic filament of its type (PLA, PETG, ABS, ASA, TPU, PA: the base library’s diameter, nozzle and bed temperatures and the first layer’s, and fan speed; a slot without a type is written as PLA), else the first slot’s that sets it, with a warning per slot (PLA Plastic (filament 2) sets no nozzle temperature, bed temperature: written as generic PLA's). The type, the colour, a preset’s name and a filament’s override of the printer’s extruder settings (nil) keep their own rules. The result’s printed gives each written part’s body, name (the part’s), material (its id) and own_values (its material’s filament values the slicer has keys for and the printer and process values it does not share with the other parts).

A part per settings group (mitcad#1061). A body’s settings are those of each placement written (of the occurrences picked, when some are). A body whose placements all print alike (the same material, values and slicers’ own keys, wherever each comes from) is one part, named after the body. One whose placements print otherwise (a material or a value of an occurrence or of a component up their path) is one part per group of placements that print alike, in the order of each group’s first placement: each part has its group’s placements, its filament slot (by its material, as any part’s) and its own values, and is named after the body and the group’s occurrences, the first three named (Body2 (Box:2), Body2 (Box:1, Box:3), Body2 (Box:1, Box:3, Box:4 and 2 more)). The parts share the body’s mesh; bodies and meshes still list the body once, filaments and printed each part. On the print bed, the pieces and the build’s objects take each placement in its part, as they are put on the bed.

  • The Bambu Studio family: Metadata/project_settings.config (JSON; lists per filament, each with exactly one entry per written filament slot wherever the value comes from: a list kept from an imported project of more filaments, such as default_filament_colour or volumetric_speed_coefficients, takes each slot’s entry of the project’s filament its material came from (by the material’s filament_self_index, else its preset among the project’s, which the printer block keeps), else the first; flush_volumes_matrix (n × n per extruder) and flush_volumes_vector (two per filament) take those filaments’ rows and columns, else the slicers’ defaults (280 between filaments, 0 to itself, 140); filament_self_index numbers the slots from 1; the printer’s and process’s preset names, the slicer’s names the profiles keep, else theirs; inherits_group and different_settings_to_system as the loader reads them, see the key map’s documentation; a printer block kept for this slicer first; a design that sets only the bed temperature writes it to every plate’s key), Metadata/model_settings.config (the object, each part’s filament and values of its own) and the model’s Application (BambuStudio-02.00.00.00, QIDI Studio QIDIStudio-02.00.00.00) and BambuStudio:3mfVersion.
  • PrusaSlicer: Metadata/Slic3r_PE.config (; key = value; the printer’s values once per filament slot, so that it has as many extruders; lists as PrusaSlicer writes them: strings ;-separated and quoted only where an entry needs it, numbers, yes/no and choices ,-separated and unquoted, uniform_cooling,uniform_cooling, since PrusaSlicer refuses a quoted choice; inherits_cummulative (PrusaSlicer’s spelling) names the presets the process, each filament and the printer inherit from: the process’s and printer’s PrusaSlicer preset names the profiles keep and each material’s PrusaSlicer filament preset, empty where there is none, left out when all are) and Metadata/Slic3r_PE_model.config (PrusaSlicer makes each mesh object an object of its own: each its extruder, its own values and its one volume), and slic3rpe:Version3mf 1.
  • Cura: each part’s extruder and process values as its mesh object’s cura: metadata (Cura’s per-model settings; its platform adhesion from the brim, raft and skirt values). Cura’s printer and global settings stay its own: a project of Cura’s would name its installed machine, quality and material containers.

STL files carry no settings.

Tests: print_profile::tests, print_profile_tests (profiles, the Print sets, inheritance, the build volume, the design file and the comparison), print_library::tests, print_library_tests (the nearest library, the design’s copies and their updates, saving into a library, the base library’s items in this repository; mitcad#655: library_items rows and places, items made, duplicated, edited and deleted in a library, the design’s copy taking an edit, chosen in one undo step; mitcad#704: a library managed on an empty design; mitcad#1135: the rows by place), print_files::tests (synthetic projects, presets and bundles of each dialect read with their reports; exports of each dialect read back), 3mf.corpus (real slicer projects under MITCAD_3MF_CORPUS, checked against their index rows and read back after an export; docs/development.md), core.3mf (settings_go_with_the_model_and_read_back), tools/ui-print-settings-test.sh.

Measure in the design

The measure query (Analysis queries) measures every selection where the design shows it (mitcad#646), as Section Analysis cuts each occurrence (world):

  • Occurrence. A selection given as fields takes an optional occurrence: the path of occurrences from the root that places its body or datum ("O1/O4"; "" or none for the root). The body is placed by that path’s transform (the body is not changed): a selection alone, and two of one placement, are measured on the body as it is and their points, circles and closest points moved by the transform when it is a rigid motion (mitcad#981: a moved copy of a body with modelled threads took seconds, each time the selection card measured a face of it); otherwise, and for two placed apart, on a moved copy. A datum is placed likewise (a construction feature’s datum is in its component’s coordinates; an origin datum with an occurrence is that occurrence’s origin). The path can also name the occurrences ("Arm:1/Pin:2", Selections by names and as entities). Without occurrence, a body or construction feature of a component placed exactly once is placed there; one placed more than once is refused with the paths that place it (body F4.b0 is in a component placed 2 times: O1/O2 (Assembly:1/Block:1), O3/O2 (Assembly:2/Block:1); give one as occurrence), and an occurrence that does not place it as well (occurrence O1 does not place body F4.b0; body F4.b0 is placed at O1/O2 (Assembly:1/Block:1), …). Text selections ("Body1/…", "F5") take the only placement the same way. The root’s bodies and datums are measured as before, without a copy.
  • Design coordinates. point, circle.center and circle.axis of each selection and between’s on_a, on_b, main_points, distance and angle are in the design’s coordinates; lengths, areas and volumes do not change with the placement.
  • Offset. When both selections are planes — planar faces (the face’s plane as the kernel gives it, Kernel::face_plane) or datum planes — and their normals are parallel or opposite within 1e-6 rad (the assembly constraints’ tolerance), between also has offset: the distance between the two planes along the normal, in mm and never negative. The closest distance stays: it is longer than the offset when the faces do not overlap across the normal. Planes that are not parallel, and bodies, edges and vertices, have no offset.
  • Main result (mitcad#1161). between.main is "offset" for these parallel planar pairs, otherwise "distance". The original distance and on_a/on_b remain the finite shapes’ closest-point measurement; existing callers do not lose the minimum. main_points: [[x,y,z], [x,y,z]] gives the main dimension’s endpoints in design coordinates. For a plane gap they are perpendicular to the planes: the closest common projection when minimum and gap agree within 1e-6 mm, otherwise the first face’s middle (or datum origin) and its foot on the second plane. mitcad-cli measure and text analysis label the selected value Distance: … mm (main: offset|distance) and add Minimum distance only when it differs by more than 1e-6 mm; the raw Offset remains in the text output for callers that read that field.
  • The app. Measure sends each pick’s occurrence, labels the main value Distance, adds Minimum distance immediately below only when distinct, and draws the line between main_points. The selection card sends the occurrence too.

A side placement’s Offset is measured this way: a profile placed on the side of an upright one from end A or end B with Offset 100 (a typed 100 is 100 mm) has its face nearer that end 100 from the end’s plane, and from the middle its middle 100 past the target’s middle, at every turn (Side placements; a tilted part’s Offset is to its foot’s long point, Tilt).

Tests: api::measure_tests (nested occurrences, a component placed twice, the root unchanged, parallel faces overlapping or not, of two occurrences, against construction and origin planes, and planes that are not parallel), build::side_offset_tests (the side placement’s Offset from end A, end B and the middle, turned, typed without a unit), on the mock kernel’s measure of the selections’ boxes (MockKernel::measures_selections); tools/cli/tests/construction.json (the offset of two faces and of a face and a construction plane on the OCCT kernel); tools/cli/tests/measure_planar.json and geometry.analysis (a synthetic stepped shell’s gaps 16/48/58 mm and distinct exact minima); the shared tools/ui-scripts/measure-planar.mitcad-ui on Linux, Windows and macOS Qt (the primary Distance, distinct Minimum distance, the perpendicular dimension and the equal-distance case).

Selections by names and as entities

The measure query’s selections (Analysis queries, Measure in the design) also take what an agent has at hand without looking up ids first, and every refusal names the values that would be taken (mitcad#985; api::analysis resolve_selection, occurrence_path, selection_transform):

  • Occurrence paths by names. occurrence is a path from the root by occurrence ids ("O1/O4"), by the occurrences’ names as the components query gives them ("Arm:1/Pin:2"), or both mixed ("O1/Pin:2"); spaces around the / do not matter. A name matches in any case, and a component’s name alone ("Arm/Pin:2") matches its occurrence where that component is placed only once. The answer gives the path resolved, by ids: a.occurrence and b.occurrence ("O1/O4") for each selection that gave one. A name that matches nothing where the path has got to is refused with the occurrences there (invalid occurrence path “…”: there is no occurrence Block:9 in Assembly; its occurrences are O1/O2 (Assembly:1/Block:1), O1/O3 (Assembly:1/Block:2)), and one that matches several likewise ('Block' in Assembly is any of …).
  • Errors name the placements. A body or construction feature of a component placed more than once, without an occurrence, is refused with each path that places it and its names (Plane1 is in a component placed 3 times: O1/O2 (Arm:1/Pin:1), O1/O3 (Arm:1/Pin:2), O1/O4 (Arm:1/Pin:3); give one as occurrence). An occurrence that does not place it, a path through the wrong parent (Pin:2 is placed in Arm, not in …) and an occurrence that does not exist (occurrence O9 does not exist) are refused with the same list (…; Plane1 is placed at O1/O2 (Arm:1/Pin:1), …); a root body or datum given another occurrence: … is in the root: give no occurrence, or "". At most ten paths are listed, then … and n more; the instances query lists them. Measurement objects’ picks (Measurement objects) are placed by the same code and refused with the same texts, and a body of Section Analysis’s shapes (section, clip) given an occurrence that does not own it lists the paths that do.
  • Origin datums by name. datum (and a text selection) takes the origin datums by id or name in any case: "xy", "XY", "xz", "yz", "x", "y", "z", "origin"; with occurrence it is that occurrence’s own origin datum. Anything else that is no construction feature is refused as invalid datum top: a construction feature ("F5") or an origin datum ("xy", "xz", "yz", "x", "y", "z", "origin"). The datum query takes them the same way.
  • The entity form. A selection can be an entity as ui_state lists the selection and ui_select takes it: kind, owner, name, occurrence (its geometry, reference and text are taken and not used, so an entity can be passed on unchanged). face, edge and vertex are {"body": owner, kind: name}, body is {"body": owner}, plane, axis and point are {"datum": owner} (name empty), each with the entity’s occurrence; so {"kind": "point", "owner": "origin", "name": "", "occurrence": "O1/O3"} is that occurrence’s origin point. Other kinds (sketch curves, profiles, components, sketches, features) are refused (a sketch entity cannot be measured: …), as is an entity that also gives body, face, edge, vertex or datum.

Tests: api::measure_tests (errors_name_the_occurrences_that_place_a_selection, occurrence_paths_are_taken_by_names, origin_datums_are_taken_by_name, the_entity_form_measures_as_the_fields: a component placed three times in a nested assembly, and twelve times for the list’s limit).

Bounded face separation

The measure query accepts optional "face_range": true with two face selections a and b (mitcad#661). Without it the existing result is unchanged. With it, between.maximum_distance is either the exact symmetric Hausdorff distance, in mm, or null when that maximum is unavailable. This is the largest nearest-face gap in either direction: max(max(p in A) min(q in B) |p-q|, max(q in B) min(p in A) |p-q|). It is not the largest distance between an arbitrary pair of points. Matching parallel plates therefore have the same minimum and maximum, without including a plate’s diagonal.

The maximum is currently supported for two bounded convex planar polygon faces, each having one closed wire of straight edges and no holes. OCCT computes the exact distance from every boundary vertex to the other bounded face; Rust checks convexity and takes the maximum in both directions. Distance to a convex face is convex, so a polygon’s vertices contain its maximum. Curved, concave, holed or unresolved/multi-piece faces return null for this optional maximum; no sampled or supporting- plane substitute is used. The ordinary exact between.distance and closest points remain available even when the maximum is unavailable. Missing b and non-face selections are refused.

Both faces are resolved with their occurrence placements, just as the ordinary measure query. Supporting planes that intersect outside the selected faces do not turn the bounded minimum into zero; touching or intersecting bounded faces do have minimum zero. Existing offset still means perpendicular separation of parallel supporting planes. The idle selection card requests this query automatically for exactly two faces.

Tests: cli.face_separation checks a known parallel gap, an angled pair with minimum 5 mm and maximum 17 mm whose supporting planes meet outside the faces, reversed picks, distinct occurrence placements, touching and intersecting faces, and an unavailable curved maximum. The selection UI test covers both Qt layouts, unchanged picks after a placement edit, document units, unavailable maxima, one-face selection and clearing.

Measure with axes

The measure query (Analysis queries) also works with axes (mitcad#647). The model takes each pick’s geometry from the kernel’s descriptions (Kernel::face_geometry, Kernel::edge_geometry, Kernel::vertex_point, Kernel::face_plane), places it by its occurrence (Measure in the design) and works out the rest itself (api::measure_axes):

  • Axis. A selection with an axis gets axis: {"origin": [x, y, z], "direction": [dx, dy, dz]} in the design’s coordinates, the direction a unit vector. A cylindrical or conical face: its axis through the origin the kernel gives (the axis point nearest to the face’s centre on the OCCT kernel, the direction along its largest component); a toroidal face: through its centre; a circle or an arc: through its centre along its normal; a construction or origin axis: through its origin. Planar faces, straight edges, vertices, spheres and bodies have none.
  • Angle. between.angle is the kernel’s where it has one (two planar faces’ normals 0 to π, straight edges, a straight edge and a planar face, as before); otherwise for every pair with a normal (a planar face, a datum plane), a direction (a straight edge) or an axis: two axes or an axis and an edge 0 to π/2, an axis against a plane 0 to π/2 from the plane. Null when either has none (a vertex, a body, a sphere).
  • Axis distance. With an axis on one side at least, axis_distance (mm) and axis_points ([on a, on b]): another axis or a straight edge’s line — parallel within 1e-6 rad: their distance, from a’s axis point (or its foot on a’s axis) across; skew: the common perpendicular’s length and ends; meeting: 0 and the point twice; a vertex, a construction point or a sphere’s centre: the perpendicular distance from the axis and the foot; a plane parallel to the axis: the offset, from the axis point to its foot on the plane; a plane across the axis: no distance (its angle tells). The closest distance stays (between the surfaces of two cylinders, not their axes).
  • Centre distance. Two circles or arcs: center_distance, the distance of their centres.
  • Text. The text form (mitcad-cli analysis, mitcad-cli measure) adds axis through [..] along [..] to a selection’s line and Axis distance: <d> mm, from [..] to [..] and Centre distance: <d> mm.

The app shows the axes and draws them (app/COMMANDS.md, Actions and tools).

Tests: api::measure_axes::tests (the geometry: parallel, skew and meeting axes, axes against edges, points and planes, circles’ centres), api::measure_tests (cylinders’ axes in the design, turned by an occurrence and repeated, against a plane, a cone’s axis against a straight edge, circles against origin axes, on the mock kernel’s surfaces and edge_curves); tools/cli/tests/measure_axes.json (cli.measure_axes, on the OCCT kernel: parallel and skew cylinders, a cylinder against its top, a chamfer’s cone against an upright edge, a circle against a construction axis, a Pin placed turned as an occurrence); tools/ui-measure-test.sh and tools/ui-windows-measure-test.ps1 (app.ui-windows-measure; the panel’s axis lines, the axis and centre distances, the axes drawn).

Placement by picked geometry

A part is placed by what the user picks in the view: a shaft or an axis, a point, or a point on a face measured from two of its edges (mitcad#656; core/model/src/features/place_at.rs the definition and its one resolver, features/drives.rs the Gear Pair and Belt Drive arithmetic, api/drives.rs the queries and commands below). The placement is kept as references (topological names, sketch entity ids, construction features), never as coordinates, so the part follows when the geometry it was placed by moves. Relations between parts (a gear meshing with another, a belt round two pulleys) come after the parts: Gear Pair and Belt Drive work from two placements and a ratio.

The at placement

Pulleys, gears, printable bearings, coils and the primitives box, cylinder, cone, sphere and torus take at instead of plane and center (a box’s corner); a hole takes it as its placement {"type": "at", "at": {...}}. The forms written before (plane and center, seat, belt_with, mesh_with, the hole’s placements) load, build and save as they did.

{"type": "pulley", "kind": "toothed", "profile": "gt2_2mm", "teeth": 20, "belt_width": 6,
 "at": {"axis": {"body": "F2.b0", "face": "F2:side(c1)"}, "offset": 3, "near": [4, 0, 28]},
 "bore_clearance": 0.2, "operation": "new_component"}
{"type": "gear", "kind": "spur", "module": 1, "teeth": 30, "face_width": 8,
 "at": {"axis": "F5", "offset": 10, "angle": "4 deg"}, "bore": {"type": "plain", "diameter": 8},
 "operation": "new_component"}
{"type": "cylinder", "diameter": 10, "height": 20, "operation": "join",
 "at": {"point": {"sketch": "F1", "point": "p3"}}}
{"type": "box", "length": 30, "width": 20, "height": 10, "operation": "new_body",
 "at": {"face": {"body": "F2.b0", "face": "F2:end(r{c5})"},
        "edge1": {"body": "F2.b0", "edge": "E{...}"}, "offset1": 12,
        "edge2": {"body": "F2.b0", "edge": "E{...}"}, "offset2": 8,
        "align": {"body": "F2.b0", "edge": "E{...}"}}}
{"type": "hole", "placement": {"type": "at", "at": {"face": "xy", "offset1": 20, "offset2": 15}},
 "diameter": 6, "extent": {"type": "through_all"}}

at is one of three forms, by the field it has: axis, point or face.

FieldValue
axisOn an axis. A shaft or a hole: a circular edge or a cylindrical face of a body, resolved as a seat is (the end measured from, the axis into the shaft or hole, its diameter). Or an axis on its own: an origin axis ("x", "y", "z"), a construction axis ("F5"), a sketch line, a sketch circle or arc (the axis through its centre normal to the sketch), a fixed axis; the part is measured from the axis’s origin point (a construction axis’s origin, a line’s start) along its direction, and the axis has no diameter
pointAt a point. A sketch point ({"sketch": "F1", "point": "p3"}), a sketch circle’s or arc’s centre ({"sketch": "F1", "curve": "c4"}), a vertex, a construction point ("F6"), the origin ("origin") or a circular edge (its centre). The axis is the normal of the point’s sketch, a circular edge’s axis, or the normal of plane
planewith point only: an origin plane, a construction plane or a planar face whose normal is the axis (outward for a face) and whose frame gives the x axis. Needed for a vertex, a construction point and the origin; it overrides a sketch’s or an edge’s own
faceOn a face. A planar face of a body, an origin plane or a construction plane: the point lies in its plane, the axis is its normal (a face’s outward normal)
edge1, offset1, edge2, offset2with face: two lines (straight edges, sketch lines, origin or construction axes; not parallel to each other, not along the normal) and the point’s distances from them in the face’s plane, mm (values, signed: negative on the other side). The positive side of each line is the side of the face’s middle on a body face, the side of near on a plane (needed there). Without the edges, on an origin plane only: offset1 along the plane’s x axis and offset2 along its y axis from the origin (the origin axes are the references)
nearwhere the pick was, mm, in the feature’s component’s coordinates: on an axis that is a cylindrical face, the end nearer it is the end measured from (as a seat’s near); on a plane (not a body face) with edges, the side of each line it lies on is the positive side
offsetmm along the axis (a value): from the end measured from (axis), from the point (point, face); 0 without it
flipthe axis turned round: axis measures from the other end of the shaft and runs back (as a seat’s flip); point and face put the part on the other side (a face: into it)
angleturns the part about its axis (a value, radians), after align
aligna line (a straight edge, a sketch line, an origin or construction axis): the part’s x axis along its direction, put square to the axis; or a planar face (a shaft’s flat; also an origin or construction plane): the x axis along its normal (a face’s outward), put square to the axis, so that a set screw or a keyway turns to the flat. Refused when the line runs along the axis, or the face lies square to it (the face to align to lies square to the placement's axis)
align_sidewith align (mitcad#656): a direction ([x, y, z]) the part’s y axis points toward; a line’s own direction is reversed where its y would point away, so that a part placed from a face’s far edge grows into the face. Without it a line is taken as it runs (designs written before are unchanged). Refused without align
  • The frame. Every form resolves into a frame: its origin (the point the part is placed at), its normal (the part’s axis) and its x axis. axis: a seat’s frame, x as a plane’s without one (References to geometry); point: the frame of the point’s sketch (or of plane) moved to the point, an edge’s x as a plane’s without one; face: the face’s plane frame moved to the point. Then flip, offset, align and angle in that order. A part runs along the normal from the origin as it runs from its plane without at (a pulley’s first flange, a gear’s teeth, a box’s height, a coil’s turns): the frame is the plane, its origin the centre (a box’s corner).
  • Bores. On a shaft or in a hole (axis on a body’s face or edge) a pulley or gear without bore has the plain bore of the shaft’s diameter plus bore_clearance, following the shaft, and a bearing without a size takes the size that fits (Seats on shafts). A bore given is kept (also a plain one, which a seat on a shaft refuses). An axis on its own, a point and a face have no diameter: the part keeps the bore it is given (none without one), and a bearing needs its size or dimensions.
  • Holes. One hole at the frame’s origin: along the axis into the shaft or hole for axis, against the normal (into the face) for point and face; the hole’s own flip turns it round.
  • What it takes. at is refused together with plane, a center or corner other than the origin, seat, belt_with and a bearing’s groove. A gear’s mesh_with goes with it (below). A rack keeps its plane and centre (at refused); so does a bevel pair. The references are of the feature’s own component: a shaft of another component (a BUILD shaft, a library part) is a seat with its link.
  • Recompute. The placement reads what it refers to: a shaft made longer, a sketch moved, a face or an edge moved, an offset edited rebuild the part where its references now are; a reference that no longer resolves fails the feature with the reason (at: ...).
  • Values. offset, offset1, offset2 and angle are values (parameters, as a feature’s other fields): slots at.offset, at.offset1, at.offset2, at.angle (a hole’s placement.at.…).

A seat (seat) also takes an axis on its own now: its shaft may be an origin or construction axis, a sketch line, circle or arc, or a fixed axis, with the rules of at’s axis (no diameter: a pulley’s or gear’s bore stays its own, and a plain bore is then allowed; no link).

Meshes and belts from placed parts

  • mesh_with on a placed gear. A gear with at and mesh_with lies where its placement puts it; mesh_with only turns it so that its teeth engage the other gear’s (the direction between the two axes takes the place of mesh_with.angle, which it refuses, as it refuses the gear’s own angle). The axes must be parallel (else the feature fails); when their distance differs from the mesh’s centre distance by more than 0.001 mm the gear is made and warns (the axes are 40.05 mm apart, the mesh needs 40 mm). Each gear is built from its placement along its own axis, so on axes that point opposite ways the two grow apart: the gear is made and warns (the gear's axis points the opposite way from its mate's: …; flip one so that both point the same way, mitcad#749). Not with a rack.
  • mesh_with.toward. For a gear placed by its mate (no at), the direction from the mate’s centre may be picked instead of typed: {"gear": "F3", "toward": <reference>} with a point (a vertex, a sketch point, a construction point, a circular edge’s centre) or an axis (a shaft or hole picked as its face, a construction axis, a sketch circle): the direction towards where it meets the mate’s plane. Not with angle or position.
  • Belts are a check. A pulley is placed on its own shaft, axis or point; the belt round two placed pulleys is checked by belt_check (below), not made. belt_with stays for the designs that have it.

Gear Pair

The gear_pair query takes two placements (the gears’ axes) and a ratio and lists the gears that fit. The centre distance a is the axes’ distance (they must be parallel). It goes through the standard modules (ISO 54 series I from 1 mm up, and below 1 mm the DIN 780 series 1 values 0.3 to 0.9; second_series adds ISO 54 series II) and, for each, through the tooth counts z1 from min_teeth up with z2 the whole numbers nearest z1 * ratio, within ratio_tolerance. Each candidate fits in one of three ways:

  • exact: m (z1 + z2) / 2 = a (within 1e-6 mm), spur teeth;
  • profile_shift: spur teeth whose centre distance with the profile shifts’ working pressure angle is a: inv(aw) = inv(alpha) + 2 tan(alpha) (x1 + x2) / (z1 + z2), cos(aw) = m (z1 + z2) cos(alpha) / (2 a). A positive sum goes more to the gear with fewer teeth, a negative one more to the other (each gear’s share in proportion to the other gear’s teeth, or to its own when negative); each x within max_profile_shift and -1 to 0.8;
  • helix: helical teeth whose helix angle makes a exact: cos(beta) = m (z1 + z2) / (2 a), beta from 5 degrees to max_helix_angle; the first gear right-handed, the second left-handed.

Undercut. A gear of z teeth with profile shift x is undercut by the basic rack when z < 2 (1 - x) / sin²(alpha) (17.1 teeth at 20 degrees without a shift), a helical gear by its virtual teeth z / cos³(beta): it needs at least x = 1 - z sin²(alpha) / 2. An undercut gear of any fit gets that shift, taken from the other gear so that their sum (and the centre distance) stays, when both shifts stay within max_profile_shift and -1 to 0.8 and the other gear stays free of undercut; an exact or helix pair so has shifts of sum zero. Each candidate’s undercut ([first, second]) says whether a gear is still undercut.

Best fits come first: the pairs free of undercut before the others; then the ratio’s deviation in steps of 0.5 % (the ratio is what is asked, and deviations within one step are of equal quality), so that pairs meeting the ratio come before those missing it, shifted or helical if need be; within a step exact, profile_shift, helix; then the pairs needing no correction against undercut (corrected false) before the corrected ones, then the fewer teeth in all (stronger and cheaper gears of a larger module), then the smaller shifts and helix angle, then the larger module, then the smaller deviation. The modules start at 0.5 mm by default (MitCad’s practical least; modules asks for smaller ones).

QueryFieldsResult
gear_pairfirst, second (at placements of the two gears, or {"seat": …}, below), ratio (z2 / z1, the first gear’s speed over the second’s; more than 0); optional kind (spur or helical; both without it), pressure_angle (radians, 20 degrees), modules ([min, max] mm; from 0.5 mm without it), second_series (false), min_teeth (12, at least 5), max_teeth (200), ratio_tolerance (relative, 0.02), max_profile_shift (0.5), max_helix_angle (radians, 30 degrees, at most 45), limit (20)center_distance (a), axial_offset (the second placement’s origin from the first’s along the first’s axis: the gears’ planes should overlap), warning (when the second axis points the opposite way from the first, mitcad#749: the second axis points the opposite way from the first: the gears would be built from their placements in opposite directions; flip one, or pick its shaft nearer its other end, so that both point the same way, and then no other, since axial_offset is measured from the wrong end; else when axial_offset is 0.0005 mm or more: the second placement lies 5 mm along the axis from the first: put the gears in one plane so that they mesh across their face width), candidates: module, teeth ([z1, z2]), ratio (z2 / z1), ratio_deviation (relative: ratio / asked - 1), fit, undercut ([bool, bool]), corrected (shifts against undercut added to the fit’s own: an exact pair so is “exact, corrected”), profile_shift ([x1, x2], when either is not 0), helix_angle (with helix), first and second (the gear fields to merge into each gear’s definition: kind, module, teeth, pressure_angle, profile_shift, helix_angle, left_handed as they apply); an error when the axes are not parallel or meet

The placements are resolved at the timeline marker in the coordinates of their references (the active component’s for its own geometry), as seat_frame resolves a seat. A shaft in another component’s occurrence (mitcad#754) is given as a seat with its occurrence link, as a part’s definition takes it: {"seat": {"shaft": <its face or edge>, "link": {"source": "O1"}, "near": [x, y, z], "offset": 3}} (Seats on shafts; only seat beside it). It resolves as seat_frame does for the active component, the shaft moved by the occurrences’ placements, so the distance is the one the view shows.

CommandFieldsResult
add_gear_pairfirst, second (gear definitions as add_feature’s def takes them, without type, usually each with its at and a candidate’s fields; the first may sit on a shaft of another component’s occurrence by its seat with the link), optional component, names ([first, second])uids, names: both gears added in one undo step (Add Gear Pair), computed once, or, when either is refused, neither, the undo and redo steps staying as they were (mitcad#758); the second gets mesh_with: {"gear": <the first>}, which turns it to engage (it must not have a mesh_with of its own, and since a gear on a seat is not placed by a mesh too, it is placed by at on geometry of its own component)

The same pair can be made with two add_features and merge_undo (Undo, revisions and the saved state): read undo_depth, add the first gear, add the second with mesh_with naming the first, merge back to the depth.

Belt Drive

The belt_drive query takes two placements (the pulleys’ axes), a ratio and a belt profile and lists the tooth counts that fit, each with the catalogue belts that go round them and the tension travel each needs: the change of the centre distance from the axes’ distance C to the distance at which that belt fits (positive: the axes must move apart). The belt’s pitch length at a centre distance is the open belt’s of Pulleys; the distance for a belt length is found from it. The catalogue (catalogue in the answer):

  • given: the pitch lengths of belt_lengths;
  • library (without belt_lengths): the closed belts of the parts library (tools/libraries/profiles/linear-belts.json, each with its supplier’s page there; the answer’s belts name their part as library, with its name and the belt’s width in mm): GT2 2 mm 200, 280, 400 and 852 mm; HTD 3M 225, 255 and 351 mm; HTD 5M 255, 355 and 575 mm. No other belt data is assumed;
  • whole_teeth (the profiles the library has no closed belts of, GT2 3 mm, T5 and XL, or with whole_teeth): every whole number of belt teeth, lengths n * pitch. The nearest is then at most one pitch of travel away (a pitch of belt length is about half a pitch of centre distance), so the travel says little: the size of the pulleys decides.

Verdict. Each belt has a fit from its travel: ok within 0.5 mm either way (it goes on as the axes are; MitCad’s default), tensioner when it fits further apart (longer than the path: the axes move apart by the travel, or a tensioner takes up the slack), short when it fits only closer (shorter than the path: the axes must move closer by the travel). A candidate’s and belt_check’s fit is its first belt’s.

Sizes. The smaller pulley has at least min_teeth_in_mesh (6) teeth in mesh, and each pulley at least min_teeth, by default MitCad’s recommended teeth (our defaults above the profile’s least teeth, so that the belt is not bent round the smallest pulley a groove allows; not a standard’s values):

ProfileLeast teeth (a pulley’s limit)Belt Drive’s default min_teeth
gt2_2mm1016
gt2_3mm1016
htd_3m1014
htd_5m1214
t51012
xl1012

A min_teeth given goes down to the least teeth, never below.

Order. The ratio is what is asked: the smallest ratio deviation (ratio_deviation, relative: ratio / asked - 1, as Gear Pair’s) first, deviations within the same 0.5 % step counting as one, so that pairs meeting the ratio come before those missing it within ratio_tolerance; then the smallest travel, travels within the same 0.5 mm step counting as one; among them the smaller pulleys first (the smaller pulley’s teeth), then the smaller ratio deviation, then the smaller travel.

QueryFieldsResult
belt_drivefirst, second (at placements, or seats with their link as gear_pair’s), ratio (z2 / z1), profile (gt2_2mm, gt2_3mm, htd_3m, htd_5m, t5, xl); optional belt_lengths (catalogue pitch lengths, mm), whole_teeth (false), min_teeth (the table above), max_teeth (150; at most 1000, mitcad#748: a larger one, meant as “no limit”, is refused with max_teeth must be at most 1000 teeth, got …; the search stops anyway at the first tooth count whose pulleys no longer fit between the axes), min_teeth_in_mesh (6), ratio_tolerance (0.02), belts (the nearest belts per candidate, 3), limit (20)center_distance (C), axial_offset, warning (as gear_pair’s: the axes pointing opposite ways, else … put the pulleys in one plane so that they run in one belt's plane), catalogue (given, library or whole_teeth), candidates: teeth ([z1, z2]), ratio, ratio_deviation, pitch_diameters, belt_length (the pitch length at C), teeth_in_mesh (on the smaller pulley), belts (length, teeth, center_distance, travel, fit, and for a library belt library, name, width; the smallest travel first), travel and fit (the first belt’s), first and second (kind: toothed, profile, teeth); an error when the axes are not parallel
belt_checkpulleys (two pulley features of one component, as built), optional belt_lengths, whole_teeth (false), belts (3)the same check for a pair of pulleys already made, from their axes as built (their mount frames bore): center_distance, axial_offset, warning (as belt_drive’s, the opposite axes included), belt_length, belt_teeth, wrap_angles, teeth_in_mesh, catalogue, belts with their travel and fit, fit (the first belt’s); an error when the pulleys share no belt (different profiles, overlapping pitch circles) or their axes are not parallel
place_frameat (as a feature takes it)where the placement puts a part at the timeline marker: origin, x_axis, y_axis, axis (the normal); with an axis form also seat (as seat_frame gives it; diameter null on an axis on its own); an error with the reason when a reference does not resolve
CommandFieldsResult
add_belt_drivefirst, second (pulley definitions without type, each with its placement and a candidate’s fields), optional component, namesuids, names: both pulleys added in one undo step (Add Belt Drive), computed once; when either is refused nothing of the pair is made and the undo and redo steps stay as they were (mitcad#758)

A belt check kept with a pulley. A pulley may keep its belt with an earlier pulley feature checked: "belt_check": {"pulley": "F3"} in its definition. It places nothing and changes no geometry; it is a relation the design keeps (saved and loaded with the definition, a reference to the other pulley by its uid as belt_with’s, so a rename does not break it and the other pulley is not deleted under it). pulley_values of the pulley (by uid, as built) then has belt_check: belt_check’s answer for the two pulleys with pulley, or {"pulley", "error"} when the check cannot be made (not built, other components, not parallel, no shared belt); its catalogue is belt_lengths of the query, else the library’s or whole teeth as above.

gear_values and pulley_values give a placed part’s bore from its at as from a seat (shaft_diameter, seat for an axis form), and bearing_values its fitting size.

Tests: features::place_at (the frames of the three forms, offsets from two lines, flip, align and angle), features::place_at_tests (pulleys, gears, coils and holes placed by a shaft, an origin or construction axis, a sketch point and an origin plane’s offsets on the mock kernel; the part following a longer shaft and a moved sketch plane; the old forms building as before; a gear turned by its mesh on its own axis; the warnings of axes pointing opposite ways; the pairs on a shaft in another component’s occurrence), features::drives (Belt Drive meeting the ratio first; the Gear Pair candidates: an exact, a profile shift and a helix case, undercut flagged and shifted out; the Belt Drive candidates, their sizes, travel and the library’s belts, checked against the parts library’s file; a huge max_teeth stopping where the pulleys no longer fit), api::drives (the queries, the axial warning, a belt check kept with a pulley, an absurd max_teeth refused).

Measurement objects

Measurements kept in the design (mitcad#649; since mitcad#702 they are Annotations, and these commands are their short forms; core/model/src/document/annotations.rs, api/measurements.rs): the application’s Annotations window. Each has a name (Distance1, Angle1, …), a color (#rrggbb, or auto: Annotations’ look), a light bulb (visible), the kind of value it shows and one or two picks a and b, given as the measure query’s selections as fields (Analysis queries: {"body", "face" | "edge" | "vertex", "occurrence"} or {"datum", "occurrence"}). The picks refer to geometry by topological names, so a measurement follows the model: it is measured at the timeline marker whenever it is asked for, as the measure query measures its picks (in the design’s coordinates, Measure in the design, Measure with axes).

The kinds (kind) and the picks they take:

kindPicksValueDefault name
distancetwothe closest distance (between.distance), mmDistance<n>
angletwo, each with a normal, a direction or an axisbetween.angle, radiansAngle<n>
offsettwo parallel planes (planar faces, datum planes)between.offset, mmOffset<n>
axis_distancetwo, one with an axis at leastbetween.axis_distance, mmAxisDistance<n>
center_distancetwo circles or arcsbetween.center_distance, mmCenterDistance<n>
radiusone with a circle (a round edge or face)the circle’s radius, mmRadius<n>
diameterone with a circletwice the radius, mmDiameter<n>
  • Kept. add_measurement measures the picks first and refuses those that are not there (the measurement's picks: …) and a kind they do not have (the picks have no offset; they have distance, angle). Without a kind it takes the first the picks have of: a circle’s diameter (an arc’s radius); of two picks offset, then axis_distance, then center_distance, then distance (each when longer than 1e-6 mm), then angle (two picks that touch), else distance. One pick without a circle has nothing to keep. Names are the measurements’ own (an analysis or a body may have the same). set_measurement_kind refuses a kind the picks do not have now.
