A view sees what it shows (mitcad#717): an edge’s part nearest the click must lie inside a detail’s circle and outside a break’s band (a long edge across a band or into a detail is picked where it shows); a section sees what lies behind its plane (an edge in front of it is no pick, one across it is cut there) and picks a planar face where its plane cuts it (the cut face’s edge in the face’s plane, found again on every draw among the projection’s cut faces). The cut edges in the face’s plane, joined end to end, are that face’s cut line in pieces (mitcad#1361: a face cut beside a hole is cut in two); a click picks the piece under it, {"body", "face", "on_cut": [u, v]}, its middle in the face’s own coordinates (as on_face’s below), found again on every draw as the piece that point lies on (one it lies on no piece of makes the annotation broken: the point picked on the cut of the face … lies on no piece of it), and its ends ("point": "start" or "end", the piece’s ends along the line, picked as corners where no edge’s end is seen) and middle ("center"). A face picked without on_cut (older files) is its whole cut line, from its first piece’s start to its last piece’s end across the gaps; no point but center goes with it. Picks as near as one another (within 0.25 mm of paper) are told apart by the view: the one the projection draws as a visible line first, then the one nearest the eye. An arc is where it is (seen end on its range of angles, from the side its reach), and a whole circle has no start or end to pick. A round face reaches between the circles of its own edges (not those of another face on its axis). Whenever the sheet is drawn each pick is found again by its name (Kernel::edge_geometry, Kernel::face_geometry), so the annotation follows the model; one that is gone (its body no longer shown by the view, its edge or face not in the body, a face that is not round) makes the annotation broken: it is not drawn or exported, the drawing query says why and gives it a small box beside its view, and the sheet’s warnings say annotation 2 on view 3: the face F4:side(c1) of Body1 is gone.

Places are kept in millimetres of paper, relative to the picks, so an annotation keeps its look at any scale and moves with its view and the model: line_offset (a linear dimension’s line across from the middle of its picks, an ordinate’s level from its origin, an angle’s arc radius; when left out, a linear dimension’s line goes 10 mm beyond the view’s box on the side of its picks), text_offset (along and across a dimension line; a leader’s text, a datum’s square, a frame, a symbol from the arrow’s point: 10, 8 by default, a datum’s square’s lower middle 0, 12; a circle’s text from its centre), at (where a leader’s pick was clicked, in view millimetres), tip_along (mitcad#1295: where a datum label’s triangle or a frame’s arrow sits along its pick, the fraction of the way from the pick’s start by its own direction, 0 to 1: an edge from its start to its end, an arc from its first end to its second, a round face along its axis, a circle seen from the side across from its low end; set when the label is added or its picks change, so the tip keeps its place on the edge when the model or the view changes; left out on a point, a whole circle seen end on, and labels of older files, whose tip is the pick’s point nearest at). slide moves the tip to the pick’s point nearest where the drag takes it, clamped to the pick’s ends (at and tip_along then that point’s), the square or the frame keeping its text_offset, so it follows; a datum label on a straight edge runs on along the edge’s line past its ends instead (mitcad#1296, below), and one on a face over the face’s plane. One undo step, Move datum A of Drawing1 (a datum label moved is named by its letter; mitcad#1294); refused for the other annotations (tests: core/model-drawing/src/annotate.rs, a quarter along an edge made twice as long, the slide and its clamp, a frame’s arrow, arcs, round faces; drawing_annotation_tests.rs, the slide, its undo and a longer edge in the model).

Datum labels on an extension line and on a face (mitcad#1296, ISO 5459):

  • A datum label on a straight edge may have its tip on the edge’s line beyond its ends (tip_along below 0 or above 1, reached by slide): it then draws its own thin extension line from 1 mm off the edge’s nearer end to 2 mm past the tip, as an edge_extension draws one. It stays an annotation of the edge, its pick unchanged, and keeps its fraction when the edge’s length changes.
  • A Datum Label click inside a planar face’s outline, where the view sees the face face on and no edge, point or round face is within reach (the drawing_pick query’s type datum, or its want datum; seen face), picks the face with the point: {"body", "face", "on_face": [u, v]}, the point in the face’s own coordinates (millimetres from its plane’s origin along axes chosen from the plane’s normal, in its body’s coordinates), so it keeps its place on the face when the model or the view changes. The face nearest the eye wins. The tip is that point; slide moves it over the face’s plane. on_face is refused with an edge or a point.
  • terminator: "triangle" or "dot" (a filled dot, 1 mm radius, the leader from its middle), given on add_drawing_annotation and edit_drawing_annotation (null: back to the default); left out, a dot on a face picked face on and a triangle on anything else. Only a datum label has one.

Tests: core/model-drawing/src/annotate.rs (a datum a quarter past its edge’s end with its extension line, on an edge twice as long and before the start; a dot on a face, the terminator chosen, the face’s axes), drawing_annotation_tests.rs (datums_on_an_edges_extension_and_on_a_face_keep_their_place: both kinds, the model twice as large, a dot slid, the terminator switched and refused for a note), tools/ui-drawing-dimension-spacing-test.sh.

series: "baseline" makes a linear dimension from the first pick to each other one, their lines 7 mm apart; "chain" from each to the next, in a row. An angle’s arc keeps a radius of 2 mm at least, whether dragged, placed or given as line_offset. The commands move a leader’s text exactly as told; the application’s drag of a note’s text, a datum’s square or a frame first asks drawing_snap, which snaps the leader to multiples of 45 degrees (Dimension spacing, Leader angles; mitcad#1294).

Pictorial views (an isometric view, a projected view from a corner, any view that does not look along an axis of its component, and their details; mitcad#717): lengths along the view’s x or y, ordinates and angles would be foreshortened, so a horizontal or vertical linear dimension, an ordinate and an angle are refused there (and drawn broken when a file has one); a linear dimension is aligned there unless told otherwise and measures the true distance of its picks’ points in 3D (a straight edge’s middle, a circle’s centre); radii and diameters are true anyway. A base view along a given direction (not a standard one) that looks square at a planar face of a body it shows, and its details, are orthographic for the annotations whose picks all lie on such bodies (mitcad#718, mitcad#722); the isometric presets and the corner views stay pictorial whatever face they look square at. An aligned dimension on any view along no axis keeps measuring its picks’ true distance in 3D (in the face’s plane the same as the projected one), so a file’s aligned dimensions keep their values.

Datum letters are one set for the model and its drawings: a datum label of a drawing takes the first letter that neither the model’s nor any drawing’s datum labels have and no frame refers to (the model’s next_datum_letter, which counts the drawings’ too), and a letter in use anywhere is refused (datum A exists: DatumA, datum B exists: a datum label of Drawing1), in the model as on a drawing. An edit that keeps an annotation’s letter is no new claim (a file where two drawings share a letter edits as before). A copy of a component (Paste New, Insert Component as a copy) gives its drawings’ datum labels the next free letters where theirs are in use in the design, and their frames refer to the new letters (mitcad#718). A datum’s new letter reaches every frame that refers to its old one, in the same undo step (mitcad#745): a model datum’s (edit_annotation with letter) the model’s frames and every drawing’s, a drawing datum’s (edit_drawing_annotation with letter) its own drawing’s frames, the other drawings’ and the model’s. A frame, of the model or of a drawing, warns of a datum no label has only when neither the model nor any drawing has that label.

Views. add_drawing_view and edit_drawing_view take center_marks (on when a view is added: a centre mark on each circle the view sees end on that turns half way round at least, a half hole’s too, concentric ones once, and a centreline on each round face it sees from the side whose ends do; inside a detail’s circle, outside breaks and behind a section’s plane only; a view without hidden lines marks only the circles and round faces it draws, not the holes the part hides, such as a cross hole seen from the side through a bar, mitcad#1286) and retrieved_dimensions (off: the dimensions of the sketches that shape the bodies the view shows (those of the features that made or name them, and of their components' features that neither make nor name a body), seen square on, where the view shows them (behind a section’s plane, in a detail’s circle, beside breaks), written by #702’s engine; the root’s drawings; not on pictorial views). A component’s sketch dimensions are drawn where its occurrences put them: once for each placement of its bodies the view shows, through that occurrence’s transform (mitcad#744; a sketch of the drawing’s own component that made a body of another component where it is), and the square-on test and the section, detail and break filters take them there; the sheet’s sketch_dimensions place them the same way. A sketch dimension a view retrieves is not drawn again by the sheet’s sketch_dimensions. A view’s deletion takes its annotations along.

The drawing query’s sheet asked for has annotations: each view annotation in its file form with view, broken, label (its words on one line: 40 ±0.1, Ø10 H7, a note’s lines joined by /, a datum’s letter, a frame’s cells joined by |), value (a dimension’s, mm or radians), measured (a dimension’s value as the sheet writes it without its own texts: its prefix, value and tolerance, 40 ±0.1, what a format.replace stands in place of; mitcad#1292), warning (a fit code out of range, a datum referred to that no label has), box (on the sheet), or error; then the text notes ("type": "text", text, at, box). Views list center_marks, retrieved_dimensions and their annotations’ ids. Groups: dimension (id A3), center-mark, note, datum, feature-control-frame, surface-finish, retrieved-dimension. The export draws them and counts the dimensions in its dimensions.

The drawing_pick query (drawing, sheet (0), view (the smallest drawn view there when left out), at, type or want: any, point, line, circle, and since mitcad#1693 dimension (neither given: as any, and a centre pattern’s circle), round (radius, diameter: a circle, a round face or a centre pattern’s circle) and straight (angle: a straight edge or a centre line the view draws)) gives the pick a click there makes: view, pick, seen (point, line, circle, axis), at (its point on the sheet) and items to show it ({"point"}, {"line"}, {"circle": {"center", "radius"}}, {"arc": {"center", "radius", "start", "end"}}, sheet mm), or "pick": null. The drawing query also gives datum_letters: the letters of the model’s and every drawing’s datum labels, what a frame can refer to.

Files: a view’s annotations (id, type, picks, along, line_offset, text_offset, at, format, tolerance, text, letter, frame, finish), center_marks, retrieved_dimensions; a sheet’s notes (id, text, at, height); left out when empty or off. Ids are unique among a drawing’s annotations and notes; a drawing’s datum letters too. A component’s copy maps its drawings’ picks (bodies, occurrences, the features in edge and face names).

Classes: the commands and drawing_pick are the model’s. Tests: the tests in core/model-drawing/src/annotate.rs (measures, layouts, checks, symbols), core/model-tests/drawing-views/src/drawing_annotation_tests.rs (dimensions by names and by clicks with tolerances and fit codes, the model changed under them, drags, broken ones, a diameter end on and from the side, centre marks automatic and on request, an ordinate, notes, datum labels, frames, finish symbols, text notes, a baseline, the file, the export, refusals), tests/drawing_tools.cpp, tools/ui-drawings-test.sh, tools/ui-windows-drawings-test.ps1, and core/model-tests/drawing-views/src/pick_tests.rs (mitcad#717: a section’s picks behind its plane and of the faces it cuts, picks across breaks and into details, edges on one another told apart by the eye, arcs and whole circles, a pictorial view’s refusals and aligned dimension in 3D, an angle’s radius kept, a round face’s own ends and a half hole’s centre mark, datum letters shared with the model, a component’s copied drawing’s picks, retrieved dimensions of the view’s own bodies once), and core/model-tests/drawing-views/src/model_follow_tests.rs (a new sheet without the last one’s text notes, mitcad#742; views, dimensions and balloons following an occurrence moved to another parent, and a component’s drawing refusing a move out of it, mitcad#743; retrieved dimensions of a translated component and of one placed twice, mitcad#744; datum letters changed in the model and on a drawing reaching every frame, mitcad#745).

Tables on drawing views

Hole tables, parts lists and balloons on a drawing’s views (mitcad#707 phase 3; core/model/src/drawing/tables_def.rs, core/model-drawing/src/tables.rs, api/drawing_tables.rs). Each is an annotation of its view (Annotations on drawing views): it takes the same commands, is kept, saved, undone, compared and copied with a component as the others are, and a view’s deletion takes it along. Its rows are worked out from the model whenever the sheet is drawn, so it follows the design.

typePicksWhat it is
hole_tablenone, or one point: its originthe round holes of the bodies the view shows that the view sees end on (Kernel::round_holes, with the threads of the threads query, as File › Export Drawing finds them), where it shows them (in a detail’s circle, beside breaks, behind a section’s plane), tagged in the view beside each hole and listed
parts_listnonethe components the view shows, each once with how many of its occurrences the view shows; numbered
balloonone: an edge or a face of a component’s bodythat component’s number in a parts list, in a circle on a leader to the pick

add_drawing_annotation takes a table’s place, at (its upper left corner on the sheet, mm; needed), and table, its settings:

  • columns: the columns shown, in order. A hole table’s: tag, x, y, size (Ø6.6, with a counterbore or countersink), depth (THRU or the depth), thread (the designation, - without). A parts list’s own: item, quantity, name (a library part’s designation, else the component’s name), part_number (the parts list’s: the component’s own Part number, else its library or BUILD entry’s, mitcad#2138), description (the property Description), material (the computed Material); any other column is a property of the components, Key or Set/Key, as the parts_list query’s properties give them (its header the key in capitals). Left out: all of a hole table’s; item, quantity, name, description, material of a parts list’s.
  • sort (a column; a hole table’s tags, a parts list’s names when left out or null) and descending (false): numbers first, by value, then tags by their letters and numbers, then other text alphabetically (cells alike in that order by their texts as they are). A table sorts by a column it does not show too (mitcad#718). A parts list is numbered in that order; sorted by item, it is numbered by name and descending lists it from the last number up.
  • A hole table’s tags: by_size (default: a letter per size, depth and thread, A, B, … without I, O and Q, then AA, AB, …, and a number per hole of it along the view’s x and then y: A1, A2, B1) or numbers (1, 2, … in that order); origin when it has no pick: corner (default: the view’s lower left corner, marked with a cross) or model (the drawing’s component’s origin). Its X and Y are measured along the view’s axes from its origin, in the sheet’s unit; a picked origin is a point of the model, found again on every draw.
  • A parts list’s levels: top (default: the components of the occurrences right below the view’s subject: a view of an occurrence lists what is in it, as do its balloons) or parts (the components whose bodies the view shows, at any depth); the bodies of the drawing’s own component are rows of their own (their name and material). On a section, a detail or a broken view it lists only the bodies the view shows something of: those whose own projection keeps a line behind the plane, inside the circle or beside the breaks (mitcad#718). The components’ BOM Structures act on its rows and balloons (mitcad#1985).
  • title: over the table; HOLES (mm) (the sheet’s unit) and PARTS LIST when left out or null.

A parts list added with "balloons": true (false when left out; mitcad#725) places a balloon on each of its rows in the same undo step (Add parts list 6 and 2 balloons to Drawing1): on the first straight edge, drawn as a visible line, of the row’s bodies that the list counts (on a section, a detail or a broken view those it shows something of); their circles in one column 15 mm right of the view’s box, 12 mm apart from its top down, the highest arrow first, so that they cover neither one another nor the view (text_offset). A row whose bodies show no such edge gets none. The result lists their ids, balloons; balloons on another type is refused.

edit_drawing_annotation takes table with what changes, picks (a hole table’s origin; []: none), and move or at (a table’s place on the sheet: whatever its picks); undo steps Add hole table 5 to Drawing1, Edit parts list 6 of Drawing1, Move balloon 7 of Drawing1. A balloon is dragged as a note is: its circle’s place is kept from its pick (text_offset, 12, 10 mm when left out), so it moves with its component.

A balloon’s number is its component’s row (by the parts list’s levels): in a parts list of its own view first, else of another view of its sheet. A balloon whose pick is gone (its occurrence deleted, its body no longer shown) or that no parts list of its sheet lists is broken (no parts list on the sheet lists Pin). Refused: a table without its place, a hole table’s unknown column, a sort column a table does not have, a parts list’s tags or origin, a hole table’s levels, table on another type, and a hole table on a pictorial view (it sees no hole end on). A base view along a given direction that looks square at a planar face of a body it shows counts as orthographic, as one along an axis does: its lengths in that face’s plane are true (mitcad#718; for the annotations on such bodies, mitcad#722). On a section, a detail or a broken view, which bodies a parts list counts and a body’s own cut faces (picks) come from each body’s own projection there, kept in a bounded cache of their own by the body’s version and placement and the view (mitcad#722), apart from the views’ projections. A placed body’s holes are kept in the document’s projection cache by its shape version, placement and threads, so a sheet drawn again finds them once; a search that fails is not kept, so it is tried again on the next draw and its warning names the body as it is then (mitcad#722).

The drawing query’s entry of a table has columns (shown), available (column and header: its type’s own and a parts list’s property columns shown), sort, rows (how many), a parts list’s empty_columns (its shown part_number and description columns that have an empty cell, for the panel’s hint, mitcad#2138) and label: a hole table’s rows’ cells (A1 20 15 Ø6.6 THRU -; A2 60 5 Ø6.6 THRU -, no holes), a parts list’s numbers, names and quantities (1 Pin x1; 2 Plate x2, no components), a balloon’s number. Groups: hole-table (its title, cells, tags at their holes and its origin’s cross), parts-list, balloon, each A<id>; the export writes them (PDF, SVG, DXF). File › Export Drawing keeps its own sheet-wide hole table (annotations' hole_table: every orthographic view’s holes, tagged per view), which is not one of these.

Files: an annotation’s table (place, columns, sort, descending, tags, origin, levels, title; each at its default left out).

Classes: the model’s. Tests: those in core/model-drawing/src/tables.rs (a table drawn, its settings checked, cells sorted), api::drawing_tables::tests (size letters), core/model-tests/drawing/src/table_tests.rs (a hole table’s tags, rows, origins, columns, sort and title, its origin following the model, moved, saved, undone, holes gone; refusals; a parts list of an assembly’s view with balloons, sorted the other way and a property column, a placement deleted and undone, a balloon without its list, the export, a parts list that places its balloons, mitcad#725), core/model-tests/drawing-views/src/follow_up_tests.rs (mitcad#718: hole tables on section, detail and broken views; two parts lists on one sheet and their balloons; a section’s parts list; a hidden sort column and the item sort; a view square to an inclined face; a copied component’s drawing with tables, balloons and re-lettered datum labels; an unchanged letter on a shared file; the caches of geometry and holes; tables in PDF and DXF), tests/drawing_tools.cpp, tools/ui-drawings-test.sh (a hole table on a top view that empties when the hole is suppressed; a parts list with its balloons, undone; a parts list and a balloon on an assembly, exported, the list following a deleted placement and its balloon broken), tools/ui-windows-drawings-test.ps1 (a parts list and a balloon).

Drawing templates and revisions

Sheet templates and revision tables of drawings (mitcad#707 phase 4; core/model/src/drawing/template_def.rs, core/model-drawing/src/template.rs, api/drawing_templates.rs). A template is data: the frame’s margins, the title block’s size, lines and fields, where the projection symbol goes, and a revision table above the block. A sheet keeps a complete copy of the template it was given (template in the file), so a drawing looks the same wherever its design goes and a library change never changes it; a sheet without one keeps the simple title block of File › Export Drawing.

Templates come from three places:

  • built-in: iso (A sizes, A3 to start with; 20 mm filing margin, 10 elsewhere; a 180 x 36 mm block) and ansi (ANSI sizes, B to start with; 12.7 mm margins; a 178 x 40 mm block), the JSON files in core/model-drawing/src/templates/;
  • user: drawing-templates/<id>.json in the user’s library folder, beside its materials and print profiles (print_library::user_library, MITCAD_PRINT_LIBRARY_DIR);
  • project: drawing-templates/<id>.json in the project’s library folder (<project>/print-library), versioned with the project.

A template file: {"format": "mitcad-drawing-template", "id", "name", "size" (the sheet a drawing made with it starts with), "projection" (its projection method, first_angleorthird_angle; ISO first, ANSI third; mitcad#725), "margins": [left, bottom, right, top], "title_block": {"width", "height", "lines": [[x0, y0, x1, y1], …], "fields": [{"label", "text", "at": [x, y], "size": [w, h], "height"}], "projection_symbol": [x, y]}, "revision_table": {"rows": 4}}, lengths in mm from the block’s lower left corner; the id is the file’s name. A field’s label is written small in its cell’s upper left corner, its text at the bottom, made smaller down to 2 mm and then cut when it is too wide. Names in braces in a text are filled in from the design whenever the sheet is drawn, so the block follows the design:

NameValue
titlethe sheet’s title (title_block.title), else the component’s property Title (the root’s is the design’s summary, Summary/Title, mitcad#1088), else the component’s or the design’s name (the drawing query’s title)
namethe component’s or the design’s name
drawingthe drawing’s name
numberthe sheet’s drawing number, else the component’s part number
part_number, descriptionthe component’s properties Part number, Description; a description without one is Summary/Comments, the component’s, else the design’s (mitcad#1088)
materialthe component’s property Material, else the materials of the bodies it shows, each once: a body without its own takes the nearest default up its path from the component, then the component’s and those above it where it is first placed, then the root’s (mitcad#758)
massthe component’s property Mass (stored or its library’s, not the one worked out; mitcad#722), else the bodies the component shows, each where it is placed: their volumes (kept by shape version) times their materials’ densities, in the design’s mass unit
authorthe sheet’s (title_block.author), else the property Author, else the design’s summary’s Summary/Author (mitcad#1088)
datethe sheet’s, else today’s
scalethe sheet’s first base view’s
sheet, sheet_number, sheets1/2, 1, 2
size, units, projectionA3 (ANSI B), the length unit, THIRD ANGLE
revisionthe latest revision’s letter, - before the first
any othera property of the drawing’s component, Key or Set/Key (empty without one)

Commands and the query:

CommandFieldsResult
add_drawing, add_drawing_sheet, edit_drawing_sheettemplate: a built-in one’s id (iso, ansi), a template’s data as drawing_templates lists it (a user’s or a project’s), or ""/null for the simple title block; add_drawing takes the template’s size and projection unless they are given (not a layout’s projection: its views are placed by it; mitcad#725); a new sheet takes the last sheet’s templateas before
add_drawing_revisiondrawing, description (needed), letter (the one after the latest: A, B, … without I, O, Q, then AA), date (today’s), authorrevision; undo step Add revision A to Drawing1
edit_drawing_revisiondrawing, revision (its letter), and what changes: letter, description, date ("": today’s, as for a new one, mitcad#722), author ("" clears)undo step Edit revision A of Drawing1
delete_drawing_revisiondrawing, revisionundo step Delete revision A of Drawing1
save_drawing_templatedrawing, sheet (0), library (user or project), name, id (from the name: Company A3 → company-a3), project (the project’s folder)path, id, choice (project:company-a3); writes the sheet’s template with its size and projection method, replacing one of the id; no undo step

The drawing_templates query (project: the project’s folder) lists templates, each a template’s data with its library (builtin, user, project) and its choice (iso, user:<id>, project:<id>), the built-in ones first, then the user’s and the project’s by name; and problems (files that are no template).

The drawing query gives each sheet’s template (id, name, library, choice; null for the simple block), the drawn sheet’s title_fields (each label with its text as drawn; the simple block’s TITLE, DRAWING NO. or BODY, DATE and DRAWN BY), and the drawing’s revisions (letter, description, date, author) and next_revision. A template’s sheet draws frame, title-block (its lines, labels, values and the projection symbol) and, once the drawing has a revision, revision-table (REV, DESCRIPTION, DATE, BY: its rows latest revisions above the block, the latest on top); the views' area is the template’s frame above its block and the revision table’s whole room (its rows and its header, 5 mm each), kept clear from the start so that the first revision overlaps no view placed in the area (mitcad#722; the export’s hole table keeps clear of it too). Exports (PDF, SVG, DXF) write them as drawn.

Refused: an unknown built-in template, a template that is not one (an id of other than letters, digits, - and _, no name, a block of no size, a field without a cell, a revision table of other than 1 to 50 rows, margins that leave no frame or a title block that with the revision table’s room does not fit in the frame of its own size), a sheet whose template does not fit it so (its size or orientation changed, or the template given; mitcad#722), a revision without a description or with a letter the drawing has, saving the simple title block as a template, and a library other than user or project.

Classes: the revision commands are the model’s; save_drawing_template and drawing_templates read and write library folders (file IO). Saved, undone, compared and copied with a component’s drawings as the rest of a drawing. Tests: those in core/model-drawing/src/template.rs (the built-in templates, fields filled, revision letters, a filled template drawn, templates checked, saved and listed in folders of the test’s own, a template fitting its sheet), core/model-tests/drawing/src/template_tests.rs (a template’s projection method brought to a new drawing, mitcad#725; a template’s block following the design’s material, mass, properties and sheets; revisions added, shown, edited, deleted, undone and saved; templates per sheet, a template’s data with a property field, copied with a component; saved to a project’s library and chosen; exported), api::drawing_templates::tests; tools/ui-drawings-test.sh (the ISO template chosen in Create Drawing, the title block’s material following the body’s, a revision added and exported).

Drawing defaults, sketches, patterns and turned views

What a drawing adds to Drawings in the design and Annotations on drawing views since mitcad#729 (core/model/src/drawing/def.rs, annotate_def.rs, core/model-drawing/src/annotate.rs, api/drawings.rs, api/drawing_annotations.rs).

The drawing’s decimals and letters. add_drawing and edit_drawing take decimals (0 to 6) and text_height (paper mm, more than 0 and at most 100); edit_drawing takes null for none (undo step Edit Drawing1; Rename Drawing1 for a name alone). They are what every dimension and annotation of the drawing takes unless it has its own: a dimension’s value its format’s decimals (else the drawing’s, else as many as it needs, up to three), and the retrieved sketch dimensions the drawing’s; an annotation’s letters (dimensions, leaders, datum labels, frames, finish symbols, balloons, tables, whose cells and rows grow with them) its own height, else the drawing’s, else 3.5 mm; a text note’s and a text’s likewise. add_drawing_annotation and edit_drawing_annotation take height for every annotation now (null: the drawing’s again; before, a text note’s only). The drawing query gives the drawing’s decimals and text_height (null when none). File: the drawing’s defaults (decimals, text_height), an annotation’s height; left out when none.

Lines, arcs and texts outside the model. add_drawing_annotation takes "type": "line" (points: its two ends), "arc" (points: its centre, its start and its end, counter-clockwise from the start; an end the way the start lies makes a whole circle) and "text" with a view (at, text, height), each with pen (thin (default), thick, extra_thick (0.7 mm, ISO 128’s extra wide line, mitcad#1402), hidden, chain; not a text’s) and, instead of a view, a sheet (0): points are sheet millimetres. On the sheet they are kept in sheet millimetres (a text on the sheet is a text note); in a view in its coordinates (model millimetres in the view’s plane), so that they move, scale and turn with the view; they pick nothing of the model and follow nothing else. Their ids are the drawing’s annotation ids: edit_drawing_annotation takes points (as when added), pen, text, height, at (a text’s place) and move (a drag on the sheet), undo steps Add line 4 to Drawing1, Move arc 5 of Drawing1, Edit text 6 of Drawing1; delete_drawing_annotation deletes them, and a view’s deletion takes its own along. The drawing query lists them among the sheet’s annotations in their file form (type, id, from and to; center, radius, start, end in radians; text, at, height; pen) with view (null on the sheet), label (a text’s lines joined by /, else line or arc) and box; a view lists their ids under sketch. Group: sketch (A<id>). Files: a sheet’s and a view’s sketch, left out when empty. Refused: other annotations’ fields on them, a line of no length, an arc of no size or turning backwards, a text without its text or place, a pen for a text, points or pen for other annotations, a text in a sheet’s sketch in a file.

A drawn line’s width and pattern (mitcad#1447). A line’s or an arc’s pen is a width (thin (default, 0.18 mm), thick (0.35 mm), extra_thick (0.7 mm)) and a pattern (continuous (default), dashed (3 mm dashes, 1 mm gaps), chain (long dash dotted, 12, 1.5, 0.5, 1.5 mm)), any width with any pattern; the dashes are the same at every width. add_drawing_annotation and edit_drawing_annotation take both (an edit changes the one given and keeps the other), and still take pen: thin, thick and extra_thick are that width and continuous, hidden thin and dashed, chain thin and chain; given with width or pattern, pen sets both first and those change their part. Refused where pen is (a text, other annotations: “no points or pen”), and an unknown width or pattern. The drawing query gives every line and arc its width and pattern beside its file form. Files: a pen one of the five names says exactly is written as before, as pen (left out when thin and continuous), so that a file of those pens is the same as before and older versions read it; the four other combinations are written as width and pattern (older versions do not read a file that has one). Old files' pen is read as above: nothing an existing drawing draws changes. The sheet draws a combination with its width’s line width and its pattern’s dashes (the drawing query’s pens thin, thick, extra_thick, hidden, chain as before, and dashed_thick, dashed_extra_thick, chain_thick, chain_extra_thick), and so do the PDF and SVG files; DXF and DWG put each new combination on a layer of its own (HIDDEN_THICK, HIDDEN_EXTRA_THICK, SECTION_LINE_THICK, SECTION_LINE_EXTRA_THICK; export_drawing’s layers). Model edges, hatching, section lines and the frame keep their fixed pens.

Centre patterns and edge extensions. Two annotation types:

typePicksShows
center_patternone circle seen end on, or severalthe circles of the pattern, found from one: those of its body (where the same occurrence places it) the view sees end on, as large and picked as it was (edges or round faces), where it shows them, each centre once, the one picked first (up to 256); kept by name, so the pattern follows the model. About one centre: the circle through their centres (long-dash dotted; an arc over them, a little beyond the outer ones, when a gap between two of them is wider than one and a half of their pitch), a radial line through each and a small cross at the centre; in a row: the line through them beyond the outer ones and a cross line on each; else a centre mark on each. Group center-mark.
edge_extensiontwo straight edges, or onetwo: thin lines from each edge’s nearer end, 1 mm off it, to 2 mm past where their lines meet (none where the corner lies on the edge); refused for parallel edges. One: thin lines beyond both its ends by line_offset (paper mm, 10 when left out). Group edge-extension.

A centre pattern and an edge extension are refused when they cannot be drawn when added (a straight edge for a pattern, parallel edges), and broken when their picks are gone or no longer draw them. Undo steps Add centre pattern 7 to Drawing1, Add edge extension 8 to Drawing1. The drawing_pick query’s type picks circles for the first, straight edges for the second.

A view turned on the sheet. edit_drawing_view takes rotation: how far the view is turned on the sheet, degrees counter-clockwise (normalised to -180 to 180), about the middle of its box, which stays where it is (refused for a detail, which turns with its parent: a detail turns with its parent). Its x axis turns the other way about its direction to the eye (DrawingSheet::axes); a view from it takes its parent’s axes as turned, so a projected view looks from its side of the turned view, and a projected view turned on its own no longer keeps in line with its parent. An isometric view stays pictorial however it is turned. The drawing query gives each view’s rotation; files its rotation (left out when 0). The view’s group keeps its direction’s id (view-front).

Views that follow a turn. Whenever a command changes the axes of views (rotation, a base view’s direction, a projected view’s side, a section’s flip, the sheet’s projection), what views keep in their coordinates is carried over, parents first (follow_turns):

  • a view turned in its own plane (its eye the same): its annotations turn with it (where a leader was clicked, a leader’s or a circle’s text from its point; a horizontal or vertical dimension keeps measuring along the same direction of the model: a quarter turn makes a horizontal one vertical or the other way, another angle keeps its turn, degrees, in the file), so do the lines, arcs and texts drawn in it, its breaks (by quarter turns only: view 1 has breaks: it turns by quarter turns only while it has them) and the circles of its details, which keep showing the same place of the model;
  • a view that looks another way: a section drawn on it is turned with it, so that its line stays where it was drawn on it (its plane edge on to the view; it then cuts what the view shows there now), a detail keeps its circle; annotations follow their picks and are broken where the view no longer sees them.

Setting a dimension’s along drops its turn (along the view’s x or y as it is). Undo steps Edit view 1 of Drawing1, Edit Sheet1 of Drawing1.

The application: the sheet’s panel (nothing selected) has the drawing’s Decimals and Text Height; an annotation’s panel its Text Height (empty: the drawing’s), a line’s or an arc’s Line (its pen), an edge extension’s Length; a view’s panel its Rotation and its menu Rotate 90° Left and Rotate 90° Right; the Geometry group Line, Arc, Center Pattern and Edge Extension, and Text’s Drawn (on the sheet or in the view clicked) (app/COMMANDS.md, Drawings).

Tests: those in core/model-drawing/src/annotate.rs (a centre pattern on a bolt circle, an arc of one, a row and scattered holes; edge extensions to a corner and of one edge; letters of a given height; a dimension turning with its view; lines, arcs and texts drawn through a view’s map, carried and checked), core/model-tests/drawing-views/src/feature_tests.rs (the drawing’s decimals and letters with the items’ own, saved and undone; lines, arcs and texts on a sheet and in a view moving and scaling with it, edited, saved, refused and deleted; a centre pattern from one hole by name and by a click, broken when a hole goes; edge extensions; a view turned with its dimension and line, saved and undone; a turned view’s detail and breaks; a base view’s direction, a projected view’s side, the projection method and a section’s flip with the sections and details on them following; files without the new fields), core/model-tests/drawing/src/stored_tests.rs (a view with sections or details turning), tests/drawing_tools.cpp, tools/ui-drawing-features-test.sh.

Inactive constraints and dimensions

(mitcad#721.) A sketch constraint or dimension can be inactive: kept in the sketch and shown, but left out of the solve until it is activated. An import makes the constraints and dimensions of a file’s sketch that keep it off the file’s geometry inactive instead of leaving every constraint out (core/import/docs/f3d.md, freecad.md); the user sees what was left out and activates or deletes it.

In the definition, an inactive constraint or dimension has "active": false and an optional inactive_reason, both written only for an inactive one:

{"id": "k7", "type": "coincident", "point": "p3", "entity": "c5",
 "active": false, "inactive_reason": "not met in the imported file"}
  • The solve leaves inactive constraints out; an inactive driving dimension keeps its parameter and value but drives nothing (its value is not checked against its range). An inactive driven one constrains nothing either way, so it still measures: its reference parameter, and what uses it, never keep a stale value (mitcad#723). The spacing dimension of an inactive equal spacing is left out with it. Drawings leave inactive dimensions out.
  • Edits keep what an inactive item asks for (mitcad#723): Extend and Trim keep an inactive length of the line, and Extend never re-measures an inactive dimension on the end it moves (an imported one keeps the file’s value); a point merge (two curve ends made coincident) that makes an inactive constraint the same as an active one keeps the active one.
  • sketch.set_active sets the flag: {"cmd": "sketch.set_active", "sketch": "F1", "items": ["k7", "k9"], "active": true}; active false with an optional reason. Activating is refused, the sketch left as it was, when the sketch then does not solve (cannot be activated: the Vertical on a line can't hold with the activated constraints, then [conflicts: k3] on its last line; see Conflicting constraints) or when an activated one is implied by the others (over-constraining, as sketch.add_constraint refuses it). One undo step, Activate in Sketch1 or Deactivate in Sketch1. An equal spacing takes its spacing dimension with it either way, and activating the spacing dimension activates its equal spacing, since it applies only with it; deactivating the dimension alone leaves the equal spacing (mitcad#723). A copy (sketch.move with copy) of an inactive constraint is inactive too.
  • The sketch query: each constraint and dimension with its active and inactive_reason as in the definition; an inactive driving dimension’s measured is its value. A spacing dimension the solve does not apply (its equal spacing inactive) has "active": false and the equal spacing’s inactive_reason there, so that it is drawn as it acts (mitcad#723). unmet_inactive (only when not empty) lists the inactive ones the solved geometry does not meet (1e-4 mm): those whose activation would move it.
  • Model: Constraint::active, Dimension::active and their inactive_reason (core/sketch/src/lib.rs), SketchDef::dimension_applied, SketchStatus::unmet_inactive and sketch::solve::unmet (solve.rs), SketchEdit::set_active (modify.rs).

The sketch view draws inactive constraints and dimensions in pink, their frames and lines dashed; the tooltip says Not applied: <reason>. The context menu of selected inactive ones offers Activate, of active ones Deactivate; Delete removes them as any other (app/COMMANDS.md).

Classes: the model’s. Tests: api::sketch_inactive_tests (the solve leaves an inactive constraint out, a contradicting activation refused, activation and undo, delete; an inactive dimension keeps its value and drives nothing; the file round trip; mitcad#723: a point merge keeps the active duplicate, an equal spacing and its dimension set aside and activated together, Extend keeps inactive values, an inactive driven dimension keeps its reference measured), the imports’ (sketch::inactive, tests::constraint_tests, freecad::tests), tools/ui-sketch-inactive-test.sh and tools/ui-windows-sketch-inactive-test.ps1 (drawn inactive, its tooltip, Activate refused and applied, undo, Delete). The sketch view logs where each inactive constraint’s symbol is (Constraint k1 glyph at x,y) when the view or the sketch moves it (mitcad#723).

Print bed faces

A body keeps the face that lies on the print bed (mitcad#731, core/model/src/document/print_bed.rs): a planar face, stored with the body’s other attributes by its topological name as it was assigned, so that it follows the body’s edits as a face appearance does (Appearances of faces) and applies to every occurrence of the body. A body has one; setting another replaces it.

CommandFieldsResult
set_print_bed_faceuid (body), face (a topological name of a planar face of the body at the marker; null or left out takes it away)undo step Set Print Bed Face of Body1 / Clear Print Bed Face of Body1 unless nothing changes; it recomputes nothing but print-shaped holes (hole print_shape, mitcad#1515), whose roofs point away from it. A body that is not there or is no solid or mesh body (a surface body is not printed), a name that is no face name or names no face of the body, and a face that is not planar are refused

  • The bodies query gives a body’s print_bed_face: {"face" (as assigned), "faces" (a name of each face it finds at the marker), "error"} (only when it cannot lie on the bed: the print bed face is gone, the print bed face is not planar when its surface is no plane, a surface body is not printed for a body that is no solid or mesh body (one that became a surface body, or a file that stored one; it can still be cleared, mitcad#737), else why its plane is not found, such as a renamed face that two faces fit alike); left out without one. A face that is gone stays kept, for when it comes back (undo).

  • The design file keeps it with the body: "print_bed_face": "F2:end(r{c5})" (left out without one; files without it have none). Copies rename the feature in the name; Paste New of a component copied as bodies names the face of the copy. The comparison of versions lists it with the body.

  • Export on the bed: export with "on_bed": true (3MF, STL and OBJ, in the design’s coordinates; other formats and coordinates: component are refused) puts the bodies written on the print bed. They are one piece, as the 3MF file’s one object:

    • with one body’s bed face among them (a body printed alone, or a component in which one body has one), placed once or placed several times turned alike (normals within 1e-9: a component placed again and moved only, as the face applies to every occurrence), the piece turns so that the face’s outward normal points straight down (−Z; the smallest turn, half a turn about X for a face up), its lowest point goes onto the bed (z = 0) and the middle of its box over the plate’s centre: the centre of the design’s printer’s bed_shape (Print profiles), else of a 256 × 256 mm plate, (128, 128);
    • with the bed faces of several bodies, or of a body placed turned differently, the bodies stay as they are assembled (a 3MF file whose occurrences picks them puts each on its face instead, Export by occurrences; a face named in bed_face turns them onto it, Print bed face chosen); with none, the automatic orientation’s face, else as the design has them (Centered, dropped and oriented on the bed);
    • a bed face that is gone or not planar is reported, and its body is written as the design has it (−Z down), or by the automatic orientation, unless another body’s face turns the piece;
    • the bed faces of bodies that are not printed (surface bodies, which 3MF leaves out) count for nothing.

    The design does not move: a 3MF part’s placements (its components), an STL file’s vertices or an OBJ file’s placements are moved after the design’s placements, and the meshes are the kernel’s. The result adds bed: body, name and face (null when nothing turned), transform (three rows [a, b, c, t] of what moved the bodies after their placements, null when nothing moved), plate ([x, y]), kept (the bodies kept as assembled) and problems (body, name, reason); and warnings, one per problem (Body1: the print bed face is gone; printed as in the design).

{"cmd": "set_print_bed_face", "uid": "F2.b0", "face": "F2:end(r{c1[c4,c2],c2[c1,c3],c3[c2,c4],c4[c3,c1]})"}
{"cmd": "export", "path": "print.3mf", "bodies": ["F2.b0"], "on_bed": true, "dialect": "bambu_studio"}

Print Analysis starts from the bed face as the export does: the application’s panel fills its Bed face with it when exactly one of the analysed bodies has a usable one (Print analysis); the analysis keeps its own bed_face.

Classes: the model’s. Tests: api::print_bed_tests (set, replaced, cleared and refused, a surface body’s face too; kept through an edit, a sketch edit that renames the face, and in the design file; a box on its top, on a tilted face, in a turned component and in a component placed twice turned and centred on the default plate and the printer’s; two bed faces kept as assembled; a surface body’s face counts for nothing; a face that is not planar or gone reported; an STL file; the formats), tools/ui-print-bed-test.sh and tools/ui-windows-print-bed-test.ps1.

Export by occurrences

A 3MF file of the occurrences chosen (mitcad#856): 3D Print sends only the placements picked, as its STL files do, and puts each one with a print bed face on its face, also when the body is placed many times turned differently (a nut in an assembly). export takes, for 3MF only and in the design’s coordinates:

  • occurrences: per body (uid or name, among those written), the occurrences whose placements are written, each a path from the root (O1/O4 or Arm:1/Pin:2; "" the design itself, for a body of the root); an empty list writes the body’s placements as the design shows them (the shown ones, all when none is). A body not listed is written as before. An occurrence that does not place the body is refused (Body1 is not placed by Nuts:1).
  • whole: occurrences sent whole (a component selected), each a path; the placements in each are one object, as they are assembled.

With on_bed the file’s objects are:

  • each occurrence of whole (the outermost one a placement is in): one object of the placements in it, put on the bed by the rule of Export on the bed (one bed face among them turns it, several keep it as assembled);
  • the placements occurrences picks of bodies with a usable print bed face (printed, the face planar and there), outside those: when there are two or more, each is an object of its own, named Body1 (Nuts:1/Nut:2), turned onto its face, its lowest point on the bed and its middle over the plate’s centre; one alone stays with the rest, so that bodies printed together (an inlay of another colour) turn with it as before;
  • the rest: the file’s own object (named after the file), as before.

The objects turned are set side by side along X, the row centred on the plate; a row wider than the printer’s bed wraps into rows along Y, centred on the plate too, and objects that still do not fit on the bed give a warning (the 10 pieces do not fit on the 256 x 256 mm bed …, mitcad#1316; … mm with their brims) when brims widen them); overlaps with an object kept as designed are left to the slicer’s arrange. Neighbours, in a row and between rows, lie apart by the spacing beyond their brims. Several objects are several build items of the 3MF file (mitcad_3mf::Model::objects), each a components object of the parts’ placements; the Bambu family’s model_settings.config names each object with its parts. One object is written as before.

The result’s bed describes the file’s own object as before (body, face, transform and kept null or empty when it has none: every placement went apart) and adds objects, the others, each name, body, face, transform (rows as bed’s) and kept, and on_faces, how many placements lie on their print bed faces in all objects (the application’s last line, 3 bodies on their print bed faces). problems lists each face once.

{"cmd": "export", "path": "nut.3mf", "bodies": ["F2.b0"], "on_bed": true, "occurrences": {"F2.b0": ["O1/O3"]}}
{"cmd": "export", "path": "nuts.3mf", "bodies": ["F2.b0"], "on_bed": true, "occurrences": {"F2.b0": []}}
{"cmd": "export", "path": "assembly.3mf", "bodies": ["F2.b0"], "on_bed": true, "occurrences": {"F2.b0": []}, "whole": ["Nuts:1"]}

Tests: api::print_bed_tests (a block with its top as the bed face in a component placed three times turned differently: one occurrence chosen one object on its top at z = 0; all three three objects side by side; the component sent whole, and no occurrences, keep the assembly; the refusals), core.3mf (several build objects written and read back), tools/ui-print-test.sh (one occurrence selected: one object).

Print bed face chosen

A piece kept as assembled because two or more print bed faces apply to it (mitcad#857) can be put on one of them: 3D Print asks the user which, and the export turns the piece onto the face named. export with on_bed (3MF, STL and OBJ) takes:

  • bed_face: {"body", "occurrence"}, or a list of them, one per piece: the body (uid or name) and the occurrence of its placement (O1/O4 or Arm:1/Pin:2; "" or left out for the design itself). The piece that placement is in (the file’s own object, or an object of Export by occurrences) turns so that the face’s outward normal at that placement points straight down, its lowest point on the bed and its middle over the plate’s centre, as for a single bed face, whatever the automatic rule says; the bodies keep their places to each other. bed.body and bed.face (or the object’s) name it, kept is empty and on_faces counts the placements of that body turned alike. Refused: a body not written (Body1 is not among the bodies written), without a print bed face (Body2 has no print bed face) or with one that cannot lie on the bed (its reason), a placement not written (Body1 is not written where Nuts:1 places it), two faces in one piece (the print bed faces of Body1 in Pair:1 and Body2 in Pair:1 are chosen for one piece; choose one), and without on_bed.
  • plan: true gives only how the bodies would lie, before anything is written: the result’s bed as the export would give it (a 3MF piece’s transform is its turn alone, without the move onto the bed), and no file is written or meshed (only the automatic orientation meshes the faces of a piece without a usable bed face, coarsely, mitcad#1109). Without on_bed it is refused.

The result’s bed, and each of its objects, has choices: the faces a piece kept as assembled for several bed faces could lie on, one per placement (a body placed twice turned differently has two), each body, name, face (as assigned), occurrence (uids, as bed_face takes it) and occurrence_name; empty when the piece turns onto a face or has none or one.

{"cmd": "export", "path": "pair.3mf", "bodies": ["F2.b0", "F3.b0"], "on_bed": true, "plan": true, "whole": ["Pair:1"]}
→ {"bed": {"kept": ["F2.b0", "F3.b0"], "choices": [
     {"body": "F2.b0", "name": "Body1", "face": "F2:end(…)", "occurrence": "O1", "occurrence_name": "Pair:1"},
     {"body": "F3.b0", "name": "Body2", "face": "F3:side(…)", "occurrence": "O1", "occurrence_name": "Pair:1"}], …}, …}
{"cmd": "export", "path": "pair.3mf", "bodies": ["F2.b0", "F3.b0"], "on_bed": true, "whole": ["Pair:1"],
 "bed_face": {"body": "F3.b0", "occurrence": "Pair:1"}}

Tests: api::print_bed_tests (a component of two bodies, each with a bed face: the plan lists both, a body placed three times turned differently three, one face none; either face chosen puts the piece on it at z = 0 with the bodies together, whole or not; the refusals), tools/ui-print-test.sh (3D Print asks, a click sends on that face, Esc as assembled).

Centered, dropped and oriented on the bed

Send to Slicer puts every piece on the plate (mitcad#1109): a body without a print bed face is no longer written where the design has it, off the plate. export with on_bed (3MF, STL and OBJ) takes, each true when left out and refused without on_bed (but center of a 3MF with a dialect, below):

  • center: the middle of each piece’s box over the plate’s center (the design’s printer’s bed_shape, else (128, 128)); false keeps its X and Y.
  • drop: each piece’s lowest point onto the bed (z = 0); false keeps its Z.
  • auto_orient: a piece without a usable print bed face (none, or only faces that are gone or not planar, which are still reported) is turned onto the face the automatic orientation finds; false leaves it as the design has it (−Z down). A body’s own print bed face, one chosen in bed_face, and the several faces of a piece kept as assembled (Print bed face chosen) always come first: the automatic face is computed again on every export and never stored.

A 3MF with a slicer’s dialect but without on_bed is centred too (mitcad#1596): its whole build moved alike in X and Y so that the box of its bodies is over the plate’s center, their arrangement and heights as designed. A slicer’s project keeps its objects where the file puts them, in the bed’s coordinates, and the design’s origin is no place on the bed: a box from the origin lay at the bed’s corner, its skirt or brim outside the printable area, which Bambu Studio and QIDI Studio refuse. center: false (allowed without on_bed only with a dialect) keeps the design’s X and Y; the print plates’ files keep their plates’ places.

center and drop apply after the turn to every piece: turned onto a face, oriented automatically, kept as assembled or as designed; the bodies of a piece keep their places to each other. The 3MF objects of Export by occurrences are set side by side along X only while center is on. A piece neither turned nor moved has no transform; with plan the transform is the turn alone (null for a piece not turned).

The automatic orientation (core/model/src/exchange/orient.rs) looks at the piece as a whole, its printed bodies’ faces where its placements put them (the kernel’s face_meshes at the low refinement):

  • candidates are the named planar faces whose plane supports the piece’s convex hull: every vertex lies on the plane or on its inner side, so the piece lies on it without going below; coplanar faces are one candidate, named by the largest; curved faces and a mesh body’s triangles are none;
  • each candidate is scored (smaller is better, each term without a unit): the overhang area after the turn (triangles facing down within 45° of straight down, those on the bed left out) over the whole area, weight 1; minus the contact area with the bed over the whole area, weight 0.5; plus the height after the turn over the box’s diagonal, weight 0.1;
  • scores within 1e-9 are alike: the face whose normal is nearest to −Z in the design wins (a piece already lying well keeps its orientation), then the face listed first;
  • no candidate: the piece stays as the design has it.

The result’s bed (and each of its objects) adds auto (true when the face is the automatic orientation’s, not a print bed face; such a face does not count in on_faces) and occurrence and occurrence_name (the placement whose face lies on the bed, as in choices; null without a face), and bed adds center and drop as used. A problem’s warning then drops printed as in the design.

{"cmd": "export", "path": "print.3mf", "bodies": ["F2.b0"], "on_bed": true}
→ {"bed": {"body": "F2.b0", "name": "Body1", "face": "F2:start(…)", "auto": true,
           "occurrence": "", "occurrence_name": "", "center": true, "drop": true,
           "transform": [[1, 0, 0, 98], [0, 1, 0, 108], [0, 0, 1, 0]], "plate": [128, 128], …}, …}
{"cmd": "export", "path": "print.stl", "bodies": ["F2.b0"], "on_bed": true,
 "center": false, "drop": false, "auto_orient": false}

Tests: api::print_bed_tests (a body without a bed face far from the origin written at z = 0 centered on the plate, as designed with both off, dropped only with center off, in an STL file too; a standing block laid on its largest face, the plan the same, standing without auto_orient; a body’s own face over the automatic one; a gone or non-planar face oriented automatically; a piece kept as assembled centered and dropped), api::print_orient_tests (a lying tube with a square flange on the flange, not on a narrow side nor its end; a block on its largest face; a cube on its bottom; no planar face, no orientation), tools/ui-print-bed-test.sh and tools/ui-windows-print-bed-test.ps1 (Send to Slicer’s Bed Face filled, a face picked stored, its highlight).

Copy and paste of sketch geometry

Copy, Cut and Paste of sketch geometry (mitcad#788): a query copies selected points, curves and texts of a sketch as a fragment, and sketch.paste adds a fragment to a sketch, of this design or of another (the fragment is plain JSON). Cut is a copy and then sketch.remove of the same items.

{"query": "sketch_fragment", "sketch": "F1", "items": ["c2", "t5"]}
→ {"sketch": "F1", "sketch_name": "Sketch1", "base": [10, 10],
   "outline": [[[10, 10], [40, 10]], ...], "points": [],
   "entities": 3, "texts": 1, "kept": 3, "left_out": 1, "held": [false, true],
   "fragment": {"version": 1, "base": [10, 10], "entities": [...], "texts": [...],
                "constraints": [...], "dimensions": [...],
                "references": [{"id": "p1", "is": "origin"}], "left_out": 1}}
{"cmd": "sketch.paste", "sketch": "F2", "fragment": {...}, "at": [30, 10]}
→ {"made": ["p2", "p3", "c4"], "kept": 3, "left_out": 1,
   "entities": [...], "constraints": [...], "dimensions": [...], "status": {...}}
  • What is copied. The selected points, curves and texts (p3, c4, t5; constraints and dimensions listed are ignored: they come with their geometry), the points the curves use, and for a text the points of its frame and the curve it runs along. Projected and intersected geometry becomes ordinary geometry: free, not reference geometry and following nothing. Patterns and offsets come as the geometry they made. Construction and centre lines, splines of both kinds, arcs, conics, points and texts (with their fonts and stored outlines) keep what they are.
  • Constraints and dimensions are kept when every entity they reference is copied or is the sketch’s origin or one of its axes (mitcad#500); an equal spacing’s common spacing goes with its equal spacing. Those that reference copied geometry and something else are left out and counted (left_out); the others are not about the copy. Inactive ones stay inactive (mitcad#721).
  • The origin and the axes are not copied: the fragment’s references name the ids that stood for them (origin, x, y, and x_end, y_end for an axis’s far end), and a paste uses the target sketch’s own, made when it has none (as sketch.axis makes them). A curve that starts at the origin point starts at the target’s.
  • Values. A driving dimension keeps its value (value, mm or radians) and, when its parameter uses other parameters (or it uses a parameter of the design as it is), its expression and the parameters it uses. A paste takes the expression where every one of those parameters exists in the target design, else the value, and lists the dimension in the answer’s values with a warning. A text that follows a text parameter (mitcad#664) keeps it the same way, else its text.
  • The base point (base) is the first selected item’s first point (a line’s or an arc’s start, a circle’s centre, a spline’s first point, a text’s anchor). sketch.paste moves the fragment by at - base; without at it goes where it was. The coordinates are the sketch’s own, so a paste into a sketch on another plane keeps the 2D coordinates.
  • Held directions. Constraints and dimensions kept to the origin and the axes hold the fragment where it was in the directions they fix, and the solve puts it back there whatever at says. The query’s held ([x, y]) gives those directions: a point at the origin (or an axis’s end) holds both; a point or line on the x axis, a vertical distance from the origin or a level alignment with it (horizontal_points) hold y (the y axis, a horizontal distance or vertical_points: x); a distance from the origin holds both; parallels, perpendiculars, angles and sizes hold none, nor inactive ones. The application places a paste only in the free directions.
  • Warnings of a paste: the constraints and dimensions it dropped itself (of a fragment that names entities it lacks; what the copy left out is said at the copy, and left_out counts both), and dimensions that took their values.
  • One undo step Paste into Sketch2; the new entities and texts get new ids, in made in the fragment’s order. Refused: a fragment of a newer version (version), one whose curves use points it lacks, an empty one, a place that is not finite.
  • outline (the curves and the texts’ glyph contours as polylines) and points (lone points) are for a preview, in the source sketch’s coordinates; sketch.paste takes only the fragment.
  • 3D sketches (mitcad#1661): the query copies a 3D sketch’s geometry too (kind 3d), which sketch3d.paste takes, as does a planar copy; sketch.paste refuses a 3D sketch’s copy. See “Copy and paste of 3D sketch geometry”.

The application keeps the query’s answer on the clipboard under the type application/x-mitcad-sketch-fragment+json (app/COMMANDS.md, Sketch mode, “Copy, Cut and Paste”).

Classes: the model’s. Code: core/sketch/src/clipboard.rs, core/model-api/src/sketch_clipboard.rs. Tests: core/model-tests/sketch/src/sketch_clipboard_tests.rs, tools/ui-sketch-clipboard-test.sh and tools/ui-windows-sketch-clipboard-test.ps1.

Redefine Sketch Plane

(mitcad#787.) sketch.redefine_plane moves a sketch to another plane or planar face and places it there: an offset along the plane’s normal, a move in the plane, a rotation about the normal and a flip. The sketch’s geometry keeps its own 2D coordinates; only its frame moves, and the features built on it (extrudes, revolves, holes, sweeps, …) follow at the recompute. One undo step, Redefine Plane of Sketch1.

{"cmd": "sketch.redefine_plane", "sketch": "F1",
 "plane": {"face": "F2:end(r{c1})", "body": "F2.b0"}, "occurrence": "",
 "offset": "5 mm", "x": 10, "y": "Gap * 2", "angle": "30 deg", "flip": false,
 "upright": true}
  • plane: as sketch.create takes it (an origin plane, a construction plane "F5", a planar face); left out, the sketch keeps its plane and only its placement changes. occurrence and context are as in sketch.create (mitcad#100): a plane of another component is linked (plane_link), from the sketch’s component.
  • A plane made by a feature at or after the sketch in the timeline (a construction plane, a face of a later feature, of a feature built on the sketch itself) is refused with the reason: Sketch1 cannot lie on a plane or face of Plane1: Plane1 comes after Sketch1 in the timeline, and a sketch's plane must be made before it. A plane the sketch does not find where it is evaluated (a face that is not planar or is gone) is refused too (Sketch1 cannot use this plane or face: …, the evaluation’s reason), unless the sketch failed before (it does not solve); so is a plane whose link or feature is not found (Sketch1 cannot use this plane: …). The document is then unchanged.
  • On another plane the own frame (frame) of the old plane is dropped. With upright the sketch gets the own frame that shows the design upright on the new plane, as Create Sketch’s (see An upright sketch frame), in the same undo step. The same plane again keeps the own frame.
  • offset, x, y and angle are values (numbers or expressions with units, parameters by name): the sketch keeps them as its own parameters in placement (slots placement.offset, placement.x, placement.y, placement.angle), so a parameter moves the sketch and a later sketch.redefine_plane or the parameters table changes them. A value left out stays; a plain zero (0, "0 mm", an expression without parameters that is zero) takes it away with its parameter. flip (left out: kept) turns the sketch over.
  • The placement acts on the base frame (the plane’s frame with the own frame): the origin moves by x and y along the base’s x and y axes and by offset along its normal; the axes then turn by angle counter-clockwise about the normal; a flip then reverses the y axis, and with it the normal, keeping the x axis. A sketch without placement keeps none in the file; files without one read as before.
  • Linked projections and section curves (Project, Intersect) follow their sources from the new plane at the recompute; those that cannot say so in the sketch’s warnings (and in the result’s). Projections that are not linked keep their geometry in the sketch’s coordinates.
  • The result: uid, name, plane, plane_link, placement (the parameters by name, null without one), plane_changed, label, parameters (those made), warnings (the sketch’s) and frame (the sketch’s frame now, when it evaluated); failed_features names the later features the move breaks.
  • The sketch query’s frame is the placed frame. Reorient Design turns the base frame and keeps the placement.

Classes: the model’s. Tests: core/model-tests/sketch (sketch_plane_tests: a plane change with the extrude following and one undo step, the offset, move and rotation as expressions and parameters changed again and taken away, a flip, a face and a construction plane, a later plane and a face that cannot take it refused, upright, the design file), core/model (sketch::placement, document::sketch_plane), tools/ui-sketch-redefine-plane-test.sh and tools/ui-windows-sketch-redefine-plane-test.ps1.

Image references

Images placed in the design to model from, such as a photo of a part or a scanned drawing (mitcad#782; core/model/src/document/image_references.rs, core/model-base/src/image_header.rs, api/image_references.rs): the browser’s Images folder. An image reference keeps the image file’s bytes (PNG, JPEG, BMP, WebP or HEIF, at most 32 MB and 32768 pixels on a side) embedded in the design, no path; it changes no geometry, and every command below is an undo step that recomputes nothing.

HEIF (.heic, .heif; mitcad#850, image_header/heif.rs): the file’s primary image, a still image coded with HEVC (an hvc1 item, or a grid or iden of hvc1 tiles), 8 to 10 bits per channel, with or without an alpha plane. Its pixels are the image as it is shown: the ispe size, then the transformations in the file’s order (irot turns a quarter or three swap the width and height, clap crops, rounded; imir mirrors), which the application’s decoder applies too. A HEIF file states no pixel size (96 to the inch). Refused with the reason: AVIF (AV1), other codecs (coded as 'jpeg'), an image sequence without a still image, a protected item, more than 10 bits per channel, a file cut short. The model keeps the file’s bytes as they are; decoding the pixels is the application’s, with the operating system’s decoder (mitcad#1304; app/COMMANDS.md, “Image references”), and its Insert › Image Reference embeds a HEIF file as a PNG file of the upright image (data), so that the design opens where no HEIF decoder is.

  • Its plane is a plane reference (an origin plane, a construction plane, a planar face or a fixed plane) with an optional occurrence (the plane’s UID path from the design root), as a section analysis’ (Analyses). It is resolved at the timeline marker each time it is asked for, so the image follows its plane or face when the model changes; one whose plane is gone says why (error).
  • Its place in the plane’s frame: center (mm, [x, y] along the plane’s x and y axes), angle (degrees, about the plane’s normal, counter-clockwise seen from the side the normal points to) and flip (mirrored left to right). Seen from the normal’s side, an image that is not flipped reads as in a picture viewer.
  • Its size is scale, the size of a pixel (mm). A new image takes the size its file states (PNG’s pHYs, JPEG’s JFIF density, BMP’s pixels per metre), else 96 pixels to the inch; width (mm) sets the scale from the image’s width instead.
  • Pixels are counted from the image’s top left corner, u to the right and v down, [0, 0] to [width, height].
  • Calibration scales the image about its first point so that two points are a typed distance apart: the first point stays where it is.
  • Display: opacity (0 to 1, a new image 0.5), its light bulb (visible), and through: drawn through the bodies (over them) instead of hidden behind them. The view never picks an image.
CommandFieldsResult

Refused: a plane that is no plane at the marker, a file that is no image of those formats, path and data both, scale and width both, a size not greater than zero, an opacity outside 0 to 1, a name in use, other fields
edit_image_referencename, and any of plane (a new plane without occurrence is in the root), occurrence (alone: the same plane in another occurrence), center, angle, flip, scale or width, opacity, through, path or data with file_name (another image in its place, at the same place and pixel size)undo step Edit Image1 unless nothing changes
