set_link_envelopeoccurrence (an occurrence of a linked component: uid, name or path), envelope (default true; false: the design’s bodies again), detail (mm, with envelope only; left out: the size the component, or another component linking the same file, is shown at, else 1 % of the design’s diagonal, at least 5 mm), all (default false: this occurrence only; true: every occurrence of its component), base (the folder of a relative link path; left out: the design file’s)component (the occurrence’s component now), envelope (shown by its envelope now), detail (null when shown in full), changed (false when it was already shown so: no undo step), bodies (that component’s bodies now)
  • The linked design’s file is read again (class file IO, as insert_component) and its visible bodies, as the link takes them, are wrapped as the feature does; a component switched to its envelope holds in its base feature that one body (Envelope) instead of the design’s bodies, with the file’s mount frames. The layout neither draws nor keeps the full geometry of a component switched so, in memory or in its file. envelope: false reads the file again and takes its bodies back.
  • Each occurrence chooses (mitcad#1276). With all, or when the occurrence is its component’s only one, the component itself is switched (every occurrence of it). Otherwise only this occurrence changes: it goes into another component that links the same file and is shown so (the same detail size, or in full), and a new one is made for it when there is none: Machine Envelope, its base feature right after the linked component’s, placed nowhere else. The occurrence keeps its uid, its placement, its joints and its number where that number is free there (Machine Envelope:2). A component whose last occurrence went into another one goes too when nothing outside it uses it (its bodies named by joints or other components’ features); otherwise it is switched itself. An occurrence shown in full while its component, shown by its envelope, has other occurrences and no component of the file shows the design in full: its component is shown in full (taking back its name when it was a … Envelope one) and the other occurrences go into a component shown at its detail size. So every component holds either the design’s bodies or one envelope.
  • One undo step: Show Machine:1 as Envelope, Show Machine:1 in Full.
  • The link records the detail size (link.envelope in the design file) and the joints’ frames (link.frames, below); update_links makes the envelope again from a changed file. The components query gives a switched component’s envelope (its detail size).
  • The design file: link.envelope and link.frames are fields of this version; a build before it refuses a design that has them, as any field it does not know inside the known ones. Show the linked components in full before saving a design for such a build.
  • Joints to faces, edges and vertices of the design’s bodies keep working while it is shown by its envelope (mitcad#1276, joints::envelope_side). An occurrence in a component of its own resolves them in the component whose bodies they name, while that one shows the design in full (the same file, the same coordinates). A component switched itself keeps, in its link, the frame every joint and as-built joint origin on its bodies had in full when it was switched (frames: [{"geometry": <the origin's geometry>, "frame": <transform>}]) and those origins use them; shown in full again, they are dropped. A joint added while the envelope is shown, on the envelope’s own faces, resolves on them. An origin on a design whose envelope keeps no frame for it, seen through a component of its own, fails with … is on Machine, which is shown by its envelope: show it in full to join to its faces. Assembly constraint rows resolve in the full component the same way; other references to the design’s faces fail until it is shown in full again.
  • Copies, moves and reparenting (mitcad#1276): an envelope feature’s occurrence path follows as other occurrence links do. Paste New of a component maps it to the copy’s occurrences (joints::remap_occurrences, as joints’); Move to… of an occurrence rewrites it relative to the feature’s component and is refused when the occurrence would leave that component (Envelope1: Machine:1 would no longer be in the component it reads it in); Move Features into a Component points an Envelope of listed bodies that went at the new occurrence.
  • Refused: an occurrence of a component that is not linked, a library part, a design linked with options, a detail size with envelope: false, a detail size of 0 or less, a file that cannot be read.
  • The application: Show as Envelope… (this occurrence), Show All as Envelope… (every occurrence of its component, offered when it has more than one) and Show in Full (this occurrence) on the linked component’s row in the browser (app/browser/BrowserController.cpp), and the Envelope command and panel for the feature (solid.envelope, app/commands/EnvelopeCommands.cpp, app/COMMANDS.md “Envelope”).

Scripts (mitcad-cli run) can expect "max_triangles" of a body: the most triangles its mesh at 0.1 mm may have.

Tests: core.model (features::envelope::wrap_tests: synthetic meshes, a box on the grid wrapped exactly, a slit closed and a tunnel kept, a cavity filled, bodies apart, edge and corner contacts, refusals; features::envelope::tests: the feature on the mock kernel), core.model.assembly (link_envelope_tests.rs: switching, the file changed, back in full, undo, refusals; each occurrence by its envelope or in full, Show All, a joint to a face of the linked design keeping its placement in a component of its own and with the component switched; envelope_source_tests.rs: Paste New and Move to… keeping an Envelope’s source, a move that would lose it refused), cli.envelope (tools/cli/tests/envelope.json, OCCT: a U frame with a 100 mm tunnel and 5 mm holes at a detail size of 20 mm keeps the tunnel and closes the holes with at most 200 triangles, a hollow box loses its cavity, an occurrence’s envelope where it is placed) and app.ui-windows-envelope (tools/ui-windows-envelope-test.ps1: Show as Envelope and Show in Full on a linked machine’s row), app.ui-windows-envelope-command (tools/ui-windows-envelope-command-test.ps1: the Envelope panel on a component at 20 mm in the Docked layout, edited and undone, and in the Floating layout; Show as Envelope… on one of two occurrences of a linked machine, the other in full).

Dimensions chosen by their picks (mitcad#1272)

add_drawing_annotation with "type": "dimension" makes the dimension its picks choose (Annotations on drawing views; the application’s Dimension tool sends it with its Type Auto, the default):

PicksMakes
one circle (whole) seen end on or from the side, or one round face seen from the sidediameter
one arcradius
one straight edgelinear from its start to its end (two picks of it are kept: its length)
one piece of a section’s cut line (on_cut, mitcad#1361)linear from the piece’s start to its end, as a straight edge’s
two straight edges that are not parallel (on a view seen from an angle: none)angle
any other twolinear

The same pick twice is one pick, so a circle or an edge picked twice gives its own dimension, never 0 mm; two picks on one point (a circle and its own centre) are refused (the picks lie on one point), as are a point alone (a point alone measures nothing), a section’s cut face picked whole, without on_cut (a cut face picked whole spans its gaps), and more than two picks (a baseline or a chain takes them). drawing_pick asked with neither type nor want (the Dimension tool’s Auto) says whether its pick makes such a dimension alone, "alone": true, else "alone": false and next, the refusal’s words (mitcad#1361): the application then waits for a second pick and says so, instead of placing. A linear one’s along (unless given) follows its placing click at, as a sketch’s dimensions do (mitcad_model_drawing::annotate::placed_along): placed above or below its picks’ points (between them along x, beyond them along y) horizontal, beside them vertical, between them both ways or beyond them both ways aligned (square to a straight edge picked, else along the line between them); points level or plumb measure along that axis wherever it is placed; without at, the axis they lie further apart along; on a view seen from an angle, aligned. The annotation is stored as the type chosen (linear, radius, …), so files keep their form. With series it is a series of linear ones.

A dimension of a type of its own (linear, angle, ordinate, …) takes its picks as given, as before; the application drops a pick its tool already has (Drawing pick: picked already).

drawing_snap (Dimension spacing) takes such a command too and its answer says what the placing click makes, for the application’s preview: type, along, and a linear one’s ends (its picks’ points on the sheet) and direction (what it measures along, a unit vector on the sheet).

A curved slot’s centre arc. A centerline of two concentric arcs seen end on (a curved slot’s sides; or an arc and a whole circle about the same centre) is the arc halfway between them, through the centres of the slot’s ends, from one end’s centre to the other’s and run on beyond each by the ends’ radius and 2.5 mm, long-dash dotted (the sides’ ranges of angles taken together). Two concentric whole circles are refused (the picks share their center).

Snapping points. drawing_pick takes "want": "snap": the nearest edge end, straight edge’s middle ("point": "center" of the edge) or circle’s or arc’s centre within 3 mm of paper; with none of them there (mitcad#1362), the click’s foot on the nearest centre line within 3 mm: a round face’s axis seen from the side (the pick its face) or a line of a centre mark the view draws (the pick that centre), its at the foot, "center_line": true and the line first among its items; nothing else. The application’s Line and Arc, Section View’s line and Break’s sides snap their clicks on a view to it. A circle or an arc seen end on that drawing_pick gives (any want) lists its centre among its items ({"point"}), where a click picks it.

Tests: core/model-tests/drawing-views/src/chosen_dimension_tests.rs (on a plate’s top: a hole’s diameter, a slot side’s radius, an edge’s length placed above, beside, between and beyond, an angle, parallel edges’ distance, a hole to an edge aligned, the slot’s centre to a hole by the placing click, the same pick twice, picks on one point, the drawing_snap answer, the slot’s centre arc, snapping points), core/model-tests/drawing-views/src/pick_tests.rs (a snap onto a hole’s axis seen from the side and onto a centre mark’s line, mitcad#1362), core/model-drawing/src/annotate.rs (placed_along, the slot’s centre arc), app/tests/drawing_tools.cpp, app.ui-windows-drawing-dimension-picks (tools/ui-windows-drawing-dimension-picks-test.ps1). A section’s cut edge (mitcad#1361): chosen_dimension_tests.rs (a_sections_cut_edge_alone_is_the_length_of_the_piece_under_the_click: a stepped part with a hole, the piece beside the hole 30 and not the line across it, its corners, alone, the face picked whole and a point in the hole refused), tools/ui-drawing-section-dimension-test.sh and app.ui-windows-drawing-section-dimension (tools/ui-windows-drawing-section-dimension-test.ps1: the cut edge beside the hole picked alone reads 30, a corner waits for a second pick).

New designs from an agent: document_new

An agent connected to the application (the live MCP server, docs/mcp.md) starts a new design with the tool document_new (mitcad#1266), not with a model command: File › New Design (file.new_design) waits for the user to name the design, so ui_command refuses it and points here.

  • It makes an empty design (the root and an active Component1, as every new design starts), in the default units for new designs, and opens it in a window (a tab) of its own beside the open designs. No design is replaced; every open design keeps its handle, and the result’s previous is the caller’s.
  • Optional folder (a folder for designs or below one) and name (the file’s name, .mitcad added; default the first free DesignN.mitcad). Without folder: the current project’s top folder when agents may use it, else with a name the first folder for designs, else an untitled design. An existing name is refused, naming the file.
  • In a project with versions the design is made by the project’s new_design command (a version Add DesignN.mitcad), as New Design makes it; elsewhere the empty design is saved to the file.
  • The caller’s later calls without a document handle go to the new design; a chat agent may still use its own design by its handle.

Tests: tools/ui-mcp-document-new-test.sh (the folders, the names, the project’s version, both designs listed, commands changing only the new design), the new-design run of tools/ui-chat-test.py (a chat agent’s design from a design), core.mcp (the catalog and the chat’s approvals) and app.unit (agent_folders.cpp: the folder and the free name).

Unions of many bodies and empty results (mitcad#1273)

A union of several bodies (a Combine’s join, a pattern’s combine) groups them by their boxes: bodies whose boxes meet, directly or through others, are one group; each group of several is united on its own, the groups beside each other, and the groups’ results go into the body without a boolean. A union that lost material (no solid where its bodies have some, or less volume than the largest of them), whose pieces the geometry kernel left unused (edges of a face it could not rebuild, faces it could not make a solid of) or where parts of one body came to meet is wrong whatever the join tolerance: the bodies whose boxes reach those places are united first, each such place with the smallest fuzzy value from 1e-4 mm up to 1e-3 mm (or the join tolerance) that gives a sound union, and the union of all is made again with those in their places. Where nothing gives a sound union, a union that lost material fails (the union of the shapes gave an empty result, the union lost material of the shapes it joins) and one that only left pieces unused stands as it was, as before. A feature’s join of targets the tool touches that gives no solid is retried the same way and fails when it stays empty (the join gave an empty result). Combine fails a join, cut or intersection of bodies with material whose result holds no solid for any kernel (the join of 257 bodies gave an empty result): the target keeps its shape and the tools stay.

Found on a reported design (GitHub #133): a Combine joining a machine’s 257 bodies, imported from one STEP file, came out empty, the target without faces and the 256 tools removed. Two places of it broke OCCT’s exact union: a nut lying inside a threaded carriage, its bore’s seam a few micrometres from the vertices of the thread’s faces (no solid; fuzzy 1e-5 mm joins them), two copies of a back plate whose side walls lie 1e-4 mm apart (the lower plate alone; fuzzy 1e-4 mm joins them), and a mount whose stud stands coaxially in the carriage’s threaded hole (a solid of its own; with fuzzy 1e-5 mm one solid missing most of their common volume, with 1e-4 mm the union). Tests: core.model.features-solid (f4_tests.rs, combine_with_an_empty_result_fails_and_keeps_its_bodies, the mock kernel’s empty results), geometry.join_many_bodies (unions in groups, and the reported design’s places from MITCAD_MITCAD_REPORTED).

Near misses in a union of many, and cuts of bodies a micrometre apart (mitcad#1278)

Before a union of 8 or more bodies whose boxes meet (a Combine’s join, a pattern’s combine), the bodies are looked at pair by pair for near misses: a vertex of one lying near a face of the other but not on it (farther than their tolerances together, at most 1e-3 mm). Those pairs, and the bodies linked to them that way, are united first, with the fuzzy value of Unions of many bodies where their exact union is wrong, and the union of all is then made once. Before, such places were found only by the union of all, which was then made a second time. A Combine’s cut or intersection whose result the geometry kernel left pieces of unused is made again the same way, with the smallest fuzzy value from 1e-4 mm up to 1e-3 mm (or the join tolerance) that leaves nothing unused; where none does, the exact result stands.

Found on the reported design of GitHub #133: its join of 257 bodies took two unions of all (35 s) and now takes one (25 s); the vertices’ distances found the design’s 7 wrong pairs among 709 in 0.3 s. A cut of one of its back plates by the other, whose side walls lie 1e-4 mm apart, gave the plate whole or nothing, and their intersection was empty. Tests: geometry.join_many_bodies (a synthetic row of blocks with a near miss; from MITCAD_MITCAD_REPORTED the join of all the design’s bodies, with its time, and the plates’ cuts and intersection against their union).

Find Repeated Parts (mitcad#1277) 

{"cmd": "find_repeated_parts", "feature": "F1"}
{"cmd": "find_repeated_parts", "feature": "F1", "tolerance": 0.001}
{"cmd": "import_file", "path": "assembly.step", "repeated_parts": true}
CommandFieldsResult
find_repeated_partsfeature (a base feature’s uid), tolerance (mm, optional)components: component, name, feature, body, occurrences, copies; kept

A file whose parts are copies with their placements baked in (a STEP file without an assembly, a flat export) comes in as one base feature of many bodies, each its own B-rep. Find Repeated Parts (document/repeated_parts.rs) finds the bodies of a base feature that are copies of one another moved by a rigid motion and makes each kind one component placed once per copy:

  • The component: the first body of each kind (in the feature’s order) moves into a new component named after it, where it is, by a component_from_bodies feature in the base feature’s component: it keeps its id, name, colour, material and appearance, in its own coordinates (the base feature’s component’s). Each copy becomes an occurrence of that component in the same parent, placed where the copy was (<component>:2, :3, …), and its B-rep data leaves the base feature, with its name and attributes.
  • What stays: bodies that copy none stay in the base feature, with their ids, names and face names: a body after one that was taken out keeps its number (F1.b6) and its first face (F1:import(32)) as number and first_face in its entry of the base feature’s bodies (left out where they are its place and the faces counted before it). Mesh bodies, bodies of another component and bodies with face-level looks (face appearances, a print bed face) are not compared, nor are bodies that a print plate item ({"body": …}) or a comment names (mitcad#1312): they keep their items and comments where they are.
  • Copies ([Kernel::rigid_copies], geometry/repeated_parts.hpp): bodies of the same topology counts (faces, edges, vertices), volume, area and principal moments of inertia, of which a frame of principal axes through the centre of mass, fitted by least squares, puts every vertex and face centroid within tolerance mm (beside the vertices' own tolerances, the file’s precision) of the other’s. A body with a symmetry has several frames (the axes’ signs; about an axis of equal moments, the directions to its farthest points): they are tried until one matches. A mirror image is not a rigid motion: the mirror image of a body without a mirror symmetry stays its own body. Bodies of another colour, material, appearance, visibility or transparency than the first of their kind are another kind, and so are bodies whose own properties (print values among them, set_property on the body) differ from the first’s (mitcad#1312): a copy’s occurrence shows the first body, whose properties are then the copy’s; a copy’s own entry goes with it.
  • tolerance: mm, greater than zero; the design’s join tolerance (an importer’s) when left out, else 0.01 mm.
  • One undo step (Find Repeated Parts in Base1). Nothing found changes nothing (no undo step).
  • Later features (a file’s bodies joined into one by a Combine, as the design of GitHub #133 has them): the component_from_bodies features go right after the base feature, before the features that use its bodies. A combine of the base feature’s component (suppressed or not) takes its tools among the bodies where the occurrences show them: a copy’s tool becomes the first body in the copy’s occurrence ({"body": "F1.b0", "occurrence": "O2"}), the first body’s its own occurrence; its target, and any body another later feature names (by its id or by one of its faces, F1:import(12)), stays in the base feature and is not compared, so nothing after it changes. A combine that consumes its tools still consumes them, now from their components.
  • Refused: another feature than a base feature, a base feature that joins, cuts, intersects or replaces bodies, one after the timeline marker or one that did not build, and a linked component’s.
  • Result: components (per component: component, name, feature (the component_from_bodies), body (the first body), occurrences (the first body’s own, then one per copy), copies (the bodies the occurrences after the first stand for)), kept (the base feature’s bodies that copy none or that a later feature names), combines (the combines whose tools it moved into occurrences).
  • At import: import_file with repeated_parts runs it in the import’s own undo step (Import assembly.step) with either structure (mitcad#1274): base (and a file without an assembly): on the one base feature; components: on each part’s base feature, so copies the file holds inside one part become occurrences of a component in that part (the parts the assembly places more than once are shared by it already). Its reply adds repeated_parts, the result above, of all of them together. A failure takes the import back. The application’s Import STEP dialog offers it as Find repeated parts (off by default, app/COMMANDS.md).

Tests: core.model.assembly (repeated_parts_tests.rs, mock kernel: components and occurrences, the ids and face names left, a colour that splits a kind, refusals, one undo step, the import’s option), geometry.repeated_parts (OCCT: a pinwheel with a quarter-turn symmetry copied four times, one turned by its symmetry, one about a slanted axis, its mirror image apart; a propeller turned by its half-turn symmetry).

set_view_showorigins, construction, sketches (each optional: true shows that kind, false hides it, left out keeps it; at least one)undo step Hide All Construction / Show All Sketches (several joined by , ) unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed

Ids of deleted features and occurrences after a reload (mitcad#1320)

A deleted feature’s or occurrence’s uid is not given out again, also after a save and a load. In a session the counters only grow; the design file keeps them as next_feature and next_occurrence (numbers) where they are not one past the largest uid listed, which is what happens when the last feature or occurrence was deleted. Without them a reload gave the deleted one’s uid to the next new feature or occurrence, and what keeps a reference to it on purpose attached to the new one: a plate item whose body or occurrence is gone (Print plates: it stays missing), a comment on a deleted feature or its body (Comments: it stays orphaned) and a base view’s recorded bodies (mitcad#1293).

  • Read as the larger of the stored number and one past the largest uid listed; a file without them (older versions) counts on from the largest, as before, and the references it keeps stay as they are.
  • A number in the top reserve of its type is refused as the ids are (mitcad#944): next_feature: invalid feature id F… (at most F….
  • Builds before mitcad#1320 handle both as fields of a newer MitCad: opened with the warning, dropped by a save over the file.

Tests: core.model.print (print_plates_tests.rs: a body item and an occurrence item of a deleted last feature and occurrence stay missing after a save, a load and a new box or placement, which print unplaced), core.model.analysis (comment_tests.rs: a comment on a deleted last feature stays orphaned after a save, a load and a new feature), core.model.files (file_tests.rs: the numbers written only when needed, read back, refused in the reserve).

Corners and centre lines on drawing views (mitcad#1338)

A corner to a centre line. A click on a line of a centre mark that a view draws (its automatic centre marks while center_marks is on, a center_mark annotation’s mark, or a center_pattern’s radial line through one of its circles, mitcad#1693), within 3 mm of paper and with no edge or point within reach, picks the centre of that mark’s circle or arc ("point": "center" of its edge), for drawing_pick (want any or point) and for a command’s picks given as sheet points. drawing_pick then answers "seen": "point", "center_line": true and items with the mark’s line first, then the centre ({"point"}). A corner and such a centre make a linear dimension (Dimensions chosen by their picks), in either order: placed above or below them horizontal, beside them vertical, so that it measures from the corner to the mark’s vertical or horizontal line. A click away from a drawn mark picks nothing there, as before (a circle without a mark keeps its rim and centre picks only); a round face seen from the side is picked on its axis, its centreline, as before.

The corners a sheet shows. The drawing_corners query (drawing, sheet (0)) gives views: for each drawn view of the sheet its view and points (sheet mm), the ends of its edges that a click picks ("point": "start" or "end", the same candidates as drawing_pick’s; on a section the ends of its cut lines’ pieces too, mitcad#1361) that lie on a line the view draws as visible and that the view sees (inside a detail’s circle, outside a break), each place once. A view the model could not draw is left out. The application draws them as dots while its Preferences › Display › Always show corners in drawings is on; they are never written to a file, an export or a print. Class: the model’s.

Tests: core/model-tests/drawing-views/src/chosen_dimension_tests.rs (a_corner_is_dimensioned_to_a_centre_marks_line: nothing on a mark’s line before the mark, then the slot’s centre with its line in the hover’s items, horizontal and vertical in both orders; the_corners_of_a_view_are_its_visible_edge_ends), tools/ui-drawing-corners-test.sh, app.ui-windows-drawing-corners (tools/ui-windows-drawing-corners-test.ps1).

Control cages of imported Form bodies (mitcad#1365)

A body of a base feature may carry cage, the control cage its faces were made from (an .f3d file’s Form body; the .f3d import sets it, see core/import/docs/f3d-fallbacks.md, Form bodies and their control cages):

{"name": "Body1", "brep": {…},
 "cage": {"source": "TSpline.<uuid>.tsm", "degree": 3,
          "vertices": [{"position": [0, 0, 0], "tag": "dart"},
                       {"position": [20, 0, 0], "weight": 0.5}, …],
          "faces": [[1, 2, 0], …],
          "edges": [{"vertices": [0, 1], "knot": 2, "crease": true, "boundary": true}, …],
          "grips": [{"vertex": 2, "position": [1, 2, 3]}],
          "settings": {"end-conditions": "SUBD_CREASES"},
          "tolerance": 0.01, "geometric_tolerance": 0.001,
          "native": ["105sym 0", …]}}

Lengths are mm in the body’s component. vertices are the control vertices with their own control points (weight when not 1; tag dart, crease or corner by the creased edges at them, absent when smooth); faces their rings (indices into vertices); edges with the knot interval (when not 1), crease and boundary; grips the secondary control points of vertices; settings, the tolerances and native (the source’s other records, as written) what the source declares. The cage is saved and read with the design and does not take part in the body’s evaluation (the body is its B-rep data; the cage is not in the definition’s fingerprint); where it maps onto a Form’s cage it opens as an editable Form (Forms from imported cages). A cage whose indices name no vertex, whose numbers are not finite or whose knot intervals are not positive fails the feature’s check.

Tests: core/model/src/features/cage.rs (cargo test -p mitcad-model cage), core/f3d-design/src/cage.rs, core/import-replay/src/cages.rs, core/dump/src/cage.rs.

Forms from imported cages (mitcad#1757)

A control cage another program made becomes a Form’s cage where it maps onto one:

  • .3dm SubD objects come in as Form features (.3dm import, SubD objects).
  • .f3d Form bodies come in as the faces the file stores, their cages kept beside them (Control cages of imported Form bodies). A kept cage maps onto a Form’s when it is uniform: a surface of degree 3 whose control points are its vertices’ own (no secondary points), each of weight 1, and whose edges all have the same knot interval. Its vertices and faces get the ids 1, 2, … in order, its faces are turned to run counter-clockwise seen from outside, its creased edges between two faces are creases sharp for good and its corner vertices corners. form.create with "primitive": {"type": "kept_cage", "body": "F4.b0"} makes an editable Form of it, where it is (center is not used), in the active component (activate the body’s component first); the imported body stays as it is: the Form’s surface is the Catmull-Clark limit surface of the cage, the same as the stored faces on the cage’s regular quads but not exactly near extraordinary vertices and T-junctions, so the import does not replace the body (hide or delete it once the Form is as wanted). A cage that does not map is refused in words (a control point of the kept cage has a weight other than 1 (a rational surface), which a Form's cage does not have, the kept cage has control points beside its vertices' own, …, the edges of the kept cage have knot intervals that are not all the same, …, the body has no control cage kept with it). The .f3d import report’s form_cages says of each kept cage (cage, the file’s entry; body) whether it maps (form) and, if not, why in words (why); its text, control cage of <body>: opens as an editable Form or … does not open as a Form, the body stays as stored: <why>.

The model side is ControlCage::form_cage (core/model/src/features/cage.rs), Document::kept_form_cage (core/model/src/document/kept_cages.rs) and mitcad_subdiv::orient (faces turned to run one way, used by both imports).

Tests: core/model/src/features/cage.rs and core/model/src/document/kept_cages.rs (a kept cage opened and edited on the mock kernel; refusals), core/import-replay/src/cages.rs (a decoded uniform cube cage mapped; a secondary point, a weight or uneven knots refused), core/subdiv/src/orient.rs, core.3dm and the .3dm import’s cli.import_3dm_subd and cli.import_3dm_subd_edit.

Midpoint lines and normal arcs (mitcad#1393)

Midpoint line. sketch.add_line with "mode": "midpoint" takes the line’s middle center and one end end (point inputs); the other end is as far on the other side of center. The middle is a sketch point (a new one, or the existing point given as center) held at the line’s middle by a midpoint constraint, so the line stays symmetric about it when an end is dragged or dimensioned:

{"cmd": "sketch.add_line", "sketch": "F1", "mode": "midpoint", "center": [0, 0], "end": [10, 5]}

Normal arc. sketch.arc with "mode": "normal" leaves the end point from of a line or a circular arc square to it (where tangent leaves along it), toward the side of the curve that end is on. Its centre lies on the line (a coincident of the centre point on the line, the infinite line), or, from an arc, on that arc’s tangent at from (a construction line from the arc’s centre to from, and a tangent of the new arc to it). The end may not lie straight across from from (the arc would be a line); from a spline or an ellipse the mode is refused.

{"cmd": "sketch.arc", "sketch": "F1", "mode": "normal", "from": "p3", "end": [15, 5]}

An arc that sweeps 180 degrees or more ends behind the curve, on the other side than it leaves toward: toward, a position [x, y], gives the side it leaves toward instead of end (mitcad#1608; the Line tool passes its cursor’s side). From p3 at (10, 0) at the end of a line along +x, this arc leaves upward and sweeps 270 degrees round the centre (20, 0) to (20, -10):

{"cmd": "sketch.arc", "sketch": "F1", "mode": "normal", "from": "p3", "end": [20, -10], "toward": [10, 5]}

The sketch Line tool draws both kinds of arc by a drag from a chain’s end or from the end of a line or an arc, and the Midpoint Line tool draws the midpoint line (app/COMMANDS.md, “The line tool’s arcs and Midpoint Line”). Tests: core/model-tests/sketch/src/sketch_line_arcs_1393_tests.rs.

Linked designs read again while open (mitcad#1416)

update_links reads the linked designs’ files when a design opens (External components). While the design is open, the links query says which of those files changed since the design took their bodies, and update_link reads them again at once. Both follow a link as update_links does: only a file in the design’s project (mitcad#929), from base, the design file’s folder (left out: the folder the design was read from; a design never saved follows no link).

CommandFieldsResult
update_linkcomponent (uid or name; left out: every linked design), base (optional)updated (the components that took their file again), messages (a line per component read)
QueryFieldsResult
linksbase (optional)links: per linked design (not library parts), in the order of the components, component, name, path (as the design saves it), file (the file it is followed to; null when not followed), options (linked with options), changed (the file is not the text the component last took), problem (why it is not followed or cannot be read, in words; for a file outside the project with the way out, mitcad#1719: “the file is outside the project, so the link is not followed; to follow it, move the file into the project, or make the folder that holds both a project (File › Project › New Project…), then Update Link”; null)
  • One undo step. update_link takes the changed files’ bodies (a design linked with options its design) as one undo step, Update Link <component> or Update All Links; their links take the files’ new digests, so links says changed: false until the files change again. A file that did not change gives the line <component> is up to date with <path> and, when no file changed, nothing changes and there is no undo step. A file not followed, not readable or not a design keeps its component’s bodies with the same lines as update_links ("…; it keeps the bodies saved with the project"). component that is no linked design (the root, a component of this design, a library part) is refused: “ is not a linked design; only a design linked from a file is read again”.
  • The same reading. update_links and update_link read a file the same way (core/model/src/document/link_updates.rs): its digest against the link’s, its design with its B-rep data from the store of the project it is in, its visible bodies (or its envelope, for a link shown by its envelope) as the component’s base feature’s bodies, its mount frames. update_links keeps the lines as load warnings (mitcad-cli info prints them as Warning: …), and the application shows them in the message band when it opens a design.
  • Both are file IO (they read the linked files): not for external clients.
  • The application’s Open Linked Design, Update Link, Update All Links and its “ changed” notice with Update (app/COMMANDS.md, “Linked designs”).
{"query": "links", "base": "/projects/lamp/assembly"}
{"cmd": "update_link", "component": "Electronics", "base": "/projects/lamp/assembly"}
{"cmd": "update_link", "base": "/projects/lamp/assembly"}

Tests: core/model-tests/assembly/src/link_update_tests.rs (a holder and its linked designs saved in a project, opened, changed while open, Update Link and Update All Links undone), the ctest cli.linked_design_update_reported (a reported holder whose linked file changed after it was saved, under MITCAD_MITCAD_REPORTED).

The model’s items in drawing views (mitcad#1406)

A drawing’s views bring in the model’s own annotations (Annotations, Datums and feature control frames, Hole callouts and the reference look), as they retrieve the sketches’ dimensions (Annotations on drawing views, retrieved_dimensions), and the Drawing tab’s Model Items switches both on for the views at once (api/drawing_annotations.rs, api/annotations.rs: model_items).

A view’s model_annotations (add_drawing_view, edit_drawing_view; off when left out; the drawing query’s views and the file list it, left out when off): the model’s shown annotations whose plane the view sees square on, each laid out by the drawing’s engine (the same as the drawing’s own annotations: its paper text height, its defaults, the drawing’s decimals where the annotation has none) with the model’s value, format, tolerance, letter, frame and words, worked out whenever the sheet is drawn, so they follow the model:

  • a length (distance, offset, axis_distance, center_distance) a linear dimension between its measured ends, horizontal or vertical where they lie level or plumb in the view, else aligned; a radius and a diameter of their circle (end on, or from the side for a diameter on a leader); an angle between its rays;
  • a note, a material or process note and a hole callout a note on a leader to the arrow’s point with the model’s lines; a datum label a datum label of its letter; a feature control frame a frame (one that stands under a dimension on a leader to that dimension’s first point);
  • a hole callout (and a frame under it) where the view sees its hole end on, whatever its own plane.

The filters of retrieved_dimensions apply: not on pictorial views, behind a section’s plane, in a detail’s circle and beside breaks only, in the root’s drawings only, and only where the view shows every body the annotation’s picks are on (one of construction geometry alone is not brought in). An annotation hidden in the model (visible: false) or broken there is not brought in.

Once on a sheet. A model annotation is drawn in the first view of the sheet (in the sheet’s order) that brings it in, and not in the views after it; so is each sketch dimension a view retrieves (each placement of it, mitcad#744, once). One kept as the drawing’s own (below) is not brought into any view of that sheet.

The drawing query’s sheet asked for lists them as model_items: {"view", "name", "kind" (the model’s), "type" (the drawing’s type that draws it), "label" (its words on one line), "box"}. Group model-annotation, its id M: and the annotation’s name (M:Offset1; not an annotation of the drawing’s, which are A<id>).

CommandFieldsResult
drawing_model_itemsdrawing, sheet (0), views (ids; all the sheet’s when left out or empty), sketch_dimensions, model_annotations (each true when left out: switched on; false leaves it as it is)views (those acted on), switched (those that changed); one undo step Model Items on Sheet1 of Drawing1, none when nothing changes; refused for a cut sheet, a view the sheet has not, and both false
keep_drawing_model_itemsdrawing, view, names (the model annotations the view draws; all of them when left out)annotations (the new ids), kept; one undo step Keep Offset1 in Drawing1, Keep 3 model annotations in Drawing1

Kept as the drawing’s own. keep_drawing_model_items makes each model annotation the view draws an annotation of that view, of the type that drew it, with its format, tolerance, letter, frame or words, and kept_from (the model annotation’s name; a rename in the model follows it, in the same undo step), so that it is moved, dragged and edited as the drawing’s own without changing the model. Its picks are the model’s picks as the view picks them: an edge by its name (with the end or middle at the measured point where there is one), a round face by its name, a planar face at the measured point on it (on_face), a vertex as the end of an edge there; refused (with why) for construction geometry or a whole body, for a view that does not draw it, and for a datum letter the drawing has already. A kept note keeps its words as they were. A hole callout is kept as the drawing’s own hole_callout on the same pick (mitcad#2054), not as a note of its words: it follows the hole and takes Text Before, Text After and Replace Value. Files: an annotation’s kept_from, left out when none.

The application (app/COMMANDS.md, Drawings): the Drawing tab’s Model Items (Dimensions group), a view’s panel’s Model Annotations beside Sketch Dimensions and its Keep Model Annotations.

Tests: core/model-tests/drawing-views/src/model_items_tests.rs (a part with a height, a datum and a hole callout: Model Items on all views draws each once in the view that faces it, the values following the model, the file and undo; the views and kinds given, refusals; hidden in the model; once on a sheet with a back and a bottom view, sketch dimensions too; kept as the drawing’s own, moved without changing the model, following a rename), app/tests/drawing_tools.cpp (the tool and its command), tools/ui-drawings-test.sh and tools/ui-windows-drawings-test.ps1 (app.ui-windows-drawings: Model Items on a sheet of three views).

Intersection Curve (mitcad#1405)

The feature. intersection_curve makes the 3D curve whose views along two sketches’ normals are curves of those sketches: each chain is swept along its own sketch’s normal, through the other chain’s extent, and the curve is where the two surfaces cross.

{"type": "intersection_curve",
 "first": {"sketch": "F1", "curves": ["c1"], "chain": true},
 "second": {"sketch": "F2", "curves": ["c1"]}}
  • first, second: curves of one sketch each, in the form of a sweep’s path ({"sketch", "curves", "chain"}, Paths); each must be a chain that does not branch. The two are curves of different sketches. Since mitcad#1777 both may instead be faces and bodies, {"geometry": [...]} (Curve tools).
  • The curve’s pieces come from the geometry kernel (Kernel::intersection_curves, geometry/src/intersection_curve.cpp: the chains swept both ways past the box of both, crossed by OCCT’s section), and are joined here into one curve, in order, each running along it, from the end nearer to where the first chain starts; its pieces are named F5:curve1, F5:curve2, … in that order.
  • The curve follows both sketches: an edit, a dimension or a parameter of either evaluates it again, and the features that take it with it.
  • It makes no body. It has a light bulb as construction geometry has (set_feature_visible; View › Show’s construction hides it too), and its results are not kept in the result store.

Refusals say why: the two chains of one sketch (both chains are curves of Sketch1); sketches in parallel planes (Sketch1 and Sketch2 lie in parallel planes: curves swept along the same normal cross in no curve); no crossing (the curves do not cross); a result that branches (the curve branches at (x, y, z), each point where more than two pieces meet); a result in pieces apart (the curves cross in 2 separate stretches (from (…) to (…); a closed loop through (…))).

As a path. {"feature": "F5"} is a path wherever one is taken: a sweep’s path and guide rails, a pipe’s path, a loft’s centre line and rails, a path pattern’s path (copies moved along it, and with along_path turned as its tangent turns), and the path of a construction plane or point along a path. The feature it names must be an Intersection Curve before the feature, in the same component. A path pattern and the construction along a path measure it along its length (CurveChain): along its exact pieces, each piece’s speed integrated (Gauss-Legendre between samples, within a B-spline’s knot spans) and a length’s parameter found by Newton’s method on the same integral, so a point at a length or a fraction lies on the curve at that length to rounding (mitcad#1417; within 1e-6 mm on a curve of 1 m, where chords were some 2e-8 of the length off).

Ribs and webs (mitcad#1417) grow from it when it lies in one plane: "curves": {"feature": "F5"} (rib, web).

In another component (mitcad#1417). The curve is in its component’s coordinates, as sketches and construction geometry are: a feature of another component that names it without a link is refused (… is in Motor; a feature of Frame cannot use it). A construction plane, axis or point takes it through its datum_links ({"F5": {"source": "O1", "target": "O2"}}), and a sketch’s projection through the occurrence that shows it (sketch.project with occurrence, and context): the curve is moved into the feature’s coordinates by the placements at its point of the timeline and follows when the occurrences move.

Projected into a sketch. sketch.project with "source": {"feature": "F5"} projects the curve along the sketch’s normal, its ends with it; with "section": true the points where the sketch’s plane crosses it instead. Linked (the default for Project and Intersect), the projection records the source {"feature": "F5"} and follows the curve; the Intersection Curve comes before the sketch, in its component, or in another one through occurrence (and context) as another component’s sketch geometry is (mitcad#1417; the projection records the link). It takes no body. The sketch’s Project and Intersect pick it in the view, on its Browser row or on the timeline (app/COMMANDS.md, “Intersection Curve”).

Drawn. The feature_curves query lists the curves of the Intersection Curves before the marker: [{"uid", "name", "points"}], each curve one polyline in its component’s coordinates (a line’s ends, other pieces at 64 points each). The view draws them as the construction geometry’s lines; a click picks the feature, which path inputs take (app/COMMANDS.md, “Intersection Curve”).

Previewed (mitcad#1496). The preview of an Intersection Curve (added or edited) adds its curve: {"points": [[x, y, z], …]}, the polyline the feature_curves query gives the finished curve, in its component’s coordinates (Document::preview_curve). A preview that fails (status error, e.g. curves that do not cross) and the previews of other features have none.

Tests: core/model/src/features/intersection_curve.rs (joining and measuring), core/model-tests/features-profile/src/intersection_curve_tests.rs (the mock kernel: the curve of an arc on XZ and a line on XY, a circle swept along it following a dimension of each sketch, construction along it, projection, the refusals; mitcad#1417: a rib and a web grown from it following it, a curve off any plane refused, construction along a 1 m curve of a line and an arc within 1e-6 mm, a construction point and a section in another component through Motor:1; mitcad#1496: the preview’s curve, added and edited, as feature_curves gives it, none for a failure or a sweep), geometry/tests/test_intersection_curve.cpp (geometry.intersection_curve: an arc and a line, two cylinders whose crossing branches), tools/ui-intersection-curve-test.sh (mitcad#1417: Project and Intersect take the curve, whole sketches as before).

Mirrors and patterns of sheet metal bodies (mitcad#1450)

A mirror or a pattern of bodies (objects: {type: bodies}) whose body is a valid sheet metal body keeps the copies sheets (core/model/src/sheet/body_copy.rs, docs/sheet-metal.md, “Implementation notes (mitcad#1450)”):

  • As a new body (F<pattern>.b<k>): the copy takes the source’s sheet state carried by the element’s transform, its charts, bends, ports and straight-cut overlays moved with the material (a mirror turns each planar chart’s material side with its plane). Its domains keep their identities (a sheet’s domains are named per body), so later sheet features on the copy name the same panels as on the original, with the copy’s body: {"type":"sheet_fold","body":"F6.b0","panel":{"feature":"F3","slot":0},...}. The copy’s faces keep the copy’s names (F6:inst1(F3:sheet_back(0))); sheet_reference reads the domain inside them. Fold, Flange, Cut, Unfold and the Flat Pattern work on it.
  • Joined (combine): the copy and the sheet become one sheet. The copy’s domains and curves are renamed as the pattern’s, {feature: <pattern>, slot: s}, each slot derived from the copy and the identity it replaces (mitcad#1462): s is the 64-bit FNV-1a hash of <body>/<element>/<identity> (F3.b0/1/F5.p0 for the copy of {feature: F5, slot: 0} of F3.b0 at element 1; a pattern of patterns puts the inner patterns’ <feature>:<element> steps before the element, F3.b0/F6:1/1; a curve’s identity as F2/c1[c4,c2] or F5/g13), its two 32-bit halves xor-ed, taken modulo 2^32 - 100000 and added to 100000; a slot taken already gives the next free one. An upstream edit that adds or removes domains therefore leaves the other copied domains' names, and a later feature that names one (a Fold on the copied flange, {"feature":"F8","slot":1108818023}) still finds it. Every copy panel in the plane of a panel of the sheet that it touches along a seam is united with it into one panel (that panel’s identity, the seam gone). Since mitcad#1558 every copy bend on the cylinder of a bend of the sheet (the same axis, radii, angle and allowance, over the same arc: a bend across the mirror plane and its image) that it touches is likewise united with it into one bend: the copy’s strip mapped into the bend’s chart (u kept or run back, v along the common axis, reversed by a mirror across it), its seams in the bend’s axial coordinate, side by side with the bend’s along each tangent line, and the bend’s record covering both axial intervals. Other bends stay bends. The sheet is built again from the merged charts and must be the two halves joined (volume, area, centre of mass); the Flat Pattern unfolds the whole part. A copy that overlaps the sheet (“the halves overlap”), does not touch it (“does not touch it”) or meets it where no coplanar panels or coaxial bends share a seam (a wall across the mirror plane at a slant: “no coplanar panels or coaxial bends share a seam”) is refused with that reason, instead of an invalid sheet.
  • Combine (mitcad#1558): a combine join whose target and tools (bodies of its own component) are all valid sheets with one set of rules merges each tool into the target’s sheet in order, as a joined copy, its domains and curves renamed as the combine’s with the tool’s body as the copy’s key (F11.b0/<identity>); a mirror made as a new body and joined afterwards is one sheet, as with the mirror’s own combine. Where they are not one sheet (a tool that overlaps the target, does not touch it, or meets it elsewhere), the combine keeps the joined solid: the sheet-domain adapter re-derives it where it can (flat material in a panel’s plane), else the sheet is invalid with the reason (the joined bodies are not one sheet: F18.b0 cannot be joined to it: the halves overlap: …). A target or tool that is not a valid sheet leaves the join to the adapter, as before.

Since mitcad#1462 the same holds for:

  • A sheet holding a fillet or chamfer overlay: the copy keeps the overlay, its change read from the body it was made on (the overlay’s source in sheet_state, "source": "F3.b0") and moved with the copy; a joined copy’s overlay joins the sheet’s.
  • Patterns of patterns of bodies (a mirror or pattern of a pattern of bodies): each copy takes the sheet its body had before the inner pattern, carried by the inner and outer elements’ transforms. With combine a copy that touches the body joins its sheet as above; one that does not is a sheet of its own. A Move between keeps the sheet (it is carried by the move); a body ordinary modelling changed there, so that it had no valid sheet, is copied as an ordinary solid.
  • combine_any: a copy of a sheet that touches one sheet of the pattern (the original or a copy that stayed a body of its own) is joined to it as one sheet, as with combine; one that touches none is a new sheet body.

A join that no sheet carries (below) first goes to the sheet-domain adapter, as ordinary modelling does: where it re-derives the joined body (flat material joined in a panel’s plane, such as two flat sheets one combine_any copy joins at once), the body is a valid sheet and nothing is said. What it cannot re-derive stays an ordinary solid, and the feature warns in words instead of leaving an invalid sheet unexplained:

  • a scaled copy (a Scale Pattern, a pattern’s or mirror’s scale): the scaled copies of sheet F3.b0 are not sheet metal bodies: scaling changes the sheet's thickness; joined to the sheet, F3.b0 is no longer a sheet metal body: it is joined to a scaled copy of it (scaling changes the sheet's thickness);
  • a combine_any copy that touches several bodies at once, F6.b0, F8.b0 are no longer sheet metal bodies: a copy of F6.b0 joins several bodies at once (a copy of a sheet is joined to one sheet at a time); only partly touching one (only part of a copy of … touches it); or a copy that is not a sheet joined to a sheet (… which is not a sheet metal body).

The sheet’s state is invalid as before (sheet_state says why).

Tests of mitcad#1558: CLI sheet_mirror_bend_join (a 60 x 20 Face folded 90 degrees at x = 0, t=2, r=3, K=0.3, 2400 + 8 pi, mirrored with Join about its y = 70 wall, which the bend crosses: one valid sheet of three charts and one bend, 4800 + 16 pi, its Flat Pattern the 60 x 40 blank; the same sheet mirrored as a new body and joined with Combine: the same; an image half over the sheet refused, “the halves overlap”, and its Combine an invalid sheet), sheet_mirror_bend_reported (the reported design of GitHub #209 under MITCAD_MITCAD_REPORTED, mirrored with Join about the wall along its sketch line c2 and joined with Combine); core/model/src/sheet/body_copy.rs’s unit tests (the bend charts’ maps).

Tests of mitcad#1450: CLI sheet_mirror_body (a folded 40 x 20 panel mirrored as a new body: a pick of its panel, a Fold on the copy 800 + 2 pi, its Flat Pattern; a pattern of three), sheet_mirror_body_join (the same joined: 1600 + 2 pi, one panel, the Flat Pattern the 80 x 20 blank at x=-40..40; a Fold across the mirrored half; the overlap, gap and wall-to-wall refusals, the last “no coplanar panels or coaxial bends share a seam” since mitcad#1558), sheet_mirror_reported (the reported design of GitHub #188 under MITCAD_MITCAD_REPORTED, as saved and joined); the copies’ face names in core/model/src/sheet/pick_tests.rs.

Spacing beyond the brims

mitcad#1491 (core/model/src/exchange/bed.rs, first_layer_reach): the export’s arranger sets the pieces it puts side by side on the bed (Export by occurrences, the pieces of a print plate and its copies) far enough apart that a slicer’s brim does not join two neighbours (a G-code path conflict on the first layer). Two neighbours, in a row along X and between rows along Y, lie apart by the spacing plus how far each one’s first layer reaches past it by the settings it prints with (a plate’s pieces by the plate’s, profile < plate < component < occurrence < body):

  • its brim: brim_width plus brim_separation (the brim’s gap from the piece), unless brim_type is no_brim or inner_only; auto_brim (and no brim_type at all) counts, as the slicer adds that brim to tall, narrow pieces;
  • a skirt of its own (skirt_per_object on, skirts loops above 0): skirt_distance plus a nozzle’s width (the printer’s nozzle_diameter, else 0.4 mm) per loop;
  • the further of the two; 0 without either. A piece of several bodies reaches as far as its furthest.

So two pieces with an 8 mm brim lie 8 + 5 + 8 = 21 mm apart, two without one 5 mm. The rows are wrapped and centred with the brims counted, and the warning that pieces do not fit on the bed gives their size with them (… (they take 300 x 40 mm with their brims): …).

export with on_bed (implied by plates and plate) takes spacing: the clearance in mm between two neighbours beyond their brims, 0 to 1000, 5 when left out, for slicer settings the export cannot see. Refused without on_bed and outside its range.

{"cmd": "export", "path": "kit.3mf", "plates": "one_file", "dialect": "bambu_studio", "spacing": 8}

Tests: core/model-tests/print/src/print_plates_tests.rs (mock kernel: two pieces on a plate whose values have brim_width 8 written 21 mm apart, 5 mm with brim_type no_brim; the copies of an item with a count not centred as far apart; spacing 12 without a brim 12 mm apart; the refusals).

Tangent dimensions between circles

A sketch dimension can measure from a circle’s or arc’s tangent side instead of its centre (mitcad#1540, GitHub #203): the gap between two circles, or from one circle’s side to a point. Each is the nearest gap, measured along the line through the centres; its value is a length that must not be negative.

  • tangent_circle_distance (a, b: circles or arcs, two different ones; optional side): with side outside (the default, not written) the gap between two circles outside each other, the distance of their centres minus both radii; with inside, one within the other, the gap between the inner circle’s far side and the outer circle: the larger radius minus the smaller one minus the distance of the centres. Which one is the outer is taken from the radii when the dimension is added; a and b may come in either order.
  • tangent_point_distance (circle: a circle or arc, point; optional side): with outside (the default) the point’s distance from the centre minus the radius, for a point outside the circle; with inside the radius minus that distance. The point may be another circle’s centre: the distance from one circle’s tangent side to the other’s centre.
  • From a circle’s side to a line stays tangent_distance; between centres, the usual distance and point_line_distance of the centre points.

Driving ones move the geometry to the value (the solver’s TangentCircleDistance and TangentPointDistance constraints, equations CircleGap and CirclePointGap in core/solver/src/equations.rs, with their derivatives by forward differentiation); a driven one ("driven": true) only measures, and the sketch query gives its measured value.

{"cmd": "sketch.add_dimension", "sketch": "F1",
 "dimension": {"type": "tangent_circle_distance", "a": "c3", "b": "c5"}, "value": 12}
{"cmd": "sketch.add_dimension", "sketch": "F1",
 "dimension": {"type": "tangent_point_distance", "circle": "c3", "point": "p4", "side": "inside"},
 "driven": true}

The Sketch Dimension tool makes them from its right-click menu: Center or Tangent for each circle or arc picked, and Driving or Driven for the dimension (app/COMMANDS.md, Sketch Dimension).

Tests: core/solver/tests/constraints.rs (tangent_circle_distance_is_the_gap_between_two_circles, tangent_point_distance_is_the_gap_between_a_circle_and_a_point), core/model-tests/sketch/src/sketch_tangent_dimensions_1540_tests.rs (tangent to tangent and tangent to centre between two circles solve to the typed value within 1e-6 mm, the gaps inside a circle, and driven ones that only measure); the UI test tools/ui-sketch-tangent-dimension-test.sh.

The closed loop of a sketch curve

{"query": "sketch_loop", "sketch": "F1", "curve": "c3"} (mitcad#1541, sketch_loop.rs, mitcad_model::sketch::loops) answers {"curves": ["c3", "c6", "c8", "c10"]}: the curves of the smallest closed loop the curve bounds, each once, in the loop’s order; what a double-click on the curve selects in the app (app/COMMANDS.md, “Chain selection by a double-click”). The curves of the picked one’s kind (construction or not; never both, the sketch’s axes and texts left out) are arranged as profile regions are (core/sketch/src/regions.rs): cut at their crossings, dangling and bridging pieces dropped. Of the regions whose outer loop runs along the curve, the one whose outer loop encloses the least area (its holes counted in) gives the loop, so it passes points where more than two curves meet: on a rectangle with a line leaving one corner, a side gives the four sides. curves is empty when the curve bounds no loop (that line, an open polyline), and for a point or an id the sketch’s curves lack. The geometry is the sketch query’s: the last evaluation’s solve, else solved by the query, linked projections where their sources are now; a sketch that does not solve is an error.

Tests: core/sketch/src/loops.rs (a rectangle with a line leaving a corner, an open polyline, a side two rectangles share, a loop with a large hole beside a smaller one, a lone circle) and core/model-tests/sketch/src/sketch_loop_1541_tests.rs (the query, with a construction line that closes a triangle with normal sides).

Line styles in drawing views (mitcad#1546)

A view of a drawing can draw the visible lines of one projected edge, of one body, or of every body a component’s occurrence places with a width and a pattern of its own (ISO 128-3: an adjacent part as a long dash double dotted line, an edge to stand out), in that view only (core/model/src/drawing/def.rs LineStyle, api/drawing_lines.rs, core/model-drawing/src/compose.rs LinePens).

The long dash double dotted pattern. Every pattern takes phantom now (ISO 128 type 05, the phantom line: 12, 1.5, 0.5, 1.5, 0.5, 1.5 mm), the lines and arcs drawn by hand too (add_drawing_annotation, edit_drawing_annotation; Drawing defaults, sketches, patterns and turned views), written as width and pattern in files. Pens of the drawing query: phantom, phantom_thick, phantom_extra_thick.

CommandFieldsResult
edit_drawing_linedrawing, view; what: body, occurrence, edge (as a pick names them: an edge of a body by its topological name, a body alone, or an occurrence alone: every body it and its occurrences place), or at (a sheet point on the view: the edge a click there picks, drawing_pick’s "want": "edge") with of (edge (default), body, component: the occurrence that places the picked body); width (thin, thick, extra_thick) and pattern (continuous, dashed, chain, phantom), one or both (a new choice starts wide and continuous, an existing one keeps the part not given); or reset: truedrawing, view, line (the choice as kept, null after a reset); undo step Edit line in view 1 of Drawing1 or Reset line in view 1 of Drawing1; a reset of what has no choice changes nothing

What wins. An edge’s choice wins over its body’s, a body’s over its occurrence’s, and a deeper occurrence’s over the one it lies in. A body is named where occurrence places it (a path from the drawing’s component; its own placement when left out), as a pick’s is. Only the visible lines change: hidden lines keep the view’s dashes. A view’s choices are its own: its projected, section and detail views do not take them.

Following the model. An edge is kept by its body and its topological name. When the view is drawn the edge is found again by its name (Kernel::edge_geometry), seen as the view sees it (a line, or a circle or an arc end on or from the side; another curve by its two ends), and its body’s projected lines that lie on it (within 0.001 mm, or the view’s deflection when it is projected from a triangulation) take its pen: the kernel’s hidden-line removal keeps no edge names. So the choice follows the edge when the model changes. A choice whose edge is gone, or whose body or occurrence the view no longer shows, is kept and is a warning of the view (the edge E{…} of F2.b0 is gone: its line style is kept, the view no longer shows the body F4.b0: its line style is kept; the sheet’s view 1: …).

The query, files and exports. The drawing query’s view gives lines, its choices in their file form (body, occurrence, edge, width, pattern); drawing_pick takes "want": "edge" (an edge, whole, whatever its curve). Files: a view’s lines, left out when empty; a component’s copied drawing maps their bodies, occurrences and edges, and an occurrence moved to another parent takes their paths along, as annotations’ picks. The sheet, the PDF and SVG files and print draw a chosen line with its width’s line width and its pattern’s dashes. Since mitcad#1546 a DXF file’s pen layers carry their line types and weights: DASHED, CHAIN and PHANTOM defined in the LTYPE table with their dashes (scaled with an inch file) on the dashed, long dash dotted and long dash double dotted layers (PHANTOM, PHANTOM_THICK, PHANTOM_EXTRA_THICK the new ones), CONTINUOUS on the others, and each layer’s weight the pen’s width in hundredths of a millimetre (group 370: 13, 18, 35, 50, 70); mitcad_dxf writes and reads Linetype and Layer::lineweight. DWG keeps the layers only.

Refused: at together with body, occurrence or edge; of without at; no edge at at; of component for a body in no component of the view; an edge without its body; neither a body nor an occurrence; a body, occurrence or edge the view does not show or the body has not; no width or pattern (and no reset); a width or pattern with reset; a cut sheet.

{"cmd": "edit_drawing_line", "drawing": "D1", "view": 1, "body": "F2.b0",
 "edge": "E{F2:end(r{…})|F2:side(c1[c4,c2])}", "width": "thick", "pattern": "phantom"}

The application: Edit Line… in a projected edge’s menu (app/COMMANDS.md, “Drawings”). Tests: core/model-tests/drawing-views/src/line_style_tests.rs (mock kernel: an edge’s lines following its edge when the model changes; a body’s lines and the edge’s choice winning; a click’s edge, its body, the refusals; the ranks of occurrences; the file and undo; the SVG, PDF and DXF exports with the DXF line types and weights), core/dxf/tests/write.rs (line types and weights written and read back, scaled, R12), app/tests/drawing_tools.cpp (the patterns, the command and the log line), tools/ui-drawing-edge-line-test.sh and tools/ui-windows-drawing-edge-line-test.ps1 (app.ui-windows-drawing-edge-line) on the shared steps tools/ui-scripts/drawing-edge-line.mitcad-ui.

3D sketches: spatial_sketch and sketch3d (mitcad#1522)

A 3D sketch holds points with three coordinates and lines, arcs, circles and splines through them, in a frame that follows its support (an origin plane, a construction plane or a planar face of the active component). It is a feature type of its own, spatial_sketch, with its own commands (sketch3d.*) and query (sketch3d): the planar sketch.* commands and the sketch query keep their meaning and refuse a 3D sketch (3DSketch1 (F2) is a 3D sketch: the sketch3d.* commands edit it), and the sketch3d commands and query refuse a planar one. A 3D sketch’s closed loops in its sketch plane bound profile regions as a planar sketch’s do (below). The model side is core/sketch/src/spatial.rs (definition, solver adapter, output), spatial_edit.rs (its edits) and core/model/src/document/spatial_sketches.rs; docs/architecture.md, “3D sketches”, says how they fit together.

Frame and values. Points are local coordinates [x, y, z] in millimetres: x and y along the support’s axes, z along its normal. Lengths, radii and arc lengths are millimetres, values follow Values (a number, a parameter’s name or an expression). The query gives each point also as position in the component’s coordinates and the frame as origin, x_axis, y_axis and normal.

Ids. Points, curves and texts share one numbering (p1, c3, t5), relations and dimensions another (k2), as in a planar sketch. A command’s result gives the ids it made: entities (new points and curves in the order they were made), points, curves, constraints, dimensions, parameters (created for new driving dimensions), removed (when anything was removed), made (the main item: the line, arc, circle, spline, point, relation or dimension) and status; take ids from there or from the query. A point input is [x, y, z] (a new point, fixed by nothing: its coordinates only start the solve) or "p3" (an existing point, which joins the new curve to it); [x, y] is refused, as is a curve’s id where a point is wanted.

One edit, one undo step. Every sketch3d.* command but sketch3d.create names its sketch ("sketch": "F2") and is one edit of the model: a segment or arc with its new points, attachments, axis or normal alignment, tangency and dimensions is solved with the support and the sources where they are now and taken whole, as one undo step (Add Line in 3DSketch1); one that does not solve, or whose input is invalid, is refused with nothing changed (definition, parameters, ids, history). The refusal says why in plain words for a person and, in its detail for agents, names the relations involved (mitcad#1644, docs/ui-conventions.md “What a message says”: shown 3DSketch1: relations of the sketch contradict each other, detail 3DSketch1: the relations k2, k7 contradict each other, carried as the refusal’s [placed: ...] tail); the sketch3d query’s failure gives a failed evaluation’s kind (definition, support, reference, value, conflict, not_converged, invalid_geometry), message (plain words), detail (the same with the ids, names and points, when it says more), places (a source’s vertex, edge or face, when it has one), constraints and entities (the sketch’s own places, by id). Refused input: a coordinate that is not finite, a segment, radius or spacing of an arc’s ends or of a spline’s successive points at most 1e-6 mm, three Three-Point points on one line, a sense without an axis, a field of another mode, a driving spline length. Consistent redundant relations are kept with one warning (a relation is redundant: ..., its detail k7 is redundant: ...) and take no freedom; the query marks them redundant.

CommandFieldsResult
sketch3d.createsupport (default xy; xz, yz, a construction plane "F5" or a planar face {"face", "body"}), name (optional)uid, name (3DSketch1)
sketch3d.add_pointat [x, y, z] (its coordinates may be expressions, mitcad#1912), source (optional: a source point the point is attached to, or a source curve or a face of a body it is put on; see “Linked references” and “Points on faces” below), fixed (default false: a Fix where it is)made the point
sketch3d.add_linestart, end (point inputs: a new point’s coordinates may be expressions, see Point coordinates as expressions in 3D sketches), construction, axis (x, y or z: the line stays along that frame axis) and sense (positive, the default, or negative: from start to end), length (a driving true length), offsets ([dx, dy, dz]: driving signed offsets from start to end, null leaves one free), start_source, end_source (attachments, as add_point’s source)made the line, start, end; a new end starts where the axis and length or the offsets put it
sketch3d.add_arcmode: three_point (through [x, y, z]: a position the arc passes, not stored), center (center point input, normal [x, y, z], or normal_axis alone for an axis’s direction; a new end is placed on the arc’s circle) or tangent (from: the line, arc or spline whose end start is; the arc continues it tangentially, in the plane of that tangent and end, with a tangent relation); start, end (point inputs), construction, normal_axis and normal_sense (Keep Plane: the normal along a frame axis), radius, arc_length (driving), start_source, end_sourcemade the arc, center, start, end; it runs counter-clockwise about its normal from start to end
sketch3d.add_circlecenter (point input), radius (value), normal [x, y, z] or normal_axis (with normal_sense: kept along that axis), or plane (xy, yz or zx: bound to the plane square to that axis, mitcad#1550), through (existing points held on it), dimension (default true: a driving radius dimension; false: the radius is a plain number and only starts the solve), diameter (the dimension and radius a diameter), constructionmade the circle
sketch3d.add_splinepoints (point inputs), degree (left out: a cubic through the points, chord-length parameters; given: a B-spline by these control points, clamped uniform knots, weights 1), closed (fit points only: periodic through the first point), ends ([start, end] of an open fit-point spline: natural, the default, or free), constructionmade the spline, spline_points its points in order; a fit-point spline’s hidden control points are the solver’s, not addressable
sketch3d.add_constraintconstraint: as in the definition without id: coincident (a, b: points), fix (point; at left out: where it is now), attach (point, source), align (line, axis, sense), point_on (point, curve: a line between its ends, an arc’s full circle, a spline within its range), midpoint (point, curve: a line or an arc), tangent (a, b: curves, at: their shared point; sense left out: taken from the geometry and then kept), equal (two lines’ lengths or two arcs’ or circles’ radii), normal_align (curve, axis, sense: an arc’s or circle’s free normal), on_sketch_plane (points: their elevation groups join the sketch’s one On Sketch Plane relation), and parallel, perpendicular, symmetric, concentric, curvature and on_plane (see “3D relations and dimensions” below, mitcad#1661)made the relation (the On Sketch Plane relation it joined); in-plane relations are a converted sketch’s only and refused
sketch3d.add_dimensiondimension: as in the definition without id and value: length (line), offset (a, b: points, axis: the signed b - a), radius, diameter, arc_length (curve), spline_length (curve: driving or driven, mitcad#1661), angle (a, b: two lines, or a line and an arc or circle whose normal is the direction, or two normals; radians strictly between 0 and pi, a person’s value in degrees; no intersection implied, mitcad#1661), tangent_magnitude (curve: an open spline, end: start or end; abs(C'(t)) in its parameter, the stored tangent’s length, mm; a fit-point spline’s end must be free or held by a tangency or curvature continuity, mitcad#1661); value (default: what it measures now), driven (default false; a driven one takes no value; it gets a read-only reference parameter d<n> that the features after the sketch and the sketch’s own driving dimensions may use, mitcad#1661)made the dimension; a driving one’s value is a parameter owned by the sketch, or the named parameter given
sketch3d.set_dimensiondimension (k3), valuea number or expression changes its own parameter, a parameter’s name binds it to that parameter, name = expression renames its parameter and sets it; a value that uses the dimension’s own parameter keeps that parameter as a user parameter, and its bare name only moves it there (result user_parameters and notes, as sketch.set_dimension’s; see Values); a driven one becomes driving; undo step Edit Dimension in 3DSketch1
sketch3d.set_drivendimension, driven (default true)driven: it only measures, its parameter goes when nothing else uses it; driving: at its measured value
sketch3d.set_constructioncurves, construction (default true)
sketch3d.fixpoints, fixed (default true)Fix where each point is now; fixed: false (Unfix) removes the Fix only, an attachment stays (removed)
sketch3d.detachpointsremoves each point’s attachment, or its Point on Curve and Midpoint relations with reference curves (a reference curve nothing uses any more goes with them); the point stays where it is, free as far as the other relations allow (removed)
sketch3d.release_from_planepointstheir elevation groups (coincident points, a plane-bound curve’s points) leave the On Sketch Plane relation, which goes when it is empty; released: the representatives taken out
sketch3d.release_planecurves (plane-bound arcs and circles, as a converted sketch has them)Release Plane: the normal starts along its axis and is free from then on
sketch3d.removeitems (p3, c4, k5), dependents (default false)relations and dimensions, then curves (with their own relations; their points stay where another curve or relation uses them), then points; a point that a curve or relation not listed uses is refused naming them, unless dependents; a relation that only lists a point in a plane (on_sketch_plane, on_plane, a plane-bound shape’s) is no use of it: the point leaves its list and the others stay (mitcad#1834)
sketch3d.dragpoints [{point, to [x, y, z]}], tangents [{curve (an open fit-point spline), end (start or end), to [x, y, z]: the wanted end tangent C’(t), the spline’s parameter running from 0 to 1}] (mitcad#1526: a tangent handle’s drag, at an end that is free or held by a tangency; a natural end is refused), at least one of the two; preview (default false)pulls the points and the end tangents toward the targets as far as the relations allow (soft goals: no relation is stored; a tangent reached is kept with the spline as its tangents), one undo step Drag in 3DSketch1; preview: only points (every point where it would go), curves (each curve’s geometry as the query gives it, where the drag would take it) and status, nothing changes
QueryFieldsResult
sketch3duid; path (optional: {curves, chain, reversed}, mitcad#1527)uid, name, type (spatial_sketch), support, frame {origin, x_axis, y_axis, normal} (null when the support was not found), points [{id, at (local, solved), position (component), determined, on_sketch_plane}], curves (as in the definition, with plane_bound, determined and geometry: a line’s start, end, length; an arc’s or circle’s normal, radius and an arc’s sweep and length; a spline’s degree, knots, weights, control_points, and an open fit-point spline’s end_tangents [start, end] (C’(t), where its tangent handles are, mitcad#1526); a reference curve’s, as found from its source before the solve, also when it failed: kind line (start, end), conic (center, normal, x_axis, major, minor, start, end, closed), bspline (degree, poles, weights, knots) or helix (center, axis, x_axis, radius, pitch, start, end), local coordinates, mitcad#1524), constraints (as in the definition, with in_plane, a tangency’s solved sense, an attachment’s target as found before the solve, redundant), dimensions (as in the definition with value the parameter’s name, driven, expression, measured, in_plane, redundant), references (the linked reference records, see “Linked references” below), chains (the chains chain selection finds, see “Pipe and Sweep along 3D sketch curves” below), evaluated, status {dof, fully_constrained, determined {points, lines, curves}, redundant, measured {k3: value}} (null when it did not solve), failure (when it failed), warnings, texts (a converted sketch’s), plane_curves (its curves in its sketch plane, when it solved: see “Curves of 3D sketches that grow walls and surfaces” below), route (with path: see “Routes in the query” below)

In the timeline and the browser (mitcad#1524) a 3D sketch is a sketch: the timeline query gives its dof (when it solved) and its light bulb (visible, visible_set), which set_feature_visible sets as a planar sketch’s (Hide 3DSketch1, one undo step); it is shown unless hidden.

The definition (add_feature, edit_feature, the design file) is written flat, ids with each item; the stored positions, normals and radii are where the last solve left them and where the next one starts:

{"type": "spatial_sketch", "support": "xy",
 "points": [{"id": "p1", "at": [0, 0, 0]}, {"id": "p2", "at": [40, 0, 0]}],
 "curves": [{"id": "c3", "type": "line", "start": "p1", "end": "p2"}],
 "constraints": [{"id": "k1", "type": "attach", "point": "p1", "source": "origin"},
                 {"id": "k2", "type": "align", "line": "c3", "axis": "x", "sense": "positive"}],
 "dimensions": [{"id": "k3", "type": "length", "line": "c3", "value": "d1"}]}

Curves: line (start, end), arc (center, start, end, normal, plane {axis, sense} for a plane-bound one), circle (center, radius, normal, plane), spline (degree, control, weights, knots), fitted_spline (points, closed, ends, tangents: the end tangents C’(t) [start, end] the last solve left at a free or tangent end, null at another; the next solve starts from them, so a dragged handle stays, mitcad#1526), and a converted sketch’s ellipse, elliptical_arc and reference; each with construction when it is one. Relations as sketch3d.add_constraint takes them, with id (and a Fix’s at, a tangency’s sense); a converted sketch’s in_plane and in_plane_fixed.
