cam_machine_to_librarymachine, library, project, as_id{path, version}: the design’s machine written as the next version of its file; the copy names it as its origin (undo Save CAM Machine; the file stays)
QueryFieldsResult
cam_setupssetups: each setup’s fields (visible always) with operations (each with its state), work ({origin, x, y, z} in model coordinates, stock_min, stock_max, bodies_top, safe_z in work coordinates; or {error}) and effective_dialect; machines: [{id, name, controller, tools}]
cam_operationssetup{setup, operations} as above
cam_toolpathssetup, operations (ids; all when left out){setup, work, operations: [{id, name, state, toolpath: {moves: [{kind: rapid | line | arc, to, feed, center, ccw}]}, tool, spindle_rpm, cut_length, duration, bounds, error}], findings}: computed now, in work coordinates (work places them in the model); findings the machine check’s ({message, operation, at}) when the setup has placement and every operation computed
cam_postsetup, dialect, units (millimetres, inches){text, extension, dialect, label, units}: the setup’s G-code, starting (after a tape mark) with four comment lines saying that MitCad CAM is highly experimental and the code is to be checked in a simulator and run with care before cutting, written even when comments are off. Refused while an operation fails or the setup has no machine
cam_machinesmachines: each with its tools and used_by (setup ids)
cam_dialectsdialects: [{id, label, extension}]
cam_libraryprojectmachines: [{library, id, name, controller, version, tools, path, in_design}], folders, problems

Adaptive clearing is the engine’s pocket with its adaptive option (phase 2), with the engine’s settings (45 degrees of engagement at most). Rest machining ({"type": "rest", "from_tool"}) cuts what the bigger tool from_tool (its number in the setup’s machine’s library) left: its diameter, and the stock to leave of the last operation before it that cut with that tool, go to the engine’s rest clean-up; it is refused without from_tool or when that tool is not in the library. Entries (entry), holding tabs (laid out by their count) and leads go to the engine’s contour, pocket and rest as they are, a helix without a radius turning at a quarter of the tool’s diameter. Drilling takes chip_break (pecks that back off instead of leaving the hole) and canned_cycle (on by default: the holes may be written as the controller’s canned cycle); whether cycles are written at all is the setup’s post.canned_cycles (off by default). Probing the work zero (probe_work_zero, MillenniumOS’ G6600) is passed to the post settings.

Code: core/model/src/cam/ (types, outlines, machine library), core/model/src/document/cam.rs, core/model-api/src/cam.rs. Tests: core/model-tests/cam, core/model/src/cam/outline.rs.

CAM: stock simulation

The stock as a setup’s program cuts it (mitcad#1013, phase 3; docs/cam.md “Stock simulation”): a height map of the stock in work coordinates (a Z per node of a grid over the stock’s box), each move swept by its tool’s cutting end (flat, ball, bull nose, drill point, V-bit), rapids as the posts write them. The grid is an eighth of the smallest tool’s diameter apart (at least 0.01 mm), coarser until it has at most max_nodes nodes (1 000 000 by default); what lies between nodes is not seen. Heights are written to the micrometre as runs: pairs of a height (µm) and a count of nodes, row by row from the grid’s origin (X first); in a snapshot a pair 0, -n is n nodes unchanged since the one before. The setup’s bodies, meshed and seen from above on the same grid, are the part: the material left over it (remaining) is the stock’s height less the part’s at each node where the part is, a gouge the part’s lowest height round a node less the stock’s, and the material beside it the stock left where the part is not.

QueryFieldsResult
cam_simulatesetup, until ({operation (id), move (index in its toolpath)}; the end when left out), frames (moves to take snapshots after, at most 1000), resolution (mm), max_nodes, tolerance (thicknesses up to it count as none; 0.01 mm), result (heights, the default, or remaining){setup, work, grid: {origin, step, nx, ny, bottom, top}, until (the last move cut), rapid_cuts: [{message, operation, move, leg, depth, at}], removed (mm³), lowest}; with heights: initial and heights (runs before and after), frames: [{operation, move, runs}] (each the changes since the snapshot before, the first since initial) and part (runs; with bodies); with bodies: remaining: {tolerance, max, mean, volume, area, thickest: [{at, model, thickness}], gouge, gouges, beside, beside_volume, part_nodes, beside_nodes} (the places in work coordinates and in the model, the thickest first, apart by the smallest tool’s diameter). Refused while an operation fails

The collision check of the spindle assembly (mitcad_cam::check_collisions) takes the stock as cut by the same simulation unless its options ask for the stock before the cut ("stock": "before_cut").

Code: core/cam/src/stock.rs, core/model/src/cam/simulate.rs, core/model/src/document/cam/simulate.rs, core/model-api/src/cam.rs. Tests: core/cam/src/stock/tests.rs, core/cam/src/collision/tests.rs, core/model-tests/cam/src/simulate_tests.rs.

CAM: 3-axis operations

mitcad#1013, phase 3 (core/cam/src/ops/surface.rs, raster.rs, waterline.rs, roughing.rs; document/cam.rs; the design in docs/cam.md, “3-axis machining”): three operation kinds of a setup that machine the bodies’ surfaces from their triangle meshes (each body meshed within 0.005 mm, CAM_SURFACE_DEVIATION, in the setup’s work coordinates), added and edited with cam_operation_add and cam_operation_edit like the others.

  • Inputs: {"kind": "body", "body", "occurrence"} for each body machined (the setup’s bodies when none is given), and faces or sketch profiles (face, region) as the boundary, the area the tool’s center stays in (the stock’s outline when none: for roughing and raster finishing; waterline finishing runs round everything). Edges, curves and points are refused for them, and bodies for the other kinds.
  • Defaults: the top is the stock’s top, the bottom the stock’s bottom; stepover and stock to leave as for the others.
  • Out of date: the fingerprint covers the bodies they read, the setup’s bodies (their versions and placements) when they pick none.
Kind (kind)FieldsWhat it does
{"type": "roughing_3d", "adaptive"}depths (step_down: the smaller of the flutes and the diameter), stepover (40 % of the diameter), stock_to_leave, direction, entry; adaptive true: each level by adaptive clearingLevels from the top down, at most the step down apart, and at each floor of the bodies raised by the stock to leave; each level a pocket of where the tool’s cylinder (grown by the stock to leave) may go, inside the boundary. A flat or bull nose end mill
{"type": "raster_finish", "angle", "slope"}angle (degrees from the work X; 0), slope (cut only where the surface is at most this steep, degrees from the horizontal; every slope), stepover (a tenth of the diameter), stock_to_leave, depths.bottom (the lowest the tool goes where nothing is under it)Parallel passes back and forth over the boundary, the tool dropped onto the surfaces (exact for flat, ball and bull nose end mills), within 0.01 mm between its points
{"type": "waterline_finish", "slope"}slope (cut only where the surface is at least this steep; every slope), depths (step_down: a tenth of the diameter), stock_to_leave, directionAt each level the loops where the tool just touches the surfaces, climb milling round the bodies by default; only their stretches inside a boundary

Angles and slopes are values with units like the others ("90 deg"). Refused in words: a drill or V-bit (raster and waterline: “The operation needs a flat, ball or bull nose end mill.”), a ball for roughing, a slope outside 0 to 90 degrees, a retract height the bodies reach up to, ramp and helix entries on the finishing kinds, nothing to cut (“The raster finishing has nothing to cut within its boundary.”).

Code: core/cam/src/ops/ (surface, zlevel, raster, waterline, roughing), core/model/src/document/cam.rs (cam_surface). Tests: their own, core/model-tests/cam (three_axis_operations_machine_the_bodies_surfaces).

A parameter’s range tried on a copy

The parameter_range query (mitcad#1730) evaluates the design at values of one parameter, by default its min and its max (Parameter limits), without changing the document: each value is set with set_parameter on a copy of the document that recomputes from its cached results, and the answer compares the design there with the design at the current value. The document, its undo history, its results and its revision stay as they were. One parameter at a time.

QueryFieldsResult
parameter_rangeparameter (name); optional values (1 to 50 numbers in mm, radians or plain numbers, as set_parameter’s value) or steps (2 to 50 values evenly from its min to its max, both included; 2 when neither is given), time_limit_s (1 to 600 seconds for all values together, default 30)parameter; current (value, text, body_count, bodies, failed_features, feature_warnings); values, one per value: value, text, then changed, body_count, body_count_change, bodies (uid, name, volume, bbox {min, max}, and volume_change and bbox_change {min, max} against the same body now, or new; changed), removed_bodies (uid, name), failed_features (feature, name, error, new when it does not fail now), new_warnings (feature, name, warning as the feature gives it, message as a person reads it), applied, applied_text and limited when the limits held the parameter at another value; or error when set_parameter refused the value; or timed_out; timing_ms each; timed_out, timing_ms and time_limit_s of the whole query; changes nothing
{"query": "parameter_range", "parameter": "HoleOffset", "steps": 3}
  • A value is set as set_parameter’s value sets it: limits that are not strict hold it at the min, the max or the step (applied, limited), a strict limit refuses it (error), and the configurations’ rules follow it.
  • changed is true when the body count differs, a body is new or gone, a volume differs by more than a millionth of it, a box corner moves more than 0.000 001 mm, a feature fails or stops failing, or a feature warns of something it does not warn of now (a region found as two regions after a sketch change, region r{…} found as r{…} + r{…} after a change in Sketch1). Bodies are those at the timeline marker, in their component’s coordinates, as the bodies query gives them; without measurements from the geometry kernel a body has no volume.
  • The time limit covers all values: a value whose recompute is still running when it passes is stopped and, with the values after it, has timed_out instead of a result; what was evaluated before is kept in the answer. A cancel of the document’s running job rejects the query.
  • A text parameter, an unknown name, a parameter without the min or the max (when no values are given), values and steps together, and a time limit out of its range refuse the query.

Code: core/model-api/src/parameter_range.rs (with Document::fork). Tests: core/model-tests/api/src/parameter_range_tests.rs and the module’s own tests (the time limit).

Linked designs from outside the project (mitcad#1719)

A link is followed only to a file in the design’s project (mitcad#929, External components). So that a link made to a file elsewhere does not silently stop following it (GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#251), the application asks link_check before Insert Component links a file and, for a file outside, offers to copy it into the project and link the copy (insert_component with copy_into_project), to insert it as a copy, or to cancel (app/COMMANDS.md, “Linked designs”). Save Component as Design asks it too before it replaces a component with a link to the new file, and offers to save that file into the folder instead (mitcad#1739).

QueryFieldsResult
link_checkpath (absolute, or relative to base), base (the design file’s folder; left out: a design not saved, which follows no link)file (absolute), followed (a link to it would be followed when the design opens again), folder (where copy_into_project puts copies: parts/ of the project, or of the design’s folder without a project; null without base); reads nothing but the file system’s folders
  • copy_into_project. With link (the default) and a path whose link would not be followed from base, insert_component first copies the file into the folder above (made when missing). A name taken there gets a suffix (plate_2.mitcad, then _3, …); nothing is written over. The designs the file links whose files are outside the project are copied there too, and so on (a design linked twice, or a loop of links, is copied once); in the copies, links to the copies name them, and links to files in the project name those files from the copies’ folder, so every one of them is followed. A copy is a single file (version 2): B-rep data the file refers to in its own project’s store goes inside; a file whose data cannot be read is refused, and so is one with fields a newer MitCad wrote. The originals are not changed. The copy is then inserted linked, its path recorded from base (../parts/plate_2.mitcad), and the component is named after the file asked for (plate, plate (1) when taken, unless name says otherwise). copied lists the files copied, the one asked for first: from, to (absolute). A file the link follows, or "link": false, is inserted as it is (copied empty). Without base it is refused: “the design is not saved yet, so there is no project to copy the file into; save the design first”.
  • Messages. A link that is not followed says so in words, with the way out and the component’s name only, no path: the update_links and update_link line and the links query’s problem above.

Code: core/model/src/document/link_copies.rs (check_link, copy_link_into_project), crate::file::relinked_text, NotFollowed (core/model/src/document/components.rs), the API in core/model-api/src/components.rs. Tests: core/model-tests/assembly/src/link_copy_tests.rs, and the UI test tools/ui-link-outside-test.sh.

The work steps of a sketch

A sketch records which use of a tool made which of its points, curves, constraints, dimensions and texts (mitcad#1750): sketch mode lists these work steps in the timeline’s place, one cell per step (app/COMMANDS.md, “The sketch’s work steps in the timeline’s place”).

  • Recording. Every sketch.* command whose edit makes items records them as one step: its id (s<n>, one more than the largest in the sketch), its kind (the command’s name without sketch.: rectangle, add_line, project, fillet, add_constraint, add_dimension, add_text, paste, import_svg, …; intersect for a sketch.project with section) and the ids of the items, texts (t<n>) among them. The command’s answer names it: "step": "s3". A command that makes nothing (a drag, a new value) records none. sketch.explode_text’s new curves and points are a step explode_text (mitcad#2163).
  • Changed items. Items a later command changes stay with the step that made them. A sketch.trim or sketch.extend is a step of its own all the same, also when it only shortens or lengthens its curve: the step names that curve as changed (and holds what it made, a piece or a constraint, as its own). A changed curve deleted later leaves the step that changed it too.
  • One go. merge_undo makes the steps recorded after its depth one step per sketch, as it makes their undo steps one: what sketch mode’s tools and command panels run as several commands (a projected edge chain, a line and the constraints its snaps add, an axis or a body edge made for a pick, a trim dragged across several curves) is one step. It keeps the first one’s id; its kind is the first that is not project, axis or add_point (what a tool makes for its inputs), else the first one’s.
  • Deletes, undo and redo. Deleted items leave their step, and a step left with none goes. The steps are part of the sketch’s definition, so undo and redo bring them back with the items.
  • Not geometry. Two definitions that differ only in their steps are equal, and the steps are no part of the definition’s fingerprint: a merge of steps evaluates nothing again.
  • Without steps. A design saved before the steps were recorded, an import (.f3d, FreeCAD, .ipt, …), and a sketch added whole with add_feature, have none; an .svg or .dxf inserted with sketch.import_svg or sketch.import_dxf is one step. The sketch query lists each point, curve, constraint and dimension no step holds as a step of its own, without id and kind (a text no step holds is not listed). Nothing is migrated: such a sketch’s later edits record their own steps beside its items.
  • Stored. The sketch’s definition has them as steps: [{"id": 2, "kind": "rectangle", "entities": ["c1", "p5", …], "constraints": ["k1", …]}] (constraints holds its constraints and dimensions; texts its texts; changed the points and curves it changed that are another step’s); left out when there are none.

The sketch query’s steps lists them in the order they were made: each recorded step where its first item comes in the order, after every recorded step made before it (a step that made no point, curve, constraint or dimension, a text’s or a trim that only shortened a curve, comes before the next recorded step, or last), each item no step holds where it comes. Each has its items (made or changed) in that order, then its texts; a step that changed curves also changed:

"steps": [
  {"id": "s1", "kind": "project", "items": ["p1", "p2", "c3", "p4", "c5"]},
  {"id": "s2", "kind": "rectangle", "items": ["c6", "p10", "p11", "k1", "…"]},
  {"id": "s3", "kind": "trim", "items": ["c3"], "changed": ["c3"]},
  {"id": "s4", "kind": "add_text", "items": ["t20"]},
  {"items": ["p21"]}
]

Code: core/sketch/src/steps.rs (record, merge_new, in_order), Document::edit_sketch and Document::merge_undo (core/model/src/document.rs), the kind and the changed curve from the command in core/model-api/src/dispatch.rs (sketch::step_kind, sketch::step_changes). Tests: core/sketch/src/steps.rs and core/model-tests/sketch/src/sketch_steps_1750_tests.rs, and the UI test tools/ui-sketch-item-list-test.sh.

The eyes of a component’s folders (mitcad#1771)

CommandFieldsResult
set_folder_visiblecomponent (an id such as C1 or a component’s name; left out: the root, C0), folder (bodies, sketches, construction, or the root’s annotations, mitcad#2041), visibleundo step Hide Sketches / Show Bodies / Hide Construction / Hide Annotations unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed; a component that is not there is refused, and annotations of another component than the root (only the root has an Annotations folder)
  • The eye of each component’s Bodies, Sketches and Construction folder in the Browser (GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#292): display state as View › Show’s (View › Show of the whole design, document/display.rs), kept in the design file as "display": {"folders": {"C0": {"sketches": true}}} (the folders hidden, by component; a component with none hidden left out, the whole object while every folder is shown), per user in a project, an undo step that the project’s versions leave out. A design saved before it opens with every folder shown. The application allows it in read-only documents.
  • A hidden folder leaves everything in it out of the view: bodies the component’s bodies (the instances query and what reads it, as an occurrence’s light bulb does; the command previews too), sketches its sketches (planar and 3D), construction its construction planes, axes, points and Intersection Curves. The component’s folder is one for all its occurrences. No item’s own light bulb (set_feature_visible, set_body_visible) and no body’s Show When condition changes, and they can still be changed while the folder is hidden: showing the folder again shows what they show.
  • annotations (mitcad#2041): the root’s Annotations folder in the Browser, which holds all the design’s annotations (the annotations query’s). Hidden, the application draws none of them in the view and none can be picked there; each one’s own light bulb (set_measurement_visible, edit_annotation’s visible) stays as it is and can still be changed, and the annotations query lists them with their own visible as before. A drawing brings in the annotations by their own light bulbs (drawing_model_items), as a hidden Bodies folder leaves a drawing’s bodies as they are. Kept in the file as "display": {"folders": {"C0": {"annotations": true}}}.
  • The document query’s display has "folders": {"C0": {"bodies": bool, "sketches": bool, "construction": bool, "annotations": bool}} (true: shown; annotations only in the root’s) for each component with a hidden folder (left out while every folder is shown).

Tests: core.model.api (folder_eye_tests.rs: two of five sketches and two of five bodies hidden by their own light bulbs stay so after their folder is hidden, shown, saved and opened; the undo steps and their labels; a light bulb changed under a hidden folder; Show When under it; each component’s own folders; the Annotations folder: one of three annotations hidden by its own light bulb stays so after the folder is hidden, shown, saved and opened, the undo steps Hide Annotations / Show Annotations, another component’s refused), the UI tests tools/ui-folder-eyes-test.sh and tools/ui-annotations-folder-eye-test.sh (also on Windows and macOS).

Show Dimensions of a sketch (mitcad#1772)

CommandFieldsResult
set_sketch_dimensions_shownsketch (a planar sketch, F3), shownundo step Show Dimensions of Sketch1 / Hide Dimensions of Sketch1 unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed; a feature that is not there, or one that is not a planar sketch (a 3D sketch, a plane), is refused
  • The sketch row’s Show Dimensions (GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#306): the application draws the sketch’s dimensions in the view while the sketch is shown and not edited. Display state as View › Show’s (document/display.rs): the sketch’s definition and light bulb stay as they are. Kept in the design file as "display": {"sketch_dimensions": ["F1", "F4"]} (left out while none has it), per user in a project, an undo step that the project’s versions leave out. Coordinate System (mitcad#1775)

The feature. coordinate_system is construction geometry: a frame with its origin at a point and its axes along edges, axes or faces, for sketches, joints, Align and exports (GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#280). It is named CoordinateSystem1, CoordinateSystem2, …

{"type": "coordinate_system",
 "origin": {"body": "F2.b0", "vertex": "V{F2:end(r{…})|F2:side(c1[c4,c2])|F2:side(c2[c1,c3])}"},
 "z_axis": {"body": "F2.b0", "edge": "E{F2:end(r{…})|F2:side(c1[c4,c2])}"},
 "x_axis": {"body": "F2.b0", "edge": "E{F2:side(c1[c4,c2])|F2:side(c2[c1,c3])}"},
 "flip_z": false, "flip_x": false, "offset": "0 mm", "angle": "0 deg"}
FieldTakesDefault
origina point (geometric references): a vertex, a construction point, the origin point, a sketch point, a circular edge (its center) or a straight one (its middle)required
z_axisa direction: an edge (straight, or a circle’s axis), an origin or construction axis, a sketch line, a plane’s normal (an origin or construction plane, a planar face, another coordinate system: its Z), a cylinder’s, cone’s or torus’s axisthe component’s Z
x_axisa direction as z_axis, turned square to Z (projected onto the plane normal to it)the component’s X so turned (its Y when X is along Z)
flip_z, flip_xturn that axis round; Y follows (the frame stays right-handed)false
offsetalong Z, mm (a value or expression)0
angleabout Z (turns X and Y), after the flips0
  • Directions. A straight edge points away from the origin: from its end nearer the origin to the other one, so that edges picked at a corner run into the body. Any other reference keeps its own direction (a face’s outward normal, an axis’s direction, a circle’s axis).
  • Its datum is a plane with the frame (as a joint origin’s): the datum and datums queries give type plane, origin, x_axis, y_axis and normal (Z). So everything that takes a plane with its frame takes it: a sketch on it (sketch.create with "plane": "F5": the sketch’s x and y along the frame’s X and Y), a joint’s or joint origin’s geometry (the frame itself), Align’s plane, and another coordinate system’s z_axis (its Z).
  • It follows its references through the timeline (topological names as elsewhere): an edit or a parameter that moves the corner or turns the edges moves the frame. The references are geometry of the feature’s own component, in its coordinates.
  • It makes no body; it has a light bulb as construction geometry has (set_feature_visible; View › Show’s construction hides it with the rest), and its datum is not kept in the result store.
  • Refusals: a point, a vertex or a body for an axis (origin is a point, which gives no direction for an axis; … is not an axis, an edge or a face with an axis); something not a point for the origin; the same reference for both axes (… is selected twice). Evaluation fails for an X axis along Z (the X axis is along the Z axis: pick an X axis across it) and for a face neither planar nor round about an axis.

Exports in a frame. export’s coordinates takes {"frame": <coordinate system>} (its uid or name, Feature names are not unique): the bodies are written where the design shows them, taken into the frame: a point at the frame’s origin is written at (0, 0, 0), one along its X at (d, 0, 0).

{"cmd": "export", "path": "for-cam.step", "coordinates": {"frame": "CoordinateSystem1"}}
  • STEP, IGES, BRep and OBJ: each placement the kernel writes (ExportBody::placements, Coordinates and placements of exports) is the design’s placement followed by the move into the frame, so a body of the root is a placed instance of its part in a STEP file, as a moved component’s body is; the geometry itself is not changed. STL and 3MF place their meshes the same way.
  • A coordinate system of a component is taken where the component’s first occurrence places it (where the view shows it).
  • Refused: a feature that is no coordinate system (Sketch1 is not a coordinate system), a name no feature has (there is no coordinate system Nowhere), one without a frame at the marker (rolled back, suppressed or failed: CoordinateSystem1 has no frame at the timeline marker), a USDZ file (a USDZ file keeps the design's coordinates), and the bodies on the print bed (on_bed, plates, plan: bodies are put on the print bed from the design's coordinates, not in a coordinate system).
  • mitcad-cli export … --coordinates <coordinate system> sends it.

Tests: core.model.features-solid (coordinate_system_tests.rs: the frame at a corner with its axes along edges, flips, offset and angle, a face’s and an origin plane’s normal, the component’s axes, following a parameter, a sketch on it, the refusals; STL, STEP, IGES, OBJ and BRep exports in it with the mock kernel), cli.export_coordinate_system (tools/cli/tests/coordinate_system.json: the block written to STEP, IGES and STL in a frame at its corner and read back with the corner at the origin and its edges along X and Z within 1e-6 mm), the UI test tools/ui-coordinate-system-test.sh.

Curve tools: Helix Curve, Intersection Curve of faces and bodies, Surface Helix (mitcad#1777)

Helical paths for a later Sweep or Pipe (GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#305): a helix curve of its own, the curve where faces and bodies meet, and a helix of open sketch curves into a helical surface.

Helix Curve. helix_curve makes a helical 3D curve about an axis:

{"type": "helix_curve", "axis": {"body": "F1.b0", "face": "F1:side0"},
 "pitch": 5, "revolutions": 4}
  • axis: an origin or construction axis, a straight or circular edge, a sketch line (a circle’s or an arc’s axis), a cylindrical or conical face (its axis) or a fixed axis. On a cylindrical or conical face the curve starts where the face starts along the way it rises (its boundary’s lowest point that way); about another axis it starts at the axis' origin (a construction axis’s origin, an edge’s start).
  • radius (optional): the distance from the axis where it starts. Left out, the picked face’s: a cylinder’s radius, so that the curve lies on the face; a cone’s radius where the curve starts, and the curve then widens or narrows with the cone (its growth per turn the pitch times the tangent of the cone’s half angle), lying on it too. Without a face it is needed.
  • pitch, revolutions: the rise per turn and the turns (need not be whole); both greater than zero. A height goes in as their ratio, as Helix’s does (app/COMMANDS.md, “Helix”).
  • left_handed, flip (optional): turning left-handed about the way it rises; rising against the axis direction.
  • start_angle (optional, an angle): where it starts round the axis, right-handed about the way it rises, from the model X axis seen along the axis (Y where the axis lies along X).
  • growth (optional, a length): how far it moves out per turn (negative: in), a conical helix; it replaces a cone’s own growth. A curve that would reach the axis before its last turn is refused (the helix curve narrows to its axis before its last turn).

A helix that keeps its radius is exact (one Curve3::Helix piece, F5:curve1); a growing one comes from the geometry kernel (Kernel::helix_curve, geometry/src/intersection_curve.cpp: a line on the cone its turns lie on, made 3D within 1e-7 mm), its pieces F5:curve1, F5:curve2, … in order. Everything the curve of an Intersection Curve does, the helix curve does: it is a path as {"feature": "F5"} (Sweep, Pipe, Loft’s rails and centre line, Pattern on Path, construction along a path), Project and Intersect take it, the feature_curves query lists it and the view draws it in the Construction folder with a light bulb, and the preview’s report carries its curve. A rib or a web refuses it, as it lies in no one plane. Refusals: a face neither cylindrical nor conical without a radius, an axis without a face and without a radius.

Intersection Curve of faces and bodies. first and second of an intersection_curve may each be faces, surface bodies or solid bodies instead of sketch curves, {"geometry": [...]}, a list of {"body", "face"} and {"body"} references:

{"type": "intersection_curve", "first": {"geometry": [{"body": "F5.b0"}]},
 "second": {"geometry": [{"body": "F6.b0", "face": "F6:side0"}]}}

The two sides meet as they are: the geometry kernel’s section of them (Kernel::shape_section, OCCT’s section of the shapes, approximated), joined into one curve as the sketches’ crossing is, from its end nearer to the component’s origin. A whole body picked takes all its faces. Both sides are sketch curves or both faces and bodies (one input is sketch curves and the other faces or bodies); faces and bodies that do not meet are refused (the faces or bodies do not meet), as is a result that branches or comes in stretches apart. Rib and Web grow from such a curve when it lies in one plane, without a sketch normal to orient the plane by.

Surface Helix. A helix with surface set makes surface bodies, as a surface revolution does (surface sweeps): the profiles’ walls without their caps, and curves (sketch curves of one sketch, open chains or closed loops, {"sketch", "curves", "chain"}) moved by the helix’s screw motion, each a new surface body:

{"type": "helix", "curves": {"sketch": "F4", "curves": ["c1"]}, "surface": true,
 "axis": "z", "pitch": 5, "revolutions": 4, "operation": "new_body"}

A line from the axis gives a helicoid. Its faces are F5:side(c1) (Kernel::helix_sheet, geometry/src/surface_sweeps.cpp: a pipe shell of each chain along a helix with the axis as its fixed binormal, within 1e-6 mm). A surface helix is always a new body, built by MitCad’s construction ("construction": "freecad" or a piece_shift is refused: a surface helix is built by MitCad's construction). A solid helix takes no curves.

A surface helix takes what a solid one takes besides (mitcad#1797): a height as a ratio ("revolutions": "20 mm / 5 mm" or "pitch": "20 mm / 4"), a growth (a conical helicoid: the curves move out by the growth per turn along the direction from the axis towards their middle) and flat ends (start, end, as above: the curves turn without rising over the flat parts, so a line’s helicoid ends in planar pieces). With a growth or ends the curves are moved by the solid helix’s motion (MitCad’s growing screw, its rise law with ends: detail::screwed_wire in geometry/src/path_sweep.cpp) in one sweep without caps:

{"type": "helix", "curves": {"sketch": "F4", "curves": ["c1"]}, "surface": true,
 "axis": "z", "pitch": 5, "revolutions": 4, "growth": "1 mm",
 "start": {"transition_angle": "90 deg", "flat_angle": "90 deg"},
 "operation": "new_body"}

A narrowing that would take the curves to the axis fails, as a solid helix’s does; a curve that starts on the axis has no room to narrow.

Tests: core/model/src/features/helix_curve.rs, core/model-tests/features-profile/src/curve_tools_tests.rs (the mock kernel: a helix curve on a 20 mm cylindrical face, pitch 5 and 4 turns, on the face within 1e-6 mm and driving a Pipe, left-handed; about an axis with a radius, a start angle and flipped; following a cone; the refusals; a helix of a line a surface body; its heights, growth and flat ends reaching the kernel and kept, mitcad#1797; an intersection curve of that surface and a body one helix, a face taken by its name, saved and read back, and the refusals), geometry/tests/test_curve_tools.cpp (geometry.curve_tools: a growing helix on its cone, a line’s helix the helicoid of its area, the helicoid and a cylinder meeting in one helix on the cylinder, a missing face refused; a growing helicoid’s outer edge on its cone within 1e-6 mm, a helicoid with flat ends planar at both ends), tools/cli/tests/curve_tools.json (cli.curve_tools: pipes along a helix curve, along the intersection of the helicoid and a cylinder and along a growing helix, by their volumes; the helicoid’s area), the UI test tools/ui-curve-tools-test.sh.

Form: subdivision surfaces from a control cage: form and form.* (mitcad#1757)

A Form is a body whose surface is the Catmull-Clark limit surface of an editable control cage, made an exact B-rep: a solid when the cage is closed, a surface body when it is open. The cage is the feature’s stored data; the form.* commands edit it, each one undo step, and the features after the Form recompute. Fillets, holes, booleans and exports work on the result as on any body. The model side is core/subdiv (the cage, its edits, the subdivision and the patches, no OCCT), core/model/src/features/form.rs (the feature) and core/model/src/document/forms.rs (one edit, one step); docs/architecture.md, “Forms”, says how the limit surface becomes faces.

The definition (add_feature, edit_feature, the design file):

{"type": "form", "operation": "new_body",
 "cage": {"vertices": [{"id": 1, "at": [-10, -10, -10]}, {"id": 2, "at": [-10, 10, -10]}],
          "faces": [{"id": 1, "vertices": [1, 2, 3, 4]}],
          "creases": [{"edge": [1, 2]}, {"edge": [2, 3], "sharpness": 2}],
          "corners": [5],
          "symmetry": {"origin": [0, 0, 0], "normal": [1, 0, 0]}}}
  • vertices: each with an id (from 1, each once) and its position at in millimetres in the component’s coordinates.
  • faces: each with an id and its vertices in order, counter-clockwise seen from outside; three or more, each once. Every edge (two vertices that follow each other in a face) is in one face or two, which run along it opposite ways; every vertex is in a face.
  • creases: an edge by its two vertices, sharp for good without a sharpness, or sharp for that many subdivision steps (a fraction blends the last), which rounds it a little; corners: vertices that stay where they are.
  • symmetry (optional): the cage stores the half on the side normal points to, its cut on the plane (vertices within 1e-6 mm of it); the other half is its mirror image. In the commands and queries the mirrored vertices and faces have the negative ids of those they mirror; a vertex on the plane is its own image.
  • next_vertex, next_face (in the cage, written once an edit gave or took out an id): the ids the next new vertex and face get at least, so that an id that went is never given again and a later feature’s reference to a face that is gone finds no new one. form.set_cage keeps the earlier cage’s.
  • operation: new_body (the default, then left out of the file), join, cut, intersect or new_component, with participants as a primitive’s; an open cage makes a surface body and is a new body only.

The cage is checked when the definition is taken; what is wrong is said in words (a face of the cage has fewer than three corners, two faces of the cage run the same way along an edge: ..., a vertex of the cage lies on the mirrored side of the symmetry plane, …).

Faces. The cage is subdivided once, so that a cage face of n corners gives n quads; each quad is one face of the body, named <feature>:cage(<face id>)#<corner> (F7:cage(3)#2), on the mirrored half <feature>:mirror(<face id>)#<corner>. A reference without the corner (F7:cage(3)) finds all of a cage face’s faces. The names stay while the cage is edited: a face keeps its id through moves and extrusions, and one half of a face an edge loop splits keeps it (the other half gets a new id). Regular quads (four quads round each corner, no crease or corner there) are bicubic patches that are the limit surface exactly; the others interpolate exact limit points, and every two faces meet without a gap.

CommandFieldsResult
form.createprimitive (one of: {"type": "box", "size": [x, y, z], "segments": [nx, ny, nz]} (default 1 each), {"type": "cylinder", "diameter", "height", "segments" (round, default 8), "rows" (default 1)} about z with a cap at each end, {"type": "sphere", "diameter", "segments"} (a box cage of that many a side on the sphere, default 2), {"type": "plane", "size": [x, y], "segments": [nx, ny]} (facing +z: a surface body), {"type": "face", "body", "face", "thickness"} (a planar face’s outline: one face, a surface body; with thickness, a slab standing on the face), {"type": "cage", "cage"} (a cage as the definition has it)); center [x, y, z] (default the origin; a face’s outline stays where it is); symmetry (optional: "x", "y" or "z", the plane through center square to that axis, the primitive’s segments along it made even (a cylinder’s round ones a multiple of four) so that vertices lie on it; or {"origin", "normal"}); operation (default new_body), participants, nameuid, name (Form1), vertices, faces (the stored half’s counts), closed, error when the Form failed
form.moveform, vertices, edges ([a, b]), faces (ids in the whole cage), by [x, y, z], previewmoved: the stored vertices that moved; undo step Move in Form1
form.rotateform, vertices, edges, faces, axis [x, y, z] (its direction), origin (default: the selection’s centre), angle (radians, right-handed), previewmoved
form.scaleform, vertices, edges, faces, factor (every axis) or factors [x, y, z] (not zero), center (default: the selection’s centre), previewmoved
form.set_positionsform, positions [{vertex, at [x, y, z]}] (a drag: where each vertex goes, in the whole cage), previewundo step Drag in Form1
form.extrudeform, faces, distance (along the faces’ normals, each vertex along the mean of its faces’; negative: inwards), previewvertices, faces (the side faces on the edges round the selection); the faces moved keep their ids
form.insert_loopform, edge [a, b], at (0 to 1 from a, default 0.5), previewvertices, faces (the halves of the quads it split that got new ids), edges (the new edges across them); the loop runs across the quads on either side of the edge, from each to the one beyond its opposite edge, until it closes, meets the cage’s boundary or a face that is not a quad (which takes the new vertex)
form.delete_loopform, edge [a, b], previewremoved_vertices, removed_faces: the edge loop through the edge (on along the edge across at each vertex of four quads) goes, the faces either side of it become one and its vertices between two edges go
form.delete_facesform, faces, previewremoved_faces, removed_vertices (those no face uses any more); the cage opens there
form.fill_hole (mitcad#1941)form, edge [a, b] (an edge of the opening: boundary in form_cage), quads (default false), previewfaces, vertices (the new ones), closed (whether the whole cage is closed now); undo step Fill Hole in Form1. The opening the edge lies on (the loop of boundary edges through it) is filled with one face, or with quads and an even number n of edges round it with a grid of a x b quads (a + b = n / 2, a = n / 4 rounded down; the corners where the opening turns most; the inner vertices on the Coons patch of its sides), as edge loops across one face would leave; an odd number of edges takes one face. The new faces run as the faces round the opening do. On a symmetric cage the mirrored opening is filled too; an opening across the symmetry plane (a face beside the plane taken out) is refused (the opening crosses the symmetry plane: take the symmetry away to fill it), as is an edge with a face on both sides (a picked edge is not on an opening of the cage: ...) and an opening that meets another at a vertex
form.bridge (mitcad#1941)form, edges ([a, b]: boundary edges of both sides), loops (default false: each edge stands for the whole opening it lies on, one edge a side is enough), segments (rows of quads across, 1 to 100, default 1), previewfaces, vertices (the new ones), closed; undo step Bridge in Form1. The picked edges make two runs along the boundary (two openings, or two runs of open edges, of as many edges each), joined with a strip of quads: the second side runs the other way along the strip, so that its faces run as the faces beside both sides; two openings are turned to where the joins are shortest; the rows between are straight between the joined vertices. On a symmetric cage the mirror image is bridged too, unless the bridge joins a side with its own mirror image. Refused in words: an edge not on an opening, more or fewer than two runs (a bridge joins two openings or two runs of open edges: the picked edges make 3 apart), sides of different lengths or an opening with a run
form.creaseform, edges, vertices (made corners), sharpness (left out or null: sharp for good; a number: that many steps; 0: smooth again, and the vertices no longer corners), previewundo step Crease in Form1
form.symmetryform, plane (null: none, the mirrored half becomes the cage’s own; "x", "y", "z" through center, default the middle of the cage’s box; or {"origin", "normal"}: the half on the side the normal points to is kept, the other becomes its mirror image), center, previewrefused when a face crosses the plane (a face of the cage crosses the symmetry plane: insert an edge loop on the plane first)
form.set_cageform, cage (as the definition has it), previewthe cage replaced whole (an editor’s own edit, an import), undo step Edit Cage in Form1

Every edit but form.create names its Form ("form": "F3") and the vertices, edges and faces by their ids in the whole cage. On a symmetric cage an edit keeps the halves equal: a mirrored vertex moves its stored one by the mirror image of the motion, a vertex on the plane moves along the plane only, and extrusions and edge loops are made on the whole cage with their mirror images and the stored half cut from the result. An edit is one undo step (Extrude in Form1, Insert Edge Loop in Form1, …); one that is refused (an id the cage does not have, a cage the edit would leave invalid) or whose Form would then fail to evaluate leaves the document as it was. With preview nothing changes: the answer has preview, the edited cage (as form_cage gives it) and its limit mesh (as form_limit gives it, 3 steps), for an editor’s drag.

QueryFieldsResult
form_cageuiduid, name, vertices [{id, at, mirror, corner}], edges [{vertices [a, b], boundary, creased, sharpness (a semi-sharp crease’s)}], faces [{id, vertices, center, normal, mirror, name: the reference that finds its faces on the body, F3:cage(2)}], closed, symmetry, stored: the cage as the definition has it. The whole cage, mirrored half and all: what an editor draws and picks
form_limituid (a Form) or cage (a cage as the definition has it), levels (1 to 5, default 3)a triangle mesh of the limit surface without the kernel: positions and normals (flat x, y, z), triangles (flat, three indices each, counter-clockwise seen from outside), faces (each triangle’s cage face id), closed

Tests: core/subdiv (core.subdiv: limit points on a regular grid, a crease’s and a boundary’s curves, the patches of a box cage, a creased box and a pentagonal prism without gaps, regular patches exact, the edits, symmetry, the primitives), core/model/src/features/form.rs (the mock kernel: a box cage’s body and its face names, refusals), core/model-tests/api/src/form_tests.rs (the commands and queries on the mock kernel: edits, symmetry keeping both halves equal, a crease kept, previews, undo and redo, saved and read back; mitcad#1941: a box’s top deleted and filled with one face or with quads, two tubes’ open ends bridged, a symmetric Form filling both openings), geometry/tests/test_form.cpp (geometry.form: patches sewn into a valid solid, rounded and cut, written as STEP, an open set a sheet, a gap refused) and tools/cli/tests/form.json (cli.form: a box cage edited into a smooth solid, a fillet and a hole on it, a creased edge, exported to STEP).

The design packed for a report (mitcad#1795)

Help › Send Feedback’s Include the design (GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#328, app/COMMANDS.md, “Feedback and error reports”) writes the open design and the files it refers to into one zip, which opens as a project again.

QueryFieldsResult
design_packagefile (the open design’s file, absolute; left out for a design never saved), zip (where the zip goes, absolute; made or written over, whole or not at all, its folder made when missing), extra (files added: name in the zip, relative with /, and text or path, one of them)zip (absolute), size (bytes), design (the open design’s name in the zip), files (every name in the zip, in the order written), missing (files the design refers to that are not there or cannot be read, by their names in the project), left_out (files it refers to that are not taken: outside the project, or not an image, by their file names)
  • What goes in. The open design as it is now, saved or not, as a single file (version 2, its B-rep data inside), at its path in its project (in no project: in its folder; never saved: design.mitcad). Then the designs it links that are followed (mitcad#929), and the designs those link, each read from its file and kept as it is; the B-rep files those refer to in their project’s store (.mitcad/brep/<aa>/<sha256>.brep.zlib); the image files (PNG, JPEG) of the appearances’ textures that are not embedded; the project’s marker .mitcad/project.json; then extra. Every file of the project is at its path in the project, so the zip unpacked is the project’s subset that opens the design.
  • What stays out. A link the design does not follow brings nothing in (its component keeps the bodies saved with the design); a texture file outside the project, or not an image, is left out (left_out); so is a file whose real path leaves the project (a symbolic link): a design file never chooses which other files of the computer a report carries. The project’s other designs, its per-user state (.mitcad/local/) and its caches never go in. Library parts come with the design (as BUILD saves them, mitcad#375).
  • Refused: an extra name that is not relative (/a, .., \, :) or that a file of the design already has, and an extra with neither or both of text and path. Files that are already compressed (B-rep data, PNG, JPEG) are stored, the rest deflated; the zip has no ZIP64 (below 4 GiB).
  • Its class is file IO: external clients (MCP) cannot ask it.

Code: core/model/src/document/design_package.rs (Document::write_design_package), the API in core/model-api/src/design_package.rs. Tests: core.model.files (design_package_tests.rs), the UI test tools/ui-feedback-design-test.sh.

Folders of the Bodies folder (mitcad#1802)

A body can be listed in a folder of its component’s Bodies folder in the browser: organisation only, like its name, kept with the body in the design file ("folder": "Glass" on the body’s entry) and restored by undo. The .f3d import puts the file’s bodies into the folders the file keeps them in, and names them as the file does.

CommandFieldsEffect
set_body_folderuid (body), folder (a name; null or left out: the Bodies folder itself)undo step Move Body1 to Glass / Take Body1 out of its Folder unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed; the body must exist at the marker; an empty name is refused
  • A folder is a name: the bodies of a component with the same folder share it, and a folder no body names any more is gone. Folders do not nest.
  • The bodies query lists "folder" for a body in one (left out otherwise).
  • Document::name_bodies names bodies and sets their folders in one undo step (Name Bodies, nothing recomputed), as the import does; a name another body of its component has, or one given twice in a component, gets (2), (3), ….
  • Body names are unique within a component (rename_body refuses a name another body of the same component has); bodies of different components may share one, as an imported design’s do. A command that takes a body by name finds the first body of that name at the marker; give the uid where names repeat.
  • The application’s browser lists a component’s folders under its Bodies folder, before the bodies in no folder, each with the bodies in it; a folder’s eye shows whether a body in it is shown and shows or hides them all (their light bulbs, one undo step: Hide Glass; bodies that follow Show When stay as they are).

Code: core/model/src/document/bodies.rs (Document::set_body_folder, Document::name_bodies), the browser’s rows in app/browser/BrowserPanel.cpp (addComponentRows). Tests: core.model (body_folder_tests.rs), core.import.

Convert to Features (mitcad#1815)

A placed library part (a derived_part, e.g. a BUILD timber member or profile) is made of its source evaluated with its configuration row and parameters; its section cannot be edited. convert_derived_part replaces it in its component with the source’s own features, evaluated with the part’s row and values, so that it can be edited like any other part, with the assembly kept as it is. One undo step, Convert to Features.

{"cmd": "convert_derived_part", "component": "C3"}
{"cmd": "convert_derived_part", "feature": "F7", "check": true}
→ {"check": false, "component": "C3", "history": true,
   "features": [{"uid": "F21", "name": "Sketch4"}, {"uid": "F22", "name": "Extrude3"},
                {"uid": "F23", "name": "mount:end_a"}, ...],
   "bodies": {"F7.b0": "F22.b0"}, "rewritten": ["Joint2", "Constraint1", "Sketch5"]}
CommandFieldsResult
convert_derived_partfeature (the derived_part) or component (the part’s component: its derived part); check (default false: with true nothing changes, the answer says what it would make, or the refusal why not)check, component, features (uid, name of each new feature, in timeline order), history (false: the source’s bodies have no history, the part became a plain body), bodies (each body of the part and the body that took its place), rewritten (the features whose references were rewritten, by name)

What it makes, at the part’s place in the timeline:

  • The source’s features copied as Paste New copies them (new uids, default names; the sketches keep their curve ids), evaluated with the part’s row: the section sketch and its extrusion. The part’s parameters stand for the source’s parameters of the same names: the extrusion’s distance is the very parameter the part’s length was (a parameter a bound_length drives keeps driving it). A copied feature’s own parameter whose expression only names one of the part’s own parameters gives its slot to that parameter; the part’s other own parameters go to the first new feature that uses them. The row’s other parameters come along as user parameters, as Paste New brings a design’s.
  • A mitred end (ends) as a construction plane at the end’s angle and tilt (a plane at an angle through the long side’s edge at the end; end B’s moved along its normal by L · cos(angle) so that it follows the length) and a box on it that cuts away what is beyond, as the part’s own cut; the angle stays the part’s parameter. Joinery and rips (cuts) as a box cut each.
  • Every mount:<name> joint origin of the source copied with its name: the component’s own mount frames, at the same places, on the copied features.
  • A source without a section to extrude (no extrusion: an imported part’s base feature, primitives) becomes a plain body of the component (history false): one base feature holding the evaluated bodies, its faces <base>:import(<j>) in the bodies’ face order, and its mount frames as fixed joint origins mount:<name> where they are.

References follow, nothing is made again. Every reference to the part’s geometry in the design is rewritten in place: joints, assembly constraints, rigid groups, motion links, bound lengths, fasteners’ joints, other components’ sketch planes, projections, construction planes and paths, and what the design keeps besides features: annotations, drawings, CAM setups, analyses, image references, print plates, filament changes, comments, the other BUILD parts’ records and faces’ appearances. A bare <F> (a comment on the part) becomes the feature of its first body; an asymmetric fillet’s or chamfer’s edges whose new names sort their faces the other way keep their sides (their set split and flipped, as Paste New does):

The part’sBecomes
<F>:part(<source face>)the copied feature’s face of the same source name
<F>:end_a, <F>:end_bthe square end’s face of the extrusion (its start or end), or the mitre box’s bottom
<F>:cut_a(<F>:<face>), <F>:cut_b(...), <F>:joint_<k>(...)that face of the end’s or the joinery’s box
{"mount": "<F>:mount(<name>)"}the copied joint origin ("F23")
<F>.b<i>the copied features’ i-th body

Joint values, limits, links and the solved placements stay as they were. A bound length may end at a joint origin as it ends at a part’s frame (to: the plane through its origin across its z axis; centre and through measure the bodies of its component). The names of the part’s bodies, their attributes and properties go to the bodies that took their place.

Refused, not half done. The command changes nothing when:

  • a reference names geometry of the part no new feature makes (a frame or face the source does not have): Convert to Features: a joint would lose the part's geometry it is on: the part's features do not make it, the part’s face painted on hover, the feature and the name in the detail;
  • a feature that built would fail, or an occurrence would move (more than 1e-6 mm), in the converted design: the failure’s places, the names in the detail;
  • the part is after the timeline marker or suppressed, its source is not in the design, its values break a rule of its source, or its source places bodies in components of its own.

What is lost. The component no longer follows its library: its BUILD record and its library record go, so library updates and configuration rows no longer change it, and the BUILD tools that need a member (spacing, fitting fasteners by section, Timber Frame membership, build_edit) no longer treat it as one; it is listed with the other parts. What its lists showed is kept as properties of the component in the Library set (source library): Designation, Supplier, Part number, Material, Grade (a member’s), Section (45 x 95 mm) and Length; the parts list reads a stored Designation and Supplier for a component that is no library part. The cut list keeps its row as it was listed (the component’s listed, saved with it: its row for itself, the section’s area and its source’s stock), counted with the part’s quantity, and cuts its stock as before. A source no derived part uses any more goes with the last one.

Code: core/model/src/document/convert_derived.rs (Document::convert_derived_part), the copy in document/copy.rs (copy_component_overriding), the api in core/model-api/src/convert_derived.rs. Tests: core.model.build-timber (convert_tests.rs), the UI test tools/ui-scripts/convert-features.mitcad-ui.

Fill Cavity 

{"type": "fill_cavity", "body": "F1.b0", "cap": "F6"}
{"type": "fill_cavity", "body": "F1.b0", "cap": {"body": "F1.b0", "face": "F1:top"},
 "seed": "F4:side(c6[c5,c4])", "offset": "-2 mm", "flip": true}

Fills a closed pocket or slit of a body with material up to a plane, the cap (mitcad#1818): where walls continue past the level (Replace Face then says the target splits the body), or where a sketch and an extrusion would be fiddly and could poke out of a thin wall. The body keeps its id.

  • cap: an origin or construction plane, a planar face (of this body or another) or a fixed plane (References to geometry). The pocket is filled on the side against the cap’s normal: below a planar face of the body (on its material’s side), below an XY plane; flip fills on the other side.
  • offset (value slot offset): moves the cap along its normal.
  • seed (optional): a face of the body inside the cavity. Only the empty spaces it bounds are filled; without it, every empty space the cap closes.

How it computes, two booleans and no flood (core/model/src/features/fill_cavity.rs, Kernel::cavity_pieces, geometry/src/fill_cavity.cpp):

  1. A box below the cap: the body’s extent in the cap’s frame, grown by 1 mm (or 1 % of the body’s size) on the sides and below, its top on the cap. With a seed, first only the seed’s neighbourhood (the seed face’s extent grown by its own size), so that heavy faces elsewhere, threads, are not cut.
  2. The box less the body: the empty spaces below the cap, one solid each. Their faces tell what they touch: the box’s top (the cap), its sides <feature>:fill_side(k) and bottom <feature>:fill_bottom, and the body’s faces by their names.
  3. With a seed the spaces that touch the seed face; without one every space that touches the cap and no side or bottom of the box (a space that does reaches out of the body: it is not a cavity). A seed’s space that leaves the seed’s neighbourhood is computed again in the whole box, which decides.
  4. The chosen spaces are joined to the body.

The filled top is <feature>:fill(<cap face>) when the cap is a face, <feature>:fill otherwise (pieces #k); the pocket’s walls are inside the body after the join and keep no faces (a wall in the plane of an outer face beside it stays only as another name of that face, as a join merges coplanar faces and keeps their names; so does a filled top in the plane of the body’s top). The preview’s tool is the filled spaces. A change of the body or the cap recomputes it; one undo step as any feature.

Failures, in words (docs/ui-conventions.md, “What a message says”), the body left as it was:

MessageWhenPlaces
the cavity opens out of the body below the capthe seed’s space reaches a side or the bottom of the whole boxthe seed face, and the boxes of the faces where its space left the seed’s neighbourhood (the opening)
the seed face does not bound an empty space below the capno space touches the seed facethe seed face
the seed face lies above the capthe seed face lies wholly on the cap’s other sidethe seed face
found no closed cavity below the cap to fillwithout a seed, every space opens out or misses the capnone
the body lies wholly above the cap: there is nothing below it to fillthe cap lies under the whole bodynone

The names, the cap’s point and normal are in the error’s detail for agents (the MCP results, the log). A mesh body is refused as in the other surface operations.

The application’s command is Fill Cavity in SOLID > MODIFY, beside Replace Face (app/COMMANDS.md).

Tests: core/model-tests/features-solid/src/fill_cavity_tests.rs (mock kernel: the box that reaches the kernel, pockets chosen with and without a seed, the failures, a moved and an offset cap), geometry.fill_cavity (geometry/tests/test_fill_cavity.cpp, OCCT: a blind V slit beside a wall, its 50 mm3 and names), cli.fill_cavity (tools/cli/tests/fill_cavity.json, OCCT: a V slit and a pocket filled up to a construction plane with analytic volumes, seeds, the cap moved and offset, a tunnel open below the cap refused), and the UI tests tools/ui-fill-cavity-test.sh, app.ui-windows-fill-cavity and app.ui-macos-fill-cavity (app/COMMANDS/).

Press Pull continued: press_pull and the face_run query (mitcad#1850)

Press Pull on a face has three ways to continue: Offset (offset_face: the face moves along its normal, its neighbours follow on their own surfaces), Straight and Along the walls, the last two a feature of their own:

{"type": "press_pull", "body": "F2.b0", "faces": ["F2:end(r{c1})"], "continue": "along",
 "distance": 25}
{"type": "press_pull", "body": "F3.b0", "faces": ["F3:top"], "continue": "straight",
 "distance": 10, "taper_type": "scale", "end_scale": 1.1}
{"type": "press_pull", "body": "F3.b0", "faces": ["F3:top"], "continue": "straight",
 "distance": -10, "taper_type": "draft", "taper_angle": "-3 deg"}
FieldValue
body, facesplanar faces of one body (each name every face it finds); each continues on its own
continuestraight (default): the face carried along its own normal, unturned, the new walls running straight from its outline (the face extruded as a profile and joined); along: the end follows the walls’ course and the face turns with them, so that it stays square to the run (below)
distancea value, mm, not zero: the length of the path of the face’s area centre, an arc’s along a turn. Positive out of the material (the new piece joined), negative into it (cut)
taper_typenone (default), draft or scale
taper_angledraft: a value, between -85 and 85 degrees; each wall of the new piece leans by it from its edge on the face, outward positive, as Extrude’s Taper Angle leans it (the outline grows, holes shrink; corners as Extrude’s taper makes them), by t tan(angle) at run length t
end_scalescale: a value, more than 0 (1.1 is 110 %): the face’s whole outline grows or shrinks about its area centre, every point in proportion, linearly with the run’s length to this at the end

Along the walls. The faces beside the face (its walls) decide the run:

  • all of revolution about one axis (tori, cones, cylinders and surfaces of revolution about it, spheres centred on it, planes square to it), as a Revolve or a bent sweep leaves them: the face is revolved about that axis. There is no limit at the walls’ inner radius: the run can go round the whole bend, up to a closed ring (the end meeting the body’s other end, both gone). A turn that would run into the body fails, “the turn runs into the body itself; make it shorter”, the body’s faces it reaches painted; one of a whole turn or more, “the turn comes round to the face itself; make it shorter”;
  • all parallel to one direction not in the face’s plane (planes containing it, cylinders and extrusions along it): the face is carried along that direction, unturned;
  • otherwise: “the walls do not continue as a turn or a straight run; use Offset or Straight”, the walls that stop it painted.

Along a turn a taper grows linearly with the arc length: the end’s section is the face scaled (Scale) or as Extrude’s taper leaves it at the run’s length (Draft), the sections between changing linearly along the arc. On a round tube the two tapers make the same cone; on a profile with corners and slots they differ (Draft narrows a slot as its walls lean, Scale keeps its proportions). A face that is not flat fails (“the face is not flat: Straight and Along the walls take a flat face; use Offset”), as does a draft that closes the face before the end of the run (“the taper closes the face to nothing before the end of the run; make the angle or the distance smaller”) and a scale of 0 or less.

Names. As an extrusion of a face (extrude with a face profile): the new walls <feature>:side(<edge>) by the face’s edge’s name in the body, the piece’s cap on the face <feature>:start(<face>) (gone in the result) and the moved end <feature>:end(<face>), which also keeps the face’s own names, so that what referred to the face finds the moved end. New walls on the surface of the walls they continue are joined with them into one face holding both names. The body is not modified otherwise: the feature changes body and keeps its uid (Kernel::press_pull, geometry/include/mitcad/geometry/press_pull.hpp).

The face_run query tells Press Pull’s panel how a face’s walls continue (its handle runs along the arc for a turn) and whether the face is a feature’s moving end, whose own edit Press Pull offers instead of a new feature (Kernel::face_run):

FieldsResult
body, facecenter (its area center) and normal (out of the material) of the face, reach (mm, how far its outline reaches from the center at its farthest point: Scale’s angle there is atan(reach (end_scale - 1) / distance)), along: {"kind": "straight", "direction"}, {"kind": "turn", "origin", "axis", "radius"} (the right hand turn about axis goes out of the material; radius the centre’s distance from it) or {"kind": "none", "refusal"} (the error a person reads, with its places); feature_end: {"uid", "name", "type", "input"} where the face is the moving end of an extrude (Distance’s end, both ends of Symmetric, Two Sides’ start for distance and end for distance2, the end up to an object), a revolve (angle, angle2 alike) or a sweep (fraction, fraction2), the input its panel moves it by (empty: none of its own); or the free end of a cut-to-length BUILD part (derived_part, input length, name the component’s name, mitcad#2030: not the end it is placed from, none while its length is bound); else null

A face that is not one face of the body, or not planar, is an error.

Tests: geometry.suite.press_pull (OCCT: a bent tube’s end along the bend past the walls’ inner radius, past the bend’s arc and round to a closed ring, square to the run, by Pappus’ volumes; Draft and Scale on a T-slot bar’s end and a round rod’s, straight and along a bend, outward and inward; the refusals), core.model.features-solid (press_pull_tests.rs, mock kernel: fields, edit, undo, names after a parameter change, the face_run query and its feature end), and the UI test tools/ui-scripts/press-pull-continued.mitcad-ui on Linux, Windows and macOS (tools/ui-press-pull-continued-test.sh, app.ui-windows-press-pull-continued, app.ui-macos-press-pull-continued).

Line art of the design: model_render’s SVG (mitcad#1736)

model_render with format: "svg" (an MCP tool, not a command: docs/mcp.md, “Line art as SVG”) answers the camera’s view as black vector lines for figures in manuals, instead of a shaded PNG. The model draws it with Document::render_lines (core/model/src/preview/lines.rs):

  • The bodies, their placements, explode and the camera are the PNG’s (Document::preview_camera), always orthographic: a view without a projection of its own is drawn orthographic, framed as the orthographic PNG of the same arguments; a perspective is refused.
  • The lines are a drawing view’s: the bodies placed where they are drawn, projected along the camera with hidden lines removed (Kernel::project_view, exact edges with the drawings’ quick path): the edges seen and the silhouettes of curved faces; with hidden_edges the hidden ones too. Edges where faces meet tangentially are left out, as a drawing view’s default style leaves them.
  • Each edge is one SVG <path> in the picture’s pixels (size, y down, numbers to three decimals, so the same arguments give the same text): <g id="visible"> black and solid, <g id="hidden"> under it dashed, <g id="highlight"> over everything in the selection blue.
  • colors strokes a body’s lines in its colour and highlight a whole body’s in the selection blue; a highlighted face’s boundary (Kernel::edge_polylines of the face) and a highlighted edge are drawn as lines over everything. An unknown reference is a warning, as in the PNG.
  • section, overlay, print_colors and edges: false are refused: they are the PNG’s.
{"document": "D1", "view": "iso", "format": "svg", "hidden_edges": true}
→ {"format": "svg", "paths": {"visible": 9, "hidden": 3, "highlight": 0},
   "svg": "<?xml …", "camera": {"projection": "orthographic", …}, …}

Tests: core.model.drawing (render_lines_tests.rs, mock kernel: the groups and paths, the frame, colors, highlight, explode, the refusals), geometry.drawing (test_drawing.cpp: a 30 x 20 x 10 box from the iso camera, nine edges seen and three hidden) and cli.mcp (test_model_render_line_art: the same box end to end, nine paths seen and three dashed).

Assembly paths

The assembly_path query (mitcad#1737) checks the way a body goes into place, where interference checks bodies only where they are: the body is slid along a direction or turned about an axis, and the answer gives the first position where it runs into one of the other bodies (a contact deeper than the tolerance), the bodies and faces that meet there, and the clearance along the path. A push-fit peg slid into its hole, a part with a lug tried past a rim, a keyed part turned from its key angle. It runs on the exact shapes and changes nothing.

QueryFieldsResult
assembly_pathbody (the body that moves, as measure takes a body: a uid or name, or {"body", "occurrence"} for an occurrence’s body as that occurrence places it, by ids or names), against (the bodies it moves past, the same way; at least one), and either slide {direction (a vector in the design’s coordinates, or an axis reference whose direction is taken: "z", a construction axis, a straight edge, a cylindrical face), distance (mm; negative: against the direction)} or turn {axis (an axis reference, or {"origin", "direction"} in the design’s coordinates), angle (radians, right-hand rule about the axis; negative: the other way)}; optional steps (1 to 1000 equal steps the path is measured at, default 20), tolerance (mm of motion of the body’s farthest point, 0.000 001 to 1, default 0.001), min_volume (mm³, the smallest overlap that counts, as interference’s; default 1e-6)body and against ({body, name, occurrence}), motion (slide or turn), unit (mm or rad: the unit of every position), length, steps, tolerance, resolution (the tolerance in the path’s unit), hit (null: the body goes all the way; else {step (the first step at or past the contact deeper than the tolerance; 0 when the body overlaps another before it moves), at (the furthest position found clear: how far the body goes, within resolution of the contact; at_deg too for a turn), contact (the first position found overlapping), at_start, bodies ({body, name, occurrence, volume_at_step: mm³ of overlap at that step} the bodies it runs into), faces ({moving_face, face (topological names), body, occurrence, distance, on_moving, on_other} the pairs of faces that meet, measured at at), point (where they meet, design coordinates), faces_error when the kernel could not measure the faces}), min_clearance ({clearance (mm), at, closest (the body nearest there)}: the smallest clearance before the hit, 0 with a hit; null when the body overlaps at the start), path ({at, clearance} at each step from the start up to the hit), touches_at_end (the body meets another within the tolerance of the path’s end: its seat, no hit), certified, probes (positions measured)
{"query": "assembly_path", "body": "Peg", "against": ["Plate"], "slide": {"direction": [0, 0, -1], "distance": 10}, "steps": 10}
{"query": "assembly_path", "body": {"body": "F11.b0", "occurrence": "Shaft:1"}, "against": [{"body": "F8.b0", "occurrence": "Hub:1"}], "turn": {"axis": {"origin": [100, 0, 0], "direction": [0, 0, 1]}, "angle": 0.1}}
  • Bodies where they are placed. Each body is taken where the design places it (an occurrence’s body moved by that occurrence, like measure), and the path is in the design’s coordinates. An axis or a direction given by a reference resolves as references do at the marker (in the coordinates of the component it belongs to); for an occurrence’s own axis give {"origin", "direction"}.
  • How the path is measured. At each step the moving body is moved (Kernel::move_shape; nothing changes the bodies), its clearance to the others is measured (Kernel::measure_between) and, where it touches one, whether it overlaps it (Kernel::interferences; bodies that only touch do not overlap, so a part sliding along a face it rests on goes on). Between two positions the clearance changes at most by how far the body’s farthest point moves (the slide’s distance, or the turn’s angle times the farthest distance of the body’s box from the axis), so a span whose two clearances add up to at least that holds no contact; other spans are halved, at most three times per step. certified is false when a span was still not ruled out: a wall thinner than an eighth of a step could be passed between the positions measured; more steps close it.
  • The contact. Between the last position clear of the others and the first that overlaps, the contact is found by bisection to resolution. It is a hit only when the body still overlaps after moving the tolerance further: a graze shallower than that is passed (the path goes on, and a step inside it has clearance 0), and a contact within the tolerance of the path’s end is the body reaching its seat (touches_at_end), no hit. A body that overlaps another before it moves is a hit at step 0 (at_start).
  • Faces. The pairs of a face of the moving body and a face of a body it hits that are closer than twice the tolerance where the body is last clear, without the pairs that were that close before it moved (a face it rests on) unless no other pair is. Topological names are for agents; nothing here is shown to a person.
  • The minimum clearance is the smallest measured before the hit, refined between the positions beside it by a golden-section search.
  • A path of zero length, a direction or axis without a length, steps, tolerance or min_volume out of range, an empty against, a body in against that is the moving body as placed, slide and turn both or neither, and a face, edge, vertex or datum in place of a body refuse the query. A cancel of the document’s running job rejects it.

Code: core/model/src/assembly_path.rs (the search, the motion) and core/model-api/src/assembly_path.rs (the query on the kernel). Tests: core.model (assembly_path_tests.rs: the search on paths whose clearance is exact: a clear path, a wall hit at its face, a contact at the start, a wall thinner than the halved step, a graze, the seat at the end, a turn), and cli.assembly_path (tools/cli/tests/assembly_path.json, the OCCT kernel: a peg slid through a hole 0.2 mm larger goes all the way with 0.1 mm clearance; a peg with a sideways lug resting on the rim hits it at the first step; a keyed shaft turned in its keyed hole hits the slot’s wall at the angle where the key’s corner reaches it).

Import reports: row statuses and the verdict (mitcad#1893)

Every import command’s result (import_f3d, import_fcstd, import_ipt, import_iam, import_ifc, import_rvt, import_solidcraft, import_dwg, import_3dm) says of each row of its report whether it is fine, and of the whole import in one line (mitcad_import::report_status::annotate, core/import-base):

  • each row (an item of items, the replay’s bodies against the file’s, an .ipt part’s imported and skipped bodies, an assembly’s files, an IFC file’s products, a SolidCraft design’s features and joints, a building project’s import.levels, a drawing’s or a .3dm model’s components) gets row_status (ok, warning, error) and row_status_message, what it means in plain words (“came in fully parametric”, “came in as a fixed body: its history could not be replayed”, “matches the file’s body (volume +0.0002 %)”);
  • the replay’s bodies also get name (the body’s name, without its uid), and the replayed bodies the file does not have are listed as extra_body_rows (name, row_status, row_status_message);
  • each design (an .f3d file’s report.designs[], every other import’s report) gets verdict, and the result gets the verdict of all its designs: {"status": "ok"|"warning"|"error", "message", "rows": {"ok", "warning", "error"}, "warnings"}, warnings the count of the report’s warnings. The status is error when a row is, else warning when a row is or the report has a warning, else ok. The message: “Everything came in: all 11 features parametric, the body matches the file.”, “Came in with 2 warnings.”, “1 feature could not be imported; 1 warning.”
StatusRows
okparametric; a FreeCAD object that came in as a body, a component, occurrences or part of another’s result; an item left out as the file has it (its note: suppressed or rolled back in the file, no geometry of its own, no mesh stored, a FreeCAD result that is the shape before it); a valid body; a body within 0.01 % of the file’s volume (BODY_VOLUME_TOLERANCE) and 0.01 mm of its bounding box (BODY_BOX_TOLERANCE, the imports’ geometric tolerance) with the same number of faces; a file found and imported; an IFC product that came in; a SolidCraft feature with nothing to bring in; levels and blocks
warningpartial; fallback; a parametric item with an accepted deviation; a body past the tolerances or with other faces; a body whose validity could not be checked; a replayed body the file does not have; a sub-assembly that contains itself; a part that came in as its stored bodies because its replay failed, or some of whose features came in partly or as fallbacks; an IFC product partial or not imported; a SolidCraft feature without a counterpart
erroran item skipped for another reason; a body of the file the import has none for; a body not built or not valid; a file not found or not imported; a part some of whose bodies are missing or not valid; an IFC product or a SolidCraft feature that could not be built

The final bodies’ warning (the final bodies differ from those stored in the file, mitcad#1175) now starts past 0.01 % of the volume, where the row turns a warning, rather than 1e-6. The level of the import’s notices (mitcad#1040) is unchanged: a row’s status is the report’s.

An item’s note_message (mitcad#1741) also says the import’s own wording plainly (report_status::plain_words): “edges whose dressup ASM history state 5 has” is “edges found from the file’s fillet history”, “2 curves within 0.00001 mm of the edges of the face it lies on put on them” is “2 curves snapped onto the face’s edges”; note keeps the import’s words for agents and the log. The timeline’s import notes of a partial item or a fallback (“Partly imported: …”, “Stands in for …”) say them plainly too.

Tests: core.import-base (report_status.rs: the statuses, the tolerances, the verdicts, the plain notes), core.import-replay (final_bodies_that_differ_are_a_warning) and the UI tests tools/ui-import-report-status-test.sh, app.ui-windows-import-report-status, app.ui-macos-import-report-status (app/COMMANDS.md, “A status on every row, and a verdict”).

References between the entries of a command array (mitcad#1897)

MCP’s model_command runs an array of commands in order as one undo step (docs/mcp.md, “Command arrays”). A later entry uses what an earlier one made without predicting its ids:

  • An entry names its result with "as": "<name>": a letter or _, then letters, digits, _ or -, at most 64 characters, each name once in an array. The name is no field of the command: it is left out before the command runs. A single command may have one too; it changes nothing.
  • A later entry takes a value of that result with {"ref": "<name>.<path>"} wherever it takes a value: an id (a sketch’s "sketch", a curve, a feature’s uid), a point input, an item of a list.
