Tests: core.model.sketch (core/model-tests/sketch/src/sketch_explode_text_2163_tests.rs), the rewrite’s own in core.model, the UI tests tools/ui-sketch-explode-text-test.sh, app.ui-windows-sketch-explode-text and app.ui-macos-sketch-explode-text.

Parameter groups (mitcad#2180)

User parameters can be put in groups, so that a design with many of them lists them by what they belong to (Table, Cabinet, Material). A group is organization only, like a comment: no value, expression or feature changes with it, and no group command recomputes.

  • A path. A group is a path of names nested with /: Cabinet/Doors is the group Doors in the group Cabinet. Each name is written trimmed (" Cabinet / Doors " is Cabinet/Doors); an empty name in a path (Cabinet//Doors, /Cabinet) is refused. A group’s parent groups always exist: making Cabinet/Doors makes Cabinet too.
  • A parameter is in at most one group. add_parameter takes group (in the same undo step; the group is made when it does not exist), and set_parameter’s group moves a parameter ("" takes it out of its group). set_parameter_group moves several in one undo step ({"cmd": "set_parameter_group", "names": ["width", "depth"], "group": "Cabinet"}, Move 2 Parameters to Group Cabinet). Only user parameters have groups: a dimension’s or a feature’s parameter is refused (d1 is not a user parameter: only user parameters go in groups). A parameter that is deleted, or that a feature adopts, leaves its group; a renamed one keeps it.
  • Groups without parameters are kept. add_parameter_group makes a group before anything is in it (Add Parameter Group Cabinet); a group whose parameters all moved away stays.
  • Rename. rename_parameter_group gives a group a whole new path ({"group": "Cabinet", "new_group": "Table"}, Rename Parameter Group Cabinet to Table): its subgroups and every parameter in them follow (Cabinet/Doors becomes Table/Doors). A new path may put the group under another one (Material/Fronts); the parents it lacks are made. Refused: a group that does not exist, a path another group has, and a path within the group itself. The same path is no undo step.
  • Delete. delete_parameter_group never deletes a parameter: the group’s own parameters move to its parent group (out of any group when it is at the top), and its subgroups with their parameters move up a level, merged with a group of the same path there (Delete Parameter Group Cabinet). The result’s moved lists the parameters that were in the group itself.
  • Undo. Each command is one undo step; a command that changes nothing (a parameter already in the group) is none.
  • Queries. The parameters query gives a grouped parameter’s group (none for an ungrouped one); the parameter_groups query lists every group with its path, its own name, its parent and the parameters in it, a parent before its subgroups, in the order the groups were made.
  • The design file. A grouped user parameter is saved with "group": "Cabinet/Doors", and the top-level parameter_groups lists every group’s path (also of a group that holds no parameter) in order. A design saved before groups has neither and opens with every parameter ungrouped. Comparing two designs reports a parameter whose group changed (group).

Edit Parameters shows the groups under User Parameters (app/COMMANDS.md, “Edit Parameters, groups”).

Code: core/model/src/parameter_groups.rs (ParameterGroups, the paths), core/model/src/document/parameter_groups.rs (the commands), core/model-api/src/parameter_groups.rs (the commands and the query). Tests: core.model (parameter_groups.rs’ own), core.model.api (core/model-tests/api/src/parameter_groups_tests.rs: nested paths, moves, rename and delete with parameters, undo, the file round trip and a file from before groups), and the UI tests tools/ui-parameter-groups-test.sh, app.ui-windows-parameter-groups and app.ui-macos-parameter-groups.

Extend to Meet in a sketch (mitcad#2178)

sketch.extend_to_meet (core/sketch/src/modify/meet.rs) extends or shortens two curves to a point where they meet, so that they end in one shared corner point: two lines, a line and an arc, or two arcs. One undo step, Extend to Meet in <sketch>; the work step’s kind is extend_to_meet, with both curves as changed.

commandfieldsresult
sketch.extend_to_meetsketch; a, at_a [x, y]; b, at_b [x, y]; result (a number, 0 by default)the editing commands’ fields, joined (the shared point), results (how many results there were), result (the one taken)
{"cmd": "sketch.extend_to_meet", "sketch": "F1", "a": "c3", "at_a": [2, 0],
 "b": "c4", "at_b": [20, 12]}
  • Where they can meet: on the whole carriers, the endless line through a line’s ends and the whole circle of an arc: two lines meet in one point, a line and an arc or two arcs in none, one (touching, within a millionth of the curves’ size) or two.
  • What stays: the part of each curve around its pick, as Trim reads a pick. A line’s end on the meeting point’s side of the pick moves there, extending or shortening the line. An arc whose circle meets the other curve on the arc moves the end on that side of the pick; at a point in the arc’s gap it can reach it either way round, giving two results, the end nearer the pick first. A result that would leave a curve without length, or close an arc, is not one.
  • Which result: the results are ordered by the sum of the distances from their meeting point to the two picks, nearest first; results at one point keep the order above. result takes one of them, counted round (so result 2 of two results is the first again): the application’s Tab steps through them. The application’s tool computes the same list for its preview (app/sketch/ExtendToMeet.cpp).
  • One point: a moving end that only this curve uses (and that is neither fixed nor projected) moves to the meeting point with its constraints and dimensions, which then measure the new place (as Extend’s end does, mitcad#362); an end shared with another curve stays with it, and the curve gets a new end. The two ends then become one point (Points that become one).
  • Constraints and dimensions keep their meaning: a length or an arc_length of either curve takes the new value (a parameter with an expression or shared with another dimension keeps its value, and the solve then follows it); a horizontal, vertical, parallel or other constraint of the curve stays; a midpoint on either curve goes, since the middle moves. Curves that meet tangentially (a line touching an arc’s circle, two touching circles) get a tangent between them when the sketch still solves with it.
  • Refused in words (the message names no ids; its detail does for agents): one curve picked twice, a curve that is no line or arc, parallel lines, lines on one line, a line that misses an arc’s circle, arcs whose circles do not reach each other or that share a centre, meeting points where a curve would shrink to nothing, and ends that already meet there. A projected curve or one a derived offset computes is refused as for sketch.extend (convert it first); an offset’s or a pattern’s curve is first freed, with sketch.trim’s notes (mitcad#1755, mitcad#2007).

Code: core/sketch/src/modify/meet.rs (meet_results, SketchEdit::extend_to_meet). Tests: core.sketch (core/sketch/src/extend_meet_tests.rs), core.model.sketch (core/model-tests/sketch/src/sketch_extend_to_meet_2178_tests.rs), the UI tests tools/ui-sketch-extend-to-meet-test.sh, app.ui-windows-sketch-extend-to-meet and app.ui-macos-sketch-extend-to-meet.

Draft analysis

A draft check before molding (mitcad#2166): each face of bodies colored by its draft from the pull direction of a mold, the angle between the face’s outward normal n and the plane square to the pull: asin(n · pull). It is an analysis only: no body, feature or export changes. The work is done in Rust (print_analysis::drafts in core/model/src/print_analysis.rs, the query in api/print.rs) on each body’s Kernel::triangle_mesh as Print Analysis meshes it (the 3MF export’s tolerance), triangle by triangle, in three classes:

ClassDraftMeans
positiveangle or more towards the pull (n · pull ≥ sin(angle))releases when the mold half is pulled along the pull
underless than angle either wayneeds more draft
negativeangle or more against the pullreleases only when pulled the opposite way (the other mold half)

A face exactly at the angle has enough; with angle 0 nothing is under and a face square to the pull is positive. Curved faces are classed where they are steep, triangle by triangle, not as a whole. A face hidden by another part of the body along the pull (an undercut) is not looked for.

A draft analysis is kept in the document as an analysis with "type": "draft" (default name Draft1, Draft2, …):

{"type": "draft", "bodies": ["F2.b0"], "pull": {"body": "F2.b0", "face": "F2:end_a"},
 "occurrence": "O1", "flip": false, "angle": 1}
FieldValue
bodiesbody uids, at least one
pullthe pull direction: a plane’s normal (an origin or construction plane, a planar face, a fixed plane) or a line’s direction (an origin or construction axis, a straight edge, a sketch line, a fixed axis) as a reference; null (the default): the design’s +Z. A face or edge follows the model by its topological name (found again after a sketch change renames it, as features’ references are), and the direction is taken where the reference is at the marker
occurrencethe pull reference’s occurrence, a path from the root ("O1/O3"), as a section’s occurrence: a component’s face, edge or datum is moved through it into design coordinates; left out for the root, or inferred when the component is placed once. Assembly moves rewrite it as a section’s
flipthe pull reversed (default false; written only when true)
anglethe least draft a face needs, degrees, from 0 to less than 90 (default 1)

Other fields are refused, in commands and in design files. add_analysis and edit_analysis refuse an angle out of range, no body, a body that is not there at the marker, and a pull reference that is neither a plane nor a line there (an origin point, a curved face, a circular edge). The analyses query gives each draft analysis its file form with pull_direction (the unit pull, flipped when it says so, in design coordinates at the marker) or error (why a body or the pull reference is not there, in words: “the pull direction: …”; the analysis stays and the application shows it red with the reason). A design turned by Reorient keeps its pull with the bodies: the design’s +Z, an origin datum or a fixed plane or axis becomes the one the turn takes it to.

QueryFieldsResult
draft_analysisbodies (all at the marker when empty or left out), pull, occurrence, flip, angle (1) as above, deviation (mm; the 3MF export’s 0.03 when left out), triangles (true; false: the areas only)pull (unit, design coordinates), angle, bodies: [{body, name, area, positive_area, under_area, negative_area (mm²), positive_share, under_share, negative_share (0 to 1), triangles: {positive, under, negative: [[x, y, z, x, y, z, x, y, z], …]}}], and area, the three areas and the three shares of all of them

A body is analysed where Print Analysis analyses it (its first shown occurrence, else its first; a mirroring placement keeps its triangles facing out), so triangles are in design coordinates. A body that is gone, a pull reference that cannot be found or a mesh the kernel cannot make answers {"error": ...}; an angle out of range or an unknown field is refused. Run inside a model job, the query stops when the job is cancelled. Results are kept by the body’s shape, its placement, the mesh tolerance, the pull and the angle (the print cache), so showing an analysis again computes nothing. model_render’s draft overlay (docs/mcp/) draws the under class and reports the other two in numbers (positive_area, negative_area).

In the application: Inspect › Draft Analysis (app/COMMANDS.md “Draft Analysis”). Code: core/model/src/document/analyses.rs (DraftAnalysis, Document::draft_pull, Document::pull_direction), core/model/src/print_analysis.rs (drafts, DraftClass), core/model-api/src/print.rs (DraftOps). Tests: core/model-tests/analysis/src/draft_analysis_tests.rs, core/model/src/print_analysis_tests.rs (a box with drafted walls of +2°, 0° and −2°, exact areas; a sphere by class), the UI tests tools/ui-draft-analysis-test.sh, app.ui-windows-draft-analysis and app.ui-macos-draft-analysis.

Selection sets

A selection set (mitcad#2192) is a name and a list of links to items of the design: bodies, occurrences and features (sketches, construction geometry and joints are features). It changes no geometry, timeline, bill of materials or export: every command below is one undo step that recomputes nothing, none when nothing changes. Members are kept by reference, the way the selection names items, never by name, so a renamed item stays a member and the query lists its new name.

A member, in commands, in the query and in the design file:

MemberFields
a bodybody (uid F2.b0; in commands also its name at the marker), occurrence (the path from the root that places it, O1/O4; left out in the root)
a featurefeature (uid F5; in commands also its name, refused when several features have it), occurrence as for a body
a component placed in the designoccurrence alone (its path from the root; the root itself is refused)

In commands an occurrence path may name the occurrences (Arm:1/Pin:2) instead of their uids. A member must be in the design: a body at the timeline marker, a feature in the timeline, placed where its path says (a feature or body of another component than the path’s end is refused, … is not in Rail:1). Each member is kept once, in the order first given.

CommandFieldsEffect
add_selection_setname (the next free SelectionSet<n> when left out or empty), members (default none)undo step Add Selection Set Favourites; refused when another set has the name; result name, members (the count)
set_selection_set_membersname, members (all of them; left out: those it has), add, removemembers replaces them, then add adds those not in it yet and remove takes those out (a member removed need not be in the design any more); undo step Change Selection Set Favourites; result name, members (the count)
rename_selection_setname, new_nameundo step Rename Selection Set SelectionSet1; refused: an empty name, a name another set has
delete_selection_setnamethe set alone, never its items; undo step Delete Selection Set Favourites
QueryFieldsResult
selection_setsevery set in the order added: name, members: each with kind (body, component, feature), its reference (body or feature), occurrence (the path, "" in the root), path_name (Arm:1/Pin:2, when placed by an occurrence), component (the component it is in), name (its current name: the body’s, the feature’s, the occurrence’s), type (a feature’s type: sketch, extrude, joint, …), exists (its item is in the design) and active (false for a feature suppressed or after the timeline marker, and a body that is not at the marker)
  • A deleted item leaves every set in the undo step that deletes it: a feature deleted takes its members and those of the bodies it made out of every set; an occurrence deleted takes itself and what it places. Undo brings them back with the item. A body that a later feature consumes, removes or that the marker rolls back stays a member, inactive.
  • The design file keeps the sets in selection_sets (name, members as above, with uids), left out when there are none; a member whose item the file does not have is left out when the design is read, a name listed twice is refused.
  • MCP has the four commands (their schemas in core/mcp/src/schemas/document.rs) and the query.

In the application: the Browser’s Selection Sets folder, Create Selection Set in the row and view menus (app/COMMANDS.md “Selection Sets”). Code: core/model/src/document/selection_sets.rs (SelectionSet, SetMember, Document::add_selection_set, set_selection_set_members, rename_selection_set, delete_selection_set, DocState::prune_selection_sets, called after every edit), core/model-api/src/selection_sets.rs. Tests: core.model.assembly (core/model-tests/assembly/src/selection_set_tests.rs), app.unit (browser_selection_sets.cpp), the UI tests tools/ui-selection-sets-test.sh, app.ui-windows-selection-sets and app.ui-macos-selection-sets.

The outline set (mitcad#2194)

A sketch’s outline set (GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#545) is the areas a person means by its closed shapes when they nest without crossing: a plate with holes is the plate less the holes, an island inside a hole is added, and separate outlines are each one. Extrude and Revolve start with it, a whole sketch picked for their Profiles gives it, and Show profiles fills it (app/COMMANDS.md “Profiles of a whole sketch and the outline set”).

  • When no two of the sketch’s own curves cross through each other, it is every region the sketch’s own curves bound (not face_bounded) at an even nesting depth, the depth being how many holes of the other such regions the region lies in. A plate with two holes and a square island inside one gives the plate’s ring and the island; two separate rectangles give both; regions side by side, which share a boundary piece (a rectangle split by a line, a cross of two lines in a rectangle), are all of it: the whole rectangle. Concentric circles alternate: the outer ring, the third ring, and so on.
  • Crossing means that two of the sketch’s own curves pass through each other at a point where one of the areas about it is outside every region or inside a hole (two overlapping circles, a circle across a rectangle’s side): which areas are meant is not clear, so the sketch has no outline set (outline_set empty, curves_cross true). A curve that ends on another, curves that touch (a slot against a rectangle, a circle inside another touching it), and curves that cross only inside an area (a cross in a rectangle, which divides it as a line does) do not cross. The supporting face’s edges are not the sketch’s own curves.
  • Regions bounded in part by the supporting face’s edges (the face’s leftover region around the drawn shapes, mitcad#1226) are not part of it, and their holes do not count in the depth: a circle drawn on a face is in the set.
  • Construction curves bound nothing, as for every profile.

The sketch query gives outline_set (region keys) and curves_cross; each row of the profiles query gives outline (true or false) for a region the sketch’s own curves bound in a sketch without crossing curves, and curves_cross: true for every region of a sketch with them. A row with "outline": false is what Show profiles draws without fill.

Code: core/sketch/src/outlines.rs (outline_set, OutlineSet), core/sketch/src/regions.rs (Arrangement::crossings, Layout::crossings), SketchOutput::outline_set (def.rs); the queries in core/model-api/src/sketch.rs and lib.rs. Tests: core/sketch/src/outlines_tests.rs (the plate with two holes and an island, separate rectangles, a split rectangle, a cross in a rectangle, overlapping circles alone and in a plate, a circle across a side, touching circles, concentric circles, a circle on a face), core/model-tests/api/src/outline_set_2194_tests.rs (the queries’ fields).

Features that follow an operation change (mitcad#2185)

An edit_feature that changes a feature’s operation between modifying bodies (Join, Cut, Intersect) and making them (New Body, New Component), or between New Body and New Component, takes along the later features that work only on the geometry the feature makes: a fillet on the extrude’s edges, a fillet on that fillet’s faces, a sketch on one of its faces.

  • Join (Cut, Intersect) to New Body or New Component: their references to the body the feature changed before ("body": "F4.b0") become the body that now carries its geometry (F8.b0; with several, the one on which their names of the feature’s faces and edges resolve), and for New Component they move into the component the feature makes. Their topological names stay as they are and resolve on that body.
  • New Body or New Component back to Join (Cut, Intersect): back onto the body the feature now merges into (or cuts), in the feature’s own component, so that the component it made can go.
  • New Body and New Component edited into each other: they move between the components, their body the same.

A later feature follows when it refers to the edited feature or to a feature that already followed, and to nothing else once its references to the old bodies are set aside. A feature that also names the old body’s own faces or edges (a fillet of an edge of the extrude and one of the block it joined) stays where it is and reports the reference that went, with its places, as before; so does one that names only the old body (a Scale of it) and one whose names of the feature’s geometry resolve on none of the bodies the feature now makes (an edge that existed only by the join). A feature of the made component that does not follow keeps the component: the edit back to Join is then refused as before (“has features or occurrences of its own”). The edit and the moves are one undo step.

The body each feature follows to is found by evaluating the edited feature with the features before it (from the cache; the features after it are not evaluated for that). The timeline query gives a feature that makes a component its made_component, and the timeline marks it in that component’s colour (the features that followed are in the component, component), at once after the edit.

Code: core/model/src/document/operation_follow.rs (Document::operation_follow, DocState::follow_operation), called from Document::edit_feature_keeping through DocState::edit_feature_following. Tests: core.model.assembly (core/model-tests/assembly/src/operation_follow_tests.rs: New Component, New Body and back, undo, mixed references stay, a feature of the made component that keeps it), cli.extrude_new_component_fillets_reported (the reported design under MITCAD_MITCAD_REPORTED, skipped without it), and the UI tests tools/ui-new-component-fillets-test.sh, app.ui-windows-new-component-fillets and app.ui-macos-new-component-fillets.

A whole design linked with its components (mitcad#2209)

insert_component linked (the default) of a whole design that has components (no parts, no parameters, not a library part) keeps the design’s structure, read only, so that its occurrence can be made Flexible (Flexible subassemblies) and moves as a flexible copy does:

  • The linked component holds the bodies of the design’s root as its base feature (the link’s feature; it may hold none, as the root of an assembly often has no bodies of its own: the base feature’s linked_tree is then true), and the design’s mount frames as before.
  • Each component of the design becomes a component of its own, named as in the design (made unique), holding the component’s own visible bodies as a base feature (linked_tree, in its own coordinates), with the materials and appearances the design gives them. Each occurrence of the design is placed where the design places it at its marker (in the linked component, or in another of these components), grounded, shown and see-through as there; a flexible one keeps its values.
  • The design’s joints, as-built joints and rigid groups come along as features of the components they belong to (a joint of the design’s root is one of the linked component), named as in the design where the name is free. A joint’s origins are fixed planes at the frames the design gives them ({"origin", "normal", "x_axis"} on the same occurrence path), its offset, angle, limits and position numbers: nothing of it depends on the design’s history. Joints that do not hold in the design, suppressed or rolled-back ones, constraint sets and motion links do not come along.
  • Read only. Every one of these components is refused as the linked component is (“Key is part of Slider, which is linked from slider.mitcad; it changes only with that file”): activating it, adding or editing its features, drive_joint of their joints, set_occurrence_transform, set_occurrence_grounded, deleting an occurrence in it, and making an occurrence in it flexible. A drag moves a part of it only inside a flexible occurrence of the linked component, for that occurrence alone; otherwise it is refused. Shown and see-through stay this design’s own.
  • Flexible. The linked component has components in it, so its occurrence can be made flexible (set_occurrence_flexible): the design’s joints then move in the parent for it alone (drive_joint with occurrence, drags, Animate), and the parent’s joints may join the design’s parts ("occurrence": "O1/O3").
  • Read again (update_link, update_links, opening the design): everything is updated in place: the bodies, the occurrences' placements and grounding, the joints (whose uids stay, so that a flexible occurrence keeps its own values of them, within their new limits), and a component renamed in the design is renamed. New components, occurrences and joints come in. Those the design no longer has go, with the features that depend on them, but a part that a feature of this design uses (a joint of the parent on it) stays where it was with its saved bodies and the line “Key:1 is no longer in slider.mitcad; it stays where it was, as this design uses it”. A flexible occurrence’s own values of a joint gone are dropped with the line “Slider:1: its own value of Joint1 is dropped, as slider.mitcad no longer has the joint”. The lines are update_link’s messages (load warnings for update_links).
  • The flat form stays. A design without components, chosen parts (Linked parts of a design), designs linked with options, library parts and every link saved before keep the design’s bodies as one base feature, also when they are read again; chosen parts made whole again by set_link_parts with null stay flat too.
  • Not with these. set_link_parts is refused (“Slider keeps the components of its design; to link chosen parts of it, insert the design again with Choose parts”), and so is set_link_envelope showing it by its envelope (“Slider:1 keeps the components of its design, so it is not shown by its envelope”): a parent’s joints may join its parts, which neither would keep. Carrying the design’s joints into those forms is a follow-up.

The design file records what was made for what in the link’s tree (components: source, name, component, feature, gone; occurrences: source, occurrence, gone; features: source, feature), by the design’s uids; Save Component as Design keeps it for a linked component inside the saved one. The components query gives the linked component "link_tree": true and each of its components "linked_in" (the linked component’s uid); the Browser disables Choose Linked Parts… and Show as Envelope… on it with the reason, and a feature of one of its components opens the linked design’s notice.

Code: core/model/src/document/link_tree.rs (Document::design_tree, DocState::build_link_tree, DocState::update_link_tree), called from Document::insert_file and Document::file_link_updates; Assembly::linked_in, DocState::editable; crate::joints::resolved_origin_frame. Tests: core.model.links (core/model-tests/links/src/link_tree_tests.rs), the UI tests tools/ui-linked-flexible-test.sh, app.ui-windows-linked-flexible and app.ui-macos-linked-flexible.

A join of faces that touch themselves a period apart, and why a union fails (mitcad#2170)

The reported join of 31 bodies (a hub with 30 blades, triangles, rods and a ring; A union holds every body it joins) now gives one body holding every body. Its finned rods’ side faces are cylinders without a seam: each one’s boundary runs down a line of the cylinder, round the rod and back up beside the fins, and meets itself across the cylinder’s period at one vertex, where two fins meet the rod; a small inner wire, where the third fin’s knife edge grazes the rod, touches it there. Where the ring or a triangle trims such a face, the geometry kernel’s boolean split it into faces that closed in space but not on the cylinder (they ran from one side of that vertex round to the other), and the union was invalid. The kernel now tells the two sides of such a vertex apart (OCCT port patch 2170, described in third_party/vcpkg-ports/docs/booleans-and-face-merge.md).

Where a wrong union is made again without the bodies lying wholly inside others and that union fails too, its reason is the reason the union fails: that union is the union of all. The mends tried after it (the bodies the first union held and those it missed, each united on their own; fuzzy values) are still tried, and where one gives a sound union it is taken, but where they fail as well their own failure is not reported. Before the port patch, the reported join failed with the union of the shapes gave an empty result: the union of the 24 bodies the first union missed (five of them rods each lying inside one of the others) was empty, while the union of the 26 bodies left after the rods was not empty but invalid. Such a union now fails with the union produced an invalid shape; Combine keeps the target and the tools as before.

Code: geometry/src/pattern.cpp (united), the port patch 2170-bopalgo-wiresplitter-vertex-met-a-period-apart.patch. Tests: geometry.port.2170 (such a face built from scratch, split from its own edges and with a section line across it, in every order of its edges), geometry.join_holds_inputs (from MITCAD_MITCAD_REPORTED: the reported join is one valid body; each body not lying inside another has its whole volume in common with it).

A loop through several sketches (mitcad#2198)

A boundary_surface loop may take sketch curves of several sketches, planar and 3D, listed in any order, one entry per sketch or more:

{"type": "boundary_surface", "boundary": [
   {"sketch": "F1", "curves": ["c1"], "chain": true, "continuity": "g1"},
   {"sketch": "F3", "curves": ["c3"], "chain": true},
   {"sketch": "F2", "curves": ["c1"], "chain": true, "continuity": "g1"}]}

Each entry’s curves are read as the runs they make: curves joined at their ends (within 1e-6 of the largest coordinate, at least 1e-6 mm) are one chain, and the curves of a sketch the loop passes twice (two runs in one entry) are two chains. The chains are then joined end to end in the loop’s order before the kernel fills them, whatever order they are listed in:

  • Without a chain of edges, the chains must close into one loop. Refused at evaluation, in words: the boundary curves do not close into a loop: the curves of Sketch1 end at (x, y, z) with no curve going on, the boundary curves do not make one loop: more than two of them meet at (x, y, z), … they close into several.
  • With one chain of edges, chains of curves that make one open path run along it from a free end, and the edges close the loop after them.
  • Anything else (a closed chain beside others, several chains of edges, chains that make no one path) is passed as listed, for the kernel to join.

Each chain keeps its entry’s continuity: g1 against the sketch’s plane for a planar sketch’s curves. The edges of a loop, the network and the definition’s form are as before.

In the application (app/COMMANDS.md, “Surface modelling”): Boundary Surface is enabled by any sketch, 3D sketches too; Fill a Loop’s Boundary Curves take curves of several sketches, one entry for each sketch in the order its first curve was picked, Tangent to Sketch Plane making the planar sketches’ entries g1 (shown only while a planar sketch’s curves are picked), Edge Continuity shown only while Boundary Edges or Open Edges Of hold something; editing such a feature lists all its sketches’ curves.

Code: core/model/src/features/boundary_surface.rs (read_loop, runs, loop_order), app/commands/SurfaceCommands.cpp (boundarySurfaceCommand). Tests: core/model-tests/features-solid/src/surface_modelling_tests.rs (a_boundary_loop_joins_curves_of_several_sketches_end_to_end, a_boundary_loop_runs_its_curves_as_one_path_before_a_chain_of_edges), tools/ui-surface-boundary-sketches-test.sh (a design with only a 3D sketch enables Boundary Surface; a loop of three lines in two planar sketches and a 3D sketch filled, Edge Continuity hidden until an edge is picked, the feature edited with its three curves).

Refused expressions in words (mitcad#2181)

A parameter command refused for its expression or a limit (add_parameter, set_parameter: a syntax error, a name that is no parameter, a value of another kind, a division by zero) says what is wrong and where in words, without the parser’s byte offset and without a parameter X: before it; the model’s own text, with the offset, is the agents’ detail, in the refusal’s last line (Errors: message, places and detail):

{"cmd": "add_parameter", "name": "cabinet_lenght", "expression": "table_lenght+sheet_thickness", "unit": "mm"}

is refused with

The expression of cabinet_lenght uses table_lenght, which is not a parameter.
[placed: {"message":"The expression of cabinet_lenght uses table_lenght, which is not a parameter.","detail":"parameter cabinet_lenght: unknown parameter table_lenght at byte 0"}]
  • The sentences. The expression of X uses Y, which is not a parameter., The expression of X cannot be read: … (a syntax error), The expression of X cannot be worked out: … (an evaluation error); for a limit The minimum of X uses Y, … and the same with maximum and step. User-given parameter names stay in them (they may look like a sketch’s ids, p1).
  • A near miss. A name that is no parameter but close to one (a letter wrong, missing, extra or two swapped, or another case; one edit for a name of 3 to 5 letters, two for a longer one, none for one or two letters) is offered: … which is not a parameter. Did you mean table_length?; never the parameter’s own name.
  • While it is typed. formula_help’s error has message in the same words (table_lenght is not a parameter. Did you mean table_length?), detail with the offset and start and end, the UTF-8 byte range a field marks; a selection’s error is in words with its detail beside it. Its optional unit ("mm", "deg", "mm^2", "" for a number, "Text") checks the value in that unit, in place of kind’s: Add User Parameter checks a new parameter’s expression with it before OK. The evaluate query’s refusal of an expression (a value field’s check) is in the same form as a command’s.

Code: core/expr/src/parser.rs and eval.rs (ParseError::message, EvalError::message), core/expr/src/table.rs (TableError::message, ParameterTable::refusal_message, eval_message, near_name), core/expr/src/near_name.rs, core/model-api/src/lib.rs (parameter_refusal), formula_help.rs, evaluate.rs. Tests: core/expr/src/tests.rs (refusals_in_words_have_no_offsets_and_offer_a_near_miss), near_name.rs’s own, core.model.api (core/model-tests/api/src/parameter_refusal_words_tests.rs), the UI tests tools/ui-parameter-error-put-right-test.sh, app.ui-windows-parameter-error-put-right and app.ui-macos-parameter-error-put-right.

BUILD: profiles in parallel (mitcad#2201)

build_place with at.place parallel lays a profile (a part cut to length) along a target profile: their length axes parallel, a long face of the new profile against the outer plane of the target’s side picked, so that it rests across the slot opening. The side may be above, below or beside the target: it is the one of the face picked (at.geometry a side face of the target, at.point where on it) or of the side frame picked (a slot frame, a member’s face frame or a side’s middle side_x+). An end face is refused.

{"cmd": "build_place", "part": {"source": "S2"},
 "at": {"occurrence": "O1", "geometry": {"body": "F3.b0", "face": "F3:part(F2:side(c2))"},
        "point": [3, 10, 120], "place": "parallel",
        "across": "middle", "from": "a", "offset": 0},
 "rotate": "0 deg"}
  • Across (at.across): middle (the default) centres the new profile’s section on the side: on the side’s middle between two or more slots (Across a side with several slots), else on its only slot or face frame. slot puts the section’s centre on one slot of the side: the slot frame picked, else the slot nearest at.point (the side’s first slot without a point). Slots that do not lie in one plane have no middle: the slot picked then.
  • Rotate (rotate, quarter turns) turns the new profile about its length axis; the face that then faces the target is the one in contact. Unturned it rests on its widest face (a section at least as wide along its X as along its Y on its −Y face, else on its −X face: a 20 x 40 on a 40 mm face); 90 degrees on the next face (the 20 mm one of a 20 x 40). Any other angle is refused.
  • Length: left out, or {"match": "target"}, the new part’s length is the target’s own length parameter (its derived part’s length slot uses that parameter), so it follows the target’s length; a value is a typed length. A bound length is refused.
  • From and Offset (at.from, at.offset) place it along the target as a part on a side is placed (Side placements): from a (the default) its end A from the target’s end A, from b its end B from the target’s end B (positive towards A), from middle its middle from the target’s (positive towards B); gap is refused. Offset 0 when left out: with the target’s length both ends are flush. Unlike a side placement it may overhang the target’s ends (a 600 mm profile from end A at offset 0 on a 400 mm target: flush with end A, 200 mm past end B).
  • flip, tilt, mitre and a bound length are refused; the systems need not fit (the profile is in no slot).

What it makes. A slider joint along the target’s frame (slide axis x, along the target), flipped, between the new part’s end_a frame with a frame_override and the target’s frame. The override puts the frame on the contact face: its origin on the face, centred on the section, at end A; its z out of the face; its x along the part. The joint’s angle is 0 (the override takes the turn). Its position.tx is bound to from as a side placement’s (an expression of the target’s length parameter from end B and the middle; with the target’s length, the offset itself, negated from end B). So the profile follows the target when the target moves or turns, and when its length changes: a matched length with it, a typed one keeping its place from its reference. The component’s record has from and parallel: true; the file keeps both, so the reference and the offset are there when the design is opened again.

Preview. build_preview’s place is parallel; side is as on a side (from, offset, point, width the part’s length, across: middle, slot, or null on a side with one frame), snaps is empty, and parallel has target (component), occurrence, frame (the target’s frame it lies on), across, rotate (radians), length (match or typed) and normal (the side’s outward normal, in the design). length.value is the target’s length or the typed one.

build_parts. A part placed so has parallel: {target, frame, across, rotate, length} (length match or typed), and its rotate is that turn (its joint does not turn); from and offset are as a part on a side has them. Null for any other part.

Editing. build_edit of such a part takes at.offset, at.from (a new From alone keeps it where it is), at.across (middle, slot), rotate (quarter turns), length (a value, or {"match": "target"}), config and parameters: the part is placed anew on the same side with what changed (its joint and its derived part edited), in one undo step (Edit <name>; changed lists offset, from, across, rotate, length, config, parameters). flip, tilt, to, lie, at.point and a bound length are refused; ends, machining, cuts, grade and limits go in a build_edit of their own (as for any part). at.across and {"match": "target"} on a part that is not placed in parallel are refused.

A matched length shares the target’s parameter: a typed length detaches it (a parameter of its own), and binding the target’s length later (Build › Length) leaves the profile at the length it had.

Code: core/model-build/src/parallel.rs (plan_parallel, contact_override, parallel_of, ParallelCrateOps::edit_parallel), place.rs (PlaceKind::Parallel, LengthInput::Match), the record’s parallel in core/model/src/build/mod.rs, core/model-api/src/build.rs (the preview’s parallel, build_parts’ parallel). Tests: core/model-tests/build-frames/src/parallel_tests.rs (a 20 x 40 on a 400 mm 20 x 20 crossmember: matched and typed lengths, the three references, above, below and beside, Rotate, a side with two slots centred and on a slot, the target moved, turned and longer, a reopened file, build_edit, refusals, side and end placements as before). The application: app/COMMANDS.md, BUILD, Parallel.

Print service check (mitcad#2214)

A component library may say that its components, or some of them, are not for print services: their authors do not allow their parts to be printed as a service. The manifest’s non_printable says it, on the library (every component) or on a component (over the library’s, also false to allow one component of a non-printable library); it is set by hand only, never inferred (docs/libraries.md, “Not for print services”). Everything is printable by default.

  • The design keeps it. A part inserted from such a library (linked or a copy) records "non_printable": true in its library record (Library parts), and so does a BUILD source’s record in library_sources; a printable part’s record leaves it out. It is copied when the part is inserted or updated (update_library_parts, another version or row takes the flag of that version), so that it holds when the design opens without the library, and it goes with the part when the part’s design is copied out (an unlinked copy, Save Component as Design of a component that holds it), as the licence does. The library_parts query’s library and library_show’s components (non_printable, the component’s else the library’s) give it.
  • It belongs to the component, not the design. The bodies of such a component and of every occurrence of it, also nested in a subassembly and also a BUILD part made of such a source, are not for print services; the design, its own bodies and the other components stay printable. A design is never non-printable as a whole.
  • It stops only print services. The user’s own export and Send to Slicer are not affected. A future cloud print upload must ask print_service_check and send only the printable bodies: the non-printable parts’ bodies are left out (the upload is refused when only such bodies were chosen), and the user is told in words which parts were left out (the answer’s message).
  • The component’s properties show the read-only row Library/Print service = Not for print services for such a part (nothing for a printable one); Insert from Library and the Build tab’s pickers say “Not for print services” in a component’s details.
QueryResult
print_service_checkOptional bodies (uids) and components (uids or names, or {"component", "occurrence"}, as the properties query takes them: a component’s bodies with its sub-components’); every body of the design when both are left out. Answers printable and not_printable (body uids), bodies (one per body: body, name, component and component_name (none for the root’s), printable, and places, one per occurrence path that places it: path (O1/O4, none for the root’s), path_name, printable, and for a place that is not printable component, component_name and library of the part that forbids it and its message), parts (each non-printable part’s placement once: component, component_name, occurrence (its path by names), library, designation, license, message), components (those asked for) and message

A body is not printable at a place when its own component, or a component its occurrence path passes through, is a non-printable library part, or when a placed part of a non-printable source made it; a body counts as not_printable when any of its places is. The messages name the part, where it is placed and its library, without ids: Square pin (TP 1 M4x16) at Bracket:1/TP 1 M4x16:1 from the library test-pins: not for print services; the answer’s message says how many bodies may go: All 3 bodies may be sent to a print service., 1 body of 3 is not for print services and is left out: ... . The other 2 may be sent to a print service., or, when none may go, The body may not be sent to a print service: ... and None of the 2 bodies may be sent to a print service: ....

Code: core/model/src/document/print_service.rs (Document::non_printable_record, Document::print_service_block), core/model-api/src/print_service.rs (the query), the manifest’s field in core/vcs/src/library/manifest.rs (Manifest::non_printable_of). Tests: core.model.links (core/model-tests/links/src/print_service_tests.rs: the record kept when saved and opened without the library, a copy and a component saved as a design keeping it, an update taking a version’s flag, the query per body with a nested occurrence, a chosen body and component, the properties row), core.model.build-frames (core/model-tests/build-frames/src/print_service_build_tests.rs: a BUILD part of a non-printable source left out, its source’s record kept without the library) and core.vcs (core/vcs/src/tests/library_print.rs: the library’s flag, a component’s override both ways, a malformed flag refused).

Group identical parts in the Bill of Materials’ views (mitcad#2215)

{"query":"parts_list","view":"parts","group_identical":true} (and "view":"structured") combines the rows of equal parts, as the list of every component does (Read-only BOM grouping): the same measured key (volume, bounding-box dimensions in the component’s own axes, face count and material ids, within 1e-6). Each placed library profile is a component of its own, so without grouping equal profiles are separate rows; grouped they are one, and a part made by hand to the same size and material joins them.

  • Parts only: rows are combined across the whole design. A part’s key is its own bodies; a Purchased, Inseparable or Reference row that holds components is keyed with what it holds; a body of the design’s own is keyed by itself and may join a component’s row.
  • Structured: only siblings (rows under the same parent row) are combined. A row that holds components is keyed with what it holds and combines with such rows only, never with a part’s; what it holds is listed once, below the row that stays.
  • Rows of different BOM Structures are never combined (a Reference never with a counted row); unmeasured rows are combined with none.
  • A combined row stays where its first member was, keeps that member’s fields (name, properties, mass and volume of one) and sums quantity and placed. Items are numbered again in the grouped order (1, 2, 2.1; none for a Reference). totals.quantity sums the grouped rows; the design’s mass and volume do not change.
  • Every view row has group_names, the names of the rows it holds (its own first; just its own when nothing was combined), which the Bill of Materials window shows as the row’s tooltip. The answer adds group_identical.
  • The hardware to buy for printable bearings is not grouped (no shape), as in the list.

A drawing parts list’s table.group_identical already combined rows at both levels (top keys a first-level assembly with what it holds; parts as the parts-only view), with every grouped source keeping the grouped item number for its balloons; it now likewise combines only rows of the same BOM Structure.

Tests: core/model-tests/build-frames/src/bom_group_view_tests.rs (four placed library profiles, three equal, and an equal one made by hand: five rows in the parts-only view, two grouped; the structured view combining siblings only; a Reference kept apart) and the UI test of the BOM Structure (tools/ui-scripts/bom-structure.mitcad-ui, run by tools/ui-bom-structure-test.sh and app.ui-windows-bom-structure): Group identical parts enabled in Parts only and Structured, combining rows in Parts only.
